title: Snapshot / Restore schemas and artifact contract
description:
Purpose: snapshot-manifest.json, restore-metadata.json, persistence layout, and artifact validation contract. This epic owns the reusable schema/artifact vocabulary. The executable Firecracker snapshot path was promoted into the warm-pool performance lane and is captured by m80-rrp.3; future schema work should not claim execution is still deferred.

Contract: five-element artifact set (vmstate, memory, runtime-rootfs, scratch, boot-identity), fresh VM identity on restore, host-local persistence path, collision fail-closed, and explicit compatibility checks where m80 can verify them.

Relationship: m80-rrp.3 is the concrete capture/restore lifecycle implementation and benchmark; m80-rrp.4+ consumes that primitive for warm-pool allocation.
notes: schema and persistence children captured; execution lane moved to/closed under m80-rrp.3; first-line sizing captured by m80-0tf.4.1 with 1 vCPU/1024 MiB bench artifact; no open children remain

title: Bug: Ubuntu image kind bypasses overlay pivot and workspace drive order
description:
Real-KVM test attempt for m80-g0v8.6.6 showed Minimal image pivots through m80-guestd overlay, but Ubuntu image boots systemd directly on /dev/vda: mount output starts '/dev/vda on / type ext4 (ro,relatime)' with no 'overlay on / type overlay'. The same run with workspace attached showed systemd ordering cycle for workspace.mount and device dev-vdb, while the overlay design says workspace is /dev/vdc after adding rootfs overlay as vdb.

Impact: Ubuntu image kind does not provide the same per-VM writable root overlay semantics as Minimal, and workspace mounting is inconsistent with the current drive order. This invalidates m80-g0v8.6.6 for Ubuntu until architecture is clarified/fixed.

Evidence: 2026-05-08 real-KVM run of proposed crates/m80-firecracker/tests/image_kind_dispatch_real_kvm.rs::overlay_assembly_per_image_kind failed on Ubuntu after Minimal passed; console log showed workspace.mount ordering cycle and dev-vdb expectation; guest mount table showed /dev/vda on /.

Acceptance: decide whether Ubuntu must use the PID-1 overlay bootstrap or has a documented separate storage contract; then add/adjust real-KVM tests so Ubuntu either proves overlay+workspace semantics or explicitly proves the documented non-overlay behavior without silent base mutation.
notes: decision=hard cutover: Ubuntu image kind now means Ubuntu userland, not systemd startup; both Ubuntu and Minimal boot m80-guestd as PID 1 with /dev/vda lower, /dev/vdb overlay upper, /dev/vdc workspace. schema=manifest v4 rejects old v3 artifacts; doc=docs/behaviors/storage/overlay-assembly-image-kinds.md; tests=crates/m80-firecracker/tests/image_kind_dispatch_real_kvm.rs::overlay_assembly_per_image_kind plus m80-image-build/image-manifest regressions

title: E2E operationalization: privileged runner, artifact cache, cleanup, reporting
description:
The e2e tree (m80-g0v8 L1-L12 + m80-3xwa parity + m80-2ggw FC alignment + m80-ekbk perf bench) is broad and well-decomposed, but operationalizing it is separate work. Without this groundwork the privileged tests are theoretically present but practically unreliable: leaked taps after a failed run break the next run, no-kvm dev boxes can't tell which tests they're skipping, ad-hoc `#[ignore]` mixes "needs root" with "needs KVM" with "slow", and there's no structured signal for which class passed/failed/skipped.

This epic is orthogonal to the behavior-decomposition epics. m80-g0v8 says **what** to test; this epic says **how to actually run** the privileged subset reliably.

## Concerns this epic captures

1. **Stable privileged runner** — somewhere the real-KVM + root + iptables/netlink + bridge tests can execute. Local dev box, self-hosted CI runner, dedicated bare-metal — pick a strategy and make it reproducible.
2. **Artifact build + cache** — m80-guestd (musl), stripped kernel, rootfs ext4, image-build pipeline output. Cached across runs by a key (git SHA + relevant inputs) so privileged tests don't pay full rebuild cost every invocation.
3. **Ignored-test taxonomy + invocation** — distinguish `#[ignore]` reasons (no-kvm vs no-root vs slow) so an env can run the right subset; provide a wrapper that detects env and runs the right slice.
4. **Pre-test reaper** — privileged failures leak taps (tfc*), bridges (m80-br*), iptables chains, run-dirs, jailer cgroup paths. A reaper run before each privileged session inventories and cleans stale state from prior runs.
5. **Post-test cleanup verification** — each privileged test asserts no leaked resources after itself; or a follow-up sweep does the same.
6. **Structured reporting** — replace cargo test ad-hoc output with JSON-shaped pass/fail/skip-with-reason output so a batch run is interpretable.
7. **CI integration** — self-hosted runner job that runs the privileged battery on tag/cron/PR-label, uploads artifacts on failure.
8. **Local-dev documentation** — what to install, how to run the privileged subset locally, common cleanup recipes when something goes wrong.

## Why this is its own epic

m80-g0v8 = decomposition of behavior-under-test. m80-3xwa = parity surface. m80-ekbk = perf bench. Each epic answers "what behavior do we want pinned?" — this epic answers "how do we actually run those tests when many require privileged real-KVM and the absence of stable infrastructure means failures cascade and resources leak". Mixing the two collapses the audit trail when a test starts flaking.

## Acceptance for sub-epic

- Privileged runner is documented and reproducible (any team member can stand one up from the doc).
- A single `cargo`-or-script command runs the full privileged battery and emits structured results.
- A failure in one privileged test does not leak state that breaks the next test.
- The dev-box experience is documented: which subset runs without KVM, how to opt into the full battery, how to clean up when things go sideways.

## Sources

- 2026-05-08 audit conversation: e2e tree filed broadly under m80-g0v8 + L11 + L12; user noted operationalization as separate work.
- L11 malicious-runner + L12 malicious-guestd both depend on stable privileged execution.
- crates/m80-test-helpers and scripts/smoke.sh are the seeds; this epic extends them into a coherent operating story.

## Out of scope

- Adding new tests (covered by m80-g0v8, m80-2ggw, m80-3xwa, m80-ekbk).
- New behavior in m80 itself.
- Performance bench harness wiring (covered by m80-ekbk).

title: Privileged runner: stable KVM+root test environment
description:
Pick and document a stable execution environment for privileged real-KVM tests. Candidates: self-hosted GitHub Actions runner on bare-metal Linux with KVM, a dedicated dev VM with nested KVM, or a documented local-machine setup. Whichever is picked, the doc must let any team member reproduce the environment from scratch.

Files:
- docs/operations/e2e-privileged-runner.md (new)
- scripts/setup-privileged-runner.sh (new; idempotent setup script — parallel pattern to setup-zfs-tmpdir.sh)

Acceptance:
- doc covers: hardware requirement (KVM-capable CPU, KVM kernel module loaded), kernel modules to load (kvm_intel/amd, tap, bridge, vhost_vsock), package list (iptables, ipset, kernel-headers, build-essential), user/group setup (kvm group, sudo for iptables/netlink), file permissions (/dev/kvm, /dev/net/tun)
- setup script applies the doc's recipe; running it twice is a no-op
- verification: after running the setup, `cargo test --workspace -- --ignored` produces no env-related failures (only test-logic failures, if any)
- CHANGELOG (Test infra)

title: Artifact build + cache: m80-guestd, stripped kernel, rootfs
description:
Privileged tests rebuild m80-guestd-musl, the stripped kernel, and the rootfs ext4 every invocation. Cache them keyed on relevant inputs so a no-source-change re-run reuses the prior outputs.

Files:
- scripts/build-test-artifacts.sh (new; or extend scripts/smoke.sh)
- crates/m80-test-helpers/src/artifacts.rs (new module: cache-key computation, lookup, build-and-cache)

Cache keys:
- m80-guestd-musl: hash of crates/m80-guestd/** + crates/m80-proto/** + Cargo.lock entries for those crates
- stripped kernel: hash of m80-stripped.config + the FC kernel version pinned in image-build
- rootfs ext4: hash of m80-image-build inputs + image manifest schema version

Cache root: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/m80-test-artifacts/ or /tank/projects/m80/.cache/test-artifacts/.

Acceptance:
- doc at docs/operations/e2e-artifact-cache.md
- test crates/m80-test-helpers/tests/artifact_cache.rs verifies: same key returns cached artifact (skips rebuild), changed input invalidates cache
- second invocation of `cargo test --workspace -- --ignored` against unchanged source completes with rebuild time near zero (verified via wall-clock delta)
- CHANGELOG (Test infra)

title: Ignored-test taxonomy + selective invocation
description:
Replace ad-hoc `#[ignore]` with structured reasons so an env can run the right subset:

- `#[ignore = "requires-kvm"]`
- `#[ignore = "requires-root"]`
- `#[ignore = "requires-network-namespace"]`
- `#[ignore = "slow"]`

Provide a wrapper (Cargo nextest profile, or a shell script) that:
1. Detects environment (kvm available, euid==0, network-namespace permitted)
2. Runs the matching subset
3. Reports skipped tests with their reason

Files:
- Audit existing `#[ignore]` attributes across the workspace; rewrite each with a structured reason string (`grep -rn "#\[ignore\]" crates/`)
- scripts/run-e2e.sh (new wrapper) OR .config/nextest.toml profile defining filter sets
- crates/m80-test-helpers/src/env_detection.rs (new helper used by tests OR by the wrapper script)

Acceptance:
- doc at docs/operations/e2e-test-selection.md (taxonomy table + invocation cheatsheet)
- script/profile detects env and runs correct subset; verified by running on (a) a no-KVM dev container and (b) a privileged runner — both produce sensible skip lists
- new tests added under any of m80-g0v8 / m80-2ggw / m80-3xwa MUST use a structured `#[ignore = "..."]` reason; lint or convention test enforces this
- CHANGELOG (Test infra)

title: Pre-test reaper: stale-state inventory + cleanup
description:
A failed privileged test leaks resources (tap devices, bridges, iptables chains, run-dirs, jailer-owned cgroup paths). The next test inherits this state and can fail in confusing ways. Add a reaper that runs before each privileged session, inventories the leftover state, logs it, and cleans it.

Files:
- crates/m80-test-helpers/src/reaper.rs (new module)
- scripts/e2e-reap.sh (new; CLI wrapper for ad-hoc invocation)

Reaper scope (each idempotent and safe to run on a clean system):
- Tap devices matching m80's deterministic naming (tfc[0-9a-f]{12}): `ip link show` filter, `ip link delete`
- Bridges matching m80's naming (m80-br* OR whatever the deterministic pattern is): same approach
- iptables FORWARD inserts matching m80's per-VM rule comment tag: parse `iptables -S`, delete by handle
- Run-dirs under the documented run-root that are older than N hours and have no live pid (jailer .pid file with a process that no longer exists)
- jailer-owned cgroup paths that hold no tasks

Acceptance:
- doc at docs/operations/e2e-reaper.md (what it catches, what it does not, when to run it)
- test crates/m80-test-helpers/tests/reaper.rs: seeds a stale tap + stale bridge + stale chain + stale run-dir, runs reaper, verifies all gone
- reaper invoked at the start of `scripts/run-e2e.sh` (sibling bead)

title: In-jail device node creation via mknod (replace bind-mount of /dev/{kvm,net/tun,urandom})
description:
FC's stock jailer creates /dev/kvm, /dev/net/tun, /dev/urandom, and optionally /dev/userfaultfd inside the chroot using mknod with the correct major/minor numbers, then chowns them to the jailed UID/GID. m80 bind-mounts these devices from the host. Bind-mounted device nodes can be remounted read-write by a privileged process inside the jail, and the bind mount creates a link between the host's device namespace and the jail that mknod does not.

## Privilege requirement
**CAP_MKNOD or root** required for the mknod step. m80 already runs with elevated privilege (m80 acquires privilege at startup per CLAUDE.md scope; m80-preflight verifies). No new privilege model needed; just confirm CAP_MKNOD is in the verified-capability list.

## Scope
- Replace bind-mount of /dev/kvm with mknod (major 10, minor 232).
- Replace bind-mount of /dev/net/tun with mknod (major 10, minor 200) when networking is enabled.
- Create /dev/urandom via mknod (major 1, minor 9).
- **Optionally** detect and create /dev/userfaultfd. Note: minor is **dynamic** — must read /proc/misc at materialize time and parse for the userfaultfd entry. FC's jailer does this in env.rs:422-451.
- chown all created nodes to jailed UID/GID.
- Create /dev and /dev/net hierarchy inside the jail.

## Cross-references
- **m80-3xwa.1 A4** (0o700 + chown) — the chown step on mknod nodes follows the same uid/gid contract; confirm the chown invocation here matches A4's pattern.
- **m80-3xwa.1 A5** (/proc, /sys handling) — if /proc gets remounted fresh inside the jail, the userfaultfd minor read must use the host /proc, not the jailed one. Read /proc/misc BEFORE mount-NS entry or via an open fd captured early.

## Child tasks
1. IMPL: PlanStep::Mknod { path, major, minor, mode } via libc::mknod + libc::chown. Requires CAP_MKNOD or root.
2. IMPL: launch pipeline switches /dev/kvm and friends to mknod-provisioned; old bind-mount steps for devices removed.
3. IMPL: userfaultfd dynamic minor — read /proc/misc, parse for "userfaultfd" line, extract minor; skip device if not present.
4. TEST/DOCS: devices accessible inside jail with correct ownership; major/minor constants documented with kernel sources.

## Acceptance
- /dev/{kvm,net/tun,urandom} exist inside jail as device nodes (not bind mounts), owned by jailed UID/GID.
- /dev/userfaultfd present when host kernel exposes it; absent (with no error) when host doesn't.
- Existing real-KVM smoke passes.
- findmnt inside jail does not show host device bind mounts.

## Audit-confirmed code references
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:422-452 — mknod_and_own_dev() helper
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:684-711 — call sites

## Sources
- /tmp/m80-proposed-epic-beads.md Epic 3.
- 12-agent audit Lens 1 (FC mount/FS isolation), 2026-05-07.

Plan rejects caller bind destinations under dev. Runtime proof: end_to_end_real_kvm_jailer_security_parity asserts /proc/<firecracker_pid>/root/dev/kvm, dev/net/tun, and dev/urandom are character devices. Unit proof: plan_compute::dev_dest_is_rejected. Gates: fresh minimal image verified; real-KVM boot smoke and jailer security parity smoke passed.

title: Reset-evidence vocabulary in Stop events (typed exit reasons)
description:
Stop events today are scalar. We need a typed exit-reason field distinguishing the genuinely different cases.

## Reference

CLAUDE.md scope boundary excludes predecessor-style "Stage-H semantic events", but VM-lifecycle reset evidence is squarely in scope. Critical for snapshot-restore (m80-rrp.3) work — knowing whether a stop was clean lets restore decide whether to reuse state or restart.

## Scope

- Add ExitReason enum to the diagnostics.jsonl Stop event: NormalStop, ForceKill, KernelPanic, OomKill, SnapshotCapture, VmmExited(code).
- m80-firecracker classifies based on host-visible truth only (signal received, exit code observed, vsock graceful-stop ack vs SIGKILL fallback).
- No log-line scraping; no guess-from-context.
- Persisted in diagnostics.jsonl Stop event; readable by m80 inspect.

## Acceptance

- Each variant has a path in m80-firecracker that produces it (vsock graceful → NormalStop, SIGKILL after timeout → ForceKill, etc.).
- Test pins one variant per scenario.
- m80-rrp.3 (snapshot capture) emits SnapshotCapture, distinguishing it from a normal stop.

Formalize what 577412f / cc2aed2 partly added: per-phase boot timing as typed events in diagnostics.jsonl, not just tracing spans.

Commit cc2aed2 added per-phase timing instrumentation to launch.rs. m80-1f8.1.2 (diagnostic phases) lists StartupScavenge through Delete. Today timing lives in tracing spans only — gone after process exit.

## Scope

- Define PhaseStarted { phase, started_at } and PhaseCompleted { phase, started_at, ended_at, duration_us, outcome } event variants in the diagnostics.jsonl schema (schema_version bump or compatible additive change).
- m80-firecracker emits the events at every phase boundary already covered by tracing.
- Phases enum is shared with m80-1f8.1.2.
- Outcome is a typed enum (Ok / Err(class) / TimedOut) — no string collapse.

## Acceptance

- A successful launch produces a sequence of paired Started/Completed events covering every phase.
- A failed launch produces a Started without Completed, or Completed with outcome=Err.

title: Vsock metrics channel: guestd publishes counters/gauges over vsock (kata-style)
description:
Add a guest-side metrics channel inspired by kata's vsock-exporter pattern (src/agent/vsock-exporter). Guestd publishes typed counters and gauges over vsock; host renders them in the Prometheus scrape output.

## Reference

kata-exploration/01-architecture-and-crate-map.md mentions the vsock-exporter crate. Kata's pattern: small in-VM crate exposes a tiny ttRPC service; host calls into it during scrape. m80 equivalent: extend m80-proto with a Metrics request that returns a fixed-shape struct (CPU usage from /proc/stat, mem usage from /proc/meminfo, guestd-internal counters).

## Why

Without this, host-side metrics show only what the host can observe (cgroup totals). Guest-internal context (per-process, per-syscall classes, agent-tier counters) is invisible.

## Scope

- Add Metrics request/response to m80-proto (typed fields, no free-form key-value).
- m80-guestd implements it: read /proc/stat, /proc/meminfo, expose internal counters (requests served, errors).
- m80-observability scrape rendering includes guest-side metrics with a m80_guest_ prefix.
- Sampled at scrape time (no host-side polling between scrapes).

## Acceptance

- Scrape output includes m80_guest_cpu_*, m80_guest_mem_*, m80_guest_requests_total.
- Test: a guest under synthetic load shows non-zero CPU + memory in the scrape.

## Out of scope

- ttRPC migration (we stay JSON-framed per m80-proto).
- Aggregation across VMs (single-VM scrape only).
notes: Moved out of the m80-1f8 Prometheus-rendering closure path. Host-visible probe/health/prometheus rendering is captured; a guest metrics vsock channel remains a future protocol feature, not required for the diagnostics tail epic.

title: Guest-side log surface (visible guest stderr → host-readable, real time)
description:
Today the m80-1f8 epic covers HOST-side observability only (diagnostics.jsonl, probe, health, scrape). Guest-side stderr is structurally invisible until you SSH in or read logs post-mortem. The CLAUDE.md "diagnostics before hypotheses" principle (added 2026-05-04) is grounded in a real incident (ubuntu/idle 40 % flake) where one timestamped guest line would have saved an hour of investigation.

This epic closes the gap. The guest emits structured stderr; the host captures it in real time and persists per-VM; consumers (m80 logs, m80 diag) read it.

## Children

- m80-guestd structured stderr emission (boot_log lines: timestamp + phase + request_id + message)
- systemd unit StandardError=journal+console wiring + PID-1 console redirect equivalent
- Host captures /dev/console output to <run_dir>/console.log

## Why

Without this surface, every host-side timeout / hang / unexpected exit forces speculation. With it, the first move on any failure is "tail the guest console" — which CLAUDE.md says should always be the first move.

## Acceptance

- A guest panic produces a visible last-line message in <run_dir>/console.log within a bounded timeout.
- m80 logs <vm> (separate bead) tails this file.
- README of m80-guestd and m80-firecracker each document their half of the contract.
notes: guest stderr/log surface captured through structured guestd stderr, systemd/PID1 console wiring, jailer stdio_log, run_dir/console.log, and stress-ng failure classification

title: IMPL m80-guestd: structured stderr emission (timestamp + phase + request_id + msg)
description:
Today m80-guestd uses ad-hoc eprintln/log. Define a single boot_log line format and route every internal log through it.

## Format

[<RFC3339-timestamp>] [<phase>] [<request_id-or-boot>] <level> <message>

- phase: matches the diagnostics.jsonl phase enum (Boot, Ready, Exec, etc.).
- request_id: opaque ID from m80-cli/m80-firecracker, or "boot" pre-first-request.
- level: ERROR / WARN / INFO / DEBUG (DEBUG only when m80_DEBUG_WIRE or equivalent set).

## Why

Without structure, host-side capture (.5.3) is just text the user has to grep. With structure, m80 logs --request-id can filter cleanly.

## Scope

- m80-guestd uses tracing or a tiny custom layer; output to stderr.
- Never panic on log-format errors — log line emission must not fail the operation.
- Match the exit-on-error discipline: structured records to boot_log + exit(1), per CLAUDE.md.

## Acceptance

- Every existing eprintln/log call migrated.
- Test: parse 100 lines, all match the format.
- README of m80-guestd documents the format.
notes: doc=crates/m80-guestd/README.md; code=crates/m80-guestd/src/guest_log.rs; tests=cargo test -p m80-guestd including tests/guest_log.rs

title: IMPL m80-image-build + m80-guestd: systemd StandardError=journal+console + PID-1 console wiring
description:
Make guest stderr reach a host-readable location. Two paths depending on init mode:

- systemd mode: m80-guestd.service has StandardError=journal+console (and matching StandardOutput).
- PID-1 mode (per m80-6a0q): guestd opens /dev/console for stderr at startup.

## Why

Per CLAUDE.md ubuntu-idle-flake postmortem: making the other side's stderr visible is THE first debugging move. Today neither path is wired correctly.

## Scope

- Edit crates/m80-image-build/assets/m80-guestd.service: StandardOutput=journal+console, StandardError=journal+console (note: this file is currently modified in working tree; coordinate).
- m80-guestd PID-1 entrypoint: dup2 stderr/stdout to /dev/console early.
- Document trade-off: console output competes with kernel messages — set printk levels appropriately or accept the noise.

## Acceptance

- A guestd panic produces a visible last line on the firecracker serial console output.
- Test that requires the rootfs and is gated on the existing real-KVM flag.
- m80-guestd README documents the contract for both init modes.

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: capture firecracker console output to <run_dir>/console.log
description:
Persist the guest console stream. Firecracker writes serial console to a file we provide via PUT /boot-source or PUT /machine-config (logger). Today we don't consume that output; it goes nowhere.

## Scope

- m80-firecracker configures the firecracker logger to a file at <run_dir>/console.log.
- Permissions match the rest of run_dir (jailer-owned, host-readable).
- Append mode; rotate / cap size out of scope (small VMs, short lifetimes).
- File survives VM stop; cleaned on Sandbox::delete().

## Coordinates with

- m80-1f8.5.2 (systemd/PID-1 console wiring) — guest emits to console; this captures it.
- m80-1f8.5.1 (structured stderr format) — defines what the captured lines look like.
- m80-cffo (m80 logs <vm>) — consumer.

## Acceptance

- After a successful launch, <run_dir>/console.log has at least one line matching the .5.1 format.
- After a guest panic, the panic message is in console.log.
- Test pins file existence and basic format.

title: INVESTIGATE: stress-ng loaded ready/exec failure with guest-visible logs
description:
Diagnose the loaded-host failure shape only after guest stderr and console capture are visible. The current data shows storage and stripped-kernel work do not fix the stress-ng saturation failure; this bead turns that into a bounded evidence-gathering/debugging task instead of another hypothesis loop.

## Current evidence

- Post-storage-pivot loaded cell still mostly fails under stress-ng --cpu $(nproc).
- Stripped-kernel loaded cell has the same failure shape.
- The failure is likely orthogonal to storage prep and kernel size, but that remains a hypothesis until host and guest logs are aligned.

## Scope

- Re-run the loaded cold-launch and snapshot-restore cells after guest stderr reaches <run_dir>/console.log.
- Capture host diagnostics, Firecracker API/log output, guest console, and vsock connection errors for each failed launch.
- Classify the first failing phase precisely: Firecracker boot, guest PID-1, overlay pivot, guestd readiness, vsock accept/connect, exec request, or host timeout scheduling.
- Add the smallest regression/integration test that reproduces the classified failure mode, gated behind the existing real-KVM/ignored pattern if needed.
- If the fix is trivial and semantics-safe, implement it in this bead; otherwise file a narrow follow-up bead with the captured evidence and leave this bead closed as investigation.

## Non-goals

- Guessing at scheduler/vsock fixes before guest logs are present.
- Changing pool sizing or warm-pool allocator semantics.
- Adapter-level retry policy.

## Acceptance

- docs/perf/cold-launch.md records a new loaded run with host+guest evidence paths and a phase classification.
- Each failure sample has a request/run id that links host diagnostics and guest console output.
- A regression test or explicit follow-up bead captures the concrete failure.
- The final notes say whether the loaded failure is a vsock timing issue, guest scheduling/startup issue, host timeout budget issue, or something else observed in logs.

title: INSTRUMENT: guestd PID-1 boot milestone timings for cold-ready path
description:
Add guest-visible timing milestones for the cold-ready path so m80 can split the current ~866 ms `phase_12b_ready_accept` chunk into concrete substeps before choosing an optimization.

Scope:
- Record structured elapsed timing from guest PID-1 entry through readiness: guestd start, stderr/log setup, pseudo-fs mounts, namespace/private mount setup, root device mount, overlay directory checks, overlay mount, pseudo-fs bind, pivot_root, workspace skip/mount, vsock listener bind, and ready connect.
- Preserve guest stderr visibility; this extends the existing guest-log surface rather than replacing it.
- Keep the signal m80-generic: VM lifecycle and guest boot diagnostics only, no adapter or agent semantic events.
- Feed a real-KVM cold-launch bench summary that identifies which guest-visible substep consumes the residual ready phase.

Acceptance:
- Minimal stock and minimal stripped idle runs with N>=30 report guest boot milestone P50/P95/max alongside `phase_12b_ready_accept`.
- Loaded evidence is either N>=5 with the existing stress-ng shape or an explicit note explaining why the loaded cell is not meaningful for this diagnostic.
- A doc artifact records the source snapshot, milestone table, and whether any substep can plausibly save >=100 ms P50 or materially improve loaded-tail failures.
- No readiness semantic is weakened: ready still means the exec listener can accept and run the documented command shape.

title: Defaults audit: every configurable knob (defaults, overrides, deadness)
description:
**Status:** planned, not yet executed.

**Angle:** For every configurable knob in m80 (Default impls, env vars, CLI flags, config-file fields, feature flags): is the default right for the v0.1 driving consumer (torpor2)? Is the override documented? Is the knob actually used anywhere?

**Why this angle:** dead config rots — it documents intent that no longer matches behavior. Wrong defaults bias consumer behavior in ways that compound. The perf epic surfaced one example (mem_size_mib default 1024 is 4× oversized for typical agent workloads — bead .29).

**Expected lens shapes (~6-8 agents), each takes one config surface:**
- `SandboxConfig` (m80-firecracker) — every field, every default, every override path
- `WarmPoolConfig` — pool sizing, target_ready, settle delays
- `JailerConfig` — UID/GID, capability defaults
- CLI flag surface (m80-cli) — every clap arg + its default
- Environment variables (`M80_*` namespace + others read at runtime)
- `[profile.release]` and friends in Cargo.toml (bead .31 partially covers)
- Per-crate constants (`FIRST_LINE_*`, timeouts, retry counts, polling intervals)
- Manifest schema defaults

**Per-knob audit produces:** what is it; what's the default; who reads it; who overrides it (actual call sites, not theoretical); is the default justified for the v0.1 profile; is it documented in the relevant README; does anything depend on a non-default value.

**Findings format:** three categories — (a) wrong default, propose new value; (b) right default, but documentation missing; (c) dead config, propose removal. Each becomes a child bead.

**Cross-link:** several perf beads already touch this (.27 CPU template default, .29 mem_size, .12 deferred env vars). This audit catches the rest.
close_reason: pure planning stub; 10 children fully decompose it

title: MEDIUM: memory_max hardcoded at 1.5GiB doesn't track SandboxConfig.mem_size_mib + Limits not exposed
description:
W6L10. crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:919 calls Limits::preset() unconditionally — DEFAULT_MEMORY_MAX_BYTES = 1.5 GiB regardless of mem_size_mib. Caller raising mem_size_mib to 2048 → cgroup-killed VM with no clean exit code (per OOM observability doc; surfaces as protocol loss).

Fix: (a) Limits::preset(mem_size_mib) accepts the guest mem and computes memory_max = mem_size_mib + FC_OVERHEAD_MB (overlap with m80-243wj.6). (b) Add SandboxConfig::limits: Option<Limits> for per-VM override; default to preset(). Per-VM override is a structural gap — currently the only way to customize is to fork launch path.

Effort: ~4h.

title: LOW: ip_forward sysctl not restored on teardown + JoinNetns DNS unfiltered
description:
W6L9. (a) ensure_ipv4_forwarding (iptables.rs:171-176) sets net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 unconditionally; never restored on teardown. Intentional (other software may depend) — but document explicitly.

(b) NetnsSpec.dns_resolvers: Vec<Ipv4Addr> is caller-supplied with no admission filter (overlap with m80-ag33f.10). m80 writes whatever the caller provides; loopback/link-local won't be caught.

(c) conntrack table size not touched — kernel default (~65536). Under high-concurrency VM load, silent packet drops. Already covered by m80-8emae.10.

Fix: doc the ip_forward non-restore as intentional; apply is_admitted_dns_resolver to JoinNetns dns_resolvers at NetworkPolicy construction.

Effort: ~1h.
notes:
Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-73qb3.13: both describe ensure_ipv4_forwarding non-restore; 73qb3.13 has fuller acceptance criteria. Keep m80-1vna7.10 as target (alphabetically earli

title: MEDIUM: --egress=outbound default is least-privilege inversion
description:
W6L4. crates/m80-cli/src/args.rs:66 (Run) and :211 (WarmEnableArgs) set default_value="outbound". The m80 value proposition is sandboxing. Every CLI invocation grants NAT egress unless caller explicitly opts out. Help text doesn't explain the default.

Worse: struct-level NetworkPolicy default IS NoEgress (correct fail-safe), but CLI flips it. Programmatic and CLI defaults are opposites — confusing and undocumented.

Fix: flip CLI default to 'none'; document in help text that 'outbound' enables NAT-backed egress; document the struct-vs-CLI default asymmetry (or remove it).

Effort: ~30min.

title: MEDIUM: M80_TEST_FAIL_* env hooks live in src/ without cfg(test) guard — accidental fault injection
description:
W6L5. Two env vars cause INTENTIONAL FAILURE INJECTION but live in production-shipping code:

- M80_TEST_FAIL_CGROUP_CREATE_FOR_VM (crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:71)
- M80_TEST_FORCE_KILL_EPERM_FOR_PID (crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:37)

No cfg(test) guard. No allow-list in production. An operator accidentally setting one in their service-unit env (or LD_PRELOAD attack scenario) gets failure-injection. Reproducibility nightmare.

Fix: gate behind cfg(test) OR check a build-time feature flag (#[cfg(feature = "test-injection")]) so prod binaries can never read them. Tests opt in via feature flag.

Effort: ~1h.

title: MEDIUM: idle_timeout Default(300s) vs CLI-always-None — documented default is dead
description:
W6L1. SandboxConfig Default impl sets idle_timeout: Some(Duration::from_secs(300)) (types.rs:266). README documents 300s default. But BOTH CLI construction sites (sandbox_config_for_run in cmds.rs + warm_sandbox_config in owner.rs) explicitly set idle_timeout: None — overriding the documented default.

Two-faced default: programmatic Default = 300s; CLI = None. README documents 300s. No --idle-timeout CLI flag exists.

Fix: pick one path: (a) align Default to None and update README; OR (b) add --idle-timeout CLI flag that respects the 300s default. Recommend (a) — short-lived agent execs shouldn't auto-timeout.

Effort: ~1h.

title: LOW: WarmPoolConfig tunables (RESTORED_SLOT_SETTLE, MAX_FILL_THREADS) not exposed
description:
W6L2. Several warm-pool defaults hardcoded as private consts with no override path:
- RESTORED_SLOT_SETTLE = 1s (warm_pool.rs:18) — fixed sleep after probe; unexplained vs RESTORE_PROBE_TIMEOUT
- MAX_FILL_THREADS = 4 (warm_pool.rs:25) — concurrency cap
- PROBE_RETRIES = 5 + PROBE_RETRY_DELAY = 50ms (warm_pool.rs:433,448) — magic numbers
- owner.rs:152,168 — hardcoded 30s drain timeout

Fix: expose as WarmPoolConfig fields with documented defaults. Pairs with m80-ag33f.7 (WarmPool ergonomics).

Effort: ~2h.
notes: 2026-05-16: q420k.4.15 work removed `RESTORED_SLOT_SETTLE` from warm-pool code and docs after real-KVM timing showed it added ~1s of dead handback latency after a successful ready probe. This bead still tracks the remaining tunables: MAX_FILL_THREADS, probe retry constants, and owner drain timeout constants.

title: LOW: new_cgroup_ns: false in JailerConfig — defense-in-depth gap untracked
description:
W6L3. launch.rs:864 hard-codes new_cgroup_ns: false. The official jailer supports --new-cgroup-ns; m80-jailer-harden exec path exists for it. A private cgroup namespace hides host cgroup hierarchy from FC. Companion to m80-8emae.34 (new_pid_ns: false).

Fix: flip to true. Or expose as SandboxConfig field. Tested alongside m80-8emae.34 since both share the same one-liner shape.

Effort: ~1h.

title: LOW: M80_JAIL_UID + M80_JAIL_GID undocumented in user-facing READMEs
description:
W6L5. Two production-tunable env vars (M80_JAIL_UID and M80_JAIL_GID, both default 3000) are read by crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs:157-163. Not documented in m80-cli README or m80-firecracker README. Only appear in config-loading tests + benches.

Fix: document in m80-cli README §config layers + m80-firecracker README. Cross-link with security bead m80-8emae.20 (jail_uid existence preflight).

Effort: ~30min.

title: LOW: Unexplained sleeps + duplicated EXEC_BUFFER_LIMIT/CAPTURE_LIMIT constants
description:
W6L7. Three small constant-hygiene gaps:

(a) RESTORED_SLOT_SETTLE = 1s (warm_pool.rs:18) — fixed post-probe sleep, no comment explaining what it covers that RESTORE_PROBE_TIMEOUT doesn't. If probe subsumes it: dead latency. If different race: needs comment.

(b) HOTPLUG_WAIT = 250ms (connection/hotplug.rs:20) — fixed sleep for uevent arrival, no comment on worst-case uevent latency.

(c) EXEC_BUFFER_LIMIT (host) and CAPTURE_LIMIT (guest) both = 1 MiB but independent constants. Future drift risk. Should share a constant in m80-proto.

Fix: add comments to (a) and (b) justifying the magic numbers (or remove if probe subsumes). Promote (c) to m80-proto::EXEC_STREAM_BUFFER_LIMIT.

Effort: ~1h.

title: LOW: Cargo workspace cleanups — result_large_err scope + toml bump
description:
W6L6. (a) workspace.lints.clippy::result_large_err = "allow" applied WORKSPACE-WIDE. If the intent is 'we have one known large variant', should be a per-site #[allow] so future regressions elsewhere are caught.

(b) toml = "0.5" — current stable is 0.8. The 0.5 API is pre-toml_edit era. Upgrade path is mechanical (toml::from_str / to_string unchanged). Missing bug fixes.

(c) Track edition 2024 when rust-version advances past 1.85.

Effort: ~30min total.

title: Reliability audit: partial-failure leak modes
description:
**Status:** planned, not yet executed.

**Angle:** Partial-failure leak audit — when something fails midway through a launch, lease, exec, snapshot, or teardown, what state remains on the host, who's responsible for cleanup, and is there a test pinning it?

**Why this angle:** the m80-ekbk postmortem (m80-lovpn) named stale mounts + dangling TAPs + EBUSY recovery as a real, recurring class of bug. Bead .16 (auto-recover stale run_root) is one slice; this audit goes broad.

**Expected lens shapes (~10-12 agents), each takes one failure point and asks "what survives, what cleans up, is there a test":**
- Drop_caches mid-launch (cold-cache fault during phase_3)
- OOM during phase_3 (storage prep) / phase_5b (cgroup create) / phase_12b (guest boot)
- SIGKILL on jailer/firecracker during each phase
- Disk-full on snapshot capture
- Disk-full on overlay write
- Sudo denied / permission boundary failures
- Jailer exec fails (binary missing, kernel mismatch)
- Guestd hangs before ready signal (timeout, deadlock)
- Vsock disconnect mid-exec (guest panic, FC crash)
- Cgroup limit hit during boot (memory.max exceeded)
- Host reboot with in-flight VMs (recovery on next start)
- Network setup partial failure (iptables ok, TAP fails / vice versa)

**Findings format:** for each failure point: what does m80 leave behind (mount, TAP, cgroup, FD, snapshot file, lock); who's supposed to clean it (Drop impl, recovery code, manual operator); does a test exist; is the failure recoverable on next launch or does it need manual intervention.

**Each finding becomes a child bead.** Expected: 20-40 findings ranging from XS (add a Drop impl) to M (build a recovery-on-startup path for class X).

**Cross-link:** m80-lovpn.2 (smoke evidence rule) — fixes touching kernel-facing primitives need real-KVM smoke.

title: CRITICAL: recover_stale_run_root deletes network-state.json before cleanup_vm — TAP+iptables permanent leak
description:
**Severity: CRITICAL** — confirmed by lens 2 + lens 7 of W1 independently

## Finding

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:252-272` (`remove_run_dir`) calls `unmount_under`, `cleanup_orphan_subtree`, then `remove_dir_all`. **It does NOT call `m80_net_outbound::cleanup_vm(vm_id, run_root)` before the dir removal.**

The `network-state.json` file (which `cleanup_vm` needs to identify the TAP name + iptables chain comment) lives INSIDE the run_dir. `remove_dir_all` deletes it. Result: TAP device + per-VM iptables chain + FORWARD + MASQUERADE rules **leak permanently until manual `iptables -F` + `ip link del`**. At density this accumulates unboundedly.

Bead m80-jp6ik.15 ("auto-recover stale run_root + clean TAP/iptables") was scoped to do this fix but it appears the cleanup_vm wiring was missed when integrating.

## Fix

In `remove_run_dir`, BEFORE `remove_dir_all(&subdir)`:
```rust
if subdir.join("network-state.json").exists() {
    let _ = m80_net_outbound::cleanup_vm(vm_id, &run_root);
}
```
Requires threading `run_root` through (currently only `subdir` is passed). Best-effort: log on failure but don't abort recovery.

## Tests

`crates/m80-firecracker/tests/recovery_cleans_network.rs` — simulate SIGKILL mid-launch (after phase_7 completes), restart Backend, assert TAP device gone, assert iptables chain gone.

## Smoke evidence: required.

## Effort: ~3h.
close_reason: W30 wave (m80-34n42) confirmed backend.rs:263-294 already calls

title: LOW-MEDIUM: StoppedSandbox lacks Drop impl — caller error paths leak TAP/iptables/run_dir
description:
**Severity: LOW-MEDIUM** (cleanup correctness gap on caller error path)

## Finding (W1L5 secondary)

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/stopped.rs:72` — `StoppedSandbox` has NO `Drop` impl. If a caller calls `force_kill()` and then drops the returned `StoppedSandbox` on an error path (without calling `delete()`), the cleanup path NEVER runs:
- TAP / iptables rules (outbound mode) survive
- Run dir survives

`StoppedSandbox::delete()` is the canonical cleanup path. If the caller takes the error-path early-return on a `?`, the destructor sequence is `Drop` only — and there's no Drop.

## Fix

Add `Drop` impl to `StoppedSandbox` that calls a `best_effort_cleanup()` method (idempotent — if `delete()` was already called, no-op via an internal `cleaned: bool` flag). Log warnings on cleanup failures but don't panic.

Or: rename `delete()` to require it to be called (make `StoppedSandbox` carry a `#[must_use]` attribute pointing at delete, and lint via clippy).

## Tests

`tests/stopped_sandbox_drop.rs` — `force_kill()` then drop without `delete()`; assert TAP / run_dir cleaned up via Drop path.

## Effort: ~2h.
close_reason: Merged into m80-xeaey.5: `StoppedSandbox` lacks `Drop` impl; caller error paths

title: LOW: Misc reliability — xtables -W timeout + non-pool dead-sandbox short-circuit + boot_identity error variant + recover docs
description:
**Severity: LOW** (operational concerns + minor reliability)

## Findings (W1 misc)

A. **xtables.lock no timeout** (W1L7) — `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs:455`. `iptables_args` passes `-w` (wait for lock) but no `-W <timeout>`. A hung iptables-using process elsewhere on the host blocks m80 launch indefinitely. Add `-W 5000` (5s timeout).

For non-pool path: add `is_dead` flag updated on first connection failure; subsequent exec calls short-circuit with `SandboxDead`.

C. **Boot-identity ENOSPC after FC running** (W1L3) — `crates/m80-firecracker/src/boot_identity.rs:40` writes after phase 9. Cleanup guards fire correctly (verified) but error type is `FcError::PathIo` — non-informative. Make it `FcError::BootIdentityWriteFailed { path, source }`.

D. **`recover_stale_run_root` concurrent-call constraint undocumented** (W1L10) — currently called once at `Backend::new`. Document explicitly that concurrent invocation with `admit` is unsafe.

notes:
Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-243wj.8: EPERM mid-launch lacks capability hints (network/jailer/

title: LOW: tmpfs-vs-persistent run_root operator docs + advisory preflight
description:
**Severity: LOW** (documentation gap with operational consequences)

## Finding (W1L8 + W1L1)

m80's default `run_root = /var/run/m80` resolves to tmpfs on systemd hosts (it's a symlink to `/run`). This means:
- Run dir state wipes on reboot (self-consistent — no recovery needed)
- Snapshot files in `<run_root>/warm/snapshot/` are pure RAM (capped by host RAM)
- Lost cleanup state on crash means kernel state (TAPs, iptables) is ALSO gone (kernel reboot wipes both)

An operator configuring persistent storage (`/var/lib/m80-run`) inherits all the reboot-recovery gaps that the tmpfs default doesn't have.

## Fix

NEW `docs/ops/run_root-storage.md`:
- Table: tmpfs default vs persistent — what survives, what doesn't
- Choose tmpfs when: short-lived host, ephemeral workloads, single-operator
- Choose persistent when: warm-pool with re-bootable host, snapshot persistence required
- Preflight check (advisory): detect tmpfs-vs-persistent of resolved run_root; warn on persistent without explicit operator opt-in.

Also add: r4 (template lock) gets worse on persistent storage — lock survives reboot but the PID encoded in it (per r4 fix) is now from a dead boot. Sweep at startup needs to handle "PID predates current boot's `boot_id`".

## Effort: ~2h docs.

title: MEDIUM: WarmLease + WarmPool Drop silently swallow discard_sandbox errors — VM process leak invisible

W8L1. crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool/lease.rs:193 and warm_pool.rs:282 both call `let _ = discard_sandbox(sandbox)` in Drop. discard_sandbox = force_kill()?.delete() — if force_kill fails (ambiguous kill), the VM process leak goes unlogged. The run_dir cleanup is also skipped. Compare to ForceKillGuard which explicitly logs kill failures.

Fix: tracing::error!(error = %e, vm_id = %vm_id, 'WarmLease drop: discard_sandbox failed') before discarding the Result. ~30min.

title: LOW: TemplateLock + LeaseGuard Drop silently discard remove_file errors
description:
W8L1. (a) crates/m80-storage/src/rootfs.rs:319 — TemplateLock Drop uses let _ = std::fs::remove_file. If removal fails (perms bug, fs error), the lock file persists; future bake attempts spin for 10s on the stale .lock. (b) crates/m80-firecracker/src/runroot.rs:104 — LeaseGuard Drop same pattern. Stale ownership.lock + PID reuse triggers RunDirOwnershipAmbiguous path on next launch.

Fix: tracing::warn!(error = %e, path = %lock_path, 'failed to remove lock') in both Drop impls. ~15min.

title: LOW: m80-storage scratch loop mounts lack CLONE_NEWNS — orphan loop mount on SIGKILL
description:
W8L3. crates/m80-storage/src/scratch.rs:86-105 (extract) and 177-187 (hydrate) use 'mount' / 'umount' binaries in the host namespace with no CLONE_NEWNS guard. If process SIGKILLed between mount and umount, loop device + tmpdir mount persist in host namespace. Mount dir is under /tmp (TempDir) not run_root, so recover_stale_run_root + unmount_under don't help.

Compare: m80-image-build pipeline.rs uses enter_private_mount_namespace() before loop_mount — orphan contained to dying namespace.

Fix: add unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) before run_mount in both Scratch::extract and hydrate paths. ~1h.

title: LOW: stdio_log + write_file_no_follow narrow CLOEXEC window in concurrent warm-pool fills
description:
W8L4. (a) crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs:153 — stdio_log File opened without O_CLOEXEC. Briefly open between OpenOptions and Stdio::from. Concurrent thread doing fork+exec in that microsecond window inherits the FD. (b) crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:299 — write_file_no_follow has O_NOFOLLOW but not O_CLOEXEC; same brief window.

In sequential launch: zero risk. In concurrent warm-pool fills (multiple threads spawning FCs simultaneously): theoretical race.

Fix: add custom_flags(libc::O_CLOEXEC) to both OpenOptions sites. ~15min.

title: MEDIUM: WarmPool::Drop hangs if fill worker panics after FillGuard disarm
description:
W8L6. crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:340 — FillGuard decrements 'filling' if thread::spawn panics. Thread body disarms guard at entry (line 341) before calling launch_slot. If launch_slot or anything after disarm panics, 'filling' never decrements. WarmPool::Drop waits on Condvar for filling==0 — hangs indefinitely.

Fix: wrap thread body in catch_unwind; on panic, decrement filling explicitly + log + re-arm-style cleanup. OR: use scope guard around the full thread body (not just thread::spawn boundary). ~2h.

title: LOW: guestd netlink listener handle silently discarded; no shutdown path
description:
W8L6. crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/hotplug.rs:288 — spawn_netlink_listener returns Ok(handle), call site discards via map_err(...) chain. Thread loops on netlink recv forever. No shutdown path, no observability.

In-guest context: bounded to VM lifetime; OS reaps on guestd exit. But: no way to gracefully shut down or observe thread exit during testing.

Fix: store handle in a struct field with explicit shutdown via channel signal. Lower priority since guestd is single-shot. ~1h.

title: MEDIUM: TemplateLock should use flock instead of create_new spin — eliminates SIGKILL stale lock
description:
W8L10 (complements m80-243wj.4). Current implementation (rootfs.rs:285-314) is create_new + 25ms spin + 10s timeout. If holder SIGKILLed during mkfs.ext4 or dig_template_holes (both subprocess calls held inside lock), .lock file persists permanently. Every subsequent launch spins 10s then errors.

Fix: replace create_new spin with fcntl::Flock on the same file. Kernel auto-releases flock on process death — no stale-lock scenario. Existing pattern in m80-net-outbound NETWORK_ALLOCATION_MUTEX. ~2h.

title: HIGH: Console log not surfaced on GuestdReadyTimeout — every guestd failure is opaque
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (every guestd startup failure shows as opaque 60s timeout)

## Finding (W1L4)

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs:83-111` — `emit_guest_boot_phase_events` reads `console.log` and emits guest phase events to host stderr. Called ONLY on the success path (after `accept_ready_signal` returns Ok).

When `phase_12b_ready_accept` times out (60s), the error is `FcError::GuestdReadyTimeout { path, timeout }` — but the guest console log is never read. Operator sees a 60-second wall-clock wait followed by an opaque error. All these failure modes produce identical output:
- guestd missing from rootfs (kernel: "No init found")
- guestd wrong arch (kernel: "Exec format error")
- guestd missing libc/loader
- guestd panics before vsock connect
- `/proc/cmdline` parse hits unhandled case → `anyhow::bail!`

For each, the actual error is in `console.log` but not surfaced.

## Fix

In `phase_12b_ready_accept`'s error path: read the last ~50 lines of `console.log` and either attach to `FcError::GuestdReadyTimeout` as a `console_tail: String` field OR emit via `tracing::error!`. Minimum: log the console.log path in the error message so operators know where to look.

```rust
// pseudocode
Err(e @ FcError::GuestdReadyTimeout { .. }) => {
    let tail = read_console_log_tail(&console_log_path, 50);
    tracing::error!(console_tail = %tail, "guestd never sent ready signal");
    Err(e)
}
```

## Effort: ~2h.

title: LOW: CLI InputThread detach on Drop + warm owner.sock CLOEXEC missing
description:
W8L6 + W8L4 misc. (a) crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/pty.rs:134 — InputThread stores JoinHandle but doesn't join in Drop. Thread blocks on stdin.read — if parent struct drops mid-session, thread leaks to process exit (bounded but un-graceful).

(b) crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/owner.rs:74 — UnixListener doesn't have a Drop guard for unlinking the socket file on abnormal exit (related to m80-8emae.24 but file-mode angle).

title: HIGH: Warm-pool slot health check + structured DisconnectBeforeTerminal cause
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (warm-pool callers absorb 2.5s retry against known-dead VM)

## Findings (W1L5)

A. **Slot with dead VM stays in ready queue** — `crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:188-199`. `try_lease` pops from `state.ready` with no liveness check. A slot whose FC died after its ready-probe (OOM, kernel panic) is handed to the caller. First `exec` fails after 25 retries × 100ms = 2.5s burn.

B. **All crash causes collapse to `DisconnectBeforeTerminal`** — `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/protocol.rs:8`. No structured cause field. Operator can't distinguish FC crash vs guest panic vs guestd OOM vs vsock muxer failure. The `context` field only encodes which m80 call site noticed, not what happened.

C. **Non-one-shot sandbox: 2.5s retry on dead VM with no is_dead guard** — `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs:848-876`. Same retry-burn pattern.

## Fix

A. **Proactive slot health check**: in `WarmPool::try_lease`, before returning the slot, send a minimal vsock ping (or check the FC process's `/proc/<pid>` existence). If dead, discard the slot, decrement `ready`, increment `discarded`, trigger background refill, and either return `PoolEmpty` or retry from the next slot. Bound retries.

B. Add structured cause to `DisconnectBeforeTerminal`:
```rust
pub enum DisconnectCause {
    FcProcessDead,    // /proc/<pid> gone
    UdsConnectFailed, // ConnectionRefused on socket connect
    MidStreamEof,     // EOF after some bytes received
    CleanRequestedClose,
}
```
Populated by examining FC pid state when the disconnect is observed.

C. In `RunningSandbox::exec` (non-one-shot), check FC liveness at entry; return `FcError::SandboxDead` immediately rather than spending 2.5s retrying.

## Tests

`tests/warm_pool_dead_slot.rs` — kill a slot's FC mid-queue, lease, assert immediate failure (not 2.5s wait).

## Effort: ~6h.

title: MEDIUM: Stale TemplateLock + orphan .tmp blocks next launches; recover doesn't scan template locks
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (next-launch blocking + permanent disk residue)

## Finding (W1L1)

`crates/m80-storage/src/rootfs.rs:106,317` — `TemplateLock` is RAII; Drop removes the `.lock` file. OOM-kill during `ensure_template` skips Drop. Stale lock at `<run_root>/.rootfs-overlay-template-v1-*.ext4.lock` persists indefinitely.

Next launch enters `TemplateLock::acquire`, hits `AlreadyExists`, spins 10s, returns `StorageError::OverlayTemplateCreateFailed { err: TimedOut }`. EVERY subsequent launch fails for 10s + errors. Manual `rm` required.

`recover_stale_run_root` does not scan the run_root ROOT level for orphan template locks — only vm_id subdirs.

Also: `crates/m80-storage/src/rootfs.rs:157-160` — on ENOSPC during `std::fs::rename(.tmp → final)`, the `.tmp` file is NOT removed. Different leak path, same outcome (orphan template fragments).

## Fix

1. Encode writer PID in lock filename: `.rootfs-overlay-template-v1-<size>.ext4.lock.<pid>`. `TemplateLock::acquire` reads the PID; if `/proc/<pid>` is dead, steal the lock.
2. `recover_stale_run_root` — sweep run_root for `*.lock.*` files with dead PIDs and clean them.
3. `create_template` rename error path: unlink `.tmp` before returning Err.

## Effort: ~3h.

title: MEDIUM: inspect_run_dir misclassifies as OrphanJail when SIGKILL hits before state-file write
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (SIGKILL window mid-spawn → live FC unkilled by recover)

## Finding (W1L2)

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:153-159` — `OrphanJail` branch of `inspect_run_dir` calls `remove_run_dir` directly WITHOUT calling `kill_orphan_pids`. Only `LiveJail` branch triggers SIGKILL.

`inspect_run_dir` (`recover.rs:67`) decides between LiveJail/OrphanJail based on `jailer-state.json` (which is written at the END of `MaterializedJail::launch`). If SIGKILL hits between FC spawn and state-file-write, FC is live but state-file is absent → classified as OrphanJail → recover unmounts under a still-running FC's chroot.

`unmount_under` will likely fail with EBUSY because FC has the chroot's mounts open. Partial cleanup, FC stays alive as a zombie until manually reaped.

## Fix

`inspect_run_dir` — when `jailer-state.json` is absent, ALSO check `firecracker.pid`. If pid file exists and `/proc/<pid>` is live, return `LiveJail` instead of `OrphanJail`. Forces the kill-orphan-pids path.

Or: always SIGKILL anything listed in `firecracker.pid` before `unmount_under`, regardless of classification.

## Tests

`tests/recover_partial_spawn.rs` — start jailer, kill m80 before state-file written, restart, assert FC was SIGKILLed during recovery.

## Smoke evidence: required.

## Effort: ~3h.

title: MEDIUM: No preflight check that memory.max >= mem_size_mib + FC_OVERHEAD
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (silent OOM → opaque timeout)

## Finding (W1L6)

`crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:27` — `DEFAULT_MEMORY_MAX_BYTES = 1536 MiB`. Default `FIRST_LINE_MEM_SIZE_MIB = 1024`. Safe shape: 512 MiB FC overhead.

But `SandboxConfig::mem_size_mib` is caller-configurable. A caller setting `mem_size_mib = 1500` (or higher) + FC's ~200 MiB process footprint = OOM-kill of FC mid-boot. `oom_score_adj = 500` biases FC as target.

Failure surface: kernel OOM-kills FC. Phase 10 times out as `ApiSocketTimeout` (if before API socket up) or phase 12b times out as `GuestdReadyTimeout`. Neither error indicates OOM. Operator sees opaque timeout, must inspect `dmesg` separately.

## Fix

Preflight or `Backend::admit` check: if cgroup v2 active, assert `limits.memory_max >= (mem_size_mib * MiB) + FC_OVERHEAD_BYTES` where `FC_OVERHEAD_BYTES = 256 MiB` (named constant). Fail closed at config time with `FcError::Config(InsufficientMemoryHeadroom { mem_size_mib, memory_max, required })`.

Also: in the timeout error path, scrape `dmesg` for `Killed process <fc_pid> .*firecracker` and include as `oom_killed: bool` in the timeout error.

## Effort: ~3h.

title: MEDIUM: Persistent run_root reboot survival — bridge state, teardown_tap ENODEV, iptables-persistent, docs
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (operator-deployment first-admit failure after reboot on persistent run_root)

## Findings (W1L8)

For operators choosing persistent run_root (`/var/lib/m80-run` or similar) instead of the tmpfs default:

A. **Bridge state=Ready but bridge interface gone after reboot** — `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/lib.rs:355-370`. On reboot the bridge interface is wiped (kernel state) but `outbound-bridge-state.json` survives with `SetupPhase::Ready`. Next `ensure_bridge_ready_with_ops` reads Ready state, calls `link_has_ipv4_address` (false), hits `InvalidNetworkState` rather than the `recover_planned_bridge` path. **Hard error on first new-VM admission.**

B. **`teardown_tap` ENODEV idempotency** — `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/link_ops.rs` (the `teardown_tap` function). After reboot the TAP device is gone but `network-state.json` exists. `recover_stale_run_root` → `cleanup_vm` → `teardown_tap` — if this errors on ENODEV instead of treating it as no-op success, recovery aborts for every VM dir that had networking.

C. **Iptables chains orphaned with iptables-persistent** — `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/teardown.rs:29-31`. When `network-state.json` is missing (crash before write), recovery only tears down TAP, NOT iptables. On distros with `iptables-persistent`, the per-VM chain survives reboot but cleanup is skipped.

D. **tmpfs-vs-persistent operator story undocumented** — `crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs:35` (`DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT = /var/run/m80`). On systemd this is tmpfs (everything wiped on reboot, self-consistent). Persistent storage = exposure to A/B/C. No doc or preflight surface.

## Fix

A. Treat "state=Ready but bridge missing" as a soft state (re-enter `recover_planned_bridge` or rebuild from scratch). Modify the `Ready` arm of `ensure_bridge_ready_with_ops` to fall through to re-creation on link-not-found.

B. Verify `teardown_tap` returns Ok on ENODEV. If it errors, fix it.

C. When `network-state.json` is missing, attempt iptables cleanup by reconstructing the comment tag from `(run_root, vm_id)` and `derive_tap_name`.

D. NEW `docs/ops/run_root-storage.md` — when to choose tmpfs vs persistent, what each survives across reboot.

## Effort: ~6h.

title: MEDIUM: Mid-launch EPERM errors lack capability hints (network/jailer/cgroup)
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (debug-unfriendly EPERM mid-launch)

## Findings (W1L9)

When CAP_NET_ADMIN / CAP_SYS_ADMIN / CAP_CHOWN is dropped mid-process (systemd reload with reduced AmbientCapabilities, or any other dynamic-cap-drop scenario), mid-launch errors surface as:

A. **iptables/sysctl EPERM** → `FcError::Network(NetError::NetworkCommandFailed { program, stderr })` — stderr has the raw subprocess message but no cap hint. CLI renders generic `EXIT_GENERIC` with no `hint()`.

B. **Jailer bind/chown EPERM** → `FcError::Jailer(JailerError::BindFailed { src, dest, source: nix::Error })` — display says "bind-mount failed: EPERM", no cap hint.

C. **Cgroup file write EPERM** → `FcError::Cgroup(CgroupError::Io { path, source })` — path preserved, no cap hint.

In all cases, partial state cleanup is correct (RAII guards work) — the gap is operator visibility.

Currently only `PreflightError::hint()` is rendered. Mid-launch errors don't get the same hint treatment.

## Fix

Extend `render_error` in `crates/m80-cli/src/errors.rs` to render `hint()` for `FcError::Network(_)`, `FcError::Jailer(_)`, `FcError::Cgroup(_)` too. Add `hint()` impls to each typed error variant suggesting which capability + which install procedure (e.g., "ensure `CAP_NET_ADMIN` in systemd unit's `AmbientCapabilities=`").

Or: add a `pre_op_capability_check` helper that re-reads caps at the start of phase_6 (network) and phase_4 (jailer) and short-circuits with a clean `PreflightError::PrivilegeUnavailable` before the syscall fails opaquely.

## Effort: ~3h.

title: MEDIUM: NETWORK_ALLOCATION_MUTEX scope — teardown + TAP creation outside lock
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (reliability flake under concurrent launch+teardown)

## Findings (W1L10)

A. **state.json removal races collision-check** — `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/teardown.rs:43` removes `network-state.json` OUTSIDE the allocation lock. Concurrent VM B launch's `reject_guest_ipv4_collision` (`lib.rs:279-298`) iterates `read_dir(run_root)`, sees the file, attempts to read, gets ENOENT or partial bytes mid-delete. VM B's launch aborts spuriously.

B. **TAP creation after lock release** — `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/lib.rs:147,155`. Lock released at line 147; `create_tap_on_bridge` at line 155 runs OUTSIDE lock. A residual TAP from VM A's crashed run (same `(run_root, vm_id)` hash) causes VM B's `ip link add` to EEXIST.

## Fix

A. Extend `NETWORK_ALLOCATION_MUTEX` + flock scope through the `remove_file_if_present(&state_path)` call in `cleanup_vm_with_ops`. Teardown of state.json must hold the same lock as launch's collision-check.

B. Hold the allocation lock through `create_tap_on_bridge` (move `drop(allocation_lock)` to after line 155 — or wrap the TAP create in a separate lock scope).

## Tests

`crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/concurrent_launch_teardown.rs` — two threads, one tearing down VM A while another launches VM B with adjacent vm_id; assert VM B launches cleanly.

## Effort: ~3h.

title: Cosign/sigstore signature verification on registry pull path (v0.3 differentiator)
description:
When m80 ships a registry / image-distribution path (deferred v0.3 under m80-qokt or successor), require sigstore signature verification on pull. Smolvm verifies sha256 only — no signatures. Shipping signed-pull on day one is a clean trust differentiator.

## Reference

smolvm-exploration/06-registry-and-image-distribution.md (gap analysis) + 00-synthesis.md "Differentiation opportunities".

## Scope

- sigstore-rs as the verification library (mature, Rust-native, no Go dependency).
- Pull path: fetch image → fetch detached signature + Rekor entry → verify against trusted root → verify sha256 → admit.
- Fail-closed by default; an --insecure-skip-signature flag at most for local dev.
- Cover both keyless (Fulcio OIDC) and key-based signing modes; document which we recommend.

## Out of scope

- Image signing tooling (a separate "publish" path, can land later).
- Building a registry server (we use existing OCI registries; this is client-side).
- Defining the trust root's policy (separate decision).

## Acceptance

- Pull from an unsigned image fails by default with a clear error.
- Pull from a sigstore-signed image succeeds without flags.
- README documents the signing requirement and the dev-only escape hatch.
- Decision doc on keyless-vs-key-based signing.

## Why deferred

No m80-registry today; bead is a placeholder + design pin for v0.3. Defer date set to 2026-09-01.

title: run_root migration leaves orphaned TAPs/rules; no recovery path or operator procedure
description:
**Finding:** If an operator changes run_root between m80 invocations (process restart, config change, or quickstart path change), the OLD run_root directory retains leftover network-state.json files. cleanup_orphan_bridge_with_ops only acts on the bridge for the CURRENT run_root; it doesn't scan sibling run-roots. Old TAPs (tfc<hash>) + iptables rules (m80:<comment>) tagged for the OLD run_root are orphaned permanently. No startup-time sweep, no cross-run_root scan, no documentation of the migration operator procedure.

Recovery requires knowing the OLD run_root path, which is not persisted accessibly to a new process.

**File:** crates/m80-net-outbound/src/teardown.rs:58 (cleanup_orphan_bridge — single-run_root scope); README gap.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (silent accumulation; only triggered by operator change, but no path to clean up).

**Acceptance:**
- Document operator procedure: 'before changing run_root, run `m80 net cleanup --all` against the OLD run_root.'
- OR: persist a list of historical run_roots in a host-level registry (e.g., /var/lib/m80/known-run-roots.json) for m80 doctor to enumerate.
- OR: m80 doctor scans by tag — find m80-tagged iptables rules + tfc* TAPs whose corresponding run_root no longer matches the current config; surface as orphans.
- Cross-link m80-wok08.5 (m80 doctor), m80-l3tiq.2 (global iptables scan), m80-243wj.7.

title: ownership.lock started_at field written but never consumed; PID-reuse window unguarded
description:
**Finding:** runroot.rs:59-60 formats started_at (Unix ms) into ownership.lock. runroot.rs:85-87 read_ownership_lock parses ONLY pid; started_at is never read back. pid_is_alive is a bare /proc/<pid> existence check with no /proc/<pid>/comm match and no started_at comparison.

If the original m80 process is SIGKILLed and the OS recycles that PID to an unrelated process before recovery runs, run_dir_liveness returns Live → recover_stale_run_root skips the subdir → stale run-dir accumulates indefinitely.

started_at field is dead weight today but worse: it LOOKS like a PID-reuse guard, so a reader assumes the file is protected when it isn't.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/runroot.rs:59-60 (write), :85-87 (read).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (probabilistic; SIGKILL is the trigger). Adjacent to m80-243wj.5 but a distinct surface (this is runroot.rs ownership.lock; m80-243wj.5 is jailer-state.json).

**Acceptance:**
- Compare started_at against /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 (process start time in clock ticks since boot, converted to ms). If mismatch → classify as Dead (PID reuse detected).
- Optionally: read /proc/<pid>/comm and verify it starts with 'm80'.
- Test pin: write a lock with a synthetic stale (pid, started_at) pair; verify recovery classifies as Dead even if PID happens to be alive.

title: WarmPoolSnapshot.discarded counts only lease returns; fill failures + shutdown discards uncounted
description:
**Finding:** WarmPoolSnapshot.discarded is incremented ONLY in lease_finished (warm_pool.rs:369) — i.e., when a leased slot is returned + discarded by the caller. Slots that fail their probe in launch_slot have filling-- but discarded++ is NOT called (fill_worker.rs:56-65). Shutdown-time discards (Drop on WarmPool) also decrement filling without incrementing discarded.

Field name + doc say 'Slots discarded since pool creation'. Operator watching it to estimate failure rate sees only lease-side returns, not the (often more interesting) fill-side failures.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:369 (lease_finished increment); fill_worker.rs:56-65 (missing increment); warm_pool.rs (snapshot field doc).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (metrics-semantics gap; pairs with m80-r4308.4 which proposes failed_fill_count).

**Acceptance:**
- Either: rename to leases_discarded with updated doc.
- OR: add parallel failed_fills + shutdown_discards counters incremented in their respective sites; expose all three in WarmPoolSnapshot.
- Cross-link m80-r4308.4 (same finding from a different lens — bundle the fix).

title: FC best-practices alignment
description:
Audit FC's documented best practices (docs/jailer.md, prod-host-setup.md, snapshotting/, kernel-policy.md, network-setup.md, network-performance.md, logger.md, metrics.md, seccomp.md, hugepages.md, entropy.md, pvh.md, etc.) plus broader community sources (AWS Lambda, Fly Machines, Marc Brooker's "Seven Years of Firecracker", arXiv "Restoring Uniqueness in MicroVM Snapshots", FC issue tracker) against m80's current implementation. 8 thematic sub-epics cover the gaps:

1. Host preflight enforcement (KSM/SMT/swap/nested-virt/KVM-timer-floor/cgroup-favordynmods)
2. Jailer flag completeness (--cgroup-version, cgroup-deferral docs, jailer-as-root euid guard)
3. FC API surface m80 leaves on the table (PUT /logger, /metrics, /network-interfaces, TAP MTU, sysctl docs, virtio-net queue depth)
4. Snapshot correctness (version validation on restore, track_dirty_pages plumbing, post-restore CSPRNG re-seed)
5. Kernel feature alignment (CONFIG audit, PVH boot, hugepages, virtio-rng, ballooning non-goal, memory-hotplug deferral)
6. IMDS link-local block regression pin (already present; tests + doc to prevent silent removal)
7. Operational design knobs (max_lifetime, prepare/start split, host-vs-VM error class, virtio queue depth)
8. Operator deployment runbook (host-hardware, host-kernel-config, threat-model, MMDS-non-use, preflight-overrides)

Total: 36 open children + 1 pre-closed (8250.nr_uarts already resolved). Audit synthesized from 7 parallel agent reports (FC docs deep-read + web/community search). Source-verified before authoring; CROSS-REFs noted where existing beads (m80-av33 cpu_template, m80-qokt.2.5 idle_timeout) cover related ground.

title: FC prod-host-setup preflight enforcement
description:
FC's prod-host-setup.md documents six host-level conditions that its threat model assumes are enforced before any VM boots. m80-preflight today verifies KVM device access, CPU extensions, kernel module load, and process privilege — but does NOT check the security-posture conditions FC calls out: KSM, SMT, swap, nested virt, KVM timer floor, cgroup-favordynmods. A host passing m80 preflight today can silently violate all six, leaving operators with a false-positive "everything looks good" report.

These six checks form a coherent safety cluster: KSM/SMT guard speculative-execution cross-tenant leakage; swap guards guest-memory data remanence on disk; nested virt guards the assumption that guests cannot escape into a hypervisor role; KVM timer floor and cgroup-favordynmods are performance-correctness hazards FC documents because they cause silent misbehavior at boot.

Several have legitimate operator overrides (single-tenant or trusted-tenant deployments may keep SMT on for throughput; dev boxes may want KSM on). Each check ships with an env-var escape hatch (M80_SKIP_CHECK_<NAME>=1) so operators record an explicit "I know, skip it" decision rather than having the check silently absent. Cross-ref: cluster-8 child 5 documents these vars in the operator runbook.

title: Preflight: KSM disabled check
description:
Read /sys/kernel/mm/ksm/run; fail preflight if not "0". KSM enables page-deduplication side channels leaking memory content across VM boundaries on shared hosts. Hard-fail by default; skippable via M80_SKIP_CHECK_KSM=1. hint() must include `echo 0 | sudo tee /sys/kernel/mm/ksm/run` and note the escape hatch.

Files: crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs, crates/m80-preflight/src/lib.rs (new PreflightError::KsmEnabled).

Acceptance:
- doc at docs/behaviors/preflight/ksm-disabled.md
- test at crates/m80-preflight/tests/ksm_disabled.rs
- preflight returns KsmEnabled with remediation hint when ksm/run != "0"
- skippable via M80_SKIP_CHECK_KSM=1; surfaced as CheckRow{passed:false, detail:"skipped by operator"}
- CHANGELOG entry

title: Preflight: SMT disabled check (warn-or-fail)
description:
Read /sys/devices/system/cpu/smt/control; warn (not hard-fail) when not "off". SMT siblings share microarch buffers; L1TF/MDS attacks exploit this. Warn-not-fail by default because single-tenant operators commonly keep SMT on for throughput. Escalation to hard-fail via M80_SMT_CHECK=fail. Skippable via M80_SKIP_CHECK_SMT=1.

title: Preflight: swap disabled check
description:
Read /proc/swaps; fail preflight if any active swap (more than header line). Guest memory swapped to disk can survive teardown as recoverable data — violates FC's data-remanence assumption. Hard-fail; skippable via M80_SKIP_CHECK_SWAP=1. hint() points at swapoff -a + /etc/fstab.

title: Preflight: KVM PIT timer floor
description:
Read /sys/module/kvm/parameters/min_timer_period_us; warn when "0" (default on most distros). Zero means KVM honors guest-requested timer intervals as low as 1us; a guest with very short PIT/HPET interval floods host with timer interrupts. FC recommends "500". Warn-not-fail (correct value is deployment-dependent). Skippable via M80_SKIP_CHECK_KVM_TIMER=1.

title: FC jailer flag alignment + jailer-harden root guard
description:
Align JailerConfig and MaterializedJail::launch with FC's official jailer flag surface, and add an early geteuid guard to m80-jailer-harden so the process fails loudly if not root before applying one-way hardening.

Audit dropped the original "--node NUMA pinning" finding: FC jailer has no --node flag. NUMA placement is achieved via --cgroup cpuset.mems=0 / cpuset.cpus=<list>, which rolls into the cgroup-deferral discussion (child 2). Three confirmed gaps remain:

1. --cgroup-version never passed; jailer defaults to v1 (modern Linux ships v2-only hierarchy)
2. --cgroup / --parent-cgroup deliberately not forwarded; m80 defers to m80-cgroup post-launch — undocumented, leaves operators without NUMA guidance
3. m80-jailer-harden has no geteuid==0 guard before applying one-way hardening; if not root, jailer silently fails after caps are dropped

title: Jailer: pass --cgroup-version 2 explicitly
description:
FC jailer defaults to cgroup v1 unless --cgroup-version 2 is supplied. Modern Linux (kernel 5.14+, systemd >=247) mounts only v2 hierarchy. Without the flag jailer silently falls back to v1 or fails to locate the controller mount; m80 has no way to communicate v2 is required.

Add CgroupVersion enum {V1, V2} + cgroup_version: Option<CgroupVersion> field to JailerConfig. Emit --cgroup-version 2 when Some(V2). Default None (matches current behavior, no silent breakage).

title: Jailer-harden: geteuid==0 guard before exec
description:
FC docs state "we run the jailer as the root user". m80-jailer-harden applies one-way hardening (drops caps, sets no_new_privs, clears signal mask) and execs the official jailer. If m80-jailer-harden runs non-root, jailer silently fails or misbehaves AFTER hardening has been applied — no recovery path. m80-preflight checks m80's own privilege but not the jailer exec path specifically.

Add geteuid()==0 check at the top of apply_process_hardening (before any caps/prctl/setgroups syscall). New HardenError::NotRoot{actual: u32} variant.

title: FC API surface m80 leaves on the table
description:
FC exposes several REST endpoints and config knobs that m80 does not touch. Wiring up the relevant subset improves two distinct concerns: (a) diagnostics — FC's own structured log and metrics give visibility into vhost, device-emulation, and virtio errors that m80's host-side Diagnostics and m80-guestd's vsock-side MetricsRequest cannot see; (b) workload operability — TAP MTU and virtio-net queue depth constrain throughput for any workload moving non-trivial network data inside the VM.

Source-verified gaps:
- m80-firecracker-client implements put_boot_source, put_machine_config, put_drive, put_vsock, patch_vm_state, put_snapshot_create/load, instance_action. NO put_logger, NO put_metrics, NO NetworkInterfaceConfig.

- m80-net-outbound::link_ops creates TAP via tun::configure() with no MTU; LinkOps trait has no set_link_mtu method.
- m80-observability records host-side lifecycle events; no FC native metrics ingestion.

title: FC snapshot best-practice correctness
description:
Three correctness gaps relative to FC's snapshot best practices:

1. SnapshotManifest.expected_firecracker_version is written at capture time but restore() never validates it against the live FC process before put_snapshot_load(). FC binary upgrade between capture and restore silently corrupts/crashes.

2. MachineConfig has no track_dirty_pages field; restore() hardwires None for enable_diff_snapshots. SnapshotKind::Diff compiles but never works in production. Prerequisite for v0.2 diff snapshot work — wire plumbing now so the flag is threaded through consistently when diff snapshots ship.

3. m80-guestd has no post-restore hook. VMGenID re-seeds kernel CSPRNG only; cached entropy tokens, /var/lib/systemd/random-seed, and userspace PRNGs survive restore byte-for-byte across all clones — clones share initial PRNG state in Python's random, Ruby's SecureRandom (if buffered), etc. (Source: FC random-for-clones.md + arXiv "Restoring Uniqueness in MicroVM Snapshots".)

title: Snapshot: post-restore CSPRNG re-seed in m80-guestd
description:
VMGenID re-seeds kernel CSPRNG only on restore; cached tokens, /var/lib/systemd/random-seed, and userspace PRNGs that buffered /dev/urandom output before snapshot survive restore byte-for-byte across all clones. Add post-restore hook in m80-guestd that:

1. ioctl(RNDRESEEDCRNG) on /dev/urandom — forces kernel re-seed from hardware
2. Delete /var/lib/systemd/random-seed if present (ENOENT ok)
3. Document residual gap: userspace PRNGs that captured entropy pre-snapshot remain at risk until next os.urandom() call

Add wire message PostRestoreReady (or restore_hook phase marker) in m80-proto so host signals guest a restore occurred and waits for ack. guestd main loop calls post_restore::run() before accepting first exec.

title: Decision: virtio-balloon as security non-goal
description:
FC supports virtio-balloon for runtime memory reclaim. FC docs explicitly warn balloon constraints void if guest driver compromised — host can be directed to over-commit by hostile guest. m80 is a security sandbox; guest is untrusted.

title: IMDS link-local block regression pin
description:
Verification: 169.254.0.0/16 IS already in permanent_deny_cidrs() in crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs:132. Materializes as REJECT rule in per-VM filter chain via ensure_filter_chain_rules(). The filter chain runs before nat/POSTROUTING (FORWARD precedes POSTROUTING in netfilter), so the block is genuinely pre-NAT — IMDS-destined packets never reach MASQUERADE. DNS bypass closed too: is_admitted_dns_resolver() rejects link-local resolvers.

What's MISSING: no regression test pins the 169.254.0.0/16 CIDR specifically OR its ordering relative to terminal ACCEPT. Existing permanent_deny_list_includes_bridge_cidr test iterates all CIDRs but doesn't isolate IMDS, doesn't check ordering. Silent removal would go undetected.

Priority: P1 (block present, regression pin missing — preventing future drift).

title: Test: IMDS CIDR REJECT present in per-VM filter chain
Test: IMDS REJECT precedes terminal ACCEPT (ordering)

description:
Capture the IMDS-block behavior so future contributors can see what the regression tests are pinning and why.

Files:
- docs/behaviors/network/imds-block.md (new)

Outline:
- Claim: guest traffic to 169.254.0.0/16 (AWS/GCP/Azure IMDS, link-local) is REJECTed before terminal ACCEPT in every per-VM filter chain
- Mechanism: permanent_deny_cidrs() includes 169.254.0.0/16; installed by ensure_filter_chain_rules() via per-VM tap FORWARD insert
- Pre-NAT guarantee: FORWARD runs before POSTROUTING; MASQUERADE never fires for IMDS-destined packets
- DNS admission: is_admitted_dns_resolver() also rejects link-local — no ACCEPT-first DNS bypass path

title: guestd connection.rs stdin_handle.write_all has no size cap
description:

finder: trim-the-fat r5
