title: DESIGN: Settle wire — READY_PORT, host-listener path, version byte
description:
Pin the implementation contract before IMPL leaves start. Most
decisions already made by parent description rewrite (2026-05-04).

## Decisions to lock

1. **READY_PORT constant**. Suggestion: `9000` (one below exec port
   9001). Defined in `m80-proto::version` as `READY_PORT_DEFAULT: u32`.
2. **Where the host binds the listener**. Suggestion:
   `m80-jailer::Plan::compute` adds a CreateInsideJail step for the
   listener's parent path; m80-firecracker's
   `phase_4_jailer_materialize` binds the `UnixListener` at
   `<jail>/vsock.sock_<READY_PORT>` and stores the FD on
   `MaterializedJail` for `phase_12b` to consume.
3. **Wire payload from guest**. Single byte:
   `m80_proto::PROTOCOL_VERSION as u8`. Mismatch surfaces as a new
   `VsockError::ProtocolVersionMismatch { expected: u8, got: u8 }`.
4. **Deadline**. Reuse `READY_TIMEOUT` from `launch.rs`. Listener's
   `accept()` is non-blocking; phase_12b polls `accept()` with a
   short epoll timeout per iteration.
5. **Fallback**. None. If `accept()` times out, surface
   `VsockError::NotReady` like today. The CONNECT/OK probe is no
   longer needed for readiness; remove `Channel::open_uds_only`'s
   role in phase_12b but keep the helper for the actual exec
   handshake later.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Three constants merged in m80-proto: `READY_PORT_DEFAULT`,
      `READY_PORT_PROTOCOL_VERSION_BYTE` (alias for `PROTOCOL_VERSION
      as u8`), `READY_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` (probably 5s, separate from
      `READY_TIMEOUT` which is the overall phase_12b budget).
- [ ] `VsockError::ProtocolVersionMismatch` variant added.
- [ ] m80-vsock README documents the new ready-listener contract.
- [ ] No phase_12b changes yet (that's IMPL host leaf .4).
close_reason: design locked in parent description; implemented in ad00c02

title: IMPL guestd: outbound connect to host CID 2 + write proto-version byte at startup
description:
Depends on m80-7tpy.2 (DESIGN). Implement the guestd side of the
inverted-readiness handshake.

## Change site

`crates/m80-guestd/src/main.rs` — between the inbound `bind` on
GUEST_PORT_DEFAULT (line ~57) and the existing
`println!(READY_MARKER_DEFAULT)` ready-marker (line ~61).

## Behavior

1. After `VsockListener::bind_with_cid_port(VMADDR_CID_ANY, port)`
   succeeds, open `VsockStream::connect_with_cid_port(VMADDR_CID_HOST,
   READY_PORT)`.
2. Write exactly one byte: `m80_proto::PROTOCOL_VERSION as u8`.
3. Flush; close (drop the stream). No reads — host already knows
   we're ready by the time the byte lands.
4. If the connect fails or the write fails, **exit non-zero** with a
   typed error logged. We don't want guestd to silently start
   listening when the host can't see it; the host's own deadline
   will surface the problem, but a fast guest-side abort produces
   better diagnostics.

## What stays the same

- Keep the `println!(READY_MARKER_DEFAULT)` print to the serial
  console for now. Removing it is a separate cleanup once the host
  side is migrated and we've verified no third path watches the
  marker.
- The vsock crate dependency is already present
  (`vsock::VsockListener` is imported; add `VsockStream`).

## Tests

- Unit test in `crates/m80-guestd/tests/` (or co-located if simpler)
  that drives a fake host UDS via `socat` or
  `nix::sys::socket` and verifies one byte == PROTOCOL_VERSION
  arrives.
- Negative test: with no host listener, the connect fails and the
  process returns non-zero (test as a child process via
  `assert_cmd` if guestd already uses it; otherwise document
  that this is covered end-to-end in the smoke test).

## Out of scope

- Removing the console-marker println — see CHANGELOG entry in
  m80-7tpy.6.
- Host-side accept; that's m80-7tpy.4.
notes: Implemented in commit ad00c02. m80-guestd outbound connect to (VMADDR_CID_HOST, READY_PORT_DEFAULT=52525) with PROTOCOL_VERSION byte, after vsock listener bind, before main accept loop. Failure is fatal.

title: IMPL host: replace phase_12b polling with accept() + version-byte read
description:
Depends on m80-7tpy.2 (DESIGN) and m80-7tpy.3 (guestd impl). Replace
the polling loop in `phase_12b_ready_probe` with a deadline-bound
accept on the ready socket.

## Change site

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:411-447` — `phase_12b_ready_probe`.

## Behavior

1. Before `InstanceStart` (i.e., earlier in launch.rs than today's
   phase_12b), bind a `UnixListener` on
   `<jail_path>/vsock.sock_<READY_PORT>`. Set non-blocking or
   accept-timeout so the deadline is enforceable.
   - If m80-7tpy.1 found we need a separate REST PUT for the
     listener port, do that instead/also here.
2. After `InstanceStart`, `accept()` with a deadline (READY_TIMEOUT,
   today's 30s but consider lowering — this is event-driven so the
   wait is bounded by guest boot, not poll-interval-quantized).
3. On `accept()`:
   - Read exactly one byte with a 5s read deadline.
   - Compare against `PROTOCOL_VERSION as u8`.
   - On mismatch, return
     `VsockError::IncompatibleProtoVersion { expected, got }` —
     no exec channel is opened. Tear down.
4. On success: drop the ready socket; proceed to
   `Channel::open_uds_only(vsock_uds, GUEST_PORT_DEFAULT)` exactly
   as today. The exec channel is the same as before.

## Error variants

- New `VsockError` variant for proto-version mismatch (mirror
  ProtoError; one variant — don't add a generic "PreflightFailed").
- Reuse `VsockError::NotReady` for the deadline case.

## Tests

- Unit test with a hand-rolled mock guestd (a thread that connects
  to the UDS and writes one byte) that verifies the host accepts
  and validates within the deadline.
- Test for proto-version mismatch: write `0xff` instead of
  `PROTOCOL_VERSION` and assert the host returns
  `IncompatibleProtoVersion`.
- Test for accept timeout: don't connect at all, assert
  `NotReady` after the deadline.

## Out of scope

- Choosing READY_TIMEOUT. Today's 30s is a reasonable starting
  point; tighten in m80-7tpy.5 once benchmarks land.
- Removing the polling code in phase_12b — this leaf replaces it,
  not gates it behind a feature flag. m80 is v0.1 and we own
  every consumer.
notes: Implemented in commit ad00c02. phase_11b_bind_ready_listener creates UnixListener at <jail>/vsock.sock_52525 before InstanceStart, chowns to jail_uid. phase_12b_ready_accept replaces polled CONNECT/OK probe with accept() + version-byte read.

title: BENCH: m80-7tpy vs m80-tv7i+m80-6gv9 — pick the winner
description:
Validate event-driven readiness beats the polling backstop (m80-bgas).

## Background

m80-tv7i and m80-6gv9 (the original alternative paths this bench was
meant to compare against) are both closed `--reason "premise-refuted"`
or `"superseded"`. The remaining comparison is m80-7tpy
(event-driven via `accept()`) vs m80-bgas (10ms-poll CONNECT/OK
backstop).

## Bench harness

On a real KVM host:
1. Run `scripts/smoke.sh launch-only` 30 times with the m80-bgas
   constants (10ms poll, 60s timeout). Record P50/P95 of "InstanceStart
   REST PUT → vsock channel ready".
2. Same, with m80-7tpy enabled.
3. Repeat both under host load (`stress-ng --cpu 8` running
   in parallel).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] m80-7tpy idle-host P50 ≤ 50ms above guest kernel boot floor.
- [ ] m80-7tpy P95-vs-P50 spread ≤ 2× (low jitter is the point of
      event-driven).
- [ ] m80-7tpy under stress: P95 within 1.5× of idle P95 (graceful
      degradation; polling would degrade linearly with host load).
- [ ] Numbers added to CHANGELOG and to m80-vsock README.

## Out of scope

- Comparing to smolvm directly. Per recon doc 03, smolvm uses 10ms
  stat-poll on a virtiofs marker — they're not on firecracker, so
  it's apples-to-oranges. The relevant differentiator is m80-7tpy's
  event-driven design, not a head-to-head latency number.
close_reason: obsolete: m80-bgas polling removed entirely, no comparison target remaining

title: DOCS: README + CHANGELOG entries for inverted-readiness contract
description:
Update docs and CHANGELOG so the new readiness contract is the single

No further closures needed from this leaf — it's a docs-only landing.

title: Untrusted-guest threat model — host-facing (W21)
description: Wave 21 of 25. Audited 10 lenses: vsock framing, balloon (null), drive write storms, network egress, cgroup memory pressure, CPU starvation, time-source/TSC, console flood, snapshot exfil, writeback. ~30% null/already-tracked. Wire framing is well-hardened (W14 confirmed). New findings: streaming byte amplification, virtio-blk rate_limiter unwired, console.log unbounded, console.log read-to-end into RAM, setuid bit propagation on writeback, NetworkInterface rate_limiter unwired, FORWARD policy not asserted, cpu_template=None default. Many findings overlap m80-8emae.10/.26, m80-2ggw.1.x/.4.3, m80-kv4ri.2/.8/.16, m80-1vna7.1, m80-3s9ak.6.

title: Writeback fs::copy preserves setuid/setgid; malicious guest plants mode 04755 host binary
description:
**Finding:** walk_for_extract (crates/m80-storage/src/scratch.rs:387) calls fs::copy which internally uses fchmod(dst, src_mode) — preserves ALL mode bits including S_ISUID/S_ISGID/S_ISVTX (high octal 04xxx, 02xxx, 01xxx). umask does NOT apply to fchmod. A guest creates /workspace/exploit with mode 04755 in the scratch ext4; after extract:
- Staging tree gets mode 04755.
- Atomic rename publishes it at workspace/exploit.
- If m80 runs as root (jailer requires root for KVM/namespace ops), file is root-owned + setuid → host has a privilege-escalation binary dropped by the guest.
- If m80 runs as a dedicated uid, still grants that uid's capabilities to any user who execs it.

The dir branch at scratch.rs:274/376 calls set_permissions explicitly (preserving full mode incl. high bits). e2fsck -p doesn't clear setuid. loop -o ro doesn't strip mode bits at the inode layer.

**File:** crates/m80-storage/src/scratch.rs:387 (regular files); :274,376 (dirs).

**Severity:** HIGH (root-on-host scenario; LOW-MEDIUM otherwise).

**Acceptance:**
- After fs::copy, mask high bits before fs::set_permissions: `let mode = meta.permissions().mode() & 0o0777; fs::set_permissions(&dst_path, fs::Permissions::from_mode(mode))?;`
- Apply same masking to dir branch (currently preserves S_ISUID/S_ISGID on dirs too).
- Test pin: guest creates /workspace/setuid_test with mode 04755 → extract → verify host mode is 0755.
- Cross-link m80-3s9ak.6 (this finding ESCALATES the mode-bit gap from LOW to HIGH and adds explicit high-bit masking).
close_reason: Fixed writeback mode sanitization in m80-storage: extracted files and directories now preserve only 0o777 bits after copy/set_permissions, with regressions for 04755 files and 02755 dirs. Verified cargo test -p m80-storage, cargo fmt --all -- --check, and git diff --check.

title: Streaming exec: no per-session byte cap; compromised guest exhausts host memory with 4 MiB frames
description:
**Finding:** The buffered exec path enforces EXEC_BUFFER_LIMIT=1 MiB per stream via append_capped (exec.rs:725-733). The STREAMING path does NOT — exec_streaming_inner passes all bytes through to a caller-supplied on_chunk closure unconditionally. A compromised guestd can sustain 4 MiB ExecStdout frames at maximum vsock rate; bounded only by the 5s I/O timeout (resets per successful frame).

Each frame allocates one 4 MiB Vec on the host. Sustained: host memory exhaustion. Per-frame size is gated by MAX_FRAME_BYTES (W14L1 null); per-session aggregate is not.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs (exec_streaming_inner; on_chunk callback).

**Severity:** MEDIUM (host-process DoS bounded by connection lifetime; not an escape).

**Acceptance:**
- Add a per-exec total-bytes-received cap on the streaming path (e.g., configurable via SandboxConfig.streaming_byte_limit; default 256 MiB).
- Track stdout_total + stderr_total (already accumulating via saturating_add at exec.rs:426/447); compare against limit before passing to on_chunk.
- On cap exceeded: send Cancel + return FcError::StreamingByteLimitExceeded.
- Cross-link m80-vpifh.1 (BRIDGE_IO_TIMEOUT) and m80-r4308.6 (similar unbounded buffer pattern in warm-owner socket).

title: console.log unbounded; guest /dev/console flood fills host disk (no RLIMIT_FSIZE)
description:
**Finding:** crates/m80-jailer/src/types.rs:80-91 ResourceLimits::default() leaves fsize: None. materialized.rs:129-133 skips the jailer --resource-limit fsize=N argument entirely when None. RLIMIT_FSIZE is unset on the FC process; console.log under run_dir grows unbounded.

A guest spamming 'echo BLOB > /dev/console' writes at host I/O throughput until run_root disk fills. Preflight's 100 MiB free check (m80-preflight) is a one-time admission gate, never re-checked during VM lifetime. Compounds m80-243wj.1 (network-state.json write fails on full run_root → mis-classified as orphan).

**File:** crates/m80-jailer/src/types.rs:80-91 (ResourceLimits default); crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs:129-133 (fsize plumbing already exists; just unused); crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:895 (phase_4 stdio_log).

**Severity:** MEDIUM (host-disk DoS; cross-VM impact via shared run_root FS).

**Acceptance:**
- Set ResourceLimits.fsize in phase_4_jailer_materialize to a chosen cap (e.g., 64 MiB or expose via SandboxConfig).
- Test: guest writes 100 MiB to /dev/console → assert FC kill with SIGXFSZ before exceeding cap.
- Cross-link m80-243wj.1 (run_root disk pressure).
notes:
Absorbed pass 2:
- m80-80htr.4: m80-80htr.3 covers unbounded console.log growth filling host disk (RLIMIT_FSIZE gap). m80-80htr.4 covers `emit_guest_boot_phase_events` read

title: emit_guest_boot_phase_events reads ENTIRE console.log into RAM; large boot output → host RSS spike
description:
**Finding:** launch/ready.rs:88-96 emit_guest_boot_phase_events calls std::fs::read_to_string(console_log) AFTER readiness handshake. NO size guard, no take(N) limit. If a compromised guest (or buggy initrd) emits large serial output BEFORE guestd sends the ready signal, this synchronous read materializes the entire console.log into host process memory before parsing as a String.

500 MiB console.log → 500 MiB RSS spike on the host m80 process + blocks launch return for I/O time.

The boot-phase events of interest are always near the END of the log; reading the whole thing is wasted.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs:88-96.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (host memory + latency DoS; bounded only by console.log size which is currently unbounded — see m80-80htr.3).

**Acceptance:**
- Cap the read at the last N KiB of console.log (e.g., 64 KiB) using seek + read; not read_to_string.
- Stream parse line-by-line via BufReader if larger context needed.
- Cross-link m80-80htr.3 (RLIMIT_FSIZE) — once that lands, console.log is bounded; this finding becomes informational.

title: VirtIO drive rate_limiter never used; guest writes overlay/scratch at peak throughput
description:
**Finding:** crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:358-375 DriveConfig has NO rate_limiter field. Firecracker's REST schema supports rate_limiter (token-bucket bytes/s + ops/s) on each drive PUT. m80 never sends it. Rootfs overlay + workspace scratch both configured with IoEngine::Async + CacheType::Unsafe (fastest host path), zero throttle.

Compounds: cgroup io.max field exists in Limits but Limits::preset() leaves io_max: Vec::new() (m80-1vna7.1 vicinity). Host-side disk throttle also unwired. Two layers of unused throttling.

Cross-VM impact: single guest fills shared host filesystem (overlay + scratch backing files), causing ENOSPC for all sibling VMs.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:358-375 (DriveConfig missing field); crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:102-120 (drive PUT call sites); crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:244 (preset io_max empty).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (multi-tenant shared-FS deployments).

**Acceptance:**
- Add rate_limiter to DriveConfig with bandwidth + ops token bucket types.

title: FORWARD chain default policy not asserted DROP; spoofed src-IP from guest may slip past
description:
**Finding:** m80-net-outbound inserts FORWARD entry rules with -I (prepend) matching -i <bridge> -s <guest_ipv4>/32. Packets NOT matching (e.g., spoofed source IP from guest) fall through to host FORWARD default policy. m80 NEVER sets the FORWARD chain default policy. On hosts with FORWARD default ACCEPT (common dev machines, not always production), spoofed-source packets pass through. They miss MASQUERADE too (which also matches -s <guest_ipv4>/32) → hit the wire raw with spoofed source.

Whether physically reachable depends on upstream router RPF/anti-spoofing. m80 itself adds zero defense.

**File:** crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs (no '-P FORWARD DROP' anywhere); preflight has no FORWARD policy check.

**Severity:** LOW (depends on host config + upstream filtering).

**Acceptance:**
- Add preflight CheckRow asserting FORWARD chain policy is DROP; warn (not fail) if ACCEPT.
- Alternative: explicitly set -P FORWARD DROP in ensure_bridge_ready_with_ops (carries operator-policy risk if other services need ACCEPT default).
- Document the assumption in m80-net-outbound/README.md.
- Cross-link m80-8emae.* security epic.

title: Default cpu_template=None exposes full host CPUID + RDTSC; no precision restriction
description:
**Finding:** SandboxConfig::default() at types.rs:285 → cpu_template: None. Every CLI call site (cmds.rs:416, warm/run.rs:260, warm/owner.rs:212) also defaults to None. Firecracker T2 template would restrict CPUID surface (mask constant_tsc/rdtscp advertisement, narrow TSC frequency). With None, guest receives the host's full CPUID, including RDTSC at native precision — prerequisite for cache-timing side channels (Spectre v1/v2, Flush+Reload).

Single-tenant: low risk (one guest = no cross-VM target). Multi-tenant: same physical core co-residence enables timing attacks.

m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs has CpuTemplate::T2 wired in cpu_template_for_cpuinfo (Intel detection) but this is only used when caller explicitly opts in; defaults None.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs:285 (SandboxConfig::default cpu_template); crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:314-319 (CpuTemplate enum); m80-73qb3.3 (AMD T2A not configured).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (multi-tenant only).

**Acceptance:**
- Change SandboxConfig::default() cpu_template to Some(T2) when Intel host detected (via cpu_template_for_cpuinfo).
- For AMD: bundled with m80-73qb3.3 (add T2A).
- Test the resulting guest CPUID surface via cpuid in guest exec to confirm masking.
- Document the trade-off in m80-firecracker/README.md.

title: m80 env --json: diagnostic dump command (host capabilities + config + versions)
description:
Modeled on kata-ctl env. Single subcommand printing host capability + runtime config + hypervisor version + kernel/image paths in a format-versioned JSON envelope.

## Reference

kata-exploration/10-dx-docs-config.md. kata-ctl env dumps: host info (kernel, CPU, memory, vsock support, KVM capability), runtime config (paths, debug flags), hypervisor info (version via subprocess, machine type), image/kernel paths. Output as TOML or JSON with a format-versioned envelope.

## Why

Bug reports today require asking the user to gather scattered facts (uname, kvm-ok, firecracker --version, m80 config show, ls of run-root). One command should produce a complete dump.

## Scope

- m80 env --json: emits {"version": 1, "data": {...}} envelope.
- Captures: kernel version, /dev/kvm accessibility, vsock kernel module, CPU count + flags relevant to KVM, total memory, current m80 config (effective after layering), firecracker version (subprocess if discoverable), kernel + rootfs paths from manifest, m80-cli version, run-root state if present.
- m80 env (no flag): human-readable equivalent.
- Format-versioned: every consumer reads `data.version` first.

## Out of scope

- Auto-uploading dumps anywhere.
- Live VM inspection (that's m80 inspect).

## Acceptance

- m80 env --json produces a single JSON document parseable by jq.
- README documents the command and points at it from a "filing a bug" section.
- A bug-report template can curl the output into an issue.
notes: captured: m80 env / m80 --json env emits host capability/config/profile/artifact/firecracker/run-root/preflight diagnostic dump without requiring successful KVM preflight; JSON uses standard envelope plus data.version=1; README and bug template point reporters at the dump. docs=docs/behaviors/cli/env-dump.md, crates/m80-cli/README.md, README.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md; tests=crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/env.rs unit tests, crates/m80-cli/tests/parse_args.rs, crates/m80-cli/tests/help_smoke.rs; subprocess smoke=target/debug/m80 --json env | jq.

title: Test-time auto-dump: on test failure, surface <run_dir>/console.log + diagnostics.jsonl
description:
Make test failures self-explaining. Today an integration-test failure leaves logs in /tmp/.../run_dir; you have to know to look. A wrapper that dumps relevant artifacts on failure makes flakes (and real bugs) cheap to triage.

## Why

Flake debugging cost is dominated by "where are the logs for that run." A drop-on-fail helper makes that cost zero. Compounds with every other observability bead.

## Scope

- Test helper in m80-firecracker (or a tests/common/ module) that wraps integration-test setup; on test panic / assertion failure, prints last N lines of <run_dir>/console.log and the full <run_dir>/diagnostics.jsonl to test stderr.
- Helper is opt-in (callers wrap the test body in a guard); not a global panic hook to avoid suppressing real bugs.
- Truncate console.log dump to a sane size (e.g. last 100 lines) but always full diagnostics.jsonl (small).
- Include the run_dir path in the dump so the user can re-inspect.

## Out of scope

- Auto-uploading to anywhere.
- Capturing host-side strace / perf data (out-of-band tools).

## Acceptance

- A deliberately-failing integration test produces a readable artifact dump in cargo test output.
- A passing test produces nothing extra.
- One canonical test demonstrates the helper.
notes: Implemented 2026-05-05. RunDirDumpGuard at crates/m80-firecracker/tests/common/mod.rs uses Drop + std::thread::panicking() check; testable dump_run_dir(&Path, usize, &mut dyn Write) factored out so unit tests can capture+assert on output via Vec<u8> sink. 8 unit tests cover all scenarios. Missing files surface as '(not found)' lines, not swallowed.

title: Security audit: guest-escape resistance (multi-agent sweep)
description:
**Status:** planned, not yet executed.

**Angle:** Guest-escape resistance — m80's load-bearing security promise per TARGET.md ("Untrusted LLM-generated input running inside the sandbox → guest-escape resistance is the security bar"). Multi-agent parallel-lens audit, methodology mirrors the perf epic (m80-jp6ik).

**Why this angle:** security audits are the canonical fit for parallel-lens methodology — each agent gets one escape vector and goes deep. Findings convert cleanly into beads with clear acceptance (the missing capability drop, the unsanitized vsock field, the unconfined cgroup controller).

**Expected lens shapes (~14-15 agents):**
- Jailer capability set: every `caps::clear` + `prctl(PR_CAPBSET_DROP)` site. Which caps survive? Why?
- Seccomp filter coverage: FC syscall surface vs jailer's BPF filter. Gaps?
- Mount-ns escape: bind-mount plan audit for symlink races, escapes via `..` traversal, propagation flags
- Vsock protocol fuzz surface: guestd parses untrusted bytes from a compromised guest? What's the trust boundary?
- Cgroup confinement: memory.max, cpu.max, pids.max — what can a guest exhaust to DoS the host?
- KVM device-emulation CVE-floor: confirm FC version is above the floor for known guest-escape CVEs
- Image integrity supply chain: manifest sha256 covers WHAT? Signing? Provenance? Reproducible builds?
- Side-channel surface: KSM (covered by preflight), SMT/HT (covered), cache-timing, rowhammer mitigations
- Host-FD leakage: which FDs survive into the jailed firecracker process? Any that shouldn't?
- /proc, /sys, /dev exposure inside the chroot
- User namespace + uid/gid mapping correctness
- Symlink TOCTOU in the host launch path
- Resource exhaustion: FD limits, inotify watches, kernel keyrings

**Findings format:** each agent returns punch list with file:line, vector description, exploit feasibility (theoretical/demonstrated), proposed mitigation, effort. Findings become child beads under this epic with priority by exploit feasibility.

**Cross-link:** AGENTS.md kernel-touching rule (m80-lovpn.2) applies — most mitigations need real-KVM smoke evidence.

title: CRITICAL: boot_args override + guest_mac space-injection → init= bypass
description:
**Severity: CRITICAL** (demonstrated escape path)

## Finding A: `SandboxConfig::boot_args` REPLACES base cmdline

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:183-191` — `boot_args_for()` uses caller-supplied `boot_args` as the entire base, NOT appending. `init=/m80-guestd` is dropped when override is set. Test `tests/lifecycle_failure_real_kvm.rs:235` already exercises `init=/bin/sh` → boots interactive shell, bypasses ALL guest-side confinement (vsock gating, exec policy, ready-marker protocol).

**Attack:** Any Rust caller constructing `SandboxConfig` with `boot_args: Some("...init=/bin/sh".into())` → VM boots to shell, guestd never starts.

## Finding B: `NetnsSpec::guest_mac` unvalidated → space injection

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:194-197` joins `extra_boot_args` with spaces. `guest_mac` is `String` (not typed). Attack input `guest_mac = "02:ab:cd init=/bin/sh"` → cmdline tokenizer sees `init=/bin/sh` as a new token, overrides PID-1. Same outcome via different vector.

## Fix

1. `boot_args_for()` — REMOVE the full-override arm. Caller's extras append AFTER hardcoded `init=/m80-guestd`. Make `init=` unconditional and not overridable.
2. `NetnsSpec::guest_mac` — change to a typed `MacAddr` newtype or validate against `^[0-9a-fA-F]{2}(:[0-9a-fA-F]{2}){5}$` at construction time. Reject any whitespace in any cmdline-bound `String`.
3. Add `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/cmdline_injection.rs` (NEW) — regression test pinning that `boot_args: Some("init=/bin/sh")` does NOT result in `init=/bin/sh` in the final cmdline; pinning that whitespace in `guest_mac` is rejected at NetnsSpec construction.
4. Document in CLAUDE.md: cmdline construction is security-critical, append-only from caller, never override.

## Smoke evidence required (AGENTS.md rule)

Yes — this is cmdline-injection class, kernel-touching effectively. PR must include green smoke from a KVM host.

## Effort: ~4h
close_reason: fixed: boot_args append-only with reserved-token rejection; JoinNetns guest_mac typed MacAddr; docs/tests added

title: HIGH: Conntrack exhaustion — preflight check + per-VM connlimit
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (single-guest cross-VM DoS in OutboundNat)

## Finding (agent 13 #2 + agent 16 #6)

`net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` is host-global. Each OutboundNat-mode guest opens TCP/UDP connections → conntrack entries. Default limit on commodity kernels is 65536-262144 entries. A guest can fill it via a connection-flood loop in seconds, blocking ALL VMs and host processes that use NAT.

m80-preflight verifies `nf_conntrack` MODULE presence but never reads `nf_conntrack_max` (`crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs:287`).

Per-VM iptables also lack `connlimit` / `hashlimit` rules — no per-source-IP cap on new connections.

## Fix

1. **Preflight check**: read `/proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`; warn (or fail) if below threshold (e.g., `2 * expected_concurrent_VMs * 1000`). Add `M80_EXPECTED_CONCURRENT_VMS` env or config. Doc the host setup: `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=N`.
2. **Per-VM connlimit**: `iptables -I FORWARD -i <tap_name> -p tcp --syn -m connlimit --connlimit-above 256 --connlimit-mask 32 -j REJECT`. Tunable per-VM via config.
3. Both batched into `iptables-restore` block (per perf bead `m80-jp6ik.19`).

## Tests

`crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/conntrack_limit.rs` (NEW) — install a small connlimit; verify SYN-flood from guest stops being accepted past the limit.

## Smoke evidence: yes (iptables changes).

## Effort: ~6h
notes:
Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-l3tiq.5: nf_conntrack_max not tuned/documented is precisely the documentation half of m80-8emae.10 (conntrack exhaustion preflight + per-VM connlimit

title: HIGH: M80_DEBUG_WIRE leaks ExecRequest env secrets in trace logs
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (operator-mistake secret exfiltration)

## Finding (agent 20 F1)

`crates/m80-vsock/src/debug_wire.rs` + `crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/debug_wire.rs` — when `M80_DEBUG_WIRE=vsock|fcrest|all`, every vsock frame and FC REST body is logged via `tracing::trace!` as raw hex/ASCII (up to 1024 bytes). The vsock channel carries `ExecRequest` which includes `env: Vec<(String, String)>` — when a caller uses `m80 run --secret-env API_KEY=...`, that secret transits the frame and lands in trace logs verbatim. Operator sets `M80_DEBUG_WIRE` for a debug session, forgets to unset, secrets leak forever after.

## Fix

1. **Type-aware redaction**: when the frame kind is `exec_request`, decode the proto, scrub `env` field, then emit a redacted preview (`env=[NN entries redacted]`). Other frame kinds preview as-is.
2. **Doc warning**: prominently document on `M80_DEBUG_WIRE` and on `SandboxConfig::env` that secrets in env propagate to vsock and may appear in trace logs when wire-debug is on.
3. **Tests**: `crates/m80-vsock/tests/debug_wire_redaction.rs` — set M80_DEBUG_WIRE=vsock, send an ExecRequest with a sentinel-secret env, capture log output, assert the sentinel string does NOT appear.

## Effort: ~3h
close_reason: Implemented vsock debug-wire redaction for ExecRequest.env, documented M80_DEBUG_WIRE secret handling, and added regression coverage.

title: MEDIUM: File-mode hardening on diagnostics.jsonl + boot-identity + console.log
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (info disclosure on shared/multi-tenant hosts)

## Findings (agent 20 F2/F3/F4)

m80 writes several files in `<run_root>/<vm-id>/` with **no explicit mode** — they inherit the process umask (typically 0o022 → 0o644 world-readable):

- `diagnostics.jsonl` (`crates/m80-observability/src/diagnostics.rs:38`) — contains netns paths, tap names, error context.
- `boot-identity.json` (`crates/m80-firecracker/src/boot_identity.rs:40`) — contains absolute paths to kernel + rootfs artifacts.
- `console.log` (`crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs:149`) — guest serial output, kernel dmesg.

On a host where /var/lib/m80-run is shared (multi-tenant deployment), any local user can read these.

## Fix

Each open site → use `std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt::mode(0o600)` (single tenant on the host has write+read; nobody else). Or `0o640` if a group operator account needs read.

```rust
use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).mode(0o600).open(path)
```

For `std::fs::write` sites: replace with `OpenOptions` + `.mode(0o600)` + manual write.

Also: `<run_dir>` directory itself should be 0o700 (only the m80 process can enter).

## Tests

`crates/m80-firecracker/tests/file_mode.rs` (NEW) — after launch, stat each known artifact file, assert mode bits exclude world+group read/write.

## Effort: ~2h

title: MEDIUM: cargo-audit in CI
description:
**Severity: process** (CI gap — no continuous advisory scanning)

## Finding (agent 19)

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs fmt+build+test+clippy+shellcheck. No `cargo audit`, no `cargo deny`, no `deny.toml`. 206 external crates with no RustSec coverage.

Plus: **4 concurrent nix versions in tree** (0.28, 0.29, 0.30, 0.31) — advisory fragmentation; a nix advisory may not be caught if checking only the workspace pin.

## Fix

1. Add `cargo audit` job to CI:
   ```yaml
   audit:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       - uses: rustsec/audit-check@v2
         with: { token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} }
   ```
2. Or `cargo deny check advisories` with a `deny.toml`. Stricter, also covers license + duplicate-dep policy.
3. Consolidate nix versions: pin all nix users to one workspace dep version. Requires unblocking `portable-pty` / `rtnetlink` / `vsock` upstreams or local-patch deps.

## Effort: ~2h for cargo-audit CI; ~1d for nix consolidation
notes: 2026-05-14 split dependency-version consolidation to m80-8emae.43 after source-checking the duplicate nix graph: portable-pty requires nix 0.28, workspace/tun use 0.29, rtnetlink requires 0.30, vsock requires 0.31. This bead now closes the continuous RustSec advisory scanning gap.

title: MEDIUM: FC advanced seccomp filter + guestd seccomp
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (defense-in-depth gaps)

## Findings (agent 2)

A. **FC's advanced seccomp filter not opted into** — m80 runs FC's default basic filter (`--seccomp-level 2` default; advanced via `--seccomp-filter <path>`). Advanced filter blocks additional syscalls (mprotect+PROT_EXEC, broader ioctl, clone variants). m80 never passes `--seccomp-filter`.

B. **guestd has no seccomp filter** — m80-guestd runs PID-1 inside the guest with no syscall confinement. A compromised guest exec attacking guestd via vsock has guestd's full syscall surface.

## Fix

A. `crates/m80-jailer/src/types.rs` — add `seccomp_filter_path: Option<PathBuf>` to `JailerConfig`. `crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs` — append `--seccomp-filter <path>` to jailer args when set. m80-preflight verifies path exists. FC releases ship pre-compiled BPF blobs alongside binaries; preflight can discover and use them.

B. NEW: install a tight seccompiler-based filter in guestd after vsock bind, before accept loop. Allowlist = syscalls actually used (bind/accept/read/write/close/execve/wait4/clone/futex/openat/fstat/...). Use the existing `seccompiler` crate (already in FC's deps; not yet in m80 workspace).

## Tests

A. `crates/m80-jailer/tests/seccomp_path.rs` — verify the arg is passed correctly.
B. `crates/m80-guestd/tests/seccomp_filter.rs` — inside-guest test that a denied syscall fails with EPERM/SIGSYS.

## Effort: ~1d (mostly enumerating guestd's actual syscall surface for B)
notes: Firecracker advanced seccomp is implemented in prior commits. Remaining work is guestd/workload seccomp and must be split: shared workload broker first, then daemon filter, then real-KVM seccomp evidence. Do not install a long-lived guestd filter in the current accept loop before routing arbitrary exec/PTY through a broker; child workloads would inherit the daemon filter.

title: MEDIUM: Workspace TOCTOU on copy_tree + extract size cap
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (TOCTOU + DoS in workspace handling)

## Findings (agent 12)

A. **Workspace copy_tree TOCTOU** — `crates/m80-storage/src/scratch.rs:255` (`copy_tree`) calls `fs::symlink_metadata` then `fs::copy`. Between the two, an adapter-side concurrent writer can swap the regular file for a symlink, and `fs::copy` opens the source without `O_NOFOLLOW`. Result: host file content (target of swapped symlink) copied into the scratch image and exposed to guest.

B. **Extract size unbounded** — `crates/m80-storage/src/scratch.rs:286-316` (`walk_for_extract`). No `total_bytes` cap. Guest fills the scratch image with up to `scratch_size_mib` of data; extract copies it ALL to the host destination in one call. Host disk DoS.

## Fix

A. Replace `fs::copy` with manual open: `OpenOptions::new().read(true).custom_flags(O_NOFOLLOW).open(src)` → `io::copy` to dest. Eliminates the race.

B. Add `max_extract_bytes: Option<u64>` parameter to `StoppedSandbox::extract_changes`. Abort `walk_for_extract` when `total_bytes > max`. Default = the scratch image size at launch.

## Tests

A. `crates/m80-storage/tests/copy_tree_toctou.rs` — concurrent symlink swap during copy_tree; assert fails (EPERM/ELOOP) rather than copying through.
B. `crates/m80-storage/tests/extract_size_cap.rs` — guest writes N bytes; extract with max < N returns size-exceeded error.

## Effort: ~4h

title: MEDIUM: Snapshot persistence_path — reject path-traversal IDs at API boundary
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (path traversal via caller-controlled IDs)

## Finding (agent 15 F4)

`crates/m80-snapshot/src/lib.rs:426-454` (`persistence_path`, currently `#[cfg(test)]`). Doc comment says "callers handling untrusted IDs must reject `/` and `..` at the API boundary." m80 has no enforcement of its own — if `workspace_id` or `run_id` is derived from untrusted input upstream and passed through, snapshot storage lands at attacker-controlled paths.

## Fix

Per CLAUDE.md "internal call graph is closed — we are the someone, don't push validation to callers":

1. Promote `persistence_path` out of `#[cfg(test)]` (likely already needed for bead `m80-8emae.s4` snapshot manifest work).
2. At the start of the function, reject any `id` containing `/`, `\\`, `..`, NULL bytes, or starting with `.`. Return `SnapshotError::InvalidId` typed variant.
3. Same guards in any other call site that takes caller-controlled IDs and constructs paths.

## Tests

`crates/m80-snapshot/tests/persistence_path_validation.rs` — table of bad IDs (`../etc`, `/etc/passwd`, `foo/bar`, empty, NULL), assert each returns InvalidId.

title: MEDIUM: Snapshot bind — canonicalize via fd + RO remount
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (TOCTOU + missing RO remount on snapshot bind)

## Finding (agent 3 F3 + agent 13 F6)

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:326-394` (`bind_snapshot_parent_into_jail`):
- `host_parent = paths.vm_state.parent()` — no canonicalize, no symlink check on caller-supplied path.
- `mount(..., MS_BIND)` — no follow-up `MS_RDONLY` remount. Snapshot files end up writable to the jailed FC UID after the chown.

1. Open `host_parent` with `O_PATH | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`; verify type via `fstatfs`. Use `/proc/self/fd/<n>` as mount source.
2. After bind, remount with `MS_BIND | MS_REMOUNT | MS_RDONLY` (same pattern as `bind_remount_flags()` in `plan.rs`).
3. Tests: snapshot bind from a symlinked parent fails; write attempt to bound snapshot returns EROFS.

## Smoke evidence: yes (mount path, kernel-touching).

## Effort: ~3h

description:

title: HIGH: Strip SUID/SGID + cap-xattr from Ubuntu rootfs; MS_NOSUID on overlay+workspace
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (in-guest privilege escalation trivially exploitable)

## Findings

A. **Ubuntu rootfs ships with SUID/SGID binaries** — `crates/m80-image-build/src/pipeline.rs:280-299` (`squashfs_to_ext4`) runs `unsquashfs` + `mkfs.ext4 -d` with no SUID-strip pass. Standard Ubuntu 24.04 ships `sudo`, `su`, `mount`, `umount`, `newgrp`, `gpasswd`, `chfn`, `chsh`, `passwd`, `ping` family all SUID-root. Non-root guest exec → `sudo -s` → root inside guest. From there, kernel exploit surface widens substantially.

B. **Overlay drive (vdb) mounted without MS_NOSUID** — `crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs:203-218`. Guest writes a SUID binary into overlay (`chmod u+s /workspace/foo`), execs it → privilege gain.

C. **Workspace drive (vdc) same** — `pid_one.rs:496` `workspace_mount_ext4` uses `MsFlags::empty()`.

D. **Capability xattrs (`security.capability`) preserved from squashfs** — `unsquashfs` keeps them; `mkfs.ext4 -d` preserves. Equivalent to SUID for cap-bearing files.

## Fix

1. `crates/m80-image-build/src/pipeline.rs:squashfs_to_ext4` — after `unsquashfs`, before `mkfs.ext4 -d`:
   ```
   find <squash_out> -perm /6000 -exec chmod a-s {} \;
   find <squash_out> -exec setfattr -x security.capability {} \; 2>/dev/null
   ```
2. `crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs` — vdb mount: `MsFlags::MS_NOSUID`. Workspace mount: `MsFlags::MS_NOSUID | MS_NODEV`.
3. Tests: `crates/m80-image-build/tests/no_suid_after_strip.rs` — find -perm /6000 on the built rootfs returns empty. Guest-side: attempt SUID exec from overlay fails with EPERM.

## Smoke evidence: yes (kernel-touching — mount flag changes).

## Effort: ~3h
close_reason: real artifact + real guest smoke passed: mounted /opt/m80/artifacts/output.ext4 read-only and sudo find -xdev (-perm -4000 -o -perm -2000) returned suid_sgid_count=0; sudo getcap -r produced no capability-xattr entries. Booted NoEgress VM with workspace: guest /proc/mounts reported / overlay rw,nosuid,nodev,... and /workspace ext4 rw,nosuid,nodev,...; boot phases included overlay_disk_mounted, overlayfs_mounted, and workspace_mounted. Source coverage includes unsquashfs -no-xattrs and SUID/SGID strip tests plus PID-1 mount-flag tests.

title: MEDIUM: discovery FC-version-match enforcement on restore (closes m80-2ggw.4.1)
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (silent failure of guard at restore boundary)

## Finding (agent 15 F3)

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:607` — `launch_from_snapshot` takes a `&Discovery` parameter and immediately drops it (`let _ = discovery; // API symmetry`). So `discovery.manifest.expected_firecracker_version` is NEVER compared against the running FC binary on restore.

A snapshot captured against FC v1.10.0 restored on v1.15.0 is undefined behavior per FC docs — vmstate format changed. Could trigger FC parser bugs (escape vector territory) or silent state corruption.

There's an open bead `m80-2ggw.4.1` for this exact gap.

## Fix

title: CRITICAL: Warm-pool owner.sock — peer-cred + size-cap + RAII unlink
description:
**Severity: CRITICAL** (unauthenticated cross-user command execution + DoS)

## Findings (BR2 — warm-pool daemon)

### A. `owner.sock` has no peer-credential check
`crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/owner.rs:74` and `control.rs` — `UnixListener::bind` with no umask manipulation or post-bind `chmod`. Socket inherits process umask (typically 0022 → 0755). Any local user can `connect()` and issue `WarmControlRequest::Run` with arbitrary program/args/env/stdin, executing inside a warm VM at the daemon's privilege context. Also `Drain` / `Disable` are unauthenticated → DoS via pool drain.

### B. `read_to_end` on owner.sock unbounded
`control.rs:288` reads until EOF with no size cap. Peer holds write-half open, streams GB of junk → daemon OOM, accept loop is sequential so no other request progresses.

### C. Stale socket on unclean exit → spoof
`owner.rs:183-185` — `remove_owner_state()` only runs on clean Ok path. On panic/SIGKILL/OOM the socket file remains. Startup guard refuses to re-launch. An attacker who can SIGKILL the daemon AND has write to `<run_root>/warm/` can unlink the stale socket, bind their own, intercept all subsequent `m80 warm run` invocations.

## Fix

1. After `bind`: `std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt::set_mode(0o600)` on socket file, OR `getsockopt(SO_PEERCRED)` check on every accepted connection — reject if peer UID ≠ daemon UID.
2. Replace `read_to_end` with `Read::take(MAX_REQUEST_BYTES)` (a few MB). Add `set_read_timeout` on the accepted stream.
3. Wrap socket lifecycle in RAII guard (struct with Drop impl); use signal-hook or panic_handler to unlink on abnormal exit.

## Smoke evidence: yes.

## Effort: ~4h

title: CRITICAL: Guest exec drops uid + caps + sets no_new_privs (workload not as root)
description:
**Severity: CRITICAL** (single FC bug = full guest-escape chain; widest possible exec surface)

## Finding (AG7 — privilege-escalation chain)

The "guest is untrusted" threat model assumes the attacker has to first escalate inside the guest. But: **guestd is PID-1 as uid 0 (root), and `ExecRequest` spawns child processes via `Command::new` with no uid drop, no seccomp filter, no `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`**.

This means: the attacker's exec process IS already guest-root with full caps and full syscall surface. SUID-strip (bead .2) and stripped kernel are defense-in-depth but a guest-root attacker bypasses them and proceeds directly to step 2 of the escape chain (FC virtio bug). Per `docs/behaviors/guest-exec/exec-privilege-policy.md`, the per-workload privilege drop is explicitly deferred.

## Fix

Add per-exec privilege drop in guestd:
1. `crates/m80-guestd/src/connection.rs` — before `Command::spawn`:
   - `setresuid(EXEC_UID, EXEC_UID, EXEC_UID)` (EXEC_UID = e.g. 1000)
   - `setresgid(EXEC_GID, EXEC_GID, EXEC_GID)`
   - `setgroups([EXEC_GID])`
   - `caps::clear(None, CapSet::Effective)` + drop all caps from Bounding
   - `prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS)`
2. Optionally: install a seccomp filter restricting exec'd processes' syscall surface.
3. `ExecRequest` proto field for caller-controlled exec UID if needed (e.g., torpor2 might want non-root anyway).

Tradeoff: some workloads (apt-install, mount, ip route) need privileged operations. Provide either (a) opt-in `privileged: true` flag in `ExecRequest`, or (b) a separate "privileged init" exec that runs first as root to set up the workspace, then subsequent execs drop.

## Tests

`crates/m80-guestd/tests/exec_uid_drop.rs` — verify default `ExecRequest` runs as non-root (`id -u` returns ≠ 0); verify `no_new_privs` is set; verify caps are empty.

## Smoke evidence: yes (kernel-touching — uid/cap drops).

## Effort: ~2d
notes: implemented locally in commit pending: guestd root execs now route pipe and PTY workloads through /proc/self/exe --m80-exec-shim, which sets no_new_privs, clears ambient/bounding caps, drops to uid/gid 1000 with groups [1000], clears effective/permitted/inheritable caps, then execs the requested program. Docs updated: crates/m80-guestd/README.md and docs/behaviors/guest-exec/exec-privilege-policy.md. Tests: cargo test -p m80-guestd; git diff --check. Added ignored root regression crates/m80-guestd/tests/exec_uid_drop.rs for uid/no_new_privs/cap proof. Leaving open pending privileged real guest/root smoke evidence.

title: CRITICAL: ICMP egress unblocked in OutboundNat (covert exfil channel)
description:
**Severity: CRITICAL** (data exfiltration / unrestricted egress in OutboundNat mode)

## Finding (AG2 channel 1)

`crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs:326-339` — `ensure_filter_chain_rules` covers DNS (UDP/TCP 53), private CIDR denies, and ends with an unconditional `-j ACCEPT`. **ICMP is not covered by any of these rules.** Final ACCEPT lets all ICMP through.

A guest can embed up to 65KB per ICMP echo request payload and send to an attacker-controlled host. Exfiltration bandwidth bounded only by guest's kernel and host bandwidth. Detection requires DPI / payload inspection that most environments lack.

## Fix

Add `-p icmp -j REJECT` before the final ACCEPT in `ensure_filter_chain_rules`. Or restrict the final ACCEPT to `-p tcp -j ACCEPT` + explicit UDP ACCEPT, leaving everything else implicit-DROP.

```rust
// In ensure_filter_chain_rules, before the final ACCEPT:
ensure_iptables_rule(["-p", "icmp", "-j", "REJECT"], ...)
```

For IPv6 (per bead .3), `-p icmpv6 -j REJECT` similarly — but ICMPv6 ND is required for v6 to function. Safer to keep IPv6 disabled per .3.

## Tests

`crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/icmp_blocked.rs` — set up outbound, `ping` from inside guest VM, assert exit code != 0.

title: HIGH: Intra-bridge L2 traffic bypasses iptables (br_netfilter + per-VM bridge)
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (direct VM-to-VM traffic bypasses iptables)

## Finding (AG3 #1)

Linux bridge forwarding operates at L2 BEFORE iptables FORWARD sees L3 packets — UNLESS `br_netfilter` kernel module is loaded AND `net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1` is set. Neither is enforced or checked anywhere in m80-net-outbound.

Result: a VM on the bridge can send L2 frames directly to another VM's TAP. iptables FORWARD never runs. ARP poisoning, direct IP-to-IP, and L2 sniffing all work between sibling VMs sharing a bridge — even though the per-VM chain has private-CIDR deny rules that LOOK like they'd block this.

Bead .3 covers IPv6, port isolation, TAP-scoped FORWARD — but doesn't address the deeper "iptables never fires for intra-bridge traffic" issue.

## Fix

Two complementary mitigations:

1. **Preflight check**: verify `br_netfilter` module loaded AND `net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables == 1`. Fail closed if not. Add to `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs`.
2. **Per-VM bridge**: each VM gets its OWN bridge instead of a shared one. Eliminates intra-bridge traffic entirely — VM A and VM B don't share an L2 segment. Higher per-launch cost but stronger isolation. Pairs with bead .3's per-port isolation (which becomes moot if each port is its own bridge).

Alternative (cheaper): `ebtables` rules to drop intra-bridge frames. Less clean than per-VM bridges.

## Tests

`crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/intra_bridge_isolation.rs` — two VMs on outbound; assert VM A cannot ping VM B's IP.

## Smoke evidence: yes (kernel-touching bridge/netfilter).

## Effort: ~1d (preflight check) + ~2d (per-VM bridges as follow-up)

title: CRITICAL: TCB binary hash verification (FC + jailer + jailer-harden + m80 + m80-cli)

title: CRITICAL: Snapshot bind chown — scope host_parent to snapshot_root prefix
description:
**Severity: CRITICAL** (CAP_CHOWN-based privilege escalation from compromised m80)

## Finding (BR1 F8)

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:370-375` — `bind_snapshot_parent_into_jail` calls `chown(host_parent, jail_uid, jail_gid)` on a path derived from `paths.vm_state.parent()`. `paths` is from caller-controlled `SnapshotPaths`.

With CAP_CHOWN (in m80's REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES), a compromised m80 process — or a callable consumer passing a hostile path — can chown ANY file or directory on the host to uid 3000 (the jail UID), stripping it from its legitimate owner.

Combined with a follow-on bind-mount (or even just `chmod`), this is reliable privilege escalation: chown `/etc/sudoers.d/` to 3000, drop in a sudoers entry granting jail UID NOPASSWD, then jail UID is root.

## Fix

1. `SnapshotPaths` constructor / validation — require `vm_state` and `mem` to be descendants of a configured `snapshot_root` (operator-configured, defaulting to `<run_root>/snapshots/` or `<run_root>/warm/snapshot/`).
2. `bind_snapshot_parent_into_jail` — canonicalize and verify `host_parent` is under `snapshot_root` BEFORE chown. Reject otherwise.
3. Tests: attempt restore with `vm_state: /etc/vm.snap`; assert rejection with `SnapshotPathOutsideRoot`.

## Smoke evidence: yes.

## Effort: ~4h
notes: Implemented locally: snapshot bind parents now canonicalize below BackendConfig::run_root before chown/bind-mount; run_root itself, outside directories, and symlink escapes are rejected. Added lifecycle unit coverage plus behavior/design/README docs. Verification: cargo test -p m80-firecracker snapshot_parent_scope; git diff --check. title: HIGH: OutboundNat — IPv6 leak + bridge port isolation + TAP-scoped FORWARD
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (cross-VM lateral attack surface in OutboundNat mode)

## Findings (from agent 16 net audit)

A. **IPv6 unfiltered** — `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs` (no ip6tables rules); `link_ops.rs:169-177` (bridge created without IPv6 disable). Kernel auto-assigns link-local IPv6; guest can egress over v6 entirely outside the v4-only iptables ruleset.

B. **No bridge port isolation** — `link_ops.rs:232-247` (`LinkBridge::new` without IFLA_BRPORT_ISOLATED). VMs sharing a bridge can ARP-poison each other / sniff each other's frames.

C. **FORWARD entry filters `-i <bridge>` not `-i <tap>`** — `iptables.rs:342-366`. Guest spoofs sibling VM's source IP → traffic routed through victim's chain, exits NAT'd as victim's IP.

## Fix

1. `iptables.rs` — alongside `ensure_ipv4_forwarding`, sysctl-write `net.ipv6.conf.<bridge>.disable_ipv6=1` + `net.ipv6.conf.<tap>.disable_ipv6=1`. Or `ip6tables -A FORWARD -i <bridge> -j DROP`. Prefer the sysctl path (prevents link-local from being assigned at all).
2. `link_ops.rs:attach_link_to_bridge` — extend to set `IFLA_BRPORT_ISOLATED=1` per TAP port via rtnetlink SETLINK. New `LinkOps` method.
3. `iptables.rs:342` — change FORWARD entry rule from `-i <bridge>` to `-i <tap_name>`. The TAP name is in `state.tap_name`.
4. Tests: NEW `crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/cross_vm_isolation.rs` — two-VM bridge with both an isolated and non-isolated config; verify the isolated config rejects ARP poisoning + IP spoofing attempts.

## Smoke evidence: yes (network + iptables + bridge — kernel-touching).

## Effort: ~1d (each finding is XS-S; combined + tests is medium).

title: HIGH: Private VMM netns for NoEgress + AllowOutbound (compromised-FC containment)
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (compromised FC has unrestricted host network access)

## Finding (BR7 F3 + existing docs/behaviors/security/compromised-vmm-network-boundary.md)

In `NoEgress` and `AllowOutbound` modes, Firecracker runs in the HOST network namespace. If FC is compromised (post-VM-escape), the attacker's code in the FC process can open arbitrary host-namespace TCP/UDP sockets, reach host services (cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254, internal APIs, sshd), exfiltrate data over any port.

Documented as a known gap in `docs/behaviors/security/compromised-vmm-network-boundary.md` but not tracked as an active bead.

## Fix

Each FC process runs in its own private network namespace:
1. Before fork+exec of jailer-harden, `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)` to give FC a fresh empty netns.
2. The TAP device (for OutboundNat) is moved into the new netns BEFORE exec.
3. For NoEgress: empty netns with only loopback. FC has nowhere to send packets.
4. For AllowOutbound: TAP in netns, NAT applied as today, but FC can't reach loopback / other interfaces.

Implementation: `crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs` — add `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)` to the `pre_exec` hook on the jailer-harden Command. Move TAP via `ip link set tap netns <pid>` (netlink API) after spawning.

## Files

- `crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs` (pre_exec hook)
- `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/lib.rs` (TAP namespace move)
- `crates/m80-jailer/src/types.rs` (new JailerConfig flag)

## Tests

`crates/m80-firecracker/tests/private_netns.rs` — verify FC process's `/proc/<pid>/ns/net` differs from m80 process's. Sniff syscalls: FC has no socket() permission to AF_INET in the parent netns.

## Smoke evidence: yes (network namespace, kernel-touching).

## Effort: ~2-3d

title: HIGH: WarmPool snapshot file immutability + re-verify on each slot fill
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (warm-pool poisoning via filesystem write)

## Finding (AG9 F3 + BR2 F5)

WarmPool golden snapshot files (`vm.snap`, `mem.snap`) are:
- Written by `m80 warm owner` at startup (`crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/owner.rs:57-72`)
- Mode/owner left at process defaults (typically owner's uid, mode from umask)
- Read repeatedly by `WarmPool::launch_slot` (`warm_pool.rs:295`) for every slot fill
- **Not re-verified on each fill** — initial sha256 hash (per bead .4 once it lands) is computed once at startup; if a writer modifies the files later, all subsequent restores load the tampered files

A process running as the same uid as the warm-owner daemon (sibling m80 instances, compromised sidecars, escaped FC via .7+.30) can overwrite the snapshot mid-pool-lifetime. All subsequent slot fills load attacker bytes.

## Fix

1. **Immutability after capture**: `chmod 0o444` on snapshot files immediately after `running.capture()`. Optionally `chattr +i` (immutable attribute, requires CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE — m80 has it).
2. **Re-verify on each fill**: in `WarmPool::launch_slot`, before passing snapshot paths to `launch_from_snapshot`, recompute sha256 and compare to the locked-in baseline. Fail the fill on mismatch (slot stays empty; alarm).
3. **Privilege separation**: golden capture writes to a staging path; a separate process with read-only access serves the pool. Higher effort.

## Files

- `crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/owner.rs` (chmod after capture)
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs` (re-verify on launch_slot)

## Tests

`crates/m80-firecracker/tests/warm_pool_snapshot_immutability.rs` — capture, tamper mem.snap, attempt slot fill, assert failure.

## Cross-link

Depends on bead .4 (snapshot manifest + integrity baseline).

## Effort: ~6h
close_reason: Implemented warm-pool snapshot hardening: foreground owner locks vm.snap, mem.snap, and snapshot-manifest.json to 0444 after capture; WarmPool verifies the snapshot manifest before every slot admission/restore, with restore still verifying again before PUT /snapshot/load. Added behavior doc and non-KVM regression coverage including tampered snapshot fill failure. Verification: cargo test -p m80-cli --lib; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --lib; cargo test -p m80-snapshot restore_rejects_tampered_memory_before_load; git diff --check.

title: HIGH: Env-overridable path validation (M80_*_BIN + M80_RUN_ROOT + config.d O_NOFOLLOW)
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (env-injection redirects entire TCB to attacker-controlled paths)

## Findings (BR1 F7 + BR8 F3 + BR1 F3)

Multiple env vars accepted with no path validation:
- `M80_FIRECRACKER_BIN`, `M80_JAILER_BIN`, `M80_JAILER_HARDEN_BIN` — point at any binary
- `M80_RUN_ROOT` — point at any directory
- `~/.config/m80/config.d/*.toml` drop-ins read without `O_NOFOLLOW` — symlink-pointing config files

A confused service supervisor, a compromised env-providing layer, or any caller able to set env can redirect the entire TCB to attacker-controlled paths.

## Fix

1. Add `M80_TRUSTED_PATH_PREFIX` (or compile-time constant) listing allowed prefixes for binary paths: `/opt/firecracker/bin/`, `/opt/m80/bin/`, `/usr/local/bin/`. Reject paths outside these in `m80-preflight/src/binary.rs`.
2. `M80_RUN_ROOT` — preflight verify resolved path is owned by root (or current uid) AND parent dir is NOT world-writable.
3. Config drop-in dir: open each `.toml` with `O_NOFOLLOW` (and `O_DIRECTORY` on the dir itself). Reject symlinks.
4. All path resolutions use `canonicalize` + prefix-check, not raw `.exists()`.
5. Optional: `--allow-env-path-override` CLI flag to opt OUT of the path restrictions for development.

## Files

- `crates/m80-preflight/src/binary.rs` (binary path validation)
- `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs` (run_root permissions)
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs:203` (drop-in O_NOFOLLOW)

## Effort: ~6h

title: HIGH: Build supply chain — protoc-vendored + quickstart self-cert + kernel-tag + apt-pin
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (build-time RCE + self-certifying-checksum bypass)

## Findings (AG10 — supply chain holes distinct from .15)

### A. `protoc-bin-vendored` ships embedded ELF
`crates/m80-proto/build.rs` invokes `protoc-bin-vendored::protoc_bin_path()` which extracts a 9.7 MB statically-linked protoc binary from the crate. Runs on the build host during `cargo build`. Cargo.lock checksum-locks the crate, but no independent verification (no Sigstore, no Reproducible Builds).

### B. `m80 quickstart` self-certifying tarball checksum
`crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/quickstart.rs:76-103` — downloads `<artifact_url>` then `tar -xzf` then `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`. **The SHA256SUMS file is inside the tarball.** An attacker controlling the tarball controls the checksum. The outer `.tar.gz.sha256` published separately on GitHub Releases is never downloaded or checked.

### C. Kernel git clone by tag not commit SHA
`kernel-builder/Dockerfile` uses `ARG KERNEL_TAG` with `git clone --depth 1 --branch ${KERNEL_TAG}`. Tag can be force-moved upstream. Commit SHA is immutable.

### D. Dockerfile `apt-get install` fetches live unpinned packages
Same Dockerfile — `apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential gcc binutils ...` with no version pins. Compromised APT mirror or BGP/DNS hijack at build time injects backdoored toolchain.

## Fix

A. Replace `protoc-bin-vendored` with system-installed `protoc` via `PROTOC` env var. Or pin and externally-verify the embedded binary's sha256.
B. Quickstart: download `<artifact>.tar.gz.sha256` separately; verify tarball BEFORE extraction. Or use cosign signatures on releases.
C. Use pinned commit SHA in Dockerfile instead of tag.
D. Pin specific apt package versions; use a Debian snapshot APT mirror with pinned date.

## Files

- `crates/m80-proto/build.rs`, `crates/m80-proto/Cargo.toml`
- `crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/quickstart.rs:76-103`
- `crates/m80-image-build/kernel-builder/Dockerfile`

## Effort: ~1d
notes:
Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-8emae.15: image build supply chain (kernel no expected-sha + Docker digest unpin + artifact perms) overlaps: same class of "we hash what we got, not w
- m80-uh6ex.4: image-build downloads no sha256 verification before consumption is a duplicate finding to .15(B). Preserve: "no merge beyond what .15 alread
close_reason: Implemented deterministic build-supply-chain hardening: quickstart now downloads <artifact-url>.sha256 and verifies the outer tarball before extraction; m80-proto prefers PROTOC and verifies the vendored Linux x86_64 protoc sha256 before fallback execution; kernel builder fetches the peeled v6.1.134 commit directly and installs packages from pinned Ubuntu snapshot 20260505T000000Z instead of live mirrors. Verification: cargo test -p m80-cli --test quickstart_smoke; cargo test -p m80-image-build --test kernel_build_pipeline; cargo test -p m80-proto; git diff --check.

title: HIGH: CAP_NET_ADMIN drop post-network-setup + enable new_pid_ns
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (CAP_NET_ADMIN retained for full m80 process lifetime + missing PID namespace)

## Findings (BR1 F6 + BR7 F6)

### A. CAP_NET_ADMIN never dropped post-network-setup
m80 holds CAP_NET_ADMIN for the entire process lifetime, even though it only NEEDS it during `phase_6_network_realize` (TAP creation, iptables setup). After that phase, the capability is dormant attack surface. A compromised m80 process can install arbitrary iptables rules, sniff traffic, modify routes — all CAP_NET_ADMIN powers.

### B. `new_pid_ns: false` — forked orphans outlive SIGKILL
`crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:857` (or thereabouts) sets `new_pid_ns: false`. PDEATHSIG is set but PDEATHSIG is not inherited across `fork`. A compromised FC that forks children before m80 SIGKILLs the FC pid leaves orphan processes that the cgroup pids.max may or may not catch.

## Fix

### A. Drop CAP_NET_ADMIN after phase_7
After `phase_7_outbound_guest_config` completes successfully, call `caps::clear(None, CapSet::Effective)` for just CAP_NET_ADMIN, or use `prctl(PR_CAPBSET_DROP, CAP_NET_ADMIN)`. Note: CAP_NET_ADMIN is needed PER LAUNCH for outbound; if m80 is long-lived (warm-pool owner), this needs careful coordination — drop AFTER pool init for owner mode, or per-launch for CLI mode.

Alternative: move network setup into a separate suid-root helper that drops caps post-setup and communicates results back via pipe. Higher effort.

### B. Enable `new_pid_ns: true`
`launch.rs:857` change to `new_pid_ns: true`. FC's children all live in a private PID namespace. Namespace teardown reaps them automatically.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs` (CAP_NET_ADMIN drop + new_pid_ns flag)
- `crates/m80-jailer/src/types.rs` (JailerConfig flag if not already there)

## Smoke evidence: yes.

## Effort: ~6h
notes: PID namespace half is implemented in prior commits. Remaining CAP_NET_ADMIN work is a process-boundary hardening sequence tracked by child leaves: helper protocol, helper-backed network calls, parent capability drop, and real-KVM smoke after drop. Do not implement a direct post-phase cap clear; long-lived launch/cleanup still needs network mutation until the helper boundary is live.

PID namespace was implemented earlier; helper boundary design, m80-net-helper protocol/discovery, helper-backed OutboundNat launch/cleanup, backend-thread CAP_NET_ADMIN drop, and real-KVM outbound smoke after the drop are all closed. Final smoke evidence: allow_outbound_survives_parent_cap_net_admin_drop passed under sudo with M80_RUN_EXTERNAL_NETWORK_E2E=1, proving DNS/HTTP, delete cleanup, stale run-root cleanup, and /proc/thread-self/status CapEff/CapPrm/CapBnd without CAP_NET_ADMIN.
