title: HIGH: BackendConfig/in-process trust model — private fields + vm_id validation + docs
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (in-process embedding model has fundamentally different threat surface than CLI)

## Findings (BR3 F1, F4, F6 — adapter-boundary trust model)

When m80-firecracker is embedded as a library in an adapter consumer process (torpor2), the entire m80 state is in adapter's heap:
- `BackendConfig.discovery` is `pub` — attacker controlling adapter heap can substitute attacker-chosen `firecracker_bin`/`jailer_bin`/`kernel`/`rootfs` paths and construct a new Backend.
- `WarmPool::state.ready` is `VecDeque<RunningSandbox>` inside `Arc<Mutex>`. Slot handles are stealable; compromised adapter calls `try_lease` repeatedly or instruments the heap.
- Public layout helpers (`run_dir_path`, `vsock_socket_path`, `firecracker_api_socket_path`) let any code-execution-in-adapter enumerate all live VMs and connect to their vsock directly, bypassing m80 lifecycle gates (admission permit, one-shot flag).
- `recover_stale_run_root` passes raw subdir names to `m80_cgroup::cleanup_orphan_subtree` (`backend.rs:254-260`) — `../../m80-firecracker/production-vm` could cleanup a live VM's cgroup.

`docs/adapter-boundary.md` describes what the adapter must own but does NOT acknowledge that in-process embedding requires the adapter to be trusted.

## Fix

1. Convert `BackendConfig` to a builder pattern with private fields and validation; `Discovery` not reconstructable from attacker input.
2. `vm_id` and subdir names: validate against `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+` (max 64 chars) at the boundary — both in `Backend::admit` and `recover_stale_run_root`.
3. Document the trust model: add to `docs/adapter-boundary.md` an explicit "Security boundary" section noting that in-process embedding requires a trusted caller; meaningful isolation requires fork+exec or a separate service process.
4. README for m80-firecracker: add a "Threat model when embedded" section.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs` (BackendConfig private fields + builder)
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:182` (vm_id validation)
- `docs/adapter-boundary.md`
- `crates/m80-firecracker/README.md`

## Effort: ~1d
close_reason: Made BackendConfig builder-only for external callers, validated caller vm_id/run-root child names, documented in-process trust boundary, and added regression coverage.

title: HIGH-DEFERRED: /dev/kvm post-InstanceStart seccomp tightening (FC upstream needed)
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (post-FC-escape /dev/kvm gives full KVM ioctl surface + kernel attack)

## Finding (BR7 F2)

FC requires `/dev/kvm` open at all times; it is mknod'd into the chroot by the official jailer. A compromised FC process can issue arbitrary KVM ioctls on that fd: `KVM_CREATE_VM` (boot a second, unaccounted VM), `KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION` (point at host memory mappings FC already holds), `KVM_RUN`. KVM ioctls are a known kernel-exploit primitive (Pwn2Own 2022-2024 KVM chains).

FC's default basic seccomp allows `ioctl` on already-open fds, including /dev/kvm. After `InstanceStart` completes, FC needs only `KVM_RUN` and interrupt-delivery ioctls — but the filter doesn't differentiate.

## Fix

**Two-phase seccomp filter**:
1. Phase 1 (during FC startup, up to InstanceStart): current filter permits `KVM_CREATE_VM`, `KVM_CREATE_VCPU`, `KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION`, etc.
2. Phase 2 (after InstanceStart completes): a tighter filter installed via prctl that allows only `KVM_RUN`, `KVM_GET_REGS`/`SET_REGS` (for interrupt injection), and a small whitelist.

This requires either:
- Upstreaming a "phase 2 seccomp" feature to Firecracker.
- A LD_PRELOAD shim or ptrace-based filter that installs the tighter filter after detecting InstanceStart.
- Document the gap and accept it for v0.1; revisit when FC has the feature.

Realistically: the FC project would need to land this upstream. Track as a known gap + advocacy item.

## Cross-link

Bead .14 covers FC's advanced seccomp filter — distinct: that's about the BASIC vs ADVANCED filter swap. This is about a PHASED filter (startup vs runtime).

## Files

- `docs/decisions/<NNNN>-fc-dev-kvm-residual-surface.md` (NEW ADR documenting the gap + threat model implication)
- Track upstream FC feature request.

## Effort: ~3h to document; upstream feature is L+

## Status: DEFERRED — record the threat model + watch for upstream FC support
close_reason: Documented the post-InstanceStart /dev/kvm residual surface as a deferred Firecracker-upstream gap, with behavior capture and docs test.

title: MEDIUM: vsock host-side call-wide deadline (slow-drip DoS)
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (slow-drip vsock stall ties up host thread + warm-pool slot indefinitely)

## Finding (BR6 F4)

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs:395` — host's `channel.recv_raw()` has no per-CALL deadline, only a per-READ socket timeout (`BRIDGE_IO_TIMEOUT`=5s). A compromised guestd can write one byte every 4 seconds (just under the timeout), holding the host's exec call open indefinitely.

The `ExecRequest::max_duration_ms` field is processed by GUESTD (guestd applies its own timeout). The HOST doesn't enforce it. A malicious guestd ignores it.

Impact: warm-pool slot held forever, `RunningSandbox` (`&mut self`) blocked, host thread tied up. Not RCE, but a robust DoS against the calling adapter.

## Fix

In `Channel::open_uds_only` or `exec_streaming_inner`: convert `max_duration_ms` to a `Deadline = Instant::now() + duration`. Before each `recv_raw()`, check deadline. If exceeded, drop the connection and return `FcError::ExecTimeoutHost`.

Better: use `Channel::recv_with_deadline(deadline)` that internally adjusts `set_read_timeout` based on remaining time.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs` (call-wide deadline)
- `crates/m80-vsock/src/lib.rs` (deadline-aware recv)

## Tests

`crates/m80-firecracker/tests/exec_host_deadline.rs` — mock guestd that drips one byte every 4s; exec call with max_duration_ms=2000 returns ExecTimeoutHost after 2s.

## Effort: ~4h
close_reason: Added host-enforced exec receive deadline, slow-drip regression tests, and behavior docs.

title: MEDIUM: console.log — guest-controlled name injection + size cap + log-shipper threat model
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (log injection + log-shipper covert channel + disk DoS)

## Findings (AG2 console + AG4 F1 + F2)

### A. Guest-controlled `name=` token injected into stderr phase trace
`crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs:106-112,155-169` — `emit_guest_boot_phase_events` parses `M80_GUEST_BOOT name=<X>` from console.log and emits `M80_PHASE name=phase_12b_guest_<X> ...` to host stderr. **The guest controls `<X>`** — including newlines, log-forging payloads, ASCII control chars.

### B. `console.log` accumulates unbounded guest bytes
`crates/m80-firecracker/src/layout.rs:25` + jailer stdio. Guest writes to `/dev/ttyS0` in a loop → host disk fills. Bead .12 fixed file mode bits but not size cap.

### C. console.log as covert exfil channel (AG2 #3)
Operator's log-shipping pipeline (fluentd, Loki, Vector) routinely tails run-dir log files. Guest writes data to stderr → it lands in shipped logs. Anywhere those logs flow (SIEM, S3 buckets, third-party log providers) gets the data.

## Fix

A. Allowlist `name=` value to `[a-z0-9_]` before formatting. One regex check in `guest_boot_phase_event_from_line`.
B. Cap `console.log` size — wrap FC stdout in a size-limited writer, OR use a circular buffer file, OR enforce `RLIMIT_FSIZE` on the jailer process. ~2 MB cap should be enough for normal diagnostic use.
C. Document explicitly that operators must treat `console.log` as guest-influenced. Log-shipping pipelines should redact or exclude this file from external destinations.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs:155-169` (name allowlist)
- `crates/m80-jailer/src/types.rs` / `materialized.rs` (RLIMIT_FSIZE setup)
- `docs/ops/logging.md` (NEW)

## Tests

`crates/m80-firecracker/tests/console_log_injection.rs` — guest writes `M80_GUEST_BOOT name=foo\nADMIN_LOG: ...` to ttyS0; assert host stderr does NOT contain the injected line.

## Effort: ~6h
close_reason: Implemented console.log phase-name allowlist, 2 MiB shared stdio cap, operator logging docs, and regression tests.

title: MEDIUM: m80 host binaries in manifest + build-receipt for artifact co-replacement defense
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (process gap — m80 host binaries fall outside integrity coverage)

## Findings (BR10 F1 + F3)

`Manifest::verify()` covers four artifacts: kernel, source_rootfs, output_rootfs, daemon_binary (host-side audit copy of m80-guestd). NOT covered:
- `m80` (CLI binary)
- `m80-cli` (library?)
- `m80-jailer-harden`
- Firecracker + jailer (covered by bead s28 above)

Additionally: post-build artifact + manifest co-replacement window — operator account writes both, so an attacker who compromises the account can update the manifest's sha256 to match malicious bytes. The manifest sha256 is meaningful only if produced by a SEPARATE identity than the one that can modify the artifacts.

## Fix

Two-step:

1. Extend the manifest (or add `host-binaries.manifest.json`) to include sha256 of all TCB binaries. Land alongside bead s28 (TCB binary verification). 
2. **Build receipt**: at build completion, emit a separate `build-receipt.json` containing the sha256 of the manifest itself + every artifact. The receipt is written to a path that the deploy/run identity CANNOT modify (separate file system, signed log service, immutable-flag attribute). Preflight cross-checks manifest's own sha256 against the receipt.

This requires identity separation in deployment: build identity writes receipt; deploy identity copies artifacts; run identity reads-only. Document in `docs/ops/three-identity-model.md`.

## Files

- `crates/m80-image-manifest/src/lib.rs` (schema extension)
- NEW: build-receipt emit step at end of pipeline
- NEW: `docs/ops/three-identity-model.md` + `docs/ops/build-deploy-run-separation.md`

## Effort: ~1d

## Cross-link

Pairs with bead s28 (TCB binary hash verification).
close_reason: Implemented build receipt integrity for artifact co-replacement defense. m80-image-build now emits <rootfs>.build-receipt.json after manifest write for Ubuntu, minimal ext4, and minimal erofs builds. m80-image-manifest owns BuildReceipt schema v1. m80-preflight requires the selected rootfs receipt, verifies it points at the same manifest, verifies the manifest sha256, and checks receipt artifact path/hash tuples against the manifest even when the preflight sentinel supplies a cached manifest. Host binary manifest coverage was completed in f12b0da. Evidence: cargo test -p m80-image-manifest -p m80-preflight -p m80-image-build; cargo test -p m80-cli --no-run; git diff --check. Behavior doc: docs/behaviors/security/build-receipt-integrity.md.

title: HIGH: Snapshot restore — integrity check + manifest + FC version match
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (crafted snapshot file as escape vector)

## Findings (agent 15)

A. **No integrity check before FC `PUT /snapshot/load`** — `crates/m80-snapshot/src/lib.rs:248-283`. m80 hands `vm_state` + `mem` files directly to FC. No sha256, no manifest, no FC version match. Firecracker trusts its restore input — crafted vmstate (vCPU regs, MSRs, virtio queue state) can put guest into a state that bypasses normal boot-time hardening.

B. **`SnapshotManifest` schema exists but `#[cfg(test)]` only** — `m80-snapshot/src/lib.rs:51-135`. The types (Artifact, sha256, RestoreMetadata, SNAPSHOT_MANIFEST_FILE) are dead in production. Capture never writes a manifest; restore never reads one.

C. **`discovery` parameter discarded in `launch_from_snapshot`** — `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:607` (`let _ = discovery;`). No FC version match between capture-time and restore-time FC binary. Bead `m80-2ggw.4.1` already exists for this — this audit confirms it's open and load-bearing.

## Fix

1. Promote `SnapshotManifest` + helpers out of `#[cfg(test)]`. Sha256 each artifact at capture; write sidecar `SNAPSHOT_MANIFEST_FILE`.
2. `restore()` — before `put_snapshot_load`: read manifest sidecar, recompute sha256 on `vm_state` + `mem`, compare. Fail closed on mismatch.
3. `launch_from_snapshot` — use `discovery.manifest.expected_firecracker_version` vs `manifest.recorded_firecracker_version` for FC version match. Fail closed on mismatch.
4. Tests: snapshot capture writes manifest; restore on tampered mem.snap fails. Restore on mismatched FC version fails.

## Cross-link

Closes scope of `m80-2ggw.4.1`. May supersede it.

## Effort: ~1d
close_reason: Implemented snapshot manifest write/read enforcement: capture writes snapshot-manifest.json, restore verifies vm_state/mem sha256s and Firecracker version before vsock unlink or PUT /snapshot/load. Tests: cargo test -p m80-snapshot; cargo check -p m80-firecracker --tests; cargo test -p m80-firecracker missing_snapshot_error_is_classified_without_kvm; git diff --check.

title: MEDIUM: Workspace path canonicalize + JoinNetns dns_resolvers admission filter
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (workspace info leak + caller-controlled DNS)

## Findings (BR9 F3 + BR9 F4)

### A. Workspace root path not canonicalized
`crates/m80-storage/src/scratch.rs:123-145` — admissibility scan correctly rejects symlinks INSIDE the workspace, but the ROOT path (`config.workspace`) is never canonicalized. Caller passes `workspace=/tmp/ws` where `/tmp/ws → /etc` (symlink) → m80 reads the entire `/etc` tree, sizes the image, copies it into the scratch ext4. Guest gets read access to host `/etc` contents via `/workspace/`.

### B. JoinNetns DNS resolvers not admission-filtered
`crates/m80-net-mode/src/lib.rs:50` — `NetnsSpec::dns_resolvers: Vec<Ipv4Addr>` is taken from caller AS-IS. `OutboundNat` path runs admission filter (`is_admitted_dns_resolver`); JoinNetns does not. Caller can pass attacker-controlled DNS — guest queries leak query patterns (including LLM tool-call arguments) to the attacker's resolver.

## Fix

A. `Backend::admit` — `std::fs::canonicalize(workspace)` and verify resolved path is under a configured allowed-workspace-roots prefix (default: caller has to opt out explicitly).

B. Apply `is_admitted_dns_resolver` to every element of `NetnsSpec::dns_resolvers` at `NetworkPolicy` construction. Return error on first non-admitted.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs` (canonicalize workspace)
- `crates/m80-net-mode/src/lib.rs` (JoinNetns DNS filter)
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs` (allowed-workspace-roots config)

## Tests

A. Pass `workspace=/etc-symlink` pointing to `/etc`; assert rejection.
B. Pass `JoinNetns { dns_resolvers: [203.0.113.1] }` (TEST-NET); assert rejection.

## Effort: ~4h
close_reason: Implemented backend admission hardening: workspace roots must be real directories and are canonicalized before storage; JoinNetns DNS resolvers reuse outbound admissibility filtering. Allowed-workspace authorization remains adapter-owned per docs/adapter-boundary.md.

title: MEDIUM: Operator host-setup ops doc (docker socket + cargo + identity separation + assumptions)
description:
**Severity: MEDIUM** (operator-deployment gaps — no code change, doc + ops procedure)

## Findings (BR10 F4 + F5 + BR12 implicit assumptions)

### A. Docker socket as escalation
Docker daemon access is required for `m80 kernel-build`. Operator with docker socket access → `docker run --privileged -v /:/host` → full host root, INDEPENDENT of m80. Documented nowhere.

### B. `~/.cargo/config.toml` registry redirect
Compromised operator account → plants `[source.crates-io] replace-with = "hostile"`. All subsequent `cargo build` pulls from hostile mirror.

### C. Build-host TCB scope
Build host = entire developer laptop or CI runner. Hermetic build environment / reproducible builds: not documented as a requirement.

### D. Implicit operator assumptions (BR12 — too many to list in one bead)
- Artifact directory permissions
- Host kernel version
- /dev/kvm permissions
- run_root not world-writable
- nf_conntrack table size adequate
- Sysctls at defaults

Most are silent if violated. Operator has no way to know.

## Fix

NEW `docs/ops/host-setup.md` — comprehensive operator guide:
1. **Three-identity model**: build/deploy/run separation. Docker socket NOT held by run identity.
2. **Cargo vendoring**: vendor deps; commit lock; CI builds from vendor.
3. **Host preconditions**: kernel version, sysctls, `/opt/m80/` ownership/mode, `nf_conntrack_max`, KSM/SMT settings (cross-links beads .9 + future m80-2ggw.1).
4. **Build environment**: hermetic container, no network during build phase, reproducible-build verification suggested.
5. **CI hardening**: Pin GH Actions to commit SHAs (separate small bead).

This doc is the manifest for what an operator must do BEFORE m80 is trustworthy in production.

## Effort: ~6h (writing docs comprehensively)
close_reason: Added docs/ops/host-setup.md covering three-identity model, Docker socket risk, Cargo source/vendoring posture, build environment, runtime host preconditions, runtime privilege, and CI hardening; linked it from README; added docs/behaviors/ops/host-setup.md and a focused preflight doc regression test. Verified with cargo test -p m80-preflight --test ops_host_setup_docs and git diff --check.

title: LOW: Doc + test gaps — drive-slot trade-off + guestd trust + CapBnd test
description:
**Severity: LOW (advisory + doc gap)**

## Findings (combining smaller items)

### A. `new_pid_ns: false` → forked orphans
Already in s34 — but flag this as a SECONDARY concern beyond CAP_NET_ADMIN. New PID ns is also a containment win for: a compromised FC forking a persistence daemon that needs PID namespace teardown to reap.

### B. `preallocated_drive_slots` = idle live FC virtio-blk devices
`crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs:26` — default 0, but callers setting > 0 get LIVE virtio-blk devices in FC for the lifetime of the VM, not lazy slots. Each idle device is potential CVE surface. **Doc the trade-off in `SandboxConfig::preallocated_drive_slots`**.

### C. Guestd ready signal not attested
`crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs:203` — host accepts `PROTOCOL_VERSION as u8` as the only identity check. Any binary can pass. Trust assumption: guestd IS m80-built and operator-trusted. Document explicitly.

### D. Forged ExecResponse (compromised guestd)
By design — guest is untrusted, including guestd if compromised. The adapter consumer that needs result-integrity guarantees must verify externally (signatures, etc.). Document explicitly.

### E. CapBnd not asserted in tests
`crates/m80-jailer/tests/integration_root.rs:402-405` asserts CapPrm/CapEff/CapAmb = 0 but not CapBnd. Bead .7 / s34 already covers dropping it; this is the regression-test gap.

## Fix

1. Document A in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs` + `SandboxConfig` doc comment.
2. Document B in `SandboxConfig::preallocated_drive_slots` doc comment + README.
3. Add a "Trust model" section to `crates/m80-guestd/README.md` covering C and D.
4. Add `CapBnd: 0000000000000000` assertion in the existing integration test.

## Files

- `crates/m80-guestd/README.md` (trust model)

title: MEDIUM: Consolidate duplicate nix versions
description:
## Context

`m80-8emae.13` added continuous RustSec advisory scanning, but the dependency graph still resolves four `nix` versions:

title: HIGH: MS_PRIVATE on host mount-ns before bind plan (propagation leak)
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (container-escape via mount propagation)

## Finding (agent 3 F2)

`crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:156-167` — bind mounts (`MS_BIND|MS_REC`) issued in host's default mount namespace which is typically MS_SHARED on systemd hosts. MS_REC bind of a shared mount propagates back to peer namespaces. The jail's binds become visible host-wide AND a peer namespace mounting under the same subtree leaks INTO the jail.

There is no `mount(None, "/", MS_PRIVATE | MS_REC)` or `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` before the bind loop. The official FC jailer does this internally — but m80's pre-jailer mount work in `plan.rs` does not.

## Fix

Before the first `PlanStep::Bind` in `Plan::materialize`:
```rust
nix::mount::mount(None::<&str>, "/", None::<&str>,
    MsFlags::MS_PRIVATE | MsFlags::MS_REC, None::<&str>)?;
```

Alternative: `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` first then operate in private namespace. But that affects subsequent jailer behavior — needs careful sequencing with FC jailer's own namespace ops. MS_PRIVATE on `/` is the standard pattern and simpler.

## Tests

`crates/m80-jailer/tests/mount_propagation.rs` (NEW) — verify after `Plan::materialize`, host `/proc/self/mountinfo` shows m80's binds as propagation=private (no shared peer group ID).

## Smoke evidence: yes (mount + propagation, AGENTS.md rule).

## Effort: ~3h
close_reason: Privileged smoke passed: sudo env PATH=... CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/m80-root-target cargo test -p m80-jailer --test integration_root materialize_creates_jail_root_and_persists_plan -- --ignored --nocapture. This exercises Plan::materialize and asserts the materialized bind mount is private after MS_PRIVATE|MS_REC.

comments.author: nathan
comments.text: Implementation landed locally: Plan::materialize now marks / recursively private with MS_PRIVATE|MS_REC immediately before the first PlanStep::Bind, exposes typed JailerError::MountPropagationFailed, and pins the flag set plus ignored mountinfo assertion in integration_root. README and jailer behavior docs updated. Verification run: cargo test -p m80-jailer; cargo check -p m80-firecracker --tests; git diff --check. Not closing yet because required ignored root smoke was attempted and failed on this host with Operation not permitted while materializing the jail root, before the mount-propagation assertion could execute.

title: HIGH: TOCTOU on rootfs verify→open (hold fd across the gap)
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (preflight bypass via artifact swap)

## Finding (agent 13 F1)

`crates/m80-preflight/src/artifacts.rs:163` opens rootfs, hashes it, closes the fd. Path string stored in `ArtifactPreflight::rootfs`. At phase_3 (`crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:120-126`), `Rootfs::prepare`/`clone_template` reopens by path for `cp --reflink=auto`. **Verified content and operated-on content can differ** — attacker with artifact-dir write swaps rootfs between verify and use.

Default artifact dir `/opt/m80/artifacts/`, mode 0644 (per agent 8 F6). Exploitability scales with directory permissions.

## Fix

1. **Hold the fd**: in preflight, open with `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW`, hash, KEEP the fd in `ArtifactPreflight` (don't close).
2. Pass fd through `Rootfs::prepare` (not path); use `/proc/self/fd/<n>` as `cp` source.
3. Bind-mount step (phase_4) also uses `/proc/self/fd/<n>` source.
4. Artifact dir permission preflight: warn or fail if `/opt/m80/artifacts/` is group/world-writable (agent 8 F6 fold).

## Tests

`crates/m80-preflight/tests/toctoc_protection.rs` (NEW) — preflight passes, then swap the file, then attempt launch; assert the launch operates on the verified content (inode pinned via fd), not the swapped content.

## Smoke evidence: yes (file ops in launch path).

## Effort: ~1d (threading fd through is the work).
close_reason: Implemented rootfs fd pinning was already present; added and ran the missing privileged materialization proof. Verification: sudo env PATH=... CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/m80-root-target cargo test -p m80-jailer --test integration_root materialize_binds_proc_fd_source_without_reopening_original_path -- --ignored --nocapture; cargo test -p m80-jailer proc_fd_bind_sources_are_not_canonicalized; git diff --check. The root-only test swaps the original path after opening and proves materialization reads the held proc-fd source.

comments.author: nathan
comments.text: Implemented rootfs fd pinning locally: preflight opens rootfs O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW, verifies sha256 from the held fd even on cache hits, carries PinnedRootfs in Discovery, launch passes the proc-fd path into storage prep, and jailer materialization preserves proc-fd bind sources instead of canonicalizing them back to pathnames. Added artifact directory/file group-world-writable fail-closed checks, behavior doc, and regressions. Verification run: cargo test -p m80-preflight; cargo test -p m80-jailer proc_fd_bind_sources_are_not_canonicalized; cargo check -p m80-firecracker --tests; git diff --check. Leaving open pending privileged/root materialization smoke for the proc-fd bind path.

title: HIGH: Prune Bounding/Effective/Permitted cap sets in m80-jailer-harden
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (cap surface wider than needed)

## Findings (agent 1)

`crates/m80-jailer-harden/src/lib.rs:259-267` (`apply_process_hardening`):
- Clears Inheritable + Ambient cap sets ✓
- **Does NOT touch Bounding, Effective, Permitted sets** ✗
- Sets `no_new_privs` ✓

Consequence: m80 host process (typically running as root or with `REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES` per `crates/m80-preflight/src/lib.rs:27-33` including CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_KILL, CAP_FOWNER, CAP_CHOWN, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SETUID, CAP_SETGID) exec's into the OFFICIAL FC jailer with those caps in Permitted+Effective. The FC jailer drops them before exec'ing FC itself, but the JAILER ITSELF runs unfiltered during its own execution window. A bug in the FC jailer (or supply-chain compromise of the binary) in the pre-drop window has full host capabilities.

## Fix

Extend `apply_process_hardening`:
1. Drop bounding set for all caps NOT required by the official FC jailer. Documented minimum: `CAP_SYS_CHROOT`, `CAP_MKNOD`, `CAP_SETUID`, `CAP_SETGID`, `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` (for mount). Drop everything else via `prctl(PR_CAPBSET_DROP)` loop.
2. Drop CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_KILL, CAP_FOWNER, CAP_CHOWN, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_RAWIO from Effective+Permitted (the FC jailer doesn't need any of these).
3. Tests: extend `tests/integration_root.rs::wrapper_applies_inherited_hardening_before_exec` to assert CapBnd, CapPrm, CapEff at the wrapper boundary, not just CapInh/CapAmb.
4. Pin the dropped-cap set via unit test (m80-lovpn.1 discipline — bitset test against future audit-sweep regression).

## Smoke evidence: yes (capability changes).

## Effort: ~6h
close_reason: Privileged smoke passed: sudo env PATH=... CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/m80-root-target cargo test -p m80-jailer-harden --test integration_root wrapper_applies_inherited_hardening_before_exec -- --ignored --nocapture. The test asserts NoNewPrivs, empty inheritable/ambient caps, and bounded/permitted/effective cap pruning at the wrapper boundary.

comments.author: nathan
comments.text: Implementation landed locally: m80-jailer-harden now prunes the bounding set to the official jailer minimum and prunes effective/permitted caps to the same allowlist before no_new_privs; preflight now requires CAP_SETUID, CAP_SETGID, and CAP_SETPCAP for non-root capability-bearing launch, with README/behavior docs updated. Verification run: cargo test -p m80-jailer-harden; cargo check -p m80-jailer-harden --tests; cargo test -p m80-preflight; git diff --check. Not closing yet because required ignored root smoke was attempted and failed on this host at setgroups([]): EPERM due missing root/CAP_SETGID privilege before the new CapBnd/CapPrm/CapEff assertions could execute.

title: HIGH: Cgroup gaps — memory.swap.max + io.weight + RLIMIT_NPROC
description:
**Severity: HIGH** (guest-induced host DoS)

## Findings

A. **`memory.swap.max` not set** (agent 5 F1) — guest can thrash host swap. `crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:122-124`, `Limits::preset()` at 222.
B. **`io.max`/`io.weight` not in default preset** (agent 5 F2) — io controller never activated; guest saturates host disk I/O.
C. **`RLIMIT_NPROC = None`** (agent 13 #1) — `crates/m80-jailer/src/types.rs:85`. Cgroup pids.max=128 is the primary guard but RLIMIT_NPROC is the per-UID defense-in-depth that's missing.

## Fix

1. `Limits::preset()` — add `memory_swap_max: Some(0)` (no swap allowed) AND `io_weight: Some(100)` (activates io controller for fair-share). For hard IOPS caps, expose `io_max: Vec<IoDevice>` for operator configuration.
2. `apply_limits` — write `memory.swap.max` if set; activate `io` controller in subtree_control when io_weight or io_max set.
3. `ResourceLimits::default()` — set `nproc: Some(256)` (covers FC threads + guestd + spawned execs comfortably; bounds runaway).

## Tests

`crates/m80-cgroup/tests/quota_enforcement.rs` (NEW) — verify each limit file is written with expected value; integration test verifying a memory-thrash workload is OOM-killed within the cgroup (not pushed to host swap).

## Smoke evidence: yes (cgroup writes, kernel-touching).

## Effort: ~6h
close_reason: Cgroup portions implemented and privileged smoke now passes: sudo env PATH=... CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/m80-root-target cargo test -p m80-cgroup --test integration_root cgroup_pids_max_enforced_against_fork_bomb -- --ignored --nocapture. RLIMIT_NPROC default is intentionally not set: docs/behaviors/jailer/privilege-drop.md and crates/m80-jailer/src/types.rs::tests::default_resource_limits_do_not_set_host_wide_nproc pin the design decision because Linux enforces nproc per real uid across the host and docs/perf/cold-launch.md records nproc=256 causing EAGAIN under same-UID loaded-host stress.

comments.author: nathan
comments.text: Partial implementation landed locally: m80-cgroup Limits now include memory_swap_max, Limits::preset() sets memory.swap.max=0 and io.weight=100, apply_limits writes memory.swap.max and explicit io.weight, and cgroup README/behavior docs were updated. Verification run: cargo test -p m80-cgroup; cargo check -p m80-firecracker --tests; cargo check -p m80-jailer --tests; git diff --check. Real cgroup probe passed, but cgroup_pids_max_enforced_against_fork_bomb smoke failed on this host at write /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control: Permission denied. Leaving open: RLIMIT_NPROC default remains unset because docs/perf/cold-launch.md records nproc=256 causing EAGAIN under same-UID stress; needs an explicit design decision or a different enforcement point.

title: Guest capability routing architecture
description:
Intent: capture the escape hatch for operations that should not be forced through plain exec when a specialized m80-backed VM/profile can provide a faster or cleaner guest capability. This is an architecture/planning umbrella only; add concrete task leaves later after the active wire and file-transfer work settles.

Boundary: m80 owns VM mechanics, profile/image capability discovery, transport, diagnostics, and cleanup evidence. Adapters own product semantics, authority, idempotency, tool names, and user-facing policy.

Why now: adapter-style workloads will route by memory, CPU, latency, capability availability, and mutating authority. Capability-aware routing is the same class of decision, but it must not turn m80 core into an agent runtime.

title: Per-VM resource limits via setrlimit (RLIMIT_NOFILE, optional RLIMIT_FSIZE)
description:
FC's stock jailer sets RLIMIT_NOFILE to 2048 and optionally RLIMIT_FSIZE before exec. m80 does not set any resource limits, so the Firecracker process inherits whatever limits the calling process (the m80 orchestrator) has. Without explicit limits, a compromised or buggy Firecracker process could exhaust file descriptors or write arbitrarily large files.

## Scope (this epic only)
NOFILE + optional FSIZE only. The other RLIMIT_* values (NPROC, MEMLOCK, AS, CORE, STACK) are tracked separately by m80-3xwa.3 C4 to keep this epic narrow and quick to land.

- Add optional ResourceLimits to JailerConfig:
  - no_file: u64 (default 2048)
  - fsize: Option<u64> (optional max file size in bytes)
- Apply via setrlimit before launching Firecracker.
- Persist limits in jailer-plan.json for reproducibility.
- Validation: error if calling process's hard limit is below the requested soft limit (FC does this — env.rs around the resource_limits.rs call site).

## Cross-references
- **m80-3xwa.3 C4** extends to NPROC/MEMLOCK/AS/CORE/STACK in the same call site. Coordinate so both PRs touch the same setrlimit module without conflict; recommend landing this one first as the foundation, then C4 as the extension.

## Child tasks
1. IMPL: ResourceLimits in JailerConfig and plan schema. Defaults match FC jailer. Serde round-trip in plan JSON.
2. IMPL: setrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE, ...) and optionally setrlimit(RLIMIT_FSIZE, ...) before FC exec. Error if calling process's hard limit is below requested soft limit.
3. TEST: jailed process sees configured limits via /proc/self/limits; default limits applied when config omits the field. Specific assertion: read /proc/<fc-pid>/limits, confirm "Max open files" line shows 2048 (or configured value).

## Acceptance
- Launched FC has RLIMIT_NOFILE capped at 2048 (or configured value).
- Explicit fsize limit is enforced.
- Validation rejects soft > hard with a typed error before exec.
- Existing smoke and bench pass unchanged.
- Integration test reads /proc/self/limits inside the jail and asserts each field.

## Audit-confirmed code references
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/resource_limits.rs (full file)
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:654 — install() call site

- 12-agent audit Lens 3 (cgroup + rlimit), 2026-05-07.

title: request_id end-to-end: CLI → host events → guest stderr → diagnostics.jsonl
description:
A single opaque request_id assigned at the CLI invocation flows through every layer. Without it, host events, guest stderr, PTY/streaming frames, warm-owner logs, and diagnostics cannot be aligned for any non-trivial debug session.

## Scope

- m80-cli generates a request_id (UUIDv7 or ULID for ordering) at command entry; binary edge.
- m80-firecracker accepts a request_id parameter at orchestration entry points (launch, exec, streaming exec, PTY exec, stop, delete, warm lease/release) and threads it into:
  - tracing spans
  - diagnostics.jsonl every event
  - console/log lines where available
  - the wire frame(s) to m80-guestd
- m80-guestd includes request_id in structured stderr and echoes it in responses/terminal frames.
- Streaming stdout/stderr and PTY terminal/control frames share the same request_id for the run.
- Warm-owner status/logs include the request_id for lease attempts and failed warm runs.
- CLI prints the request_id on wrapper error and exposes it in JSON envelopes.

## Acceptance

- A failed launch or failed run can be reconstructed from a single request_id grep across <run_dir>/diagnostics.jsonl + <run_dir>/console.log + CLI stderr/JSON.
- A streaming or PTY run has one request_id across all frames and final exit metadata.
- A warm-unavailable or PoolEmpty failure shows the same request_id in CLI output and warm-owner diagnostics.
- Tests deliberately fail a launch/run and confirm request_id appearance in host events, guest console, and response/error payload.

## Coordinates with

- m80-1f8.5 (guest-side log surface) — guestd needs the request_id available to stamp lines.
- m80-1f8.1 (diagnostics event log) — schema includes request_id.
- m80-bpuf (JSON envelope) — request_id appears in the envelope alongside version.

KVM guest-console confirmation remains covered by existing ignored e2e lanes plus guestd request-id unit coverage; not run locally.

title: vm_id has NO charset/traversal validation — silent path-traversal via admission
description:
**Finding:** vm_id flows directly into filesystem paths as a path component with NO charset, null-byte, dot-dot, or slash validation. Only gate is the path-budget arithmetic check at backend.rs:182 (AF_UNIX 107-byte limit). A caller passing vm_id = '../../../etc/evil' that fits the budget produces run_root.join('../../../etc/evil') — directory created at an arbitrary host path. vm_id = 'foo/bar' pushes the jail two levels deep, misaligning jailer --id extraction.

Call chain:
- run_dir_path → run_root.join(vm_id) — crates/m80-firecracker/src/layout.rs:31-32
- Subtree::leaf_path → /sys/fs/cgroup/m80-firecracker/<vm_id> — crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:148
- cmd_inspect / cmd_logs — crates/m80-cli/src/cmds_walk.rs:62

TAP name is immune (SHA-256-derived). Cgroup name happens to be safe (path-budget firing first).

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:182 (check_vm_id_path_budget — natural home for additional charset check).

**Severity:** HIGH (caller-controlled, undocumented surface; one of the few real internal-API holes).

**Acceptance:**
- In check_vm_id_path_budget: reject vm_id containing '/', '\\', '\0', or any component equal to '..' / '.' / empty.
- Strict allowlist preferred: regex `^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$` with non-empty constraint.
- Typed FcError::InvalidVmId variant.
- Test pins for each rejected pattern.

title: Scratch::recommended_size_for_workspace: no upper bound — 400 GiB workspace = 400 GiB ext4
description:
**Finding:** scratch.rs:38-42 computes max(64 MiB, used_bytes + 32 MiB). MIN floor exists; NO max cap. A workspace dir with 400 GiB of files requests a 400 GiB+ sparse image and mkfs.ext4 runs on it. Caller-provided trust required, but operationally undocumented in m80-storage README.

**File:** crates/m80-storage/src/scratch.rs:38-42 (recommended_size_for_workspace).

**Severity:** LOW (caller-bounded by m80 doctrine; documentation gap).

- Cross-link adapter-boundary.md.

title: idle_timeout = Some(Duration::ZERO) busy-loops the watcher thread
description:
**Finding:** lifecycle.rs:498 computes poll_interval = min(timeout/4, 30s). Duration::ZERO / 4 = Duration::ZERO. The watcher thread then calls std::thread::sleep(Duration::ZERO) in a tight loop — effectively a hot spinloop — until the idle deadline fires (immediately, since idle_ns >= 0). Caller-supplied Some(Duration::ZERO) burns a CPU while immediately requesting shutdown. Default is Some(5min) so this only surfaces from explicit caller config.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:498.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (CPU burn; only on caller-supplied zero).

**Acceptance:**
- At SandboxConfig construction (or warm_pool admission): reject idle_timeout < Duration::from_millis(100) with typed ConfigError::InvalidValue.
- Or: floor the poll_interval at e.g. 100ms inside the watcher.
- Test pin: Some(Duration::ZERO) → typed error from Backend::admit.

title: Jailer plan/state + net-outbound BridgeState: schema_version never checked on read
description:

title: guestd connection.rs pid_slot.lock().expect() panics guestd on lock poisoning
description:
site: crates/m80-guestd/src/connection.rs:461 (and similar in cancel handler path)
finder: trim-the-fat r5

Problem: If the exec thread panics while holding the pid_slot Mutex (e.g., a panic during `*guard = Some(child.id())`), the Mutex becomes poisoned. The cancel handler calls `.lock().expect("pid_slot poisoned")` which propagates the panic and CRASHES guestd entirely. Since guestd is PID 1 in Minimal images, this kernel-panics the VM via panic=-1.

Fix: replace `.expect("pid_slot poisoned")` with `.unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` matching the m80-fcc Mutex-poisoning pattern. Document why poisoned recovery is safe (the pid is just a u32; no invariant that requires drop-on-poison).
notes: Implemented poison recovery for the in-flight exec pid slot. code=crates/m80-guestd/src/connection.rs lock_pid_slot() uses poisoned.into_inner(); cancel lookup, wait-then-kill, pid publish, and pid clear no longer panic on Mutex poisoning. docs=crates/m80-guestd/README.md cancel section. tests=connection::tests::{pid_slot_poisoning_is_recovered_for_cancel_lookup,pid_slot_poisoning_is_recovered_for_wait_then_kill}. Verification: cargo test -p m80-guestd; cargo clippy -p m80-guestd --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check.

title: Wave 34 of 35: tracing/logger target taxonomy + observability hygiene
description:
**Wave 34 of 35.** Audit angle: tracing/logger target taxonomy. 10 parallel sonnets each take a distinct lens:

1. **target= grep**: enumerate every `tracing::*!(target = "...", ...)` site; classify into taxonomy; report inconsistencies (PascalCase vs snake_case vs crate::module dotted).
2. **No-target sites**: enumerate `tracing::*!` macros with NO explicit target; show which crate inherits module-path defaults; flag where filtering breaks.
3. **EnvFilter directives**: search RUST_LOG examples in READMEs/scripts; do the targets they cite actually exist in code? Stale doc check.
4. **Span vs event leakage**: events outside spans that should be inside (e.g., per-attempt logs not nested under a per-VM span); spans whose fields don't propagate.
5. **Level discipline**: error! used for non-errors; warn! for expected fallbacks; debug! for things that should be info!. Audit ~10 sample sites per crate.
6. **PII / secret leakage**: payloads, env vars, paths-with-uid, kernel cmdline, /proc contents logged at any level; should be redacted or moved to debug only.
7. **Bench/measurement instrumentation**: M80_PHASE traces — schema drift between emit sites and bench-summary.py parser.
8. **stderr vs tracing**: anyhow eprintln! / println! in library crates that should be tracing; binary-edge use OK.
9. **Test output discipline**: tracing-subscriber init in tests — duplicate init, missing init, test_writer vs ENV gating.
10. **Crate-public log API**: any tracing wrapper modules exposing log macros outward (anti-pattern); any consumer-visible target conventions that should be doc'd.

Saturation marker: ~5+ NULL findings → angle exhausted. File concrete bead per HIGH/MEDIUM finding with file:line and proposed fix size.

title: m80-guestd: PID-1 mounts /dev/shm and /dev/pts as tmpfs/devpts
description:
m80-guestd's PID-1 init mounts /proc, /sys, /dev (and overlay/workspace) but NOT /dev/shm as tmpfs and NOT /dev/pts (devpts). Workloads using POSIX shared memory or spawning their own ptys silently fail.

## Affected workload patterns
- Python multiprocessing (Pool, Manager, Queue) — uses POSIX semaphores in /dev/shm
- pytest-xdist parallel workers — same
- mmap(MAP_SHARED, ...) against shm_open()
- Workloads that spawn interactive subprocesses with their own pty (terminal embeds)

## Failure mode (today, without the mounts)
Cryptic errors like:
- `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/dev/shm/SemLock-XXXX'`
- `posix.openpty()` returns EACCES or fails on /dev/ptmx

## Site
- crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs (mount_pseudo_filesystems or equivalent — the existing /proc, /sys, /dev mount sequence)

## Scope
- Mount /dev/shm as tmpfs with mode=1777, nodev, nosuid, noexec.
- Mount /dev/pts as devpts with gid=5, mode=620, nodev, nosuid, noexec.
- ptmx symlink fixup: ensure /dev/ptmx points to /dev/pts/ptmx (smolvm pattern; check if m80 already has this in image-build).

## Acceptance
- /dev/shm exists, mounted, writable as tmpfs after PID-1 init.
- /dev/pts works for pty allocation.
- Python multiprocessing.Pool() works inside an m80 guest (smoke test or unit test).
- Existing smoke tests pass.

## Audit reference
20-agent deep audit Lens K1 (kata PID-1 init), 2026-05-07. kata mount.rs:56-62 INIT_ROOTFS_MOUNTS includes /dev/shm and /dev/pts in the mandatory mount set with the flags above.

Source: /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/agent/src/mount.rs:56-62.

title: Privilege preflight
description:
Contract: m80-preflight verifies that the process has effective privilege to invoke host-privileged operations — either euid==0 OR the effective Linux capability set contains the required caps (CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_MKNOD, CAP_CHOWN, CAP_FOWNER, CAP_KILL). If neither, startup is refused with a typed error and an actionable hint.
Surface: m80-preflight (capability detection types + check function); the rest of the workspace uses Command::new directly.
Evidence: m80/docs/behaviors/preflight/privilege.md + m80/crates/m80-preflight/src/lib.rs::tests::*.

title: API ergonomics audit: m80 surface from consumer perspective
description:
**Status:** planned, not yet executed.

**Angle:** Read m80 from the perspective of its driving consumer (torpor2 at /tank/projects/torpor2 — see MEMORY.md `project_driving_consumer`). Where would a careful consumer still get it wrong? Where do error types preserve too little info? Where are builder ergonomics missing? Where does the surface drift from docs?

**Why this angle:** m80's adapter boundary (docs/adapter-boundary.md) defines what stays in m80 vs what belongs in the consumer. The boundary is correct only if m80's public surface exposes the right primitives ergonomically. This audit reads the surface as a consumer.

**Expected lens shapes (~8-10 agents):**
- One agent per consumer-facing crate: m80-firecracker, m80-cli, m80-proto, m80-vsock, m80-snapshot, m80-image-manifest, m80-storage
- One agent on the README + docs surface: do they match the code, do they cover what a consumer needs to know?
- One agent on error types: does FcError preserve enough context for the consumer to make a recovery decision? Or do important details collapse into `Other(String)`?
- One agent on builder patterns: SandboxConfig has many fields; is the build path ergonomic? Are required vs optional fields clear?
- One agent on type ergonomics: are sandbox-vs-process identifiers (vm_id, request_id, run_dir) distinguishable in the type system or do consumers get string-stringly-typed APIs?

**Each agent investigates by:** reading the README first, then trying to construct a working invocation from docs alone, noting every gap or surprise. Then reading the actual code to confirm or contradict the doc claim.

**Findings format:** each gap becomes a child bead. Three categories: (a) doc-only fix; (b) surface change (rename, restructure); (c) new feature to make a common case ergonomic.

**Cross-link:** torpor2 issues / its m80 integration code (read-only, sibling repo) — what hacks did the consumer have to do that should have been m80-provided primitives?

description:
Wave 37/45. 10 sonnets on serialization invariants.

title: Add schema_version probe to m80-net-outbound state + m80-jailer Plan/JailerState reads

m80-net-outbound:
- state.rs:292 read_json_state — BridgeState + VmNetworkStateRecord — typed deserialize with no SchemaVersionProbe. Future schema bump surfaces as InvalidNetworkState { detail: "unknown field" } instead of UnsupportedSchemaVersion.

m80-jailer:

- Hoist literal versions to pub(crate) const JAILER_PLAN_SCHEMA_VERSION + JAILER_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION + NETWORK_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION (already exists).

title: Enforce LoadSnapshotConfig invariant: exactly one of mem_backend or mem_file_path must be Some
description:
**Finding (W37.4):** m80-firecracker-client::LoadSnapshotConfig doc says "exactly one of mem_backend or mem_file_path must be present" — both are Option<T> with no m80-side validation. Caller can construct with both None; Firecracker rejects at runtime over HTTP. The invariant is in prose, not in types.

Severity: LOW.

Acceptance:
- Encode the invariant in the type: enum MemSource { Backend(MemBackend), File(PathBuf) } as a single required field.
- OR: add LoadSnapshotConfig::validate() called at REST-PUT time that returns a typed error.

- Add a test that constructs both-None and both-Some and asserts validation error.
- Cross-link m80-emon8.6 (mem_file_path deprecation drift).

title: serde enum tag-name inconsistency: warm/control uses 'type', diagnostics uses 'status'/'reason'
description:
**Finding (W37.6):** Three tag-name conventions for internally-tagged enums:
- "kind" (majority): m80-cgroup CpuMax, m80-jailer PlanStep, m80-net-mode NetworkPolicy.
- "type": m80-cli warm/control.rs:17,39,57 — WarmControlRequest, WarmControlResponse, WarmStreamFrame. Wire protocol surface (pub(super) for now, but observable on warm-pool channel).
- "status": m80-observability diagnostics.rs:184 PhaseOutcome.
- "reason": m80-observability diagnostics.rs:199 ExitReason.

No untagged enums anywhere (NULL on collision risk).

Severity: LOW (semantic; both "status"/"reason" are defensible self-describing tags; "type" is the sharpest deviation).

Acceptance:

title: Attack the 785ms phase_12b_ready_accept (kernel-boot bottleneck)
description:
phase_12b_ready_accept (kernel boot + guestd ready) is 785 ms P50 on minimal stripped idle (N=30) — the dominant cost in cold launch (1117 ms total). Guest PID-1 milestones proved guestd userspace only consumes ~55 ms; the other ~730 ms is kernel/early boot. Firecracker advertises ~125 ms kernel boot — the ~660 ms gap suggests significant room for improvement in the kernel config or boot path.

Already-shipped optimizations (m80-f2zc storage pivot, m80-ci9i stripped kernel, manifest verify relocation, graceful-stop migration, overlay template/reflink, guest milestones) collectively saved ~778 ms but did not attack ready_accept itself.

## Audit-validated context (from 20-agent deep audit, 2026-05-07)
- **smolvm/libkrun has no easy lever on this axis.** smolvm uses libkrunfw with an embedded kernel, but the boot-time savings come from a different shape (libkrun's lighter VMM, no virtio-mmio init for unused devices). Adopting libkrun would require swapping the entire VMM (out of scope per CLAUDE.md scope boundary). The Firecracker kernel-boot path is the right target.
- **No DAX trick available**: smolvm's virtio-fs DAX mappings are not on Firecracker's roadmap; m80's overlayfs + virtio-blk path can't borrow this optimization.
- Confirms that the four sub-investigations below are the actual surface to attack.

## Scope — four parallel investigations

The four investigations below are **independent** and can run in parallel sonnet lanes (each is its own perf measurement + recommendation).

### 1. cpu_template C3/T2 evaluation
Firecracker supports C3 and T2 templates that pre-filter CPUID emulation. Less KVM CPUID emulation work and potentially fewer guest kernel subsystem initializations. Currently not set. Measure boot-time delta with each template.

### 2. RAM reduction (1024 → 128 MiB)
Firecracker itself uses ~128 MiB. Current allocation is 1024 MiB. Kernel memory init (page tables, buddy allocator, per-CPU data) scales with RAM size. Set at VM creation time, cannot hot-add later. Measure boot-time delta at 256, 192, 128 MiB.

### 3. Deeper kernel stripping with initcall_debug
The current stripped kernel only saved ~100 ms vs stock — keep-list may still be too generous. initcall_debug + printk timestamps in a one-off boot identify which subsystems consume the 785 ms. Use those traces to guide a second pass at CONFIG removals.

### 4. KVM setup overhead measurement
Part of the 785 ms may be Firecracker's KVM setup (memslots, IRQ chip, etc.), not purely guest kernel. Compare wallclock-to-ready against the kernel's own boot timestamp (printk %.6f) to split the budget.

## Acceptance
- Each of the 4 investigations produces a measured number and a recommendation.
- At least one of (1)(2)(3) yields ≥100 ms P50 saving on minimal/stripped/idle without regressing reliability.
- Investigation (4) clarifies the kernel-boot vs KVM-setup attribution so future budgets are accurate.
- Findings landed in docs/perf/cold-launch.md as a "ready_accept attack" section with per-investigation deltas + final recommended config.

## Out of scope
- Snapshot/restore tuning (already shipped via m80-rrp.3).
- Warm-pool allocation tuning (separate concern).
- Ubuntu-image boot path (dominated by systemd; not the agent path).
- VMM swap to libkrun or alternative (out of scope per CLAUDE.md; m80 is Firecracker-targeted).

Source: /tmp/m80-hermes-notes.md "Remaining Bottleneck" + "Undiscovered / Unexplored Optimizations". 20-agent deep audit Lens 3 (smolvm perf/launch) confirms no Firecracker-applicable lever exists outside the four investigations above.

title: Copy Firecracker binary into jail instead of bind-mounting (covert-channel hardening)
description:
FC's stock jailer deliberately *copies* the Firecracker binary into the chroot rather than hard-linking or bind-mounting. This prevents two FC processes from sharing the same .text pages in memory — in FC's threat model shared memory pages could be a covert channel between VMs. m80 bind-mounts the FC binary today, so all VMs on the same host share .text pages.

Minor hardening gap — the risk is low but the fix is straightforward.

## Scope
- Replace bind-mount of firecracker_bin with a file copy.
- Verify the copy is not a hard link (check nlink() == 1).
- chown the copy to jailed UID/GID.
- Set permissions matching source file mode.

## Performance considerations (from 12-agent audit)
FC uses plain std::io::copy. For a ~30 MB binary, expected impact is <5 ms P50. If profiling shows significant impact:
- **reflink** via std::fs::copy() on filesystems that support it (XFS, btrfs, recent ext4 with --reflink). Reflink avoids the disk write but creates a separate inode (still satisfies nlink == 1 since it's a fresh entry).
- **copy_file_range(2)** syscall as a kernel-side optimization for in-kernel copy without userspace round-trip.

Note: reflink/copy_file_range still produce nlink == 1 destinations (different from hard linking), so the covert-channel mitigation is preserved. Hard-link via std::fs::hard_link is the wrong tool — explicitly excluded.

## Child tasks
1. IMPL: copy step in materializer (new plan step or modify existing bind step). Copy via std::io::copy with O_NOFOLLOW on destination. Verify nlink == 1 after copy.
2. BENCH: launch-time impact of copy vs bind-mount. Target: <5 ms P50 regression vs bind-mount on a ~30 MB binary. If exceeded, evaluate reflink/copy_file_range fallback.
3. TEST/DOCS: in-jail binary is a separate inode from host binary; permissions and ownership correct.

## Acceptance
- FC binary inside jail is a separate file (different inode) from host binary (verifiable via stat + comparison).
- nlink() on the in-jail copy is exactly 1.
- Launch-time regression <5 ms P50 vs bind-mount on a ~30 MB binary; documented in cold-launch.md if measured.
- Permissions match source file mode; ownership is jailed UID/GID.

## Audit-confirmed code references
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:468-518 — copy_exec_to_chroot()
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:493 — O_NOFOLLOW on destination open
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:500 — nlink check

## Sources
- /tmp/m80-proposed-epic-beads.md Epic 5.
- 12-agent audit Lens 1 (FC mount/FS isolation), 2026-05-07.

Added root and real-KVM assertions that /proc/<pid>/root/firecracker has different dev/ino from the host binary, nlink == 1, jail uid/gid ownership, and owner-only 0700 mode under m80-jailer-harden umask 0077. No launch-path code changed, so there is no new bind-to-copy launch-time regression to measure. docs=docs/behaviors/jailer/asset-binding.md,docs/behaviors/jailer/security-parity.md; tests=crates/m80-jailer/tests/integration_root.rs::launch_with_new_pid_ns_records_sentinel_and_firecracker_is_pid_one,crates/m80-firecracker/tests/end_to_end_real_kvm.rs::end_to_end_real_kvm_jailer_security_parity; verification=cargo test -p m80-jailer -p m80-firecracker --tests; cargo clippy -p m80-jailer -p m80-firecracker --all-targets -- -D warnings; sudo root jailer test; sudo real-KVM jailer security parity test; git diff --check

title: Quick wins in phase_12b_ready_probe — 10ms poll, 60s timeout
description:
Cheap parity backstop independent of m80-7tpy: tighten the existing
CONNECT/OK polling loop in `phase_12b_ready_probe`. Lands risk-free.

## Today

- READY_POLL_INTERVAL: 500 ms
- READY_TIMEOUT: 30 s

## Proposed (revised after smolvm recon)

- READY_POLL_INTERVAL: **10 ms** (was 100 ms in the original bead).
  Smolvm polls at 10 ms (`smolvm/src/process.rs:22` and
  `smolvm/src/agent/manager.rs:1457` per recon doc 03). Each
  `Channel::open_uds_only` attempt costs ~10 ms on success and the
  5 s read timeout caps failed attempts, so even 10 ms intervals leave
  room.
- READY_TIMEOUT: 60 s (matches smolvm's tolerance for slow hosts).

## Why 10 ms is safe

Each `Channel::open_uds_only` attempt does:
1. `UnixStream::connect` to vsock.sock (microseconds when guestd not up;
   succeeds + completes handshake quickly when it is)
2. Read banner / OK with 5 s read timeout

Failed attempts return immediately (ECONNREFUSED on connect, or fall
through to error after the muxer rejects). Successful attempts return
in ~10 ms. So 10 ms polling adds at worst 1 wasted RTT per probe,
which is fine.

## Relationship to m80-7tpy

m80-7tpy supersedes the polling design entirely with `accept()`-based
event-driven readiness. m80-bgas is the BACKSTOP: it lands cheaply
today, gives us most of the win until m80-7tpy lands, and stays as a
fallback path if m80-7tpy ever needs to be disabled.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Constants updated in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:50-53`.
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry under v0.1.x or v0.2.0.
- [ ] `scripts/smoke.sh` retry loop dropped from 3 attempts to 1.
- [ ] No flake on smoke.sh after the change (verify on idle host).
notes: post-2026-05-04 m80-7tpy: the polled CONNECT/OK probe this bead tuned has been removed entirely. Inverted readiness (event-driven accept) replaced it. The 10ms cadence and 60s timeout are no longer active in code; this bead's optimizations are historical.

title: Format-versioned JSON output envelope for all m80 commands (cross-cutting)
description:
Every m80 command that emits structured output (--json, machine-readable formats) wraps payload in a versioned envelope: {"version": 1, "data": ...}. Free if designed in from the start; expensive to retrofit later.

## Reference

kata-exploration/10-dx-docs-config.md. kata-ctl env emits a format-versioned envelope; consumers can branch on version for schema migrations.

## Why

Consumers (scripts, monitoring agents, m80-adapter) need to detect schema changes. Without a version field, schema migration breaks silently. With one, consumers refuse-or-adapt explicitly.

## Scope

- Define a shared envelope type (probably in m80-cli, possibly in a foundation crate if multiple binaries emit JSON).
- All m80 --json output uses the envelope.
- Document the contract: integer version, monotonically increasing, breaking changes bump it.
- Audit existing --json output points (m80 list, m80 inspect, m80 config show) and migrate.

## Out of scope

- Human-readable output formatting.
- Backwards-compat shims for un-envelope'd output (this lands before any external consumer exists).

## Acceptance

- Every existing --json command emits an enveloped document.
- The new m80 env --json bead (m80-81rw) starts on this from day one.
- README documents the envelope contract.

## Coordinates with

- m80-6jni epic (DX v0.2) — the README mention belongs there.

title: stress-ng loaded: 0% launch success under full CPU saturation
description:
## Symptom
Under stress-ng-induced full CPU saturation on the host, all m80 launches fail. Idle launches succeed at 100 % at N=20; under stress-ng saturation the success rate drops to 0 %.

## Suspected location
Failure is downstream of phase_3 (storage prep) and is likely vsock/ready_probe contention. The warm-pool P95 also spikes to 623 ms under CPU saturation (vs 21 ms idle) due to restored-vsock retry delays — same family of contention but a less severe expression.

## Why this matters
Hermes notes flag this as "fix before GA". It is a release-gating reliability defect for any deployment that could see noisy-neighbor or burst CPU pressure. The multi-tenant pool architecture (m80-iswt) cannot be claimed reliable until this is closed.

## Investigation directions
- Add diagnostic timing to ready_probe / vsock connect path so saturation behavior is visible.
- Compare saturation behavior of cold-boot vs snapshot-restore vs warm-pool allocation (snapshot/warm may bypass the contended path).
- Check whether ready_accept timeout budgets shrink effectively under saturation (proportional vs fixed).
- Check whether host-side vsock muxer accept loop loses to higher-priority threads under saturation.

## Acceptance
- A repro script that reliably triggers the failure under stress-ng -c \$(nproc).
- A diagnosis identifying the contended resource (vsock muxer? ready_probe budget? cgroup CPU shares? scheduler class?).
- A fix bringing success rate to ≥80 % under CPU saturation, with documented residual failure modes.

## Out of scope
- Memory-pressure or disk-saturation reliability (separate investigations if needed).

title: phase_restore_snapshot_prime runs AFTER phase 9; ~20ms readahead window before mem.snap read
description:
**Finding:** prime_snapshot_files (launch.rs:588-595, launch/snapshot_prime.rs:8-29) issues posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED) on vm.snap + mem.snap. Current placement: AFTER phase 9 (jailer exec) and BEFORE phase_restore_load. Only ~15-30ms window between prime and the actual PUT /snapshot/load — insufficient for the kernel to fault in any meaningful fraction of mem.snap on a cold cache.

Moving the fadvise call earlier (before phase 9, or even before phase 3 storage prep) gives readahead more lead time while serialized host-side work completes. Zero risk — fadvise is non-destructive, file is opened read-only.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:588-595 (call site); crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/snapshot_prime.rs:8-29 (impl).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (warm-cache: ~0 impact; cold-cache: potentially 30-100ms recovery).

**Acceptance:**
- Move prime_snapshot_files call to before phase 9 (after path validation but before jailer launch).
- Measure cold-cache restore P50 before/after; target ~30-50ms recovery on m80-rrp.3.6 P50.
- Cross-link m80-kv4ri.12 (mem.snap sparsity) and m80-jp6ik (perf epic).

title: RESTORE_PROBE_SLEEP fixed 50ms wastes up to 40ms on first-attempt failure
description:
**Finding:** launch.rs:431-432 + :757 — RESTORE_PROBE_SLEEP=50ms fixed between probe attempts. The probe loop races against FC's VIRTIO_VSOCK_EVENT_TRANSPORT_RESET processing after resume. If transport reset settles in 10ms (warm case), first probe attempt fails, code sleeps 50ms, then second attempt succeeds — wasting ~40ms.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:431-432 (constant); :757 (sleep call).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (warm-restore latency tax).

**Acceptance:**
- Replace fixed 50ms sleep with exponential backoff starting at 5ms, doubling, capped at 50ms.
- 5s overall RESTORE_PROBE_TIMEOUT cap unchanged.
- The FcError::Vsock arm already handles arbitrary transient failures; safe.
- Bench warm restore P50 before/after; target ~30-45ms recovery.

title: phase_5b_cgroup_create has 2.2× P50→max spread (18.7→41.8ms); P99 variance driver
description:
**Finding:** N=200 baseline (crates/m80-firecracker/benches/baseline.json) shows phase_5b_cgroup_create P50=18.7ms, P99=26.7ms, max=41.8ms — a 2.2× spread. This is the widest variance of any non-boot phase and the primary driver of cold-launch P99 variance. No existing bead targets phase_5b variance specifically.

Likely causes:
- cgroup.subtree_control walk contention if first VM races with concurrent VMs at startup
- write to /sys/fs/cgroup files contended by other system services (systemd-cgroup-agent etc.)
- VFS-level lock contention on the m80-firecracker parent cgroup directory

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:936-956 (phase_5b_cgroup_create); crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:55-109 (Subtree::create).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (perf tail; matters for P99/P999 SLA claims).

**Acceptance:**
- Add per-step phase events inside Subtree::create (subtree_control_check, leaf_create, limits_write, procs_enroll, cgroup_path_write).
- Measure where the 41.8ms max is coming from — likely one specific kernel syscall.
- If kernel-side: document as host-tunable (e.g., advise against running cgroup-busy services concurrently).
- Cross-link m80-jp6ik.32 (cgroup micro-cuts) — current scope is one-time first-VM costs; this is per-VM.

title: Warm-pool restore could pre-allocate run-dir + overlay before launch_from_snapshot
description:
**Finding:** Phase 3 (storage prep — overlay clone, optional scratch) runs on the launch_from_snapshot critical path (launch.rs:481-502, storage_prep.rs:27-50). For restore, the overlay's contents don't matter (guest's dirty pages live in mem.snap; overlay file just needs to exist for jailer's bind plan). On ext4/tmpfs (no reflink), the sparse clone costs 5-20ms warm cache, more cold.

Pool-side opportunity: warm pool pre-allocates per-slot run-dir + overlay before the user request arrives. When launch_from_snapshot is called, phases 1-3 become no-ops (already done), saving ~12-30ms off the restore P50.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:481-502 (phase 3 on restore path); crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs (pool-side pre-allocation candidate).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (warm-pool restore latency).

**Acceptance:**
- WarmPool::ensure_pre_allocated_slot(slot_id) creates run-dir + overlay + LeaseGuard ahead of time.
- launch_from_snapshot accepts an optional 'pre_allocated_run_dir: Option<PathBuf>' arg; if Some, skips phases 1-3.
- Pool-side: triggered on FillGuard arm, before the slot becomes 'ready'.
- Bench warm restore P50; target ~15-25ms reduction.
- Cross-link m80-jp6ik (perf epic), m80-r4308 (warm-pool).

title: Bimodal warm restore distribution (50-58ms cluster vs 67-75ms cluster); unexplained
description:
**Finding:** N=50 warm restore (crates/m80-firecracker/benches/snapshots/cold-restore-N50.json) shows P50=55.3ms with raw sample distribution clustered in TWO modes: roughly half land in 50-58ms, half in 67-75ms. Not explained by any single phase in the breakdown. Could indicate:

- Page-cache cliff (one cluster gets mem.snap from cache, other faults a few pages)

- guestd Tokio runtime startup variance (some restores hit the cold-cache build cost)

title: Density scaling: 'linear' claim true only through C=16; per-VM cost +20% at C=64 + 0.3% failure rate
description:
**Finding:** crates/m80-firecracker/benches/snapshots/density-extended.json (N=20 per step, minimal/stripped/idle, 48-CPU host):
- C=1..16: per-VM P50 flat at 1515-1517ms, zero failures
- C=32: per-VM P50 jumps to 1616ms (+100ms / +6.6%)
- C=48: per-VM P50 1718ms + 3 failures (0.3%)
- C=64: per-VM P50 1818ms (+20% vs C=1) + 2 failures

Scaling is sub-linear (good) but per-VM cost grows AND failures appear above C=32. The concurrent.csv shows fast-fail VMs (~400-600ms exit=1) at C=32+ — likely vm_id path budget or cgroup creation race per m80-9ihnr.1 / m80-cef00.3.

'Scales linearly' claim only holds through C=16. Saturating density on this host: somewhere C=16..C=32.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/benches/snapshots/density-extended.json; crates/m80-firecracker/benches/concurrent.csv.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (m80-ekbk B3 density claim needs root-cause + threshold).

**Acceptance:**
- Investigate the fast-fail signal: read concurrent.csv exit=1 rows; correlate with phase events for those vm_ids.
- Root-cause the per-VM degradation at C=32: cgroup contention? Loop device exhaustion? netlink contention?
- Update m80-ekbk B3 density claim to specify the C ceiling.
- Cross-link m80-9ihnr.1 (vm_id charset → traversal/cgroup leaf issues), m80-cef00.3 (phase_5b variance).

title: Channel::open_uds_only per-exec ~0.5ms tax; no connection reuse across sequential execs
description:
**Finding:** send_envelope_with_open_retry (exec.rs:849) calls Channel::open_uds_only on EVERY exec. No connection pool. Every exec pays: UDS connect + CONNECT/OK handshake RTT + try_clone for buf_reader ≈ 400-800µs on a warm host before the ExecRequest frame even leaves.

For a sandbox running 50 sequential tool calls that's ~25ms of pure handshake tax over the session.

No structural blocker: exec.rs uses &mut self exclusion so concurrent access is impossible and reuse is safe.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs:849 (per-exec open_uds_only).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM (sessionwide consumer perf; per-exec is small but cumulative).

**Acceptance:**
- Cache Option<Channel> in RunningSandbox; reopen only on transient error (existing retry path).
- OversizedPayload unrecoverability contract: drop and reopen.
- Bench: 100 sequential /bin/true execs, compare with-cache vs without-cache.
- Cross-link m80-vpifh.1 (BRIDGE_IO_TIMEOUT exec channel) — same channel; both fixes share the channel lifetime change.

title: docs/diagnostics/failure-modes/: known-failures catalog + ubuntu-idle-flake seed
description:
Stand up a directory of known failure modes. Each entry: the symptom, the misleading hypothesis, the actual root cause, the visible signal that pinpoints it (per CLAUDE.md "visibility cuts across layers; speculation doesn't").

## Why

The ubuntu-idle-flake postmortem (CLAUDE.md "When debugging — diagnostics before hypotheses") cost ~1 hour because the diagnostic visibility was missing. Future incidents will recur in shape if not in cause; a catalog teaches the pattern. Each entry pins one regression test where feasible.

## Scope

- Create docs/diagnostics/failure-modes/README.md (index) + 00-template.md.
- Seed: docs/diagnostics/failure-modes/01-ubuntu-idle-systemd-ordering.md — full incident writeup, the three-line fix in the service unit, link to the regression test if one exists (bead m80-tv7i's test, possibly).
- Each entry has a "Pinpoint signal" section: the one log line, file, or condition that would have surfaced the cause immediately.
- Index ordering: incident-date-asc.

## Out of scope

- Backfilling every prior incident (only ubuntu-idle for the seed; future incidents add entries as they happen).
- A doctest harness verifying every entry is current (overkill for v0.x).

## Acceptance

- docs/diagnostics/failure-modes/{README.md, 00-template.md, 01-ubuntu-idle-systemd-ordering.md} exist.
- Each entry follows the template structure.
- CLAUDE.md's "diagnostics before hypotheses" section links to the catalog.

title: Stripped guest kernel: minimal config + cmdline trim + init-baked
description:
The firecracker-ci stock kernel takes ~890ms to reach userspace on minimal/idle (P50, m80-f2zc.7 baseline). A purpose-built kernel with the smallest config set m80 needs (vsock, virtio-blk, virtio-net, ext4, overlayfs, devtmpfs; everything else off) plus a trimmed cmdline reaches userspace in ~150-300ms typically — saving 500-700ms per cold launch.

Independent of and complementary to: storage pivot (m80-f2zc) which removes ~700ms of rootfs clone, and snapshot/restore (m80-rrp.3) which skips kernel boot entirely for warm-pool launches but still needs a fast cold boot to fill the pool.

PLAN: docs/planning/agent-roadmap.md (full sequencing).

Sub-leaves:
- DESIGN: lock the kernel config delta (CONFIGs to keep, drop, modify), build environment (Docker? chroot? upstream kernel-build container?), kernel version
- IMPL m80-image-build: kernel build pipeline producing kernels/vmlinux-m80-<sha>.bin; manifest gains a kernel.kind discriminator parallel to image_kind
- IMPL m80-firecracker: cmdline trim — quiet loglevel=0 8250.nr_uarts=0, dropped pci=off duplicate, kept reboot=k panic=-1
- BENCH: measure boot-to-guestd-bind delta on minimal/idle and minimal/loaded; target <300ms
- DOCS: manifest schema bump if needed; README delta in m80-image-build

NON-GOALS: kernel security hardening beyond what minimal CONFIG provides; multi-arch (x86_64 only in v0.2); kernel-source vendoring (use upstream linux.tar.xz).

title: DESIGN: kernel config delta + build environment + version
description:
Pin the contract:

1. Kernel version: latest LTS (5.15.x or 6.1.x) or align with firecracker-ci's track. Decide.
2. CONFIG keep list: CONFIG_VSOCKETS, CONFIG_VIRTIO_VSOCKETS, CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK, CONFIG_VIRTIO_NET, CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO, CONFIG_EXT4_FS, CONFIG_OVERLAY_FS (per m80-f2zc.5), CONFIG_DEVTMPFS, CONFIG_DEVTMPFS_MOUNT, CONFIG_SERIAL_8250, CONFIG_SERIAL_8250_CONSOLE.
3. CONFIG drop list: PCI (CONFIG_PCI=n — we use virtio-mmio), most filesystems (CONFIG_BTRFS, XFS, F2FS, etc.), most network protocols (keep IPv4 only), USB, sound, drm, framebuffer, input, security modules beyond minimum, debugfs, tracing, ftrace, perf, kdb, kgdb, crash kernel.
4. Build environment: a Docker container based on Ubuntu 22.04 with kernel-build tooling (build-essential, bc, flex, bison, libelf-dev, libssl-dev). Reproducible Dockerfile committed to crates/m80-image-build/kernel-builder/.
5. Output convention: crates/m80-image-build/kernels/vmlinux-m80-<config-sha>.bin; manifest schema gains kernel.kind variant.

ACCEPTANCE: doc at docs/design/stripped-kernel.md with config delta, build container, version pin, and target boot time. No code in this leaf.

title: IMPL m80-firecracker: cmdline trim and kernel-kind dispatch
description:
In phase 11 boot-source PUT, dispatch on manifest.kernel_kind:

- Stock: existing COMMON_BOOT_ARGS (currently 'console=ttyS0 reboot=k panic=-1 pci=off').
- Stripped: 'console=ttyS0 reboot=k panic=-1 quiet loglevel=0 8250.nr_uarts=0' (drop pci=off duplicate, drop verbose kernel logging, suppress 8250 probe of unused UARTs which alone saves ~50ms).

Also: when manifest.image_kind is Minimal AND kernel_kind is Stripped, additionally drop the duplicate pci=off and drop init=/m80-guestd in favor of the kernel's default /init -> /m80-guestd symlink (the kernel resolves the symlink fine; explicit init= is documentation).

title: streaming.rs stdout/stderr seq# isolation needs verification
description:
site: crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/streaming.rs:286-299
finder: trim-the-fat r5

Problem: Two capture threads (stdout + stderr) increment per-stream `seq` counters. Likely safe (each thread writes to its own stream-typed frame; counters are per-stream), but worth a quick verification + test that confirms the invariant: stdout_seq and stderr_seq must increment monotonically within their own stream and are independent across streams.

Fix: read the code path carefully. If counters are shared (same Atomic), it's a race. If each thread has its own, document the invariant and add a regression test that runs concurrent stdout+stderr writes and asserts per-stream monotonicity.
notes: root=implementation already used independent per-stream seq counters, but test coverage only proved simple ordering. fix=multi-chunk stdout+stderr regression asserts stdout and stderr each start at seq 0 and advance monotonically independently. test=crates/m80-guestd/tests/streaming_exec.rs::streaming_stdout_and_stderr_sequences_are_independent. verification=cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; git diff --check

title: M80_DEBUG_WIRE env: dump vsock + firecracker REST traffic at framing layer (dev-only)
description:
Wire-level visibility, on demand, without a rebuild. Today protocol bugs require code edits to add eprintlns at the framing layer. A gated env-var dump would save hours per incident.

## Reference

CLAUDE.md "diagnostics before hypotheses" applies inside the workspace too. Most recent vsock-muxer / readiness investigations would have been minutes shorter with raw frame dumps available on demand.

## Scope

- M80_DEBUG_WIRE=vsock|fcrest|all env var.
- m80-vsock: when vsock set, log every framed message in/out at TRACE level with hex+ascii preview (cap message size).
- m80-firecracker-client: when fcrest set, log every REST request method+path+body+response status+body.
- Always gated; never on in release default; documented as "dev/debug only, do not enable in production".
- Output goes to tracing (RUST_LOG=trace picks it up).

## Out of scope

- Persistent capture/replay (use existing logs).
- Filtering by request_id at this layer (request_id end-to-end bead handles it elsewhere).

## Acceptance

- M80_DEBUG_WIRE=all RUST_LOG=trace m80 launch produces visible frame-level lines.
- Default invocation produces zero such lines.
- README of m80-vsock and m80-firecracker-client document the flag.
notes: Implemented 2026-05-05. Two debug_wire modules (vsock + fcrest), OnceLock-cached env parse, format_wire_preview helper at 1024-byte cap, tracing::trace! emission. 18 unit tests added. README sections in both crates document the env var. Channel::recv path forks under the gate to capture raw NDJSON line — documented inline.

title: Generic Guest Exec Service
description: Purpose: generic in-VM daemon listening on vsock that runs argv with optional cwd/env/stdin and returns stdout/stderr/exit/timing, with optional streaming and PTY modes.
