title: L8: m80-preflight capability detection completeness
description:
m80-preflight should fail fast with typed errors before launch when host setup is incomplete. Several capabilities are missing from preflight checks despite being required for launch — failures surface as cryptic launch-time errors instead of clean preflight rejections.

## Items

1. /dev/kvm missing — preflight typed error pointing user at "enable KVM" (not later cryptic open() error).
2. /dev/kvm permission-denied (open(O_RDWR) → EACCES) — typed error vs later fail.
3. KVM CPU flags (vmx/svm) collected but never validated — virtualization unsupported even with /dev/kvm; add typed PreflightError::KvmCpuExtensionMissing.
4. Vsock module missing — env.rs probes vhost_vsock but preflight ignores it; required for guest IPC.
5. TUN module missing — required for AllowOutbound but no preflight check.
6. nf_conntrack module missing — required for NAT but no detection anywhere.
7. Cgroup v2 availability — checked at launch phase 5 (after 4 phases of work), not preflight; surface typed PreflightError::CgroupV2Unavailable at preflight.
8. m80 --json env JSON shape on broken preflight — schema stable on error path (not just happy path); test PreflightDump fields when checks fail.

## Acceptance for sub-epic
- 8 tests under crates/m80-preflight/tests/ + crates/m80-cli/tests/.
- Mock-host-state tests refactor checks into testable fns parameterized by mocked readers.

title: L9: Multi-VM concurrency + race conditions
description:
**Most subtle sub-epic of the survey.** m80 is multi-tenant by design — many VMs may be in flight simultaneously. The behaviors that matter under concurrent load aren't pinned by single-VM e2e. These race conditions are also the cases most likely to bite under real load and not under a unit test.

m80-5vlb.5 covers PoolEmpty single case. This sub-epic covers the harder concurrency questions.

## Items

1. Admission semaphore N+1 concurrent overflow — barrier-synchronized N+1 threads call admit(); exactly N enter, +1 returns AdmissionRefused.
2. Permit return on launch panic mid-flight — panic injection during phase_3/4/11; semaphore restored, second admit succeeds.
3. Concurrent stop + concurrent launch on same run_dir — VM-A stop racing VM-B launch (same vm_id reused); ownership.lock atomicity holds.
4. Recovery loop running mid-launch of fresh VM — background recover.rs while a launch is mid-flight; doesn't kill the fresh VM.
5. Two cancel requests to same exec idempotent + race-safe — both responses arrive; second is AlreadyExited or reflects first cancel.
6. Warm-pool simultaneous lease + refill race — last 2 ready slots leased by 2 threads; refill restarts; both leases succeed.
7. Snapshot + launch concurrency — VM-A captures while VM-B launches from same snapshot parent; no deadlock or partial overwrite.
8. Persistent-VM concurrent exec serialization — Arc<RunningSandbox> with two threads attempting exec — must not compile (Send-bound) or fail safely.

## Acceptance for sub-epic
- 8 tests using barrier-synchronized threading primitives (Arc<Barrier>, parking_lot::Condvar).
- Each captures a specific race window with deterministic synchronization.

## Sources
- 2026-05-08 e2e gap survey, Lens 9.
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/{backend.rs,launch.rs,warm_pool.rs,runroot.rs}.
notes: All L9 concurrency leaves are closed. Final leaves added same-run-dir ownership lease coverage and snapshot capture/restore concurrency coverage.

title: Reject any frame whose post-trim length exceeds 4 MiB
description:

title: Wave 41 of 45: filesystem path handling + symlink safety + canonicalization
description:
Wave 41/45. 10 sonnets on path-handling discipline.

Lenses:
1. Path::join vs string concat — naive concat risks
2. PathBuf vs &Path on public fn signatures (cloning waste)
3. Symlink handling: openat(O_NOFOLLOW), lstat vs stat
4. canonicalize() use sites — TOCTOU risk
5. Path prefix checks (starts_with/strip_prefix) — correctness w/ trailing slash
6. Hardcoded paths: /tmp, /var/run, /sys, /proc, /dev — should be config?
7. Cross-platform Path display: lossy vs to_string_lossy
8. relative path construction across jail boundary
9. Path traversal defense (.. components) in user-controlled inputs
10. Linux-specific path semantics: O_PATH, O_DIRECTORY, openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH

title: Add typed Host/Jail path wrappers; 5 sites mix host vs in-jail paths under same identifier
description:
**Finding (W41.8):** Host vs in-jail path coordinate spaces are enforced only by naming convention; no typed wrapper. 5 candidate mix-up sites where a refactor would compile cleanly and fail at Firecracker/kernel level.

HIGH:
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/hotplug.rs:152-157 — HotplugDriveAttach.path_on_host validation error message says "must be absolute and visible inside the Firecracker jail" but only checks is_absolute(). A caller supplying a host-rooted absolute path passes validation; Firecracker PATCH errors at runtime.
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:329-397 — bind_snapshot_parent_into_jail takes &SnapshotPaths (host paths) and returns SnapshotBind whose .paths field contains REWRITTEN in-jail paths — same type, different coordinate space. Refactor that passes snapshot.paths instead of snapshot_bind.paths compiles and fails at restore time.

MEDIUM:
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:221+:258 — api_socket and host_api_socket both = firecracker_api_socket_path() (host path). MaterializedJail::launch silently strips to basename via api_socket.file_name(); the strip is undocumented at the call site.
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:95-119 — DriveConfig.path_on_host receives in-jail absolute paths like /rootfs.ext4 (cold-boot uses chroot-relative). Field name misleads; comment exists on BootSourceConfig.kernel_image_path but not on DriveConfig.path_on_host.
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:154-157 — VsockConfig.uds_path is the in-jail /vsock.sock. Same field elsewhere refers to the host UDS path. No type-level guard.

Severity: MEDIUM (latent refactor hazards; correctness depends on naming + comments).

Acceptance:
- Introduce HostPath<T> and JailPath<T> newtypes (or `pub struct JailRelative(PathBuf)`).
- Apply at: HotplugDriveAttach.path_on_host (JailRelative), DriveConfig.path_on_host (JailRelative), VsockConfig.uds_path (JailRelative), SnapshotPaths {host: HostPath, jail: JailPath} OR split into HostSnapshotPaths and JailSnapshotPaths.
- Strip "host_" / "api_socket" duplication at launch.rs:221,258.
- Update path_on_host validator: in addition to is_absolute, accept JailRelative type and reject HostPath at compile time.
- Cross-link m80-emon8.7 (newtype leakage audit).

title: m80-guestd fileops: missing sandbox-root containment + traversal check on path inputs
description:
**Finding (W41.9):** Host-supplied paths in guestd fileops requests have no `..` filtering and no sandbox-root containment check.

Sites (crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/):
- fileops.rs:194 write_file
- fileops.rs:226 begin_upload (temp path also derived from raw input)
- fileops/read.rs:15 stream_file_read
- fileops/metadata.rs:13 list_dir
- fileops/metadata.rs:57 stat_file
- fileops/metadata.rs:69 remove_file
- fileops/metadata.rs:92 mkdir

Threat model dependency: m80's contract is "host is trusted, guest kernel is the boundary." Under that model, these are acceptable because guest-side compromise has no way to send vsock requests to guestd impersonating the host. However:
- The cost of adding sandbox-root containment is low and provides defense in depth against future relaxations (e.g., a hostile mode where host_id != trust_root).
- m80-attack-runner scenarios specifically test for this — should validate the surface.

ALSO:
- m80-cli/src/profile.rs:142 validate_absolute_path — accepts absolute paths with `..` components (/opt/m80/../../etc/shadow). is_absolute() doesn't catch traversal. Add components()-walk check that rejects ParentDir.
- m80-image-build/src/config.rs:56 guestd.binary: PathBuf — no absoluteness/traversal check; passed to Command but quiet relative paths accepted.
- m80-image-build/src/config.rs:63 output.dir: PathBuf — same.

NULL audits:
- W41.1 path-concat: no exploitable risks; lower_sentinel env-controlled but inside-VM attack-runner only.
- W41.2 PathBuf vs &Path: all pub fn signatures correctly typed.
- W41.3 symlink safety: guestd uses O_NOFOLLOW + symlink_metadata throughout; jailer chroot setup host-controlled.
- W41.4 canonicalize: only one prod call site (jailer bind mount); narrow TOCTOU acknowledged.
- W41.5 starts_with/strip_prefix: every path-typed site uses Path methods correctly; str sites all on bare filenames.
- W41.10 openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH: not justified given the VM boundary already provides containment.

Severity: MEDIUM (defense in depth).

Acceptance:
- Add a `validate_request_path(p: &Path, sandbox_root: &Path) -> Result<&Path, FileError>` in guestd fileops common module that rejects ParentDir components AND ensures starts_with(sandbox_root).
- Update profile.rs validator to walk components.
- Update image-build config to reject relative/traversal in guestd.binary + output.dir.

title: Hardcoded path inconsistencies: /run/m80 vs /var/run/m80; DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT duplicated; /tmp test collisions
description:
**Finding (W41.6):** Path-literal duplication risks consumer-visible inconsistency.

MEDIUM (correctness — divergent defaults):
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/layout.rs:130 — Path::new("/run/m80") (no /var/). Inconsistent with DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT = "/var/run/m80" in preflight.
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/boot_identity.rs:104 — PathBuf::from("/run/m80"). Same drift.

LOW (duplication of DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT):
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs:35,317 — "/var/run/m80" inlined twice.
- crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/status.rs:104,137,200 — PathBuf::from("/var/run/m80") as fallback (3 sites).
- crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/quickstart.rs:289 — env_path("M80_RUN_ROOT", "/var/run/m80").

LOW (fallback binary paths shouldn't be hardcoded):
- crates/m80-jailer/src/recover.rs:137-139 — /usr/bin/jailer, /usr/bin/m80-jailer-harden, /usr/bin/firecracker as recovery fallback in live logic. Should come from config (which has binary path fields).

LOW (test /tmp collisions on parallel runs):
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:769 — "/tmp/m80-idle-watcher-test.sock" in #[test] inside src/. Use tempfile::Builder.
- crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/network-outbound-nat/teardown.rs (8 sites) — Path::new("/tmp/m80-teardown-run") shared across multiple test fns; guaranteed collision under `cargo test --test-threads N>1`.
- crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/network-outbound-nat/iptables.rs:387 — Path::new("/tmp/m80-outbound-run") same issue.

LOW (path display lossiness):
- crates/m80-jailer-harden/src/lib.rs:165,206,213 — to_string_lossy() on CLI OsString args; lines 206/213 parse numeric values. Non-UTF8 byte → U+FFFD silently corrupts parse. Switch to to_str().ok_or(...).
- crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/fileops/metadata.rs:44 — to_string_lossy() emits directory entry names over vsock wire protocol. Should error at boundary OR document UTF-8 requirement in proto.
- crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs:66 — to_string_lossy().into_owned() to extract vm_id from run_dir basename. Internally generated, low risk; explicit to_str().expect(...) + comment would be cleaner.

NULL (kernel ABI): /proc/, /sys/, /dev/, /etc/ guest write paths — all correctly fixed Linux ABIs.

Severity: LOW-MEDIUM (correctness on /run vs /var/run mismatch).

Acceptance:
- Resolve /run/m80 vs /var/run/m80 — pick one; replace literal in layout.rs + boot_identity.rs with import of DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT.
- Replace 5 other literal sites with import of preflight::DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT.
- recover.rs fallback paths → config-derived.
- Switch tests to tempfile crate.
- Fix to_string_lossy parse sites in jailer-harden.
- Add UTF-8 contract note to proto FileEntry name field (or error at boundary).

title: Audit: typed error variants visible at m80-cli + m80-firecracker public surface (no string collapse)
description:
Sweep public error surfaces and ensure typed thiserror variants stay typed at the boundary. Don't collapse to string-wrapped Other / Generic on the way out (kata's mistake at the ttRPC shim boundary).

## Reference

kata-exploration/07-public-api-and-shim.md. Kata's internal errors are typed (ContainerNotFound, ProcessNotFound, AgentConnectionClosed), but at the shim boundary they collapse to ttrpc::Error::Others(string) — losing type information for consumers. m80 should not repeat this.

## Why

CLAUDE.md ("What we don't want") forbids reclassification that hides which call site lost the file; the same principle applies to error type collapse. m80-cli's class-based exit codes (EXIT_PREFLIGHT=2 etc.) only work if the underlying error variants are still discriminable.

## Scope

- Audit m80-firecracker public Error type: are all variants concrete? any "Other(String)" / "Generic"?
- Audit m80-cli error mapping (m80-cli/src/errors.rs): does every internal error variant map cleanly to an exit code, or do some funnel through a string wrapper?
- Where collapse exists, replace with concrete variants.
- Document the policy in CLAUDE.md ("What we don't want") if not already covered.

## Out of scope

- Internal-only error types (those can be richer; the audit is at the public boundary only).
- anyhow at binary edges is fine (that's already the policy).

## Acceptance

- m80-firecracker::Error has no String-wrapping fallback variant (or has one with a written justification).
- m80-cli error → exit-code mapping is exhaustive over the underlying error type (compile-time match coverage).
- One regression test pins at least one specific error → specific exit code.
notes: policy=AGENTS.md,CLAUDE.md; firecracker-readme=crates/m80-firecracker/README.md documents FcError::Config(String) as config-only not fallback; fix=warm owner error wire now carries WarmErrorKind + exit_code and render_owner_error no longer reconstructs lossy Config/Generic; tests=cargo test -p m80-cli, cargo test -p m80-cli --test output_error_contract, cargo clippy -p m80-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings

title: exec_streaming truncated flag invisible to streaming callers
description:
site: crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs:88 (exec_inner truncated callback)
finder: trim-the-fat r5

Problem: `truncated` flag is set only via the closure passed by `exec_inner` (the buffered-exec wrapper). `exec_streaming()` and PTY callers have no path to observe truncation; their ExecExit / PtyExit terminal frames hardcode `truncated: false`.

Fix: thread truncation signal through ExecExit / PtyExit terminal frames so streaming callers know the output was capped. May require adding a CAPTURE_LIMIT to the streaming path (currently no cap; see related bead for #9).
notes: resolved with same explicit no-cap policy as m80-otr1. Streaming callers already receive ExecExit::truncated=false because direct streaming is intentionally not capped; truncation remains visible only on buffered exec, where m80-firecracker constructs ExecResponse and applies the 1 MiB per-stream buffer cap. docs/tests shared with m80-otr1 prove >1 MiB streaming and PTY output are not truncated.

title: FileError::Io is an opaque catch-all: erases ENOSPC, EROFS, EFBIG, etc. at wire boundary
description:
**Finding:** crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/fileops.rs:408-418 map_io_error converts any io::Error not in {ELOOP, EISDIR, ENOTDIR, NotFound, PermissionDenied} to FileError::Io. This includes ENOSPC, EROFS, EFBIG, EACCES-on-root, ENOMEM — all surface on host as 'file operation: Io' with no path or syscall context. Variant is erased at the wire boundary; host cannot recover or branch.

Most consequential: disk-full (ENOSPC) and read-only-fs (EROFS) errors look identical to any other I/O failure.

**File:** crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/fileops.rs:408-418 (map_io_error); crates/m80-proto/src/types/fileops.rs:63 (FileError enum).

**Severity:** MEDIUM (CLAUDE.md: 'No typed error collapse at public boundaries').

**Acceptance:**
- Add typed variants: FileError::NoSpace, FileError::ReadOnlyFs, FileError::FileTooLarge, FileError::OutOfMemory.
- Or minimally: add FileError::OsError(i32) carrying raw errno; host can branch on common values.
- Update map_io_error to surface specific cases; keep Io as 'truly unknown' fallback.
- Cross-link m80-mrjqs.8 (FcError::Io → PathIo class).

title: Guest mount_one orphans mount dir on partial failure (today VM-discarded; future retry-risk)
description:
**Finding:** crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/hotplug.rs:190-194 mount_one creates the mount dir successfully, then mount_ext4 fails. The empty mount dir is left on the guest filesystem. No rollback. Returns failed(spec, DriveHotplugError::MountFailed).

Today: benign. Host discards the VM on any Failed response → guest disk is gone with the VM. Future retryable-attach paths (re-entry after partial mount) would silently pass the create_dir_all and mount on top of the stale empty dir.

**File:** crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/hotplug.rs:190-194.

**Severity:** LOW (today; MEDIUM when retry semantics added).

**Acceptance:**
- On mount_ext4 failure, attempt to rmdir the just-created mount dir before returning failed.
- Test pin: mock mount_ext4 returns Err; assert mount dir cleaned up.
- Cross-link m80-ag33f.6 (RunningSandbox recovery docs).

title: WarmPool::new doesn't reject preallocated_drive_slots > 0; restore path skips slot PUTs → confusing failures
description:
**Finding:** WarmPool::new validates workspace.is_none() but not preallocated_drive_slots == 0. The golden VM is captured with slots=0 hardcoded in warm_sandbox_config (owner.rs:219, run.rs:267). The RESTORED VM's SandboxConfig may independently specify slots > 0:
- phase_3_storage_prep creates placeholder files
- phase_4_jailer_materialize bind-mounts them into the jail
- BUT phase_11_rest_puts is SKIPPED on the restore path — Firecracker's drive table comes from vm.snap (with 0 slots).
- Caller's attach_drive_verified(slot=0) on the restored VM → PATCH /drives/hotplug_slot_0 → Firecracker returns 400/404 (drive_id unknown).
- Confusing error: 'drive write failed' (per m80-i8rua.1) with no hint that slots-on-restore aren't wired.

Also m80-i8rua.5 (backing file landmine): golden's run-dir is deleted (owner.rs:60). If golden HAD slots, restored VM's drive paths point to deleted files → first read EIO.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:139-175 (WarmPool::new validation); crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:459 (launch_from_snapshot skips preboot PUTs).

**Severity:** MEDIUM (latent landmine — currently blocked by 0-slot defaults but unenforced).

**Acceptance:**
- In WarmPool::new: if sandbox.preallocated_drive_slots != 0 → ConfigError::InvalidValue with reason explaining the snapshot/restore PUT-replay gap.
- Document the limitation in WarmPool docstring.
- Alternative (more work): on restore, replay PUTs for preallocated_drive_slots after snapshot_load completes.
- Cross-link m80-r4308.2, m80-i8rua.1.
close_reason: Merged into m80-qei44.2: preallocated_drive_slots == 0 check is a second validation in the same WarmPool::new block; preserve: the golden-VM-capture / restore-path skip scenario as rationale + a dedicated test for the drive-s

title: UeventState.cache unbounded growth; kernel change-event flood inside guest accumulates
description:
**Finding:** crates/m80-guestd/src/uevent.rs:88 — UeventState.cache: Vec<Uevent> has no bound and no eviction. spawn_netlink_listener pushes every parsed uevent without trimming. Normal hotplug attach produces 1-2 events; cache stays small. But:
- Some kernels emit 'change' events alongside 'add' on virtio-blk hotplug
- A retry/flapping scenario can compound

In single-VM-lifecycle today: bounded by VM lifetime. Becomes a real concern if the registry is ever reused across warm-pool iterations.

**File:** crates/m80-guestd/src/uevent.rs:87-89.

**Severity:** LOW (today; bounded by VM lifetime).

**Acceptance:**
- Cap cache at e.g. 2 × preallocated_drive_slots + 8 entries.
- Or: drain matched entries after wait_for returns successfully.
- Test pin: simulate kernel sending 1000 change events; assert cache stays bounded.

title: FileRemoveRequest accepts arbitrary guest path; chunked upload temp dir is guest-controlled
description:
**Finding:** Two related fileops path-confinement gaps:

1. crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/fileops/metadata.rs:69-90 FileRemoveRequest accepts arbitrary path. guestd as root in VM can delete /sbin/init, guestd binary, /sys/firmware paths, kernel module files. Trusted-caller model means OK today; gap exposed if any future adapter exposes remove_file to untrusted code.

2. crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/fileops.rs:249 — chunked upload temp file path is constructed as 'format!("{}.m80-upload.{upload_id}", req.path)' — placed in same DIRECTORY as final target, name derived from guest-supplied req.path. Directory components from req.path are not validated; '..'-traversal req.path creates temp file outside intended scope. O_NOFOLLOW guards leaf-symlink but not directory components.

**File:** crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/fileops/metadata.rs:69-90 (remove); crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/fileops.rs:249 (upload temp).

**Severity:** LOW (trusted-caller assumption; exposure when untrusted adapter is added).

**Acceptance:**
- Optional path-prefix allowlist (e.g., /workspace only) in fileops handlers; configurable.
- Validate req.path components (no '..') before constructing temp path in upload handler.
- Document the trusted-caller assumption in fileops module rustdoc.
- Cross-link m80-9ihnr.1 (vm_id traversal — same path-validation discipline).

title: Audit: #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] across all m80 config / manifest types
description:
Sweep m80 for serde-deserialized types where unknown fields should fail loudly instead of silently dropping. Bug found during kata recon: BuildConfig in crates/m80-image-build/src/config.rs is missing #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)].

## Reference

kata-exploration/05-image-build-and-rootfs.md flagged m80-image-build/src/config.rs as a concrete miss.

## Why

With the missing attribute, a typo in a config field name silently drops the value. CLAUDE.md ("What we don't want") explicitly forbids "be tolerant" wrappers on internal data. A typo should be a parse error, not silent acceptance.

## Scope

- Grep all #[derive(Deserialize)] in the workspace.
- Add #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] to every internal config / manifest / wire type unless there is a specific written reason not to (e.g. the m80-image-manifest schema if it has a forward-compat clause — but verify).
- Add a regression test for at least m80-image-build BuildConfig: unknown field → error.
- Document the policy in CLAUDE.md's "What we don't want" section if absent.

## Out of scope

- External-facing wire formats with explicit forward-compat semantics. Verify each before applying.

## Acceptance

- All internal config / manifest types either have the attribute or have a one-line comment explaining why not.
- One regression test pinning the BuildConfig case.
notes: policy=AGENTS.md,CLAUDE.md; audit=all Deserialize derives strict with documented partial version/schema probes only; tests=cargo test -p m80-image-build build_config_, cargo test -p m80-image-build --test dry_run_smoke, cargo test --workspace; clippy=cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

title: Documentation drift audit: READMEs vs reality
description:
**Status:** planned, not yet executed.

**Angle:** Per CLAUDE.md "A change to a crate's public surface updates that crate's README in the same diff. Drift is a bug." Audit every crate README + workspace-level docs against current code. Flag drift.

**Why this angle:** mechanical, high-confidence audit. Findings convert directly to fix beads (rewrite the affected README section). Catches the inevitable per-PR drift that the same-diff rule misses.

**Expected lens shapes (~10-12 agents), each takes one crate or doc cluster:**
- Per-crate README: claimed public surface vs actual `pub` items in `lib.rs`
- README behavior claims: claimed behaviors vs actual test coverage (cross-references e4)
- CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md vs actual workspace conventions
- docs/behaviors/<area>/ files: each one references a test path; does the test still exist?
- docs/decisions/<NNNN>-*.md: do referenced decisions still hold? Marked superseded if not?
- docs/positioning.md, docs/adapter-boundary.md: still describe current state?
- docs/perf/cold-launch.md: numbers, phases, claims — match current behavior?
- README.md (workspace root): does it match `cargo doc` output?
- docs/postmortems/: are remediations cited as bead IDs still open? Closed? Documented as not-justified?
- CHANGELOG.md Unreleased section: does it actually list every user-visible change since last release?

**Findings format:** each drift = one finding citing the doc line + the contradicting code line + the correct text. Aggregated into per-crate "fix README drift" beads (XS effort each).

**Cross-link:** AGENTS.md same-diff rule. Suggestion: also propose a CI check that diff-vs-readme-update for crate-touching PRs, if mechanical detection is feasible.
close_reason: pure audit-wave summary; 10 children filed (status was "planned"; children have the substance)

title: LOW: m80-guestd uses anyhow in pub library modules — clarify CLAUDE.md rule
description:
W5L10. CLAUDE.md L39: 'thiserror for library errors; anyhow only at binary edges.' m80-guestd has src/lib.rs exposing pub mod connection + pub mod guest_log. Both use anyhow::Result extensively. Strict reading: violation.

Practical impact: low — m80-guestd ships a binary and no external crate depends on its lib surface. But the rule as stated doesn't cover this nuance.

Fix: either (a) refactor m80-guestd public modules to thiserror, or (b) clarify CLAUDE.md to say 'binary-first crates may use anyhow throughout even in their pub lib surface IF no other crate depends on that surface'. Recommend (b) — typed errors here would be ceremony without consumer. ~15min for doc clarification. ~6h if we go option (a).

title: m80-side primitives for conveyor-belt pool (drive hot-plug + tenant-identity vsock + one-shot lifecycle)
description:
The conveyor-belt strategy (one-shot VMs from a generic pool with on-demand tenant drive attach) is detailed in docs/future-directions/bestiary-conveyor-belt.md. Pool management, profile catalog, elastic buffer, scale-to-zero, and tenant routing live in the Bestiary, an external orchestration daemon **outside m80 core scope per CLAUDE.md**. This epic captures only the m80-side primitives the Bestiary will call.

## In scope (m80-owned)

### 1. Drive hot-plug
- m80-firecracker-client: add PATCH /drive REST method to attach a virtio-blk device to a running VM after boot. Verify the FC version we ship supports drive hot-plug (older versions only allowed pre-boot drive PUT).
- m80-guestd: udev/uevent watcher that detects newly-attached block devices, mounts them at a configured path (/workspace by default), with idempotent retry, ~100 ms timeout, and post-mount verification (filesystem readable, expected fixture present).
- m80-proto: extend the request/response set so the host can drive the attach + signal the guest where to mount.

### 2. Tenant-identity vsock contract
- m80-proto: new envelope payload for the guest to read /workspace/.tenant-identity (UUID or signed token) after mount and report it to the host.
- m80-firecracker host-side: compare the reported identity against the expected tenant supplied at allocation; mismatch = immediate VM kill (no leak window).
- The signature scheme + token format is Bestiary-defined; m80 only carries opaque bytes.

### 3. One-shot lifecycle flag
- m80-firecracker: SandboxConfig (or equivalent) gains a one_shot mode that says "destroy this VM after the next exec/stop, do not return to caller for reuse". The Bestiary uses this so it never has to manage cleanup state.
- Lifecycle state machine refuses subsequent execs once one-shot has been triggered.

## Refinements added by 12-agent audit (2026-05-07)

### E1 — Pre-allocated drive slots pattern
kata reserves N (typically 6) placeholder drives at boot, all PATCH-updateable. Pre-allocation enables PATCH (which only updates existing drives) without an insertion step. Reference: /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/runtime-rs/crates/hypervisor/src/firecracker/fc_api.rs:147-169.

For m80: at warm-pool VM boot, reserve N placeholder drives (e.g., 4: workspace + 3 spare). The Bestiary picks one and PATCHes the path on allocation. Avoids a "create drive then attach" two-step on the request path.

### E2 — Two-phase device removal
kata splits drive detach into PrepareRemove (guest eject signal + bounded timeout for guest to flush/unmount) → RemoveBlockDevice (host-side cleanup). Reference: /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/runtime-rs/crates/hypervisor/src/dragonball/vmm_instance.rs:263-278.

For m80: needed for safe detach when a Bestiary slot is reused (one-shot makes reuse rare, but graceful drive removal is still needed during teardown if any guest activity is mid-flight).

### E3 — Sync RPC with timeout for hot-plug verification
kata uses a sync channel + ACK + bounded wait for hot-plug operations. Reference: /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/runtime-rs/crates/hypervisor/src/dragonball/vmm_instance.rs:245-260.

For m80: the drive hot-plug should not return success until the guest acknowledges device-detection and successful mount; today we have to design this contract from scratch. kata's pattern is the template.

## Refinements added by 20-agent deep audit (2026-05-07)

### E4 — Device matcher trait registry pattern
kata defines a UeventMatcher trait (uevent.rs:37-39) plus concrete matchers (VirtioBlkPciMatcher, ScsiBlockMatcher, VfioMatcher) — each filters uevent messages by devpath regex + subsystem. Pattern lets new device types plug in without touching the dispatch loop.

For m80: as drive hot-plug grows (workspace, scratch, cache slots), matcher trait avoids ifelse soup in m80-guestd. Reference: /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/agent/src/uevent.rs:37-39 + /tank/projects/kata-containers/src/agent/src/device/.

### E5 — Multi-device atomicity / partial-failure handling
kata's add_devices() (device/mod.rs:184-251) loops per device, accumulates updates in a HashMap, returns on first handler error. No rollback today; the device is already in uevent_map. Cgroup updates per-device.

For m80: when the Bestiary attaches multiple drives at once (workspace + cache + scratch), document the partial-success contract — does m80 commit the successful subset and surface a typed error for the failed ones, or revert all? Recommend: surface partial-success in response envelope; Bestiary chooses to discard the slot or proceed.

### E6 — Idempotent pre-mounted detection
kata skips re-mount if the storage source matches a pre-mount tag and the mount already exists (storage/mod.rs:389-397). Avoids EBUSY on idempotent retries.

For m80: m80-guestd's mount handler should check if /workspace is already mounted (with the right device + matching identity) and treat re-attach as a no-op. Useful for E5's partial-success retry case.

### E7 — Hybrid wait-for-device polling
kata's wait_for_uevent (uevent.rs:115-160) checks a cached uevent_map first, then waits on a oneshot channel with tokio::time::timeout(hotplug_timeout, rx). Matcher checked at dispatch time. Default 3 s (kata config.rs:66 DEFAULT_HOTPLUG_TIMEOUT).

For m80: combine cached-map (covers cold-plug at boot before listener was ready) + uevent listener (covers hot-plug) + bounded timeout (covers slow VMs). Avoids busy-poll. Same pattern as m80-3xwa.5 F3 (online CPU/memory on hot-plug) — share the infrastructure.

## Cross-references
- m80-3xwa.5 F3 (online CPU/memory) uses the same uevent listener infrastructure — shared implementation.
- m80-3xwa (umbrella) tracks this epic as a parent-child child.

## Acceptance
- The Bestiary (or an integration test standing in for it) can: allocate a generic pool VM, hot-plug a per-tenant drive, see guest mount + identity-verify within ~45 ms P50, run a workload, destroy the VM, and never see leftover state in the next slot.
- Drive hot-plug works at FC's documented version requirement; below that, m80 returns a typed error so the Bestiary can fall back.
- Pre-allocated drive slots pattern (E1) means the request-path drive attach is a PATCH, not a CREATE+PATCH.
- Detach uses two-phase removal (E2); guest gets a bounded eject window before host-side cleanup.
- Hot-plug RPC uses sync ACK with timeout (E3); failure returns a typed error so the Bestiary can discard the slot.
- Device handler dispatch is matcher-trait-based (E4) — adding a new device type does not touch the listener loop.
- Partial-success in multi-device attach (E5) returns a typed response with per-device status.
- Re-attach of an already-mounted drive (E6) is idempotent.
- Wait-for-device (E7) uses the cached-map + uevent + bounded-timeout pattern; no busy-polling.

## Out of scope
- Pool itself (Bestiary).
- Profile snapshots (Bestiary).
- Scale-to-zero / elastic buffer (Bestiary).
- Tenant authentication or token signing (Bestiary).
- Cross-host pool federation.

## References
- /tmp/m80-conveyor-belt-strategy.md (hermes, 2026-05-07) — full product strategy.
- docs/future-directions/bestiary-conveyor-belt.md — captured strategy in repo.
- m80-rrp.3 (closed) — snapshot/restore substrate the Bestiary uses for refill.
- m80-c78m — stress-ng saturation reliability bug; gates under-load reliability claim.
- m80-3xwa — parent umbrella for jailer/sandbox parity work.
- m80-3xwa.5 — m80-guestd hardening; F3 shares infrastructure with E7.
- 12-agent audit (2026-05-07) — kata storage/network/device hot-plug lens (E1/E2/E3).
- 20-agent deep audit (2026-05-07) — kata device hot-plug deep-dive (E4/E5/E6/E7).

title: Optional PID namespace isolation per VM (CLONE_NEWPID)
description:
FC's stock jailer can fork Firecracker into a new PID namespace via --new-pid-ns. In that namespace FC becomes PID 1 and cannot see or signal processes outside it — limiting blast radius of a compromised FC process. m80 launches FC directly in the caller's PID namespace; a compromised process could enumerate and potentially interact with other host processes.

## Scope
- Add optional new_pid_ns: bool to JailerConfig.
- When enabled, clone(CLONE_NEWPID) to fork into a new PID namespace before exec; child becomes PID 1.
- Handle session leadership correctly (avoid spurious SIGHUP, as FC jailer does).
- Persist inner PID in a .pid file for monitoring.

## Cross-references
- **m80-3xwa.2 B1** (session leadership check + setsid) shares the same call site — they MUST land together. B1 cannot be applied cleanly without isxo because setsid in a fresh PID NS creates a new session at PID 1, which is the desired state. Sequence: clone(CLONE_NEWPID) in this epic, then 3xwa.2 B1 adds the pre-clone session-leadership check + post-clone setsid().
- **m80-3c9b** (daemonize double-fork) uses the same session leadership semantics — the daemonize epic builds on top of this and 3xwa.2 B1.
- **m80-jmqg** (mount NS) ordering: when both this and m80-jmqg are configured, mount-NS first, then PID-NS. Both are clone-time flags so they can also be combined into a single clone() call (CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWPID).

## Child tasks
1. IMPL: clone(CLONE_NEWPID) with null stack pointer (FC's approach); session leadership; PID file persistence.
2. IMPL: lifecycle management — inspect_run_dir checks the inner PID, not the outer clone parent; graceful shutdown signals namespace PID.
3. TEST/DOCS: getpid() inside the jail returns 1 when enabled; jailed process cannot see host PIDs via /proc.

## Acceptance
- When new_pid_ns is true, FC runs as PID 1 in its own namespace.
- **getpid() == 1 verification**: integration test exec's a probe inside the jail, captures `cat /proc/self/status | grep Pid:` output, asserts the value is 1.
- Process-list isolation test: jail process listing /proc/ shows only its own PID + children, not host PIDs.
- Existing smoke and bench pass with both new_pid_ns true and false.
- Lifecycle (stop, snapshot) works correctly with namespace PIDs.

## Audit-confirmed code references
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:328-383 — exec_into_new_pid_ns() (the model for m80's implementation)
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:346-359 — pre-clone session leadership check (paired with m80-3xwa.2 B1)
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:369 — post-clone setsid() (paired with m80-3xwa.2 B1)

## Sources
- /tmp/m80-proposed-epic-beads.md Epic 4.
- 12-agent audit Lens 2 (process/PID/session isolation), 2026-05-07.

title: LaunchProcessCleanupGuard kill failures silently swallowed; no FcError signals orphan pid risk
description:
**Finding:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/failure_cleanup.rs:122-152 LaunchProcessCleanupGuard fires kill_and_reap_pid in Drop on phase failure. Kill/reap failures are logged at error! but SWALLOWED — Drop can't return Err. Caller sees the original phase error (e.g., FcError::Cgroup) with no indication that the process cleanup also failed and a Firecracker pid may still be alive.

No FcError variant for 'cleanup also failed'. Callers can't distinguish 'phase X failed, VM cleanly disposed' from 'phase X failed, orphan FC pid running'.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/failure_cleanup.rs:122-152.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (resource leak class; pairs with m80-ag33f.2 'no is_retryable').

**Acceptance:**
- Add FcError::CleanupIncomplete { phase_error: Box<FcError>, cleanup_errors: Vec<String> } variant.
- Or: track cleanup result in a side channel on the guard (Arc<Mutex<Option<io::Error>>>) and inject at error-return time.
- Document in error.rs: 'every launch error implies caller may want to issue force_kill / recover sweep'.
- Cross-link m80-ag33f.2, m80-ag33f.6.

title: No protocol-tainted flag: post-FcError::Protocol/Vsock, subsequent exec may misattribute frames
description:
**Finding:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs:35-46 begin_exec_activity checks idle_timed_out and one_shot_consumed gates. But there's NO 'protocol_tainted' flag for the case where a prior exec returned FcError::Protocol(DisconnectBeforeTerminal | UnexpectedFrame | SequenceMismatch) or FcError::Vsock.

After such a mid-stream protocol error: the vsock channel is dropped, but the guest-side child may still be running AND guestd's state machine may be desynchronized. A subsequent exec opens a fresh vsock channel that guestd will accept — but the prior child may still be writing frames into the same socket buffer, mis-attributed to the new exec.

No documentation states callers must NOT retry after Protocol/Vsock errors. RunningSandbox::Drop calls force_kill anyway, but the contract gap is real.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs:35-46 (entry gate).

**Severity:** MEDIUM (correctness; misattributed output on retry).

**Acceptance:**
- Add tainted: AtomicBool to RunningSandbox.
- On FcError::Protocol or FcError::Vsock from exec_streaming_inner / exec_pty_inner, set tainted = true before returning.
- begin_exec_activity returns FcError::ProtocolTainted (new variant) if set.
- Document: 'Any FcError::Protocol or FcError::Vsock from exec means the VM should be force-killed; retry is unsafe.'
- Cross-link m80-ag33f.6.

title: ExecRequest.streaming is dead public knob — host always overwrites to true; misleading API

title: 6 adapter-boundary trust invariants in m80-ag33f.10 confirmed; snapshot-dir-lifetime is HIGH

**Finding:** All 6 invariants from m80-ag33f.10 confirmed against current code. Severity ranking:
1. **HIGH**: Snapshot directory must outlive the restored VM (it's bind-mounted). Deletion mid-VM causes silent, unrecoverable in-VM fault. SnapshotPaths comment frames for capture, not restore. crates/m80-snapshot/src/lib.rs:147, RestoreRequest:181, launch.rs:434.

title: Jailer pivot_root + dedicated mount namespace per VM
description:
m80's jailer bind-mounts firecracker, rootfs images, and sockets into a directory structure but does NOT call unshare(CLONE_NEWNS), pivot_root, or unmount the host root. The Firecracker process inherits the caller's mount namespace and retains visibility of the host filesystem tree. FC's stock jailer enters a new mount namespace, bind-mounts the jail root over itself, calls pivot_root, then umount2(MNT_DETACH) on the old root — so the FC process literally cannot see anything outside the chroot.

Highest-security-value gap of the six FC-jailer hardening features m80 currently lacks (proposed-epic-beads.md ranking).

## Scope
- Add a new plan step (PlanStep::IsolateNamespace or equivalent) that calls unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) + mount(_, _, _, MS_SLAVE | MS_REC, _) to make propagation slave.
- After bind-mounts are in place, pivot_root into the jail directory.
- umount2 the old root with MNT_DETACH, then rmdir the old_root stub.
- MaterializedJail::Drop must reverse the operation or at minimum guarantee the host mount table is not polluted on teardown.

## Cross-references
- **m80-3xwa.1 (Mount/FS hardening, Group A)** is the follow-up sweep that hardens flags WITHIN the new mount NS this epic creates. Land m80-jmqg first; then 3xwa.1's six items (MS_SLAVE/REC propagation, MS_REC bind, MS_NODEV/NOEXEC/NOSUID, 0o700 perms, /proc-/sys handling, O_NOFOLLOW + canonicalization) become straightforward sweeps inside the established namespace.
- **m80-isxo (CLONE_NEWPID)** pairs at the same call site if they ever land together; ordering is mount-NS first, then PID-NS.
- **m80-3xwa.2 B1** (session leadership + setsid) shares the same call path for daemonized launches.

## Child tasks (to file when claimed)
1. IMPL: namespace + pivot_root in m80-jailer plan step. Needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN (already required for bind mounts). Must work with existing MaterializedJail Drop guard.
2. TEST: pivot_root integration test — jailed process cannot stat paths outside jail root; Drop cleans up mount namespace.
3. DOCS: docs/behaviors and m80-jailer README updates documenting the isolation guarantee; plan-schema bump if new steps added.

## Acceptance
- Jailed Firecracker process cannot access host paths outside its chroot.
- Existing real-KVM smoke and bench pass with new isolation.
- Crash recovery (orphan jail detection) still works after pivot_root.
- m80-jailer's MaterializedJail::Drop runs before mount-NS exit so the reverse plan executes correctly. Document this invariant in the integration test.

## Out of scope
- PID namespace isolation (m80-isxo).
- Mount-flag hardening within the new namespace (m80-3xwa.1).
- Network namespace changes.

## Audit-confirmed code references (12-agent audit, 2026-05-07)
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/chroot.rs:20-25 — unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) + initial setup
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/chroot.rs:74-92 — pivot_root() + chdir() + umount2(MNT_DETACH)
- /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/env.rs:644-676 — full chroot ceremony in run() method

## Sources

- 12-agent audit Lens 1 (FC mount/FS isolation), 2026-05-07.

**Measurement track (.41-.48)** — playbook doc + 7 specific experiments. Each measurement bead BLOCKS a subset of candidate beads, so gated work can't false-close on guesswork.

- **.8 phase_12b decomp** (already filed; effectively a measurement bead) — blocks .5, .6, .23, .39, .46, .48 (need per-phase attribution to verify gains).

Verify via `br dep tree m80-jp6ik`.

## How to work this epic

1. Land .41 (playbook doc) + .8 (decomp). Those are the universal prereqs.
2. Run the measurement beads in parallel — each is 1.5-4h of bench cycle.
3. As each measurement lands, the gated candidate beads it unblocks become claimable WITH `verified` acceptance per m80-lovpn.3 discipline.
4. Tier-A candidates (P1) without measurement deps are claimable immediately: .2, .3, .4, .5 (after .8), .6 (after .8), .21, .23 (after .8).

## Investigated and found inert (cross-round nulls — DO NOT re-explore)

**Round 2 (9):** Seccomp filter caching; vsock listener ordering; virtio num_queues; alternative allocator; phase_11c boot_identity_record; workspace lazy-attach; hot-path logging overhead; initramfs/CONFIG_RD_*; guestd signal handlers.

title: Decompose phase_12b: earlycon + M80_GUEST_BOOT parse + per-PUT + I/O+cgroup stats
description:
## Why

`phase_12b_ready_accept` is a single ~1017ms timer covering: Firecracker `InstanceStart` returning → kernel decompress → kernel init → devtmpfs+virtio probe → init=guestd → guestd pseudo-fs+overlay+pivot → guestd vsock connect → host accept. We cannot pick the right optimization without splitting it. Three pieces of instrumentation, all cheap, would carve this into ~8 named sub-intervals.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:33-34` — add `earlycon=uart8250,io,0x3f8,115200n8` (or `earlyprintk=ttyS0,115200`) to `STRIPPED_BOOT_ARGS` so kernel prints timestamps before `start_kernel` completes.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs:82-121` — wrap the `accept_ready_signal` call in a `phase_event` named `phase_12b_host_waiting_accept` so the bare wait is separable from FC-startup.
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/guest_log.rs:208-210` — already emits `M80_GUEST_BOOT name=X elapsed_us=Y` lines to console.log. NEW: post-accept parser in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch/ready.rs` that scans `<run_dir>/console.log` for these markers and re-emits each as a host `phase_event` (`phase_12b_guest_<name>`). The format is already stable.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:133-145` (`apply_preboot_puts`) — wrap each PUT arm with its own `phase_event` (`phase_11_put_machine_config`, `phase_11_put_drive_rootfs`, ...). Lets us see which PUT is slow.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs` (post-phase_12b) — read `/proc/<firecracker_pid>/io` (rchar, read_bytes, major faults from `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 12) and `<cgroup_path>/cpu.stat` (usage_usec); emit as diagnostic events.

## Acceptance

- Real-KVM run produces phase events for: earlycon kernel timestamp range, FC InstanceStart wait, each guestd milestone (process_start, stdio_redirected, pseudo_fs_mounted, base_mounted, overlay_disk_mounted, overlayfs_mounted, pivot_rootfs_done, network_configured, workspace_mounted, exec_listener_bound, ready_signal_sent), each individual phase_11 PUT, and post-launch I/O + CPU-stat snapshot.
- `bench-summary.py` snapshot includes the new phase events with histograms.
- `docs/perf/phase-12b-decomposition.md` written naming what dominates the 900ms (the data drives the next bead's priority).

## Out of scope

- Don't yet act on what the decomp reveals. This bead produces the data; the next-tier beads (B5 kernel cmdline, B6 erofs, B11 guestd defer) consume it.
- Don't add Firecracker `/logger` UDS yet (separate bead — needs `LoggerConfig` client surface).

## Effort

~6h. Mostly mechanical instrumentation; the console.log parser is the only real code.

## Done

After landing this and running N=50 minimal/idle, we know which of these dominates: kernel decompress, kernel init code path, devtmpfs/virtio probe, init=exec, guestd overlay/pivot, guestd vsock handshake, or host accept latency.

title: Hugepages backing for guest RAM (machine-config huge_pages)
description:
## Why

Firecracker's `machine-config` API has supported a `huge_pages` field since v1.5 / stable v1.7+. m80's `MachineConfig` struct (`crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:313-326`) has only vcpu_count/mem_size_mib/smt/cpu_template; the huge_pages field doesn't exist and is never sent. Guest memory uses default `mmap(MAP_ANONYMOUS | MAP_PRIVATE)` with 4KiB pages, faulted lazily as guest touches each page.

Savings: 50-80ms P50 on hosts with hugepages pre-reserved (fewer TLB misses + no per-4K-page-fault during guest RAM init).

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:313-326` — add `huge_pages: Option<HugePageSize>` to `MachineConfig`; new enum with `None`, `Mb2`, `Gb1` (serde to "None"/"2M"/"1G").
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/config.rs` — add `huge_pages: Option<HugePageSize>` to `SandboxConfig`.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/preboot.rs:151-157` — pass through.
- `crates/m80-preflight/src/checks.rs` — NEW check: if huge_pages configured but `/sys/kernel/mm/hugepages/hugepages-2048kB/free_hugepages` < required, fail preflight with `huge_pages_unavailable` and hint at `sysctl vm.nr_hugepages=N`.

## Acceptance

- Config + client + preflight wired.
- Bench with huge_pages=Mb2 (after `sysctl vm.nr_hugepages=512` ≈ 1GiB for one VM): phase_12b_ready_accept P50 drops 50-80ms vs default; cold-cold penalty smaller too.
- Without preflight reservation, helpful error rather than FC opaque failure.
- Document in `docs/perf/hugepages.md` including the host setup procedure.

## Effort

~1d.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e5-tlb-and-cache-miss-counters.
close_reason: not-justified: m80-jp6ik.46 measured dTLB-load-misses P50 40.5K/P95 44.5K, below the 100K cutoff in docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md; hugepages payoff is bounded on this host

title: Defer guestd network + workspace mount to post-ready
description:
## Why

Two guestd PID-1 steps run BEFORE signaling ready, but neither is required for host-side accept:

1. **Network config** (`crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs:48` → `pid_one_network.rs:105-118`) — builds a Tokio current-thread runtime, opens rtnetlink, makes 3 sequential `block_on` netlink calls (get link, add IPv4, set link up, add route), writes `/etc/resolv.conf`. **10-50ms** on the critical path.
2. **Workspace mount** (`crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs:50` → `pid_one.rs:442-458`) — mounts /dev/vdc if present; on dirty fs, spawns blocking `e2fsck -y -f` + `resize2fs`. **2-20ms clean, 200-500ms on repair.**

The host's first exec lands AFTER its own request/parse window; both can complete in the background before that exec needs them. Moving them off the critical path also protects P99 from e2fsck blowups.

## Files

- `crates/m80-guestd/src/pid_one.rs:39-53` — restructure: required-pre-ready steps only (stdio, panic hook, pseudo-fs, overlay+pivot, vsock bind, ready signal). After signal: spawn deferred network + workspace work on a background thread.
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/main.rs:163-166` — accept loop must check workspace-mount-complete before serving the first exec that touches it; cheap wait (one OnceLock or AtomicBool).
- `docs/behaviors/guestd/ready-signal-deferred-init.md` — NEW. Documents what guestd promises is true at "ready" vs what's still in flight.

## Acceptance

- Network + workspace mount move off the pre-ready path.
- A request that lands before workspace is mounted blocks at most until workspace-ready (with a timeout returning typed error).
- Bench phase_12b_ready_accept P50 drops by ≥10ms (network deferred).
- Worst-case P99 drops dramatically when workspace fs is dirty (no e2fsck on critical path).
- Test: artificially-dirty workspace image; verify ready signals at clean-path latency, first workspace-exec waits for repair.

## Effort

~1-2d.
close_reason: Rejected: conflicts with current readiness invariant; docs/behaviors/guest-exec/deferred-storage-readiness.md already rejects deferred storage/workspace readiness because ready means final rootfs and configured workspace view are usable.

title: iptables-restore batching (replace per-rule subprocess loop)
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs:91-103` (`apply_outbound_nat_policy_with_ops`) calls `ensure_iptables_rule` ~25 times per launch (DNS accepts, denies, FORWARD inserts, MASQUERADE). Each `iptables` invocation is a subprocess fork + acquires `/run/xtables.lock` exclusively. At C=4 concurrent launches the lock queue is ~100 sequential lock-acquire ops; at C=16, far worse.

`iptables-restore` accepts a batched ruleset over stdin and acquires the xtables lock once for the entire batch. Net wallclock saving: 20-40ms per launch in NoEgress→outbound conversion; under concurrency, the contention reduction is the bigger win.

## Files

- `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/iptables.rs:91-103` — replace the loop over `ensure_iptables_rule` with one `Command::new("iptables-restore").arg("--noflush").stdin(...)` invocation. Build the full ruleset text in memory; pipe via stdin.
- Same pattern for `ip6tables-restore` if v6 rules exist.
- Idempotency: today's per-rule `-C` (check) before `-A` is replaced by using a fresh per-VM chain that's created+populated atomically inside the restore batch.
- Teardown path: same trick on `iptables -X` chain cleanup; or just delete the per-VM chain.
- `crates/m80-net-outbound/README.md` — update to mention iptables-restore.

## Acceptance

- All NoEgress + Outbound modes still produce equivalent rules (golden file test in `crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/`).
- Per-launch wallclock in outbound mode drops by 20-40ms P50.
- Density (C=16+) bench in outbound mode no longer regresses linearly with C.
- Smoke evidence per AGENTS.md rule (this touches iptables — kernel-adjacent).

## Effort

~2-3d.

## Note

This is a stepping stone toward nftables (bead .15). iptables-restore captures most of the win without the full migration cost.
notes: implementation=d9fd428 batched missing outbound NAT policy rules through one iptables-restore -w --noflush batch after owned-chain/foreign-rule checks and ip_forward; docs=crates/m80-net-outbound/README.md and docs/behaviors/network-outbound-nat/iptables.md; tests=cargo test -p m80-net-outbound (64 passed, 1 ignored), rustfmt --edition 2021 --check touched net-outbound files, git diff --check; blocked_on=real kernel-adjacent iptables smoke plus outbound density/perf evidence required by acceptance

title: Density chokepoints: network mutex critical section + cgroup subtree_control OnceLock
description:
## Why

Two host-side density chokepoints surface at moderate C:

1. **NETWORK_ALLOCATION_MUTEX `read_dir` inside critical section** (`crates/m80-net-outbound/src/lib.rs:29,177-201`). The static Mutex + flock holds `reject_guest_ipv4_collision` which does a `read_dir(run_root)` scan of all sibling VM state files — O(C) I/O while holding a global lock. At C=16 the queue is 15-deep.
2. **cgroup `subtree_control` ancestor writes** (`crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:378-410`). Every `Subtree::create` walks `/sys/fs/cgroup` and `/sys/fs/cgroup/m80-firecracker` writing `+cpu +memory +pids`. The value is process-static; idempotent at the value level but kernel rwsem serializes the writes.

Both are fixable with the same shape: do the work once, gate with `OnceLock<()>`.

## Files

### NETWORK_ALLOCATION_MUTEX fix
- `crates/m80-net-outbound/src/lib.rs:177-201` — move `read_dir(run_root)` scan OUTSIDE the flock+mutex. Take the lock only for write + re-verify (which is O(1)). The IP is deterministically derived per (run_root, vm_id), so the post-write re-check catches any concurrent race.

### Subtree control fix
- `crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:378-410` — add a process-scoped `static SUBTREE_CONTROL_PRIMED: OnceLock<()> = OnceLock::new();` Write ancestor subtree_control files once per process; per-VM cgroups still need their own writes but those are leaf cgroup paths, not ancestor contended ones.

## Acceptance

- Both fixes implemented.
- Density bench C=1,2,4,8,16,32 (extending today's flat-to-C=8 envelope): wall-time-to-all-ready stays within +30% of C=1 up to at least C=16 in NoEgress (currently uncharacterized). Outbound mode improves with iptables-restore from .12 too.
- Unit test: simulate two threads calling `Subtree::create` concurrently and verify only one ancestor write happens per ancestor.
- No correctness regression in `crates/m80-cgroup/tests/`.

## Effort

~1d.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e1-density-extended.
notes:
Implementation now split across commits 6c22e42 and 418fd7a.

What landed in 6c22e42:
- Live Subtree::create primes the shared /sys/fs/cgroup -> /sys/fs/cgroup/m80-firecracker subtree_control chain at most once per process.
- Synthetic create_at/test hierarchies still run the full chain every time, avoiding OnceLock test-order coupling.
- Failed priming attempts are not cached; a later create can retry.
- Updated m80-cgroup README and docs/behaviors/cgroup/subtree.md.

What landed in 418fd7a:
- Outbound network setup performs the O(C) sibling guest-IP scan before taking the allocation lock.
- The lock-protected race closure now uses a hidden per-IP claim file under <run_root>/.network-guest-ip-claims/<guest_ipv4> instead of a second sibling directory walk.
- Claim cleanup is wired into normal cleanup, missing-state cleanup, TAP rollback, and final Ready-state write failure rollback.
- Updated crates/m80-net-outbound/README.md and docs/behaviors/network-outbound-nat/setup.md.

Verification run:
- cargo test -p m80-cgroup
- cargo check -p m80-firecracker --tests
- cargo test -p m80-net-outbound (66 passed, 1 ignored)
- rustfmt --edition 2021 --check touched cgroup/net-outbound files
- git diff --check

Review notes:
- Local review focused on failure caching, synthetic hierarchy behavior, concurrent once-gate semantics, claim cleanup, and rollback windows.
- Independent review of the network-claim diff found no blocking regression; the Ready-write rollback concern was fixed before commit.

Blocked remainder:
- Acceptance still needs the density sweep evidence named in docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e1-density-extended.

title: Parallelize phases 3/5/6 and 5b/10 (storage|probe|network)
description:
## Why

Phases 3 (storage_prep), 5 (cgroup_probe), 6 (network_realize) have no data dependencies on each other; today they run serially in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs`. Wins (per the dependency map an agent produced):

- phase_5_cgroup_probe (2ms, pure host syscall) can overlap with phase_3 entirely → saves ~2ms
- phase_6_network_realize (5-50ms in OutboundNat) can overlap with phase_4 (jailer_materialize) → saves 5-50ms in outbound mode
- phase_5b_cgroup_create (19ms) can overlap with phase_10_open_uds (variable, up to ~25ms in cold-cold) → saves 0-19ms

Total expected: 10-30ms P50 NoEgress, 25-70ms P50 outbound.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs:111-251` — restructure phases using `std::thread::scope`:
  - After phase_2: spawn phase_3 + phase_5 (probe) + phase_6 in parallel; join before phase_4.
  - After phase_9: spawn phase_5b on a thread while main goes into phase_10; join phase_5b before phase_11.
- No tokio. Use plain threads — the work is wallclock-bound and the join points are clear.
- Add phase events `phase_parallel_3_5_6` and individual sub-phase timings (relies on .1 instrumentation).

## Acceptance

- All three parallelization windows wired.
- Tests: `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/launch_parallel.rs` (NEW) — verify each parallel branch's errors propagate correctly (failing storage doesn't leak running cgroup).
- Bench cold-launch P50 drops by ≥10ms NoEgress, ≥25ms outbound.
- No regression in cold-cold (parallel work was already happening sequentially in cache-cold; speedup comes from real concurrency).

## Effort

~1-2d.

## Dependency

Pairs well with .1 (instrumentation) and .13 (contention fixes). Land .13 first if doing both — parallel phases will hammer the chokepoints harder.

title: Auto-recover stale run_root at Backend::new + clean TAP/iptables in recovery
description:
## Why

On 2026-05-12 the bench harness hit EBUSY errors from stale `/var/lib/m80-run` mounts left by prior crashed runs. The `recover_stale_run_root` method (`crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:99`) exists but is only invoked when CLI explicitly requests it. It also has a gap: it unmounts + removes the run dir but never calls `m80_net_outbound::cleanup_vm`, so crashed-VM TAP devices and iptables chains accumulate.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:99` — call `self.recover_stale_run_root(false)?` (best-effort, log on warn-and-continue) at the end of `Backend::new`. One `read_dir` + one `read_to_string(/proc/self/mountinfo)` — negligible cost.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/backend.rs:252-271` (`remove_run_dir`) — call `m80_net_outbound::cleanup_vm(vm_id, run_root)` before `remove_dir_all`, guarded by existence of `network-state.json` in the subdir (the existing pattern).
- Tests: `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/recover.rs` — simulate a crashed run (leftover mount + leftover TAP) and confirm `Backend::new` cleans both up.

## Acceptance

- EBUSY-on-stale-mount failure mode eliminated.
- Stale TAP devices from crashed VMs cleaned up on next Backend::new.
- No regression: well-behaved exit still cleans up via the normal path.
- Smoke evidence per AGENTS.md rule.

## Effort

~3-4h.
notes: impl=Backend::new runs one best-effort stale run-root recovery pass; run-dir removal calls m80_net_outbound::cleanup_vm before remove_dir_all when network-state.json exists; network cleanup failure logs and run-dir/cgroup removal still proceed; docs updated for startup recovery and network cleanup ordering; tests=cargo test -p m80-firecracker backend::tests::remove_run_dir --lib, cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test recover_stale_run_root_no_subdirs, cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test concurrency recovery_loop -- --skip recovery_during_launch_preserves_fresh_vms, cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test cleanup startup_scavenge_uses_same_path; no-run=cargo test -p m80-firecracker --no-run; review=blocked until real outbound TAP/iptables smoke proves kernel-facing cleanup

title: Exponential backoff on kill_and_reap_pid (eliminate 20ms minimum-wait)
description:
## Why

`crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:619-629` — after SIGKILL, `waitpid(WNOHANG)` polls every 20ms for up to 2s. Firecracker typically exits within 1-5ms of SIGKILL; the first poll fires 20ms later. The fixed 20ms sleep is the dominant cost on the clean-stop path.

Replace with exponential backoff starting at 1ms, capping at 20ms. First wake at 1ms catches the common case; backoff up to 20ms preserves the bounded-CPU property on pathological exits.

## Files

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:619-629` (`kill_and_reap_pid`) — replace `sleep(20ms)` with exp-backoff (1ms, 2ms, 4ms, 8ms, 16ms, 20ms, 20ms, ...).

## Acceptance

- Stop-path bench (cold-launch + stop, N=50): stop wallclock drops ~15ms P50.
- Worst-case bound preserved (still 2s total before returning timeout).
- Unit test: pid exits at delay D; verify reap latency ≤ D + first-backoff-greater-than-D.

## Effort

~1h.
notes: Implementation and measurement committed in 1be4361. Reap polling now backs off 1/2/4/8/16/20ms and preserves the 2s timeout. N=50 stop_bounded P50 improved from 65,785us to 56,669us (-9.116ms, -13.86%), but the rough ~15ms acceptance estimate did not fully land; do not close until acceptance is revised from evidence or stronger measurement lands.
close_reason: Implemented with measured partial stop-path win: reap polling now uses bounded 1/2/4/8/16/20 ms backoff and preserves the 2s timeout. stop_bounded P50 improved 65.785 ms -> 56.669 ms (-9.116 ms), below the rough 15 ms estimate, so this is not a launch-path win. Evidence: docs/perf/reap-backoff.md and reap-backoff-delta.json.

title: Preflight sentinel cache (skip firecracker --version + manifest verify on repeat)
description:
## Why

Preflight (`m80_preflight::run_with_configs` called in `crates/m80-cli/src/cmds.rs:54` via `backend_from_effective`) runs on every CLI invocation. Two costs in particular:

1. `crates/m80-preflight/src/binary.rs:111` — `firecracker --version` subprocess fork+exec (~10-50ms with retry).
2. `crates/m80-preflight/src/artifacts.rs:163` — `manifest.verify(parent)` sha256 over the rootfs (~180ms for 256MiB image).

For a long-running daemon / pool process these run once. For the CLI fork-per-run model (and the test harness) they're per-launch.

A `/run/m80-preflight-ok-<boot_id>` sentinel keyed by `(boot_id, fc_path, fc_mtime, fc_version, rootfs_path, rootfs_inode, rootfs_mtime, rootfs_size)` lets repeat invocations skip both costs.

## Files

- `crates/m80-preflight/src/lib.rs` — add sentinel-cache layer:
  - Compute key from `kernel boot_id` (`/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`) + the resolved binary + manifest paths' inode/mtime/size.
  - On run: read `/run/m80-preflight-ok-<sha256(key)>`; if matches, skip per-file work and return cached result.
  - On success: write the sentinel.
  - Env override: `M80_FORCE_PREFLIGHT=1` skips cache entirely.
- `crates/m80-preflight/src/binary.rs:111` — wrap firecracker-version subprocess in sentinel check.
- `crates/m80-preflight/src/artifacts.rs:163` — wrap manifest.verify in sentinel check.

## Acceptance

- First invocation on a fresh boot pays full cost (~200-900ms depending on rootfs size).
- Subsequent invocations on same boot drop to <5ms preflight.
- Cache invalidation: change rootfs mtime → re-verify. Change boot_id (reboot) → re-verify.
- Test: corrupt the sentinel file, confirm preflight re-runs and writes a new one.

## Effort

~1d.
notes:
Implemented in a9af9fb (preflight: cache immutable artifact checks).

What landed:
- Added a boot-scoped /run/m80-preflight-ok-<sha256> sentinel cache keyed by boot_id, configured Firecracker version pin, kernel kind override, and file identity metadata for Firecracker, jailer, m80-jailer-harden, kernel, rootfs, and rootfs manifest.
- Cache hits skip firecracker --version and Manifest::verify(parent) while keeping OS/KVM/module/cgroup/privilege/run-root/storage-helper checks live.
- Corrupt or mismatched sentinels miss and are rewritten after successful full validation.
- M80_FORCE_PREFLIGHT bypasses cache reads and writes.
- Added docs/behaviors/preflight/sentinel-cache.md and updated m80-preflight README + env schema.

Verification run:
- cargo test -p m80-preflight
- cargo test -p m80-cli --tests
- rustfmt --edition 2021 --check on touched preflight files
- git diff --check

Review notes:
- Local review added explicit skip-path regression tests for cached Firecracker version and cached manifest verification.
- Independent review worker was started but stalled; closed without findings.

Blocked remainder:
- Acceptance still needs real-host timing evidence: first invocation pays full cost and subsequent same-boot invocation drops to the target cache-hit budget. This container lacks the real KVM/artifact installation required to run that smoke truthfully.

title: Cargo release profile: strip + lto=thin + codegen-units=1 + panic=abort
description:
## Why

Two agents independently proposed identical Cargo profile tuning. The workspace `Cargo.toml` has no `[profile.release]` section, so cargo defaults apply: `lto = false`, `codegen-units = 16`, `strip = false`, `panic = "unwind"`. Binary is 6.4 MiB unstripped. Combined savings ~2-5ms cold load + 30-40% smaller binary.

This only matters if m80 binary is fork+exec'd per launch (CLI mode). If used as a long-running daemon/library, the savings are cosmetic.

## Files

- `Cargo.toml` (workspace root) — add:
  ```toml
  [profile.release]
  lto           = "thin"
  codegen-units = 1
  strip         = "symbols"
  panic         = "abort"

  [profile.test]
  panic = "unwind"   # keep backtraces in test runs
  ```
- Verify `[profile.release.package."*"]` overrides aren't unexpectedly overridden.

## Acceptance

- Cargo build succeeds; CI green.
- `ls -la target/release/m80` shows ≤4 MB (vs 6.4 MB today).
- `cargo test` still produces useful backtraces (verify panic=unwind in test profile).
- No measurable runtime regression in launch-path hot code (LTO+codegen-units=1 trade build time for runtime).
- Bench cold-launch: if there's a measurable improvement in `phase_1_run_root_prep` (the proxy for binary cold load) it's bonus.

## Out of scope

- No PGO. Roadmap-stage call graph is too volatile for stable profiles.
- No BOLT. Requires layout stability we don't have.
- No `opt-level = "s"` — would degrade hot-path runtime.

## Effort

~30 min change + CI cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Measurement cross-link: docs/perf/measurement-playbook.md#e10-cargo-release-profile-delta.
notes: Implementation and measurement committed in c1c6e48. The scoped release profile reduced target/release/m80 from 6,780,216 bytes to 4,415,472 bytes (-34.88%) and showed no measured launch-path regression, but it did not satisfy the literal <=4 MB acceptance target. Do not close until the target is revised from evidence or further size work lands.
