title: Add publish=false workspace-wide; reconcile version 0.0.0 vs git tag v0.2.6 mismatch
description:
**Finding (W45.9 + W45.10):**

HIGH (operational risk):
- No crate — workspace or member — sets publish = false. A `cargo publish` (intentional or CI accident) would push all 21 members to crates.io. m80 is a v0.x internal crate set per CLAUDE.md "closed call graph — we own every consumer".

MEDIUM (versioning drift):
- workspace.package.version = "0.0.0" inherited by all 21 members. Git tags reach v0.2.6 with several intermediate releases. Two independent versioning schemes.
- Decide: bump workspace version to match tags (e.g., 0.2.6) OR document intentional "0.0.0 = pre-pub" in Cargo.toml comment.

LOW (workspace.package metadata gaps applicable to all 20 members):
- readme not set anywhere; cosmetic.
- keywords, categories missing; would be required before public release.
- authors, description missing from workspace.package.

NULL: license/repository/description PRESENT on all 20 members via workspace.package.

Severity: HIGH (publish-safety gap).

Acceptance:
- Add `publish = false` to [workspace.package] in root Cargo.toml. Cargo 1.75+ supports it; current MSRV is 1.82 so it's available.
- Optionally add `publish.workspace = true` to each member for explicit inheritance.
- Bump workspace.package.version to 0.2.6 (current tag) OR add code comment explaining 0.0.0 intent.
- Add readme/keywords/categories before any external release (defer until that need arrives).

title: Inter-crate cycle: m80-cgroup ↔ m80-jailer in runtime dependencies
description:
**Finding (W45.2):** Genuine runtime dependency cycle between m80-cgroup and m80-jailer.

- crates/m80-cgroup/Cargo.toml [dependencies] m80-jailer.workspace = true
- crates/m80-jailer/Cargo.toml [dependencies] m80-cgroup.workspace = true

Cargo resolves it because both live in the same workspace, but it is a layering design flaw. cgroup managing jailer state, or jailer managing cgroup paths — at least one direction is wrong.

Likely fix paths:
a) Move shared types (e.g., cgroup path helpers, jailer state references) into a third crate (but CLAUDE.md forbids junk-drawer crates like m80-common/-shared/-utils — so this isn't open).
b) Pick the canonical direction (probably jailer → cgroup, since cgroup is lower-level) and inline-or-relocate the offending types in the depending crate.

ALSO (lower-impact dep graph notes):
- m80-firecracker has 12 runtime inter-crate deps. De-facto integration layer; fan-out is wide. Any leaf change recompiles the whole chain. Acceptable for v0.x; flag for refactor when build times bite.
- High-centrality nodes: m80-proto (7 dependents), m80-image-manifest (4), m80-test-helpers (4 dev-only).
- m80-jailer-harden → m80-close-range (in support/, workspace-excluded). Invisible to `cargo tree`; fragile path.

Severity: MEDIUM (cycle is real but quietly resolved by Cargo; refactoring may surface broader layout issues).

Acceptance:
- Audit what specifically m80-cgroup pulls from m80-jailer (likely state inspection paths or path helpers).
- Decide direction; move the offending types.
- Make the change in a single focused PR with full workspace cargo build + clippy + test gate.
- This touches cgroup wrapper code — per CLAUDE.md, sweep-ineligible. Single-purpose diff with smoke evidence required.

title: net-outbound ensure_bridge_ready_with_ops missing Planned recovery guard
description:
site: crates/m80-net-outbound/src/lib.rs:255 (around the SetupPhase::Ready branch)
finder: trim-the-fat r5

Problem: `ensure_bridge_ready_with_ops` checks if existing state is Ready and returns early. But for SetupPhase::Planned (state file says Planned but kernel may already have the bridge from a prior crashed attempt), there's no early-detect: the function falls through to `create_bridge()` which may fail with EEXIST or — worse — collide with a partial bridge. Recovery from partial-failure is untested.

Fix: add a Planned-phase branch that probes the kernel for the bridge by name; if present and matches identity, transition state to Ready without re-creating. If absent, proceed with create. Add a regression test for the partial-failure recovery scenario (state file Planned, bridge half-created, retry should converge).
notes: root=SetupPhase::Planned retry fell through to create_bridge even when the bridge already existed from a prior partial attempt. fix=LinkOps::link_exists plus recover_planned_bridge converges existing/absent Planned bridge state to Ready without blind recreate. docs=crates/m80-net-outbound/README.md. test=crates/m80-net-outbound/tests/network-outbound-nat/setup.rs::planned_bridge_state_recovers_existing_kernel_bridge_without_recreate. verification=cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; git diff --check

title: Comprehensive m80-jailer vs Firecracker-jailer audit (produce findings doc)
description:
Perform the side-by-side audit of m80-jailer (crates/m80-jailer/src/) against Firecracker's jailer (/tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/) per the brief at /tmp/m80-jailer-audit-brief.md. Produce docs/audit/jailer-vs-firecracker.md as the deliverable. Use audit findings to confirm or grow the jailer-hardening epic set (m80-jmqg, m80-8o58, m80-16oi, m80-isxo, m80-bcb6, m80-3c9b).

## Audit checklist (from brief)

### Already-hypothesized gaps — confirm with file:line refs
- m80-jmqg pivot_root + mount NS — FC chroot.rs and env.rs:644-676
- m80-8o58 setrlimit — FC resource_limits.rs and env.rs:654
- m80-16oi mknod — FC env.rs:422-452 (mknod_and_own_dev) and 684-711
- m80-isxo CLONE_NEWPID — FC env.rs:328-383 (exec_into_new_pid_ns)
- m80-bcb6 binary copy vs bind-mount — FC env.rs:468-518 (copy_exec_to_chroot)
- m80-3c9b daemonize — FC env.rs:662-669 (dev_null) and 716+ (double fork)

### Architectural divergence (probably not a gap, document and dismiss or escalate)
- netns joining via setns(CLONE_NEWNET) — FC env.rs:520-532. m80 handles networking via m80-net-outbound (different model). Decide whether to track or formally rule out.

### Items not yet captured as epics — verify and file beads if real gaps
- Bind-mount option flags MS_NODEV | MS_NOEXEC | MS_NOSUID parity on m80's bind mounts.
- O_NOFOLLOW usage to prevent symlink attacks during file operations within the jailer.
- 0o700 + chown(uid,gid) permissions model on jail folder (FC: setup_jailed_folder).
- cgroup configuration parity — m80 uses cgroups, may not match FC's per-controller property setup. FC: cgroup.rs.
- /proc/self and /proc/sys handling inside the jail.
- CLI argument validation parity from FC main.rs (anything m80-jailer should validate by analogue).

### m80 advantages (worth documenting, FC lacks these)
- Plan persistence + jailer-state.json crash recovery.
- Deterministic, replayable plan steps (pure data first, materialize after).
- Drop-based cleanup via MaterializedJail.
- recover.rs orphan inspector distinguishes live vs orphaned jails.

## Output document shape

docs/audit/jailer-vs-firecracker.md with sections:
1. Methodology and source pointers (both repos, exact files).
2. Confirmed gaps — for each: FC behavior + line refs, m80 behavior, security/durability implication, suggested approach, effort (low/medium/high).
3. Newly-discovered gaps — same shape, plus a recommendation on bead-creation.
4. Architectural divergences (not gaps).
5. m80 advantages.
6. Priority ordering (security impact × effort) and recommended sequence.
7. Cross-references to filed epics (m80-jmqg, m80-8o58, m80-16oi, m80-isxo, m80-bcb6, m80-3c9b).

## Source files to read (in order, per brief)

2. /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/chroot.rs (pivot_root)
3. /tank/projects/m80/crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs (materialize)
4. /tank/projects/m80/crates/m80-jailer/src/types.rs
5. /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/resource_limits.rs
6. /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/cgroup.rs
7. /tank/projects/m80/crates/m80-jailer/src/recover.rs
8. /tank/projects/firecracker/src/jailer/src/main.rs

## Acceptance
- docs/audit/jailer-vs-firecracker.md exists with all 7 sections populated.
- Each gap (filed and newly-discovered) has FC file:line, m80 behavior, and recommendation.
- Each newly-discovered actionable gap has either a filed bead ID or a closed-with-reason note.

title: Shared-rootfs warm pool: layered images + DAX-shared toolchains + snapshot-restore
description:
## Purpose

m80 needs to deliver large read-only artifacts such as toolchains and base data to many concurrent Firecracker guests without copying bytes into every rootfs or guest page cache, and it needs a path to low-latency warm leases. This super-epic tracks that work after the Phase 0 real-KVM PoC and the completed implementation slices.

The current architecture has three independent axes:

1. **Writable rootfs state**: shared read-only base rootfs plus a per-VM writable overlay. Phase A optimizes only the empty overlay-template clone: mandatory reflink on capable host filesystems, explicit byte-copy fallback otherwise. The old "full per-VM base rootfs copy" model is not the target.
2. **Read-only data delivery**: no pmem layers, `PmemSharing::PerVm`, or `PmemSharing::Shared(TrustDomainAck)`. PerVm gives each VM its own backing inode; Shared deliberately reuses one canonical image-store inode and is same-trust-domain only.
3. **Warm lease mechanism**: boot-fill fallback or snapshot-template restore. Snapshot templates are fingerprinted artifacts with stable backing paths and host-driven post-restore hooks before lease hand-back.

## Current state

- **Phase 0 PoC is closed.** It proved erofs over virtio-pmem with DAX on the rebuilt stripped kernel, proved snapshot/restore preserves an already-mounted pmem erofs layer when the backing path is stable, and proved Firecracker emits VMGenID updates that the current stripped guest kernel cannot consume because ACPI/VMGENID is absent.
- **Phase A is closed.** The live rootfs path is shared base plus gated overlay-template clone; the real-KVM divergence smoke showed overlay growth while the template stayed unchanged.
- **Phase B is closed.** `PmemLayer` / `PmemSharing::PerVm`, image-store artifacts, pmem jail bindings, Firecracker `PUT /pmem`, guestd erofs+DAX mount handling, fail-closed validation, docs, and real-KVM e2e are landed.
- **Phase C is implemented except for its verified density close.** `PmemSharing::Shared`, `TrustDomainAck`, shared active-use markers, docs, and non-density e2e are landed. `m80-q420k.8.12` resolved the erofs DAX layout gate: Shared density artifacts must use an uncompressed, non-inlined erofs payload layout that reports guest-visible DAX. `m80-q420k.3.8` remains blocked until a quiet real-KVM host produces a committed N>=10 density artifact at `docs/perf/pmem-shared-density.md`.
- **Phase D is implemented except for its verified latency close.** Snapshot-template lifecycle, content-addressed template store, host-driven post-restore hooks, template build path, warm-pool integration, docs, and real-KVM scenario coverage are landed. `m80-q420k.4.15` remains open until a quiet real-KVM host produces a committed N=20 x 3 restore-to-handback artifact satisfying the <=200ms p99 observable.
- **Phase E is closed.** Image/template CLI, BootSpec configuration surface, operator docs, observability, runbooks, and migration examples are in place. Template prune is deliberately scoped by BootSpec inputs rather than broad destructive store pruning.
- **Phase F driver is implemented; closure is measurement-only.** `m80-q420k.6.1` landed the composed e2e real-KVM driver and fixture. `m80-q420k.6.2` through `.6.5` remain blocked until a quiet real-KVM run emits the three committed artifacts for restore latency, host memory delta, and residue, and `docs/perf/composed-e2e.md` interprets them with smoke evidence. Proxy, mock, noisy-host, and calibration runs do not close it.
- **Phase G is a follow-up holding area and is not on the A-F close path.** `.8.12` was the only Phase G item that gated the Phase C/F memory-sharing claims, and it is closed. Open Phase G measurements such as `.8.9` and `.8.16` are optional follow-ups unless their results create new blocker beads.

## Substrate facts from Phase 0

- Firecracker does not support virtio-fs; the design uses virtio-pmem for read-only layer delivery.
- The pinned rebuilt stripped kernel supports erofs, virtio-pmem, libnvdimm, block pmem, and filesystem DAX. Guest mounts use erofs with `dax=always`.
- Snapshot restore preserves the pmem device and already-mounted erofs DAX filesystem when the backing host path is stable.
- Firecracker v1.15.1 logs VMGenID changes on restore, but the current stripped guest kernel has no guest-observable VMGenID counter. Phase D uses host-driven `PostRestoreHookRequest` plus explicit guest `RNDRESEEDCRNG`; it must not block on `/sys/class/misc/vmgenid/generation_counter`.
- Phase 0 N=4 memory numbers and N=10 load API timings are calibration only. They do not close Phase C or F measurement beads.

## Target API direction

```rust
struct PmemLayer {
    image: ErofsImageRef,
    sharing: PmemSharing,
    mount_at: GuestMountPath,
}

enum PmemSharing {
    PerVm,
    Shared(TrustDomainAck),
}

enum WarmStrategy {
    BootFill,
    SnapshotRestore {
        template: TemplateRef,
        hooks: HookSpecSet,
    },
}
```

`TrustDomainAck` is a typed witness carrying a finite `TrustReason`. `HookSpec` is a closed typed enum; arbitrary post-restore shell/user commands are rejected unless a future bead proves typed variants cannot cover a real need.

## Phasing

- **Phase A — Reflink overlay-template clone**: closed.
- **Phase B — `PmemLayer` + `PmemSharing::PerVm`**: closed.
- **Phase C — `PmemSharing::Shared` opt-in**: open for verified density artifact on the `.8.12`-valid erofs layout.
- **Phase D — Snapshot-template warm pool**: open for verified restore-latency artifact.
- **Phase E — UX surface**: closed.
- **Phase F — Composed e2e**: open for quiet-host measurement artifacts and composed receipt.
- **Phase G — Follow-up questions**: rolling holding area; currently outside the A-F close path.

## Doctrine

This path is kernel-touching: pmem device attach, guest DAX mounts, jail bindings, snapshot capture/restore, hook sequencing, and smoke scripts all inherit the real-KVM evidence rule. Audit sweeps are not eligible for kernel/cgroup/seccomp/capability/sudo/smoke hunks. Measurement-shaped beads close only with committed real-substrate artifacts per ADR 0002.

Shared pmem is same-trust-domain only. The DAX/cache-timing side channel is load-bearing design context, not incidental documentation.

## References

- `docs/perf/erofs-dax-sharing-layout.md`
- `docs/future-directions/pmem-and-warm-templates.md`
- `docs/decisions/0006-pmemlayer-api.md`
- `docs/behaviors/warm-pool/vmgenid-reseed-path.md`
- `docs/decisions/0002-bead-closure-scaffolded-vs-verified.md`
- `docs/decisions/0003-audit-sweep-eligibility.md`
- `docs/postmortems/2026-05-12-ms-bind-and-sudo-escape.md`

title: Phase A — Gated reflink overlay-template clone (XFS/Btrfs CoW; ext4 fallback)
description:
## Scope

Refine `m80-storage::rootfs` overlay allocation, not the base-rootfs path. Live code already uses a shared read-only base plus a per-VM writable overlay; there is no per-VM base copy left to optimize. Phase A makes the run-root-local empty overlay-template clone explicit: mandatory reflink on capable host filesystems and explicit byte-copy fallback on non-reflink filesystems.

## Why

This is the cheapest storage-side launch improvement still left after the shared-base pivot. The optimization keeps the public `Rootfs::prepare` shape and makes operator observability honest: reflink-capable hosts get metadata-only overlay clones; ext4/tmpfs/overlayfs hosts still work through a permanent byte-copy path with a single fallback event.

## What changed

- `crates/m80-storage/src/reflink.rs` — per-device runtime capability probe using statfs + safe FICLONE.
- `crates/m80-storage/src/rootfs.rs` — gated overlay-template clone path: `cp --reflink=always --sparse=auto` or `cp --reflink=never --sparse=always`.
- `crates/m80-storage/README.md` and `docs/behaviors/storage/reflink-rootfs.md` — contract and behavior capture.
- `crates/m80-storage/tests/reflink_probe.rs` and `crates/m80-storage/tests/reflink_rootfs.rs` — probe, fallback, event-dedupe, and concurrent-fill coverage.
- `scripts/smoke.sh` and `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/reflink_rootfs_real_kvm.rs` — optional real-KVM divergence proof.

## Acceptance

- [x] Reflink-cloning lands behind a per-device probe gate; ext4/tmpfs/overlayfs byte-copy fallback works and is observable.
- [x] Behavior doc at `docs/behaviors/storage/reflink-rootfs.md`.
- [x] Storage tests cover detect + clone + fallback + concurrent fill.
- [x] Real-KVM smoke: boot from a prepared overlay, write inside the guest, and verify host-side overlay/template divergence. Smoke passed 2026-05-16: overlay 1→32929 blocks, template 145→145 blocks, `REFLINK_DIVERGENCE_OK`.
- [x] No public API change; `BootSpec` untouched.

## Doctrine

This does not reintroduce the old full base-rootfs copy model. The shared base remains the only base image path; this phase only governs how the empty writable overlay template becomes each per-VM overlay.
close_reason: Phase A complete: gated reflink overlay-template clone implemented, documented, covered by storage tests, and verified by real-KVM divergence smoke (overlay 1->32929 blocks, template 145->145 blocks, REFLINK_DIVERGENCE_OK); all children m80-q420k.1.1-.1.5 closed

title: m80-storage: add reflink capability probe (statfs + safe FICLONE) with process-lifetime memoization
description:
## Why

Phase A needs a per-device gate for the overlay-template clone path. Probing on every `Rootfs::prepare` would be wasteful and noisy; the result is stable enough for the process lifetime on the run-root device.

## What to touch

- New module `crates/m80-storage/src/reflink.rs` with crate-private typed results:
  - `ReflinkCapability::{Supported, Unsupported, ProbeFailed}`
  - `UnsupportedReason::{FsTypeKnownNoReflink, FicloneRejected, CrossDevice, Other}`
  - `FsKind` for XFS, Btrfs, ext*, tmpfs, overlayfs, FUSE, ZFS, and unknown types
  - `probe_for(dir)` for direct statfs + safe FICLONE probing
  - `probe_cached_for(parent_dir)` memoized per `st_dev` through `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<...>>>`
- Root `Cargo.toml` and `crates/m80-storage/Cargo.toml`: add `rustix` through workspace deps for the safe `ioctl_ficlone` wrapper. The workspace forbids unsafe code; do not use a raw nix ioctl call here.
- `crates/m80-storage/tests/reflink_probe.rs`: tmpfs known-unsupported classification, parseable tempdir result, same-device memoization.

## Acceptance

- [x] `reflink.rs` exposes crate-private probe/cached-probe helpers and typed sub-reasons.
- [x] ext2/ext3/ext4/tmpfs/overlayfs/FUSE short-circuit as known non-reflink.
- [x] XFS/Btrfs/ZFS/unknown filesystems run a same-directory safe FICLONE probe and report `Supported` only when it succeeds.
- [x] Memoized per `st_dev` for the process lifetime.
- [x] `tests/reflink_probe.rs` covers tmpfs classification, memoization by device ID, and default tempdir no-panic behavior.
- [x] No unsafe code and no public API change.

## E2E note

Scaffolding only; Task 2 wires the probe into `Rootfs::prepare`. Real smoke later proved this host ZFS supports mandatory reflink, so ZFS must be probed rather than hard-classified as unsupported.
close_reason: implemented crate-private reflink probe in crates/m80-storage/src/reflink.rs using statfs classification plus rustix safe FICLONE probe; memoized by st_dev; tests: cargo test -p m80-storage (3 reflink_probe tests plus full storage suite)

title: m80-storage: gate overlay clone with --reflink=always/never + single tracing event on fallback
description:
## Why

Today `clone_template` used `cp --reflink=auto`, which silently fell back on unsupported filesystems with no observability. Phase A demands mandatory reflink on capable hosts and a clean byte-copy path with a single tracing event on fallback so operators can confirm reflinks are active.

## What to touch

- `crates/m80-storage/src/rootfs.rs`:
  - Route through `reflink::probe_cached_for(template.parent())`.
  - On `Supported`, invoke `cp --reflink=always --sparse=auto template dest`. GNU `cp` rejects mandatory reflink with `--sparse=always`; real ZFS smoke proved `--sparse=auto` is the correct mandatory-reflink form.
  - On `Unsupported`/`ProbeFailed`, invoke `cp --reflink=never --sparse=always template dest`.
  - Runtime mandatory-reflink rejection emits one `tracing::warn!` for that call and retries byte-copy.
  - Unsupported/probe-failed branch emits one `tracing::info!` per dev_id per process with `mode="byte_copy"`.
- `crates/m80-storage/tests/rootfs_prepare.rs` and `crates/m80-storage/tests/reflink_rootfs.rs`: pin fallback and event-dedupe behavior.
- `crates/m80-storage/README.md`: document the explicit gate.

## Acceptance

- [x] `clone_template` routes to `--reflink=always --sparse=auto` or `--reflink=never --sparse=always` based on `probe_cached_for`.
- [x] Runtime `cp --reflink=always` failure with reflink-rejection signature emits one warn then byte-copies; non-reflink failures propagate.
- [x] Unsupported branch emits exactly one `mode=byte_copy` info event per dev_id per process.
- [x] Storage tests cover non-reflink fallback and single-event emission.
- [x] README `Rootfs::prepare` paragraph reflects gated behavior.

## Smoke note

Real-KVM smoke belongs to Task 5.
close_reason: wired Rootfs::prepare overlay-template clone through probe_cached_for: Supported uses cp --reflink=always, unsupported/probe-failed uses cp --reflink=never with per-device info event, mandatory reflink rejection warns once and retries byte-copy; README updated; tests: cargo test -p m80-storage, cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check

title: m80-storage: add concurrent-fill regression test for reflink clone path
description:
## Why

Phase A acceptance enumerates "8 reflink clones created in parallel from one base; no corruption, all VMs boot, all writes isolated" (scenario 4). Existing `prepare_creates_template_metadata_once_and_reuses_it` exercises the template-lock serialization but NOT the **clone** step under contention or per-clone independence. Pins concurrent-fill at the storage-crate boundary so regressions surface in `cargo test`, not production.

## What to touch

- New test file `crates/m80-storage/tests/reflink_rootfs.rs` (phase scope names this exact path):
  - `concurrent_fill_produces_eight_independent_overlays`: spawn 8 OS threads, each calls `Rootfs::prepare(&base, &per_vm_overlay, 64 MiB)` against a shared run-root tempdir. Assert (a) each overlay exists with expected apparent size, (b) all 8 are sparse, (c) template created exactly once (single `.rootfs-overlay-template-v1-*.ext4`), (d) no lock-file leaks, (e) writing different bytes into each overlay post-prepare leaves template byte-stream unchanged.
  - `concurrent_fill_does_not_double_emit_byte_copy_event`: on `/dev/shm` (tmpfs, guaranteed ext4-fallback) spawn 4 threads, each calls `prepare`, then assert via captured tracing events that `mode=byte_copy` info event fired exactly **once** total (dev-id-keyed dedupe from Task 2 holds under contention).
- Move `assert_sparse_file` / `assert_reflink_always_is_unsupported` helpers from `rootfs_prepare.rs` to shared `crates/m80-storage/tests/common/reflink_helpers.rs` mod; re-include via `mod common;` in both test files.
- If `tracing-subscriber` is not yet dev-dep (added by Task 2 if needed), no change here.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `tests/reflink_rootfs.rs` exists with both named tests; green on `cargo test -p m80-storage`.
- [ ] `tests/common/reflink_helpers.rs` extracts shared assertions (move-not-copy from `rootfs_prepare.rs`).
- [ ] No new public API added.
- [ ] Template-created-once invariant pinned: exactly one template file after 8 parallel `prepare` calls.

## E2E note

Covers phase-bead scenario 4 (concurrent fill) at storage-crate level. Boot-side concurrent fill is exercised in Task 5 (smoke) by running smoke N times in parallel or via existing density bench.

## Smoke note

Does NOT touch kernel-facing primitives. Cargo test only. No real-KVM smoke required.

## Dependencies

Task 2 (the single-event behavior under assertion is implemented by Task 2; tests imported from `rootfs_prepare.rs` reference the gated clone semantics).
close_reason: added crates/m80-storage/tests/reflink_rootfs.rs with 8-way concurrent Rootfs::prepare invariant and tmpfs byte-copy tracing dedupe assertion; moved reflink helpers to tests/common/reflink_helpers.rs; tests: cargo test -p m80-storage, cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check

description:
## Why

Phase A acceptance: "Real-KVM smoke: boot a reflink-cloned rootfs, write inside the guest, verify host-side CoW divergence. Smoke paste in PR." (scenario 3). The only acceptance bullet that cannot be satisfied by `cargo test`; the kernel-touching evidence per CLAUDE.md — the overlay file we boot from is the bytes the guest writes through virtio-blk. Produces the smoke artifact the bead-closure verifier reads.

## What to touch

- `scripts/smoke.sh`: append a new optional pass after default `launch → exec → stop` flow, gated by `M80_VERIFY_REFLINK_DIVERGENCE=1`:
  1. Locate per-VM overlay under `$RUN_ROOT/<vm_dir>/`.
  2. Locate template `$RUN_ROOT/.rootfs-overlay-template-v1-*.ext4`.
  3. Before guest exec: capture `stat -c '%b %B' <overlay>` (allocated 512-byte blocks) and `filefrag -v <overlay> | head -5`.
  4. Execute guest command that writes ~16 MiB into rootfs overlay (`M80_IMAGE_KIND=minimal` busybox + `dd if=/dev/urandom of=/divergence-marker bs=1M count=16`).
  5. After stop: capture stat + filefrag again. Assert allocated blocks strictly increased by ~16 MiB worth (>= 30000 512-byte blocks), extent map differs from template's. Assert `stat -c '%b' <template>` unchanged before vs after.
  6. Print labeled `REFLINK_DIVERGENCE_OK` and captured stats so PR-paste verifier can grep.
- Optionally also assert on XFS/btrfs: pre-write, overlay allocated blocks << apparent size (reflink-cloned, near-zero allocation); on ext4, allocated ~= apparent (byte-copy). Binds smoke to the gating decision from Task 2.
- `docs/perf/reflink-rootfs-smoke.md` (new) — note linking to smoke flow and reproducing the divergence check.
- `crates/m80-storage/README.md` — under "Tests" add smoke-script invocation under "Real-KVM smoke" bullet pointing at `M80_VERIFY_REFLINK_DIVERGENCE=1 ./scripts/smoke.sh`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `scripts/smoke.sh` accepts `M80_VERIFY_REFLINK_DIVERGENCE=1` and performs pre/post stat + filefrag capture + assertions.
- [ ] On XFS/btrfs host: smoke prints `REFLINK_DIVERGENCE_OK` plus pre/post block counts showing template unchanged and overlay divergence.
- [ ] On ext4 host: smoke still passes (byte-copy path), prints single `mode=byte_copy` tracing line, prints `REFLINK_DIVERGENCE_OK` (divergence check operates on overlay regardless of clone strategy).
- [ ] PR description contains green smoke paste from `/dev/kvm` host per CLAUDE.md "kernel-touching diffs require smoke evidence."
- [ ] `docs/perf/reflink-rootfs-smoke.md` documents reproduction.

## E2E note

Covers phase-bead scenario 3 (boot-from-clone with host-side CoW divergence). Also touches scenario 4 in practice: running this smoke twice in parallel covers concurrent-fill at the VM-boot level; scenario 4's primary assertion lives in Task 3's cargo test — this is corroboration.

## Smoke note

Yes, this IS the smoke task. Touches boot-from-cloned-rootfs path which transitively involves Firecracker virtio-blk attach (kernel-touching per phase doctrine). PR for this task MUST contain a smoke paste per CLAUDE.md. Per ADR 0003, sweep-ineligible — single-purpose diff only.

## Dependencies

Tasks 2 (gated clone semantics this smoke exercises) and 3 (cargo-side concurrent-fill regression should be green before asking a human to run real KVM). Lands last in the phase; its successful smoke paste is the artifact letting parent `m80-q420k.1` close.

title: Phase B — PmemLayer + PmemSharing::PerVm (erofs + virtio-pmem + DAX)
description:
## Scope

Introduce `BootSpec.pmem_layers: Vec<PmemLayer>` supporting `PmemSharing::PerVm` only. Read-only erofs images mounted via virtio-pmem with DAX inside the guest. Per-VM backing files (reflink-cloned from the source where host FS allows; full-copy otherwise). New erofs image-build tooling and content-addressed image store.

## Why

Largest single architectural step in the super-epic. Establishes the public API shape that Phases C and D extend. PerVm-first means **no trust-domain ack is required yet** — defer that lock-in to Phase C.

Per-VM pmem (without sharing) already buys real wins:

- Guest avoids double-caching toolchain bytes — working set lives in host-budgeted memory, not guest-ballooned RAM
- mmap reads bypass the guest page cache entirely
- Fast device attach + RO mount with no overlay choreography

## What to touch

- New types in m80 public API (validated at construction):
  - `PmemLayer`
  - `PmemSharing` (PerVm variant only this phase)
  - `ErofsImageRef`
  - `GuestMountPath`
  - `ImageDigest`
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs` — pmem device attach via FC API (confirm exact endpoint at impl time)
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/runroot.rs` — bind pmem backing into jail before FC start
- `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs` — jailer-plan extends to include pmem backings as host sources
- `crates/m80-guestd/` — guest mount sequence: mount erofs over pmem with `-o dax,ro` at `GuestMountPath`. Fail closed on mount error (do not finish guestd init if a declared layer fails)
- New crate: `crates/m80-image-erofs/` (image builder + store layout + CLI helpers used by Phase E)
- New doc: `docs/behaviors/rootfs/pmem-layers.md`
- New decision record: `docs/decisions/00NN-pmemlayer-api.md`
- New future-direction: `docs/future-directions/pmem-and-warm-templates.md` (created here at super-epic level, expanded in C/D)
- New future-direction (if the store grows beyond a flat dir): `docs/future-directions/image-store-layout.md`

## Validation (CLAUDE.md untrusted-input-to-kernel-primitive checklist)

Walk every item explicitly in the PR:

- **`ErofsImageRef`**: validated digest (sha256 hex, fixed length), no path components, no whitespace, no relative segments.
- **`GuestMountPath`**: canonicalized; rejected if not under an m80-approved root (e.g. `/opt/m80-layers/<name>`); rejected on `..` escape; rejected if it shadows `/`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/etc`, or any m80-owned mount.
- **`ImageDigest` → host path**: store path canonicalized before bind into jail. `O_NOFOLLOW` on any host-created placeholder.
- **Pmem device size**: derived from the erofs image's on-disk size — caller cannot influence.
- **No caller-controlled strings into kernel cmdline**: mount layout is communicated to `m80-guestd` via the existing guestd contract, not via cmdline tokens. If a cmdline token is unavoidable, it follows the m80-owned-token discipline (`m80.pmem.*` etc., admission-rejected if caller-supplied).

## E2E — new paths this phase enables (explicit)

1. **Image build**: build a small erofs image via the new image builder; confirm content-addressed storage and digest stability across rebuilds of the same source tree.
2. **PerVm mount + DAX**: boot a VM with one `PmemLayer { sharing: PerVm }`. Inside the guest, verify the layer is mounted at `GuestMountPath` with DAX flag set (e.g. `/proc/mounts` shows `dax`) and is read-only.
3. **PerVm isolation property**: two VMs declaring the same `PmemLayer { sharing: PerVm }` — verify their backing files are DISTINCT inodes on the host (the safety property that makes `PerVm` not require a trust-domain ack).
4. **No cross-VM guest cache sharing under PerVm**: read the same file from the layer in two VMs; verify the guest pages are NOT shared (also a PerVm property; matters as a baseline for the Phase C delta).
5. **Fail-closed validation**: boot with invalid `PmemLayer` — bad digest, missing image on disk, escape mount path, mount path shadowing `/proc` — each fails closed with a typed `FcError`, no jail or FC process created.
6. **No-leak teardown**: boot, exec workload that reads from the layer, teardown; verify no pmem backing file leaks into `/tmp`, `/var/run/m80`, or stray FC working directories.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `PmemLayer` / `PmemSharing::PerVm` public API lands with full validation at construction.
- [ ] Erofs image builder (crate + CLI helper) produces deterministic content-addressed images.
- [ ] Pmem device attach + guest DAX mount works on real KVM.
- [ ] All six e2e paths above pass on real KVM.
- [ ] Behavior doc + decision record + future-direction doc committed.
- [ ] Real-KVM smoke paste in PR including a multi-pmem-layer boot.
- [ ] PR description explicitly walks the CLAUDE.md untrusted-input checklist with each item ticked.

## Doctrine

Sweep-ineligible (touches in-guest mount, FC device attach, jailer plan). Real-KVM smoke mandatory. Mock-based e2e does NOT satisfy acceptance — see 2026-05-12 postmortem.

## UX implications (forward-looking → Phase E)

- CLI: `m80 image build`, `m80 image list`, `m80 image show <digest>`, `m80 image rm <digest>`, `m80 image verify <digest>`
- BootSpec config schema: `pmem_layers` shape needs YAML/JSON shape docs + examples
- Operator runbook: where erofs images come from in deployment, how to verify integrity, retention policy for the image store

## PoC back-propagation (2026-05-16)

Phase 0 evidence in `docs/poc/2026-05-16-layered-rootfs-poc-findings.md` changes the Phase B entry condition: direct Firecracker with the m80 Ubuntu guest kernel accepted `PUT /pmem/pmem0` and exposed `/dev/pmem0`, but `mount -t erofs -o dax,ro /dev/pmem0 /opt/toolchain` failed with `unknown filesystem type 'erofs'`. An ext4 pmem detour mounted with `dax=always` and ran `cargo 1.82.0`, proving pmem/DAX/toolchain content worked while erofs guest support did not. New blocker `m80-q420k.2.15` must land or explicitly redesign this phase before the erofs-only `PmemLayer` path is implemented.
notes: PoC refinement 2026-05-16: original profiles split support (Ubuntu vmlinux had pmem/ext4 DAX but no erofs; committed stripped kernel had erofs but no pmem/DAX). Follow-up m80-q420k.2.15 updated the stripped kernel config and real-KVM smoke proved /dev/pmem0 mounted as erofs with dax=always; cargo/rustc exited 0. Phase B can proceed against that pinned stripped profile, but should not claim Shared/page-cache behavior from this smoke alone. Evidence: docs/poc/2026-05-16-layered-rootfs-poc-findings.md and docs/behaviors/image-build/pmem-erofs-dax-kernel.md.
close_reason: Phase B complete: PmemLayer/PmemSharing::PerVm API, image-store erofs/ext4 artifacts, jailer pmem backing binds, Firecracker PUT /pmem, guestd PmemMountRequest DAX mount handler, phase_13 pmem guest mount, behavior docs, decision/future-direction docs, fail-closed validation tests, smoke harness, and real-KVM e2e all landed in closed children m80-q420k.2.1-.2.15. Verification highlights: cargo test -p m80-proto; cargo test -p m80-guestd --lib; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --lib; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test pmem_layers_fail_closed; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test pmem_preboot_real_kvm --no-run; cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test pmem_layer_real_kvm --no-run; cargo check -p m80-cli; cargo fmt --all -- --check; bash -n scripts/smoke.sh; shellcheck scripts/smoke.sh; git diff --check. Real-KVM evidence: M80_PMEM_LAYERS=0 launch-only baseline passed; M80_PMEM_LAYERS=1 launch-only passed with /dev/pmem0 erofs dax=always and no-leak teardown; M80_PMEM_LAYERS=2 launch-only passed with /dev/pmem0 and /dev/pmem1 erofs dax=always and no-leak teardown; pmem_layer_real_kvm ignored suite passed 4/4 for DAX mount, distinct PerVm backing inodes, nonzero per-VM pmem mapping RSS, and teardown cleanup. Untrusted-input checklist text is recorded in m80-q420k.2.14 close reason for PR description use.

title: docs/decisions: land 0006-pmemlayer-api decision record
description:
## Why

Super-epic requires the decision record to land BEFORE implementation so reviewers (and Phase C) can compare every diff against a stable target. Doctrine: ADRs precede the code that implements them. Paperwork-only; unblocks every later API task.

## What to touch

- `docs/decisions/0006-pmemlayer-api.md` (new — confirm next free number). Standard ADR shape: Context / Decision / Consequences / Alternatives.
- Cover:
  - PerVm-first rationale; `PmemLayer` / `PmemSharing` / `ErofsImageRef` / `GuestMountPath` / `ImageDigest` shapes and why each is a typed newtype with construction-time validation
  - Why `PmemSharing::Shared` is deliberately deferred to Phase C
  - Why `TrustDomainAck` is named but not implemented here
  - Where the `WarmStrategy` field will land (Phase D, not B)
  - **Polymorphic image store**: erofs and ext4 are sibling `ImageArtifact` variants in a single content-addressed store (`m80-image-store`, not `m80-image-erofs`); consumer-facing `ErofsImageRef` stays distinct for type safety but store internals are polymorphic. Phase B Task 5 implements this.
  - **`MountSpec` polymorphic enum deferred**: we considered collapsing rootfs / scratch / pmem under one `MountSpec` enum. Rejected for Phase B because rootfs/scratch are exactly-one-each with FC-specific plumbing while pmem layers are zero-or-many and RO-only. Future generalization is non-breaking via composition. Re-evaluated in Phase G (`m80-q420k.8`).
  - **Image-build pipeline explicitly out-of-scope for m80**: the crate ingests pre-built `.erofs` / `.ext4` artifacts and verifies digests. Build tooling (Nix, mkosi, custom scripts) lives in operator/CI infrastructure, NOT in this repo. A minimal `build_minimal_test_image` helper exists for tests and local dev only. This matches CLAUDE.md's "VM mechanics only" scope boundary.
- Reference `docs/decisions/0003-audit-sweep-eligibility.md` and `docs/postmortems/2026-05-12-ms-bind-and-sudo-escape.md`.
- "Alternatives considered" must include: (a) `pmem_layers: Vec<PmemLayer>` as free-form list vs length-bounded newtype; (b) `GuestMountPath` as `String` vs validated newtype; (c) shipping `PmemSharing::Shared` in the same phase; (d) collapsing rootfs/scratch/pmem under `MountSpec`; (e) shipping an opinionated build pipeline (Nix or otherwise). Each rejected with one sentence.

## Acceptance

- [ ] File exists with standard ADR shape.
- [ ] PR description quotes CLAUDE.md "Untrusted-input-to-kernel-primitive checklist" items and notes each will be ticked in Phase B implementation PRs.
- [ ] All five rejected alternatives listed with rationale.
- [ ] No source code touched.

## E2E note

Scaffolding — no new e2e path.

## Smoke note

Not kernel-touching. No smoke required.

## Dependencies

None. First task in Phase B; blocks every other Phase B task.
notes: ADR landed at docs/decisions/0006-pmemlayer-api.md. It covers PerVm-first typed API shape, Shared deferral/TrustDomainAck, WarmStrategy Phase D boundary, polymorphic image store, MountSpec deferral, image-build out-of-scope, all five rejected alternatives, and the Phase B untrusted-input/kernel-touching checklist expectation.
close_reason: docs/decisions/0006-pmemlayer-api.md landed with standard ADR shape, required alternatives, implementation checklist for untrusted-input/kernel-touching PRs, and no source changes for this bead

title: scripts/smoke.sh: extend gate harness for one-pmem-layer and multi-pmem-layer cold boot
description:
## Why

Phase-bead acceptance: "Real-KVM smoke paste in PR including a multi-pmem-layer boot." `scripts/smoke.sh` is the canonical real-KVM gate (`crates/m80-firecracker/tests/end_to_end_real_kvm.rs` uses its env setup). Per CLAUDE.md, mock-based e2e does NOT satisfy acceptance.

- `scripts/smoke.sh`:
  - New env knob `M80_PMEM_LAYERS=<count>` (default 0). When >0, build that many tiny erofs images (via `m80-image-erofs` CLI helper from Task 5), import into image store, pass through to CLI launch as additional config.

  - Echo digest of each layer and resolved jail path under `<run_dir>/firecracker/<vm_id>/root/pmem.<slot>.img` so smoke output is grep-able for digest stability.

title: tests: real-KVM e2e for scenarios 2/3/4/6 — one #[test] per scenario
description:
## Why

Phase-bead acceptance requires "All six e2e paths above pass on real KVM." Scenarios 1 and 5 handled by Tasks 5 and 11 (no KVM needed); scenarios 2, 3, 4, 6 do require KVM. Per CLAUDE.md "No bundling failure scenarios" and 2026-05-12 postmortem, one `#[test]` per scenario, `#[ignore]`d, exercised via `sudo cargo test -- --ignored`.

## What to touch

- `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/pmem_layer_real_kvm.rs` (new, mirroring `end_to_end_real_kvm.rs`):
  - `pmem_layer_per_vm_mount_dax_real_kvm` (scenario 2) — boot one VM with one `PmemLayer { sharing: PerVm }`, exec `cat /proc/mounts`, assert exactly one line contains mount path AND `dax` flag AND `ro`.
  - `pmem_layer_per_vm_distinct_backing_inodes_real_kvm` (scenario 3) — boot two VMs with same `PmemLayer { sharing: PerVm }`, use `std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt::ino` on each VM's `<run_dir>/pmem/<slot>.img`, assert inodes differ.
  - `pmem_layer_per_vm_no_cross_vm_page_sharing_real_kvm` (scenario 4) — boot two VMs reading the same file from the layer, capture `/proc/<fc-pid>/smaps` (or `/proc/<fc-pid>/maps`-derived RSS), assert file-backed page counts are non-zero per VM independently. Read host-side FC state; guest cannot observe own shared-vs-private accounting. Establishes baseline for Phase C delta.
  - `pmem_layer_per_vm_teardown_leaves_no_leak_real_kvm` (scenario 6) — boot a VM, exec a workload that reads from the layer (`wc -c <layer>/somefile`), stop, delete, then `find /var/lib/m80-run -name 'pmem.*.img'` returns empty AND `/tmp` does not contain stray `pmem*` files AND no FC working dirs survive.

title: m80-image-build: pin erofs + virtio-pmem + DAX guest kernel support before PmemLayer smoke
description:
## Why

The Phase 0 PoC on 2026-05-16 proved Firecracker v1.15.1 can attach pmem and that one m80 guest kernel/rootfs can expose `/dev/pmem0`. It also proved the support is split across current kernel profiles:

- `/tmp/m80-build/ubuntu/vmlinux` exposes `/dev/pmem0` and mounts an ext4 pmem image with `dax=always`, but `mount -t erofs` fails with `unknown filesystem type 'erofs'`.
- The newest committed stripped kernel (`vmlinux-m80-a096548e...bin`) has erofs built in, but the same direct Firecracker probe saw no `/dev/pmem*` device and `mount -t erofs -o dax,ro` logged `erofs: dax options not supported`.

So the blocker is not merely "turn erofs on". Phase B needs one pinned guest kernel profile with erofs, virtio-pmem/block-pmem, and the exact DAX mount form the guest will assert. Until that is explicit and proved by real-KVM smoke, the erofs-only `PmemLayer` design is not ready for implementation.

Evidence: `docs/poc/2026-05-16-layered-rootfs-poc-findings.md`.

## What to touch

- Audit the guest kernel config/build path used by `m80-image-build` and identify the exact config controlling erofs, DAX, and virtio-pmem/block-pmem support. Expected symbols include `CONFIG_EROFS_FS`, `CONFIG_FS_DAX`, `CONFIG_DAX`, `CONFIG_BLK_DEV_PMEM`, `CONFIG_ND_PMEM`, `CONFIG_LIBNVDIMM`, and `CONFIG_VIRTIO_PMEM` or their built-in/module equivalents.
- Update the kernel builder config or kernel-selection policy so the Phase B guest has all required support in one profile. Do not rely on late-loaded out-of-tree modules after guestd starts.
- Add a narrow real-KVM smoke/probe that boots the selected m80 guest kernel, attaches the PoC erofs image as pmem, and proves the guest can mount it from `/dev/pmem0` before any production `PmemLayer` API PR depends on it.
- Document the exact supported mount option spelling discovered on the real guest (`dax`, `dax=always`, no-DAX erofs fallback if the design changes) and feed it into Task `m80-q420k.2.9`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Kernel config audit identifies current erofs/DAX/virtio-pmem support status for each m80 guest kernel profile involved in Phase B.
- [ ] The selected Phase B kernel profile is updated or the Phase B design is explicitly changed away from erofs+DAX-on-pmem.
- [ ] Real-KVM smoke shows `/dev/pmem0` mounted as erofs with the intended DAX semantics, or captures the exact unsupported/failure mode and updates Phase B design.
- [ ] `docs/poc/2026-05-16-layered-rootfs-poc-findings.md` remains linked from the PR/bead notes as the motivating failure.

## Smoke note

Kernel-facing. This is not audit-sweep eligible. Mock tests do not prove the filesystem, pmem device, or DAX mode exists in the guest kernel.
close_reason: config/tests/docs updated; real-KVM smoke proved rebuilt stripped kernel mounts /dev/pmem0 as erofs with dax=always and cargo/rustc exit 0. Evidence: docs/behaviors/image-build/pmem-erofs-dax-kernel.md; docs/poc/2026-05-16-layered-rootfs-poc-findings.md; /tank/tmp/m80-q420k-poc/fc-pmem-erofs-rebuilt-boot-verified/probe-summary.txt

title: m80-firecracker: add typed PmemLayer / PmemSharing / ErofsImageRef / GuestMountPath / ImageDigest with validation
description:
## Why

Load-bearing API task: every downstream task consumes these types. Construction-time validation per CLAUDE.md ("validated at the typed API boundary, before it becomes a string, argv token, file path, mount option") is the only thing standing between caller input and `mount(2)` / cmdline tokens. No consumer wiring yet — pure types + tests.

## What to touch

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs` (or new sibling module `crates/m80-firecracker/src/pmem.rs` if it would push `types.rs` over 1000 lines):
  - `pub struct ImageDigest(String)` with `ImageDigest::parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, FcError>`. Accept 64-char lowercase hex sha256 only. Reject non-hex, wrong length, mixed case, embedded whitespace.
  - `pub struct GuestMountPath(PathBuf)` with `GuestMountPath::parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, FcError>`. Reject if not absolute, if it contains `.`/`..`, if it shadows `/`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, `/etc`, `/lower`, `/upper`, `/merged`, `/workspace`, or any m80-owned mount point. Require prefix `/opt/m80-layers/<name>/` where `<name>` is `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}`.
  - `pub struct ErofsImageRef { digest: ImageDigest }`. Construction via `ErofsImageRef::from_digest(ImageDigest)`. No raw paths.
  - `pub enum PmemSharing { PerVm }`. Single variant for Phase B. **No `#[non_exhaustive]`** per CLAUDE.md. A future `Shared(TrustDomainAck)` addition becomes a compile error in every match (intentional signal).
  - `pub struct PmemLayer { image: ErofsImageRef, sharing: PmemSharing, mount_at: GuestMountPath }`.
  - `pub fn validate_pmem_layers(layers: &[PmemLayer]) -> Result<(), FcError>` — reject duplicate `mount_at`, reject more than `MAX_PMEM_LAYERS` (small const, e.g., 8).
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/error.rs`: extend `ConfigError` (or new `PmemLayerError` under `FcError::Config`) with finite variants — `DigestInvalid { reason }`, `MountPathInvalid { reason }`, `MountPathShadowsReserved { path }`, `MountPathDuplicated { path }`, `TooManyLayers { max, got }`. **No `Other(String)`.**
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lib.rs`: re-export new public types.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/README.md`: extend public-surface section (drift is a bug per CLAUDE.md).
- Per-type unit tests in `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/pmem_layer_validation.rs`: one `#[test]` per rejection scenario (no bundling).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each newtype has a private inner and only constructs through `parse` or `from_*` ctors.
- [ ] Negative tests pin each rejection: bad-hex digest, whitespace digest, mixed-case digest, relative mount path, `..` in mount path, mount path `==` `/proc`, mount path under m80-reserved root, duplicate `mount_at`, too many layers.
- [ ] `PmemSharing` is **not** `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- [ ] README diff lands in the same PR.
- [ ] No `mount(2)` / FC API consumer wired yet.

## E2E note

Scaffolding — no new e2e path. Phase-bead scenario 5 (fail-closed validation) consumes this surface but is exercised by the dedicated e2e task (Task 11).

## Smoke note

Not kernel-touching at this layer (validation only). No smoke required.

## Dependencies

Task 1 (ADR pins shapes), Task 2 (forward refs resolved).
notes: Implemented in crates/m80-firecracker/src/pmem.rs as an admission-only surface: ImageDigest parses exactly 64 lowercase sha256 hex chars; GuestMountPath accepts exact /opt/m80-layers/<name> with name [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} and rejects trailing/deeper paths; ErofsImageRef/PmemLayer fields stay private behind constructors/accessors; PmemSharing has only PerVm and no non_exhaustive. README public surface updated. Focused validation: cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test pmem_layer_validation (24 passed), cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test error_variant_displays (15 passed), cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check for touched paths. No FC API or mount consumer wired.

title: m80-image-store: scaffold polymorphic content-addressed image store (erofs + ext4 artifacts)
description:
## Why

Phase bead names the image-store crate as sibling to the API work. Scaffolding as its own PR keeps the API-types PR small and pins the public surface every downstream FC/jailer task depends on.

Per Phase B Task 1 ADR: m80 ingests pre-built image artifacts and verifies digests. Opinionated build pipelines (Nix, mkosi, custom scripts) live OUTSIDE m80. Erofs and ext4 are sibling artifact types in one polymorphic store.

## What to touch

- `crates/m80-image-store/Cargo.toml`: new member. Deps: `m80-image-manifest.workspace = true`, `m80-firecracker = { path = "../m80-firecracker" }` (re-export `ImageDigest`), `sha2`, `hex`, `thiserror`, `serde`. `anyhow` only at bin edge per CLAUDE.md.
- Root `Cargo.toml`: add `m80-image-store = { path = "crates/m80-image-store" }` to `[workspace.dependencies]`.
- `crates/m80-image-store/src/lib.rs`: `#![deny(missing_docs)]`. Public surface:
  - `pub enum ImageArtifact { Erofs(ErofsImage), Ext4(Ext4Image) }` — sibling artifact types.
  - `pub enum ImageKind { Erofs, Ext4 }`
  - `pub struct ErofsImage { path: PathBuf, size_bytes: u64, digest: ImageDigest }`
  - `pub struct Ext4Image { path: PathBuf, size_bytes: u64, digest: ImageDigest }`
  - `pub struct ImageStore { root: PathBuf }` with `ImageStore::open(root: &Path)`. Root is `/var/lib/m80-images/` (constant; admission-validated).
  - `pub fn import_existing(&self, source: &Path, kind: ImageKind) -> Result<ImageDigest, StoreError>` — **primary entry point**. Ingests a pre-built artifact, hashes it, lands it at its content-addressed path.
  - `pub fn build_minimal_test_image(&self, source_dir: &Path, kind: ImageKind) -> Result<ImageDigest, StoreError>` — small helper wrapping `mkfs.erofs` / `mkfs.ext4` for tests and local dev. **NOT an opinionated build pipeline.** Documented as such.
  - `pub fn resolve(&self, digest: &ImageDigest) -> Result<ResolvedImage, StoreError>` — canonicalized host path with `O_NOFOLLOW`. Verify-on-write, trust-on-read with explicit `verify(&ImageDigest)` per CLAUDE.md.
  - `pub enum StoreError { DigestMismatch { expected, got }, NotFound { digest }, Io { path, source }, UnsupportedKind { kind }, MkfsFailed { kind, detail }, ... }` — typed variants only.
- `crates/m80-image-store/src/store.rs`: path scheme — `<root>/<digest[0..2]>/<digest>/{image.erofs|image.ext4}` + sidecar `metadata.json` (manifest-style, `deny_unknown_fields`, kind discriminator).
- `crates/m80-image-store/src/build.rs`: subprocess wrappers for `mkfs.erofs` and `mkfs.ext4`. Capture stderr in errors. No retries. Used by `build_minimal_test_image` only.
- `crates/m80-image-store/src/lock.rs`: file-lock — `flock(LOCK_EX)` on `<store_root>/.image-store.lock` during write, `LOCK_SH` during read. Tests pin both paths.
- `crates/m80-image-store/README.md`: black-box contract. **Explicitly documents**: opinionated image-build pipelines (Nix, mkosi, etc.) live outside m80; this crate ingests pre-built artifacts. The minimal-build helper is for tests and local dev only.
- `crates/m80-image-store/tests/`: per-concern unit tests covering both kinds (build determinism, digest stability across rebuilds, store layout, lock acquisition, `verify` mismatch, `O_NOFOLLOW` on placeholder writes, cross-kind isolation, `import_existing` flow).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `cargo build -p m80-image-store` and `cargo test -p m80-image-store` pass with no warnings.
- [ ] `import_existing` works for both erofs and ext4; digest is content-addressed and stable.
- [ ] `build_minimal_test_image` for erofs produces byte-identical artifact + identical digest across rebuilds of same source (one explicit test — exercises scenario 1).
- [ ] `build_minimal_test_image` for ext4 produces consistent output (mkfs.ext4 is less deterministic; document the floor).
- [ ] Store path scheme pinned by `#[test]` covering both kinds.
- [ ] No `unsafe`, no `Other(String)` error variants.
- [ ] README written; "opinionated build pipelines live outside m80" stated explicitly.

## E2E note

Scenario 1 ("Image build") exercised by integration tests in this crate. No real-KVM path required for scenario 1 — pure host-side determinism.

## Smoke note

Not kernel-touching (no mount, no FC API, no jailer plan). `mkfs.erofs` / `mkfs.ext4` subprocesses are host-only. No smoke required.

## Dependencies

Task 3 (re-uses `ImageDigest` from m80-firecracker).

## PoC back-propagation (2026-05-16)

`mkfs.erofs` success is not sufficient evidence that the produced artifact is usable by m80 guests. The PoC produced and host-mounted a valid erofs image, but the current guest kernel rejected erofs at mount time. Keep this crate host-only, but its README and tests must be clear that image-store determinism is separate from guest-kernel compatibility; `m80-q420k.2.15` owns the real-KVM erofs/DAX support gate.
notes: Post-close correction while preparing m80-q420k.2.7: removed the upward m80-image-store -> m80-firecracker dependency and made m80-image-store own its store-local ImageDigest. This avoids a Phase B cycle when m80-firecracker later needs to consume ImageStore for backing resolution. Revalidated with cargo test -p m80-image-store and cargo build -p m80-image-store.

Evidence: crates/m80-image-store plus root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock. Validation: cargo test -p m80-image-store; cargo build -p m80-image-store; cargo fmt --all -- --check; git diff --check touched paths.

title: m80-jailer: bind pmem backings as host sources in jailer plan + dest collision rejection
description:
## Why

FC opens the pmem `path_on_host` from inside the jail, so each backing file must be bind-mounted into the chroot before FC starts. The jailer plan is the choke point; touching it lands sweep-ineligible per CLAUDE.md decision 0003 and needs its own single-purpose diff with smoke.

## What to touch

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs::phase_4_jailer_materialize`:
  - Accept new `pmem_layers: &[ResolvedPmemBacking]` parameter on `JailerMaterializeInput` (`ResolvedPmemBacking` = new internal struct with `host_path: PathBuf` and `jail_basename: String`, computed by new `phase_3b_resolve_pmem_backings` pre-phase that talks to `m80_image_erofs::ImageStore::resolve` and produces per-VM backing files).
  - Append one `Binding { source: backing.host_path, dest: PathBuf::from(format!("pmem.{}.img", backing.jail_basename)), mode: BindMode::Ro }` per pmem layer. RO bind is correct: FC opens RO when `read_only: true` + DAX-mmaps; guest mounts erofs RO. Both ends agree.
  - Reject in `Plan::compute` if any pmem dest collides with `kernel`, `rootfs.ext4`, `rootfs.overlay.ext4`, `scratch.ext4`, or preallocated drive slot paths. Add dest collision check inside `m80_jailer::plan::Plan::compute` so it fails closed at plan compute, not at mount time.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/layout.rs`: new `pub(crate) fn pmem_layer_jail_path(slot: usize) -> PathBuf` returning canonical `/pmem.<slot>.img`. Pin by unit test.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/storage_prep.rs` or new `crates/m80-firecracker/src/pmem_prep.rs`: implement `phase_3b_resolve_pmem_backings` — for each `PmemLayer` with `PmemSharing::PerVm`, ask `m80_storage` (or `m80_image_erofs`) for a per-VM reflink-cloned backing under `<run_dir>/pmem/<slot>.img`. Use `cp --reflink=auto --sparse=always` (same pattern as `m80-storage/src/rootfs.rs::TEMPLATE_CLONE_ARGS`). Per-VM = each layer gets a distinct inode → scenario 3.
- `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs`: extend `is_hidden_kernel_dest` collision check + positive test that pmem dests under `/` are accepted but cannot escape via `..`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Per-VM backing files exist at `<run_dir>/pmem/<slot>.img` with distinct inodes (verified by Task 13 real-KVM e2e via `stat::st_ino`).
- [ ] Jailer plan rejects pmem dest collisions with kernel / rootfs / scratch / hotplug slot paths.
- [ ] Each backing file is bound `BindMode::Ro` into the jail.
- [ ] No caller-string flows into jail dest (caller controls only `digest`; jail dest is `pmem.<slot>.img`).
- [ ] Unit test pins canonical jail path scheme.

To avoid a dependency cycle, m80-image-store no longer depends on m80-firecracker; future implementation should have m80-firecracker depend on m80-image-store and convert from m80_firecracker::ImageDigest.as_str() to m80_image_store::ImageDigest at the boundary, or deliberately consolidate digest types in a separate follow-up.

description:

title: m80-proto + m80-guestd: PmemMountRequest wire + DAX guest mount handler with fail-closed DAX assertion
description:
## Why

Phase bead: "mount layout is communicated to `m80-guestd` via the existing guestd contract, not via cmdline tokens". The existing wire has `DriveMountRequest` for hotplug; pmem is a different lifecycle (preboot-declared, mounted before workload starts) and different mount type (erofs over `/dev/pmem0` with `dax,ro`). Typed wire variants, not stringly-overloaded reuse.

## What to touch

- `crates/m80-proto/src/types/`: new `pmem.rs` next to `hotplug.rs`:
  - `pub struct PmemMountSpec { pub device_path: String, pub mount_path: String, pub digest_hex: String }` — `digest_hex` is opaque to guestd; guest does not verify.
  - `pub struct PmemMountRequest { pub devices: Vec<PmemMountSpec> }`.
  - `pub enum PmemMountStatusKind { Mounted, AlreadyMounted, Failed }`.
  - `pub enum PmemMountError { DeviceNotFound, MountFailed, DaxFlagAbsent, InvalidDevicePath, InvalidMountPath, Io }` — finite typed variants.
  - `pub struct PmemMountStatus { pub device_path: String, pub mount_path: String, pub status: PmemMountStatusKind, pub error: Option<PmemMountError> }`.
  - `pub struct PmemMountResponse { pub statuses: Vec<PmemMountStatus> }`.
  - `pub const PAYLOAD_KIND_PMEM_MOUNT_REQUEST: &str = "pmem_mount_request";` and `..._RESPONSE`.
- Wire protobuf definitions + conversions following pattern in `crates/m80-proto/src/wire/conversions/`.
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/connection.rs`: extend dispatch to recognize `PAYLOAD_KIND_PMEM_MOUNT_REQUEST` and route to new handler.
- `crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/pmem.rs` (new module): mount sequence:
  1. Validate `device_path` is `/dev/pmem<N>` and `mount_path` is absolute non-shadowing.
  2. Poll for `/dev/pmem<N>` block-device presence with bounded timeout (mirror `hotplug.rs::HOTPLUG_WAIT`).
  3. `create_dir_all(mount_path)`.
  4. `mount("/dev/pmem<N>", mount_path, "erofs", MsFlags::MS_RDONLY | MsFlags::MS_NOSUID | MsFlags::MS_NODEV, Some("dax"))` — confirm exact `dax` spelling against running guest kernel during real-KVM smoke (`dax`, `dax=always`).
  5. After mount, read `/proc/mounts` and assert mount line for `mount_path` contains `dax` token (fail-closed otherwise — `PmemMountError::DaxFlagAbsent`).
  6. Return per-spec status.
- Host-side caller: after `phase_12b_ready_accept` in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs`, add new `phase_13_pmem_guest_mount` that sends `PmemMountRequest`. Fail closed: any `PmemMountError` causes launch failure + run-dir cleanup guard.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/error.rs`: extend `FcError` with `PmemMount(PmemMountError)` typed variant.

## Acceptance

- [ ] New wire kinds round-trip in `crates/m80-proto/tests/`.
- [ ] Guest handler mounts erofs over `/dev/pmem0` with DAX flags and reads `/proc/mounts` to confirm DAX active.
- [ ] Host launch fails closed when guest reports `DaxFlagAbsent` — verified by test (test-injection trait, mirroring `hotplug.rs::MountOps`).
- [ ] No guest-side path that swallows a mount error — fail-closed pinned by regression test.
- [ ] `m80-guestd` does not depend on `m80-firecracker` types directly.

## E2E note

Scenarios 2, 4, 5 all exercise this code. Mount handler itself is kernel-touching (`mount(2)`).

## Smoke note

Kernel-touching — `mount(2)` in `m80-guestd/src/connection/pmem.rs`. PR must include green `./scripts/smoke.sh` paste, ideally with smoke variant exercising at least one `PmemLayer` (Task 12 introduces the extension). Sweep-ineligible per CLAUDE.md "mount/ns/caps/signal/seccomp/cgroup/sudo wrapping".

## Dependencies

Tasks 7 and 8 (device must appear in guest as `/dev/pmem0`).

## PoC back-propagation (2026-05-16)

The PoC observed two mount facts on the real substrate: erofs mount failed with `unknown filesystem type 'erofs'`, while ext4 over pmem mounted successfully with `/proc/mounts` showing `dax=always`. title: Phase C — PmemSharing::Shared opt-in (TrustDomainAck + threat-model doctrine)
description:
## Scope

Add `PmemSharing::Shared(TrustDomainAck)` variant. Single canonical m80-image-store erofs artifact is used across all VMs that reference the image with `Shared`. Mechanical implementation change is small; the lift is doctrine — making the trust-domain assumption legible in code and docs.

## Why

Cross-VM cache sharing (host page cache amortized across N guests pointing at one inode) is the killer benefit for shared toolchains. Phase B's `PerVm` got per-VM memory benefits; Phase C gets aggregate fleet memory benefits. The architecture stops short of compromising tenant isolation by requiring an explicit, typed acknowledgment from the caller.

## Prerequisites (hard)

- Phase B has shipped.
- Trust-model paragraph merged in `docs/positioning.md` (or a dedicated `docs/threat-model.md`) **before** this phase opens. Specifically: m80 assumes guests sharing a pmem image share a trust boundary; cross-tenant isolation between Shared-pmem-sharing guests is out of scope; the side-channel exposure is a cache-timing channel via the shared DAX-backed pages.

Without that paragraph merged first, `Sharing::Shared` cannot be exposed.

## What to touch

- m80 public API: `PmemSharing` gains `Shared(TrustDomainAck)` variant.
  - `TrustDomainAck` is a newtype with a `reason: TrustReason` field.
  - `TrustReason` is a typed enum (no free strings); initial variants: `SameOperator`, `KubernetesSameNamespace`, `ResearchSandbox`. New variants added via PR when real callers need them.
  - No `Default` for `TrustDomainAck`. Construction is explicit only.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs` — when `Shared`, point multiple FC instances at the same host backing inode rather than cloning.
- `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs` — Shared backing is bind-mounted RO into N jails simultaneously; must verify FC opens the device `O_RDONLY` (assertion + test).
- `crates/m80-image-store/src/store.rs` — Shared active-use markers under `shared/<digest>/refs/<vm_id>`; markers never delete canonical artifacts.
- `docs/positioning.md` or `docs/threat-model.md` — trust-model paragraph (prereq).
- New doc: `docs/behaviors/rootfs/pmem-shared.md`
- Extend existing decision record: `docs/decisions/00NN-pmemlayer-api.md` adds the Shared variant rationale and an explicit "DAX side-channel acknowledged" section.

## Validation

- `TrustDomainAck` cannot be constructed implicitly. No `Default`. Constructor takes the typed enum.
- Same-inode-reuse-across-N-VMs is a deliberate code path, not a coincidence of "they happened to have the same digest". `PerVm` always clones even when the digest matches; only `Shared` reuses the inode.
- Shared active-use markers are tracked in m80. Markers are acquired during Shared storage prep, released only after jail bind mounts are dropped, and swept on startup for VM ids no longer present under `run_root`.
- The canonical image-store artifact is operator-managed input. It is never deleted as an implicit side effect of the last Shared VM stopping; artifact GC is a future explicit retention feature.

## E2E — new paths this phase enables (explicit)

1. **Inode identity**: two VMs with `Shared` pmem referencing the same digest; verify the device-backing file inside each jail resolves to the SAME host inode (`stat` returns matching `st_ino`).
2. **Host page sharing**: read the same large file from the layer in both VMs; assert host page cache shows shared pages — preferred check: total host memory delta after N concurrent attaches ≤ (one base image size) + (per-VM overhead × N). Direct check via `/proc/kpageflags` if practical.
3. **Compile-time safety**: attempt to construct `PmemSharing::Shared` without a valid `TrustDomainAck` — compile error.
4. **Mixed sharing**: boot one VM with `Shared`, one with `PerVm` referencing the same image — verify Shared uses the shared backing, PerVm uses its own clone, both work, no cross-talk, no leak.
5. **Active-use marker lifecycle**: tear down all Shared-referencing VMs serially; verify marker count drops per stopped VM, stale-marker sweep removes non-live markers, and the canonical shared artifact remains present at zero active refs.
6. **Negative**: attempt to declare a `Shared` layer with any caller-introduced writability hint — API rejects at construction.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Trust-model paragraph merged in `docs/positioning.md` (or `docs/threat-model.md`) **before** this PR opens.
- [ ] `Shared` variant + `TrustDomainAck` + `TrustReason` enum land with full validation.
- [ ] All six e2e paths above pass on real KVM.
- [ ] Behavior doc committed.
- [ ] Shared active-use marker lifecycle verified by teardown e2e; no canonical image-store artifact deletion at zero active refs.
- [ ] Real-KVM smoke paste in PR including a ≥4-VM concurrent-Shared boot with measurable host memory delta.
- [ ] PR description explicitly acknowledges the DAX cache-timing side channel and the trust-model paragraph it ships behind.

## Doctrine

Sweep-ineligible. Real-KVM smoke mandatory. The side-channel acknowledgement must be explicit in the PR description AND in the decision record extension.

## UX implications (forward-looking → Phase E)

- BootSpec config: how does a caller declare a `TrustReason`? Probably an explicit field in the config (e.g. `pmem_layers[].sharing = "shared"`, `pmem_layers[].trust_reason = "same_operator"`) parsed into the typed witness. Phase E owns the schema.
- Operator runbook: when is `Shared` appropriate? Decision tree by deployment context. Phase E adds.
- Observability: per-layer attach counts grouped by sharing mode; helpful for capacity planning and audit.

Do not close Phase C from noisy-host diagnostics or scaffolded artifacts.

title: m80-firecracker: add typed TrustDomainAck + TrustReason + PmemSharing::Shared variant (types only)
description:
## Why

Compile-time safety is the load-bearing property of this phase. Landing types in their own PR means the impl PRs (Tasks 3–5) build on a stable, reviewed API surface and downstream callers can see the construction shape before the runtime path changes.

## What to touch

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs` (or wherever Phase B placed `PmemSharing`):
  - `pub struct TrustDomainAck { reason: TrustReason }`. **No `Default`.** Constructor is `pub fn new(reason: TrustReason) -> Self`. Field private — read via accessor `pub fn reason(&self) -> TrustReason`.
  - `pub enum TrustReason { SameOperator, KubernetesSameNamespace, ResearchSandbox }`. Adding a variant is a PR with justification. **NOT `#[non_exhaustive]`** per CLAUDE.md.
  - Extend `PmemSharing` with `Shared(TrustDomainAck)` variant. No string fields, no boolean writability hints.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs` — temporarily `unimplemented!()` or typed `FcError::PmemSharedNotYetImplemented` for the `Shared` arm of any match on `PmemSharing`. Compile clean.
- `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs` — same: `Shared` arm in any `match PmemSharing` returns typed `JailerError::PmemSharedNotYetImplemented`. Validation only; no bind-mount changes yet.
- Update `crates/m80-firecracker/README.md` — public surface change requires same-diff README update (CLAUDE.md cardinal rule).
- Tests in `crates/m80-firecracker/src/types_tests.rs` (or wherever Phase B placed `PmemSharing` tests):
  - Compile-failure test (trybuild or rustdoc `compile_fail`) proving `PmemSharing::Shared` cannot be constructed without a `TrustDomainAck`.
  - Test proving `TrustDomainAck` has no `Default` — `static_assertions::assert_not_impl_any!` style guard.
  - Test pinning initial `TrustReason` variant set.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `cargo check --workspace` clean.
- [ ] `cargo test -p m80-firecracker types_tests` green.
- [ ] Compile-failure test exists and is referenced from README.
- [ ] Runtime arms for `Shared` are typed errors, not panics, in both `exec.rs` and `plan.rs`.
- [ ] README for `m80-firecracker` updated.
- [ ] Task 1 doc commit is reachable in `main` at PR open time (reviewer-enforced).

## E2E note

Scenarios 3 ("Compile-time safety") and 6 ("Negative: caller-introduced writability hint rejected") fall here as compile and unit tests. Real-VM scenarios stay in Task 7.

## Smoke note

Not kernel-touching at this task. `Shared` runtime arms are stubs returning typed errors. No real-KVM smoke required for this PR; smoke gate moves to impl PRs (Tasks 3, 4).

## Dependencies

Task 1 merged. Blocks Tasks 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.

title: m80-firecracker: implement Shared backing inode reuse in lifecycle/exec.rs
description:
## Why

This is the killer benefit. PerVm clones the backing per VM (Phase B). `Shared` points multiple FC instances at the same backing inode so host page cache is amortized. Mechanical change; the architecture work is deciding that "same digest in Shared mode" is a deliberate code path distinct from "same digest in PerVm mode coincidentally".

## What to touch

- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs` — replace the `Shared` stub from Task 2 with the real path:
  - When `PmemSharing::Shared(_)`, resolve to the canonical shared-backing path under the m80-owned image-store layout (Phase B established the store; this task adds a `shared/` subtree or equivalent — pin chosen path in the ADR extension, Task 6).
  - Shared backing is the erofs image file itself (read-only, content-addressed by `ImageDigest`); no per-VM clone.
  - Path resolution refuses to fall through to PerVm semantics on `Shared` — `PerVm` always clones even when digest matches; only `Shared` reuses.
- `crates/m80-firecracker/src/runroot.rs` — bind shared backing into per-VM jail. Bridge to Task 4's jailer-plan change.
- Touch only `PmemSharing` match arms; do not refactor unrelated code.
- Lifecycle path remains idempotent under concurrent attach: two VMs starting simultaneously and both pointing at same digest both succeed and observe the same host inode.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Shared` no longer returns a typed-not-yet-implemented error.
- [ ] Code path for `Shared` resolves to a single host inode regardless of how many VMs are starting — checked by unit test plus Task 7 e2e (scenario 1).
- [ ] `PerVm` path unchanged — pinned by regression test that boots `PerVm` and asserts distinct inodes (exists from Phase B; verify still passes).
- [ ] No silent fallback from `Shared` to `PerVm` if shared backing is missing — fail closed with typed `FcError` variant.
- [ ] PR description walks CLAUDE.md untrusted-input checklist for new shared path bind (host source canonicalized, `O_NOFOLLOW` on any placeholder, dest path validation re-checked).

## E2E note

Enables scenarios 1 (inode identity) and 2 (host page sharing). Both verified in Task 7.

## Smoke note

Kernel-touching. Modifies `lifecycle/exec.rs` (sweep-ineligible per CLAUDE.md decision 0003). PR **must** include real-KVM smoke paste — minimum 2-VM `Shared` boot showing both attach to same backing. The 4-VM density measurement is Task 8; non-trivial smoke paste belongs in this PR.

## Dependencies

Task 2 merged. Coordinates with Task 4 (same e2e scenarios stress both). Blocks Tasks 7, 8.

title: m80-jailer: implement Shared bind-mount in plan.rs + O_RDONLY assertion
description:
## Why

Phase C's safety property is that all consumers of a `Shared` backing see it read-only. The jailer plan is the chokepoint where the host source is bound into the jail; it owns the RO enforcement. Phase bead explicit: must verify FC opens the device `O_RDONLY` (assertion + test).

## What to touch

- `crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs`:
  - Extend the plan model so `PmemSharing::Shared` produces a `PlanStep::Bind { mode: BindMode::Ro, ... }` pointing at the single host inode resolved by Task 3.
  - This step participates in the same `make_mounts_private` + `MS_BIND | MS_REMOUNT | MS_RDONLY | MS_NODEV | MS_NOEXEC | MS_NOSUID` regimen Phase B established for pmem backings — but with source path being the shared store path rather than a per-VM clone.

  - Same configs with `PerVm` produce **distinct** host source paths (Phase B reflink/clone path).

title: m80-image-store: active-use markers for Shared pmem artifacts
description:
## Why

Phase C current implementation uses the canonical m80-image-store artifact as the Shared pmem backing inode. That artifact is an operator-managed content-addressed input, not a temporary per-VM backing. Therefore the early wording about deleting the backing when refcount reaches zero is wrong and unsafe: it would delete the source artifact needed by future launches.

This leaf tracks active use of Shared artifacts without making the image-store artifact temporary.

## What changed from the original plan

- There is no m80-image-erofs crate; the store is m80-image-store.
- Ref state lives under the image store as markers: store/shared/digest/refs/vm_id.
- Markers are active-use evidence only. They never delete canonical artifacts.
- Artifact garbage collection is explicitly out of scope and must be a future operator-controlled retention feature, not implicit last-ref deletion.

## Acceptance

- m80-image-store exposes typed acquire/release/sweep APIs for Shared active-use markers.
- Marker names reject escaping or non-marker VM ids before touching paths.
- Duplicate marker acquisition fails closed with a typed error.
- Startup recovery sweeps stale markers for VM ids no longer present under run_root.
- m80-firecracker acquires markers during Shared pmem storage prep and releases them after jail bind mounts are dropped on stop/force-kill.
- Tests prove acquire/release, duplicate failure, stale sweep, concurrent Shared attach, and no canonical artifact deletion at last release.
- ADR and behavior docs state that markers are active-use tracking, not artifact GC.
