title: Phase G — Followup open questions surfaced or anticipated post super-epic close
description:
**Phase G — Open architectural and operational questions surfaced or anticipated post super-epic close.**

A holding area for items that do not block the production plan but should be addressed before scaling beyond the first v0.1 adapter consumer. Some entries were pre-seeded from the current design, and Phase 0 PoC (`m80-q420k.7`) closure added more.

## Structure

Each task here is one of:

- **Investigation** — answer a specific open question with research / measurement / prototyping. Output is a decision record or a follow-up bead.
- **Decision record extension** — extend an existing ADR with a section.
- **Deferred design exploration** — a future-direction item we know we want to address eventually but not before v0.1 ships.

## Pre-seeded entries

See child tasks. The list is non-exhaustive; the PoC and Phase A–F implementation work can surface more. New entries can be filed under this epic at any time.

## Triage rules

When closing a Phase G item, each task either becomes its own sub-epic (if the answer requires a multi-task implementation) or a decision record plus a small implementation task. **No "investigation" task closes without a written output** (decision record, follow-up bead, or sub-epic).

## Closure

Phase G itself never "closes" in the sense the other phases do; it is a rolling holding area. Individual entries move out as they are answered. The super-epic `m80-q420k` closes when Phases A–F plus Phase 0 are closed; Phase G persists as the long-tail of refinement work.

title: Investigate: MountSpec polymorphic enum (defer or adopt after B/C/D + consumer feedback)
description:
## Why

The earlier-conversation design surface proposed collapsing rootfs / scratch / pmem layers under one `MountSpec` enum. Deferred in Phase B (see Task 1 ADR: kept distinct because rootfs/scratch are exactly-one-each with FC-specific plumbing while pmem layers are zero-or-many and RO-only). ## What to investigate

- Do the lifecycle semantics of rootfs / scratch / pmem actually converge in practice, or do they stay distinct?

- What would a non-breaking migration look like (composition over enum-collapse)?

- If kept distinct: a one-paragraph note appended to Phase B's ADR + close this task.

title: Future-direction: multi-host template distribution (defer to post-v1)
description:
## Why

The template store is single-host today. For scaled deployments running m80 across many hosts, rebuilding the same template on each host is wasteful — both in time and in the surface area for template-fingerprint drift across hosts.

**Future-direction. Defer until a real multi-host deployment scenario surfaces.**

## What to investigate

- Distribution mechanism: shared filesystem, content-addressed registry (OCI-style or similar), explicit push/pull.
- Trust: how does a host verify a template received from elsewhere (signing — see G-11)?
- Versioning: how do fingerprint mismatches interact with distribution? Should a "shared" template be lazily verified on first restore on each host?
- Cache locality: how does the host-local template store interact with a shared upstream registry?

## Output

- Future-direction doc `docs/future-directions/multi-host-template-distribution.md`.
- No implementation in v0.x; this is post-v1 work.

## Dependencies

Phase D shipped + a real multi-host deployment scenario.
close_reason: Added future-direction doc docs/future-directions/multi-host-template-distribution.md. It keeps the v0.x store single-host, compares build-per-host, shared filesystem, registry, and explicit push/pull, preserves local template-store restore authority, requires fingerprint/local-input verification before restore, and defers signing/provenance to G-11. No implementation planned until a real multi-host deployment scenario exists. Verification: git diff --check --no-index for the new doc.

title: Future-direction: image/template signing (sigstore/in-toto, defer until threat model requires)
description:
## Why

Content-addressing prevents bit-rot but not malicious substitution at the source. A supply-chain attack at the build pipeline (Nix dependency compromise, mkosi rootfs poisoning, etc.) could introduce a malicious image whose digest is "correct" in the sense that `sha256(file) == claimed digest` — the digest hashes the malicious bytes. Signing the build provenance is the mitigation.

**Future-direction. Defer until a threat model requires it.**

## What to investigate

- Sigstore / cosign integration model for image artifacts.
- In-toto attestations for build provenance.
- Where signing checks fit: at `import_existing` (verify signature alongside digest), at `resolve` (re-verify on each attach), or both.
- Key management story: per-operator keys, organization root, or both?

## Output

- Future-direction doc `docs/future-directions/image-template-signing.md`.
- No implementation in v0.x.

## Dependencies

Phase B shipped + a threat model that requires it (cross-tenant deployment, untrusted operators, supply-chain compliance requirement).

title: Resolve: erofs image layouts that actually provide DAX/file-level sharing
description:
## Why

The Phase 0 PoC proved the rebuilt stripped kernel can mount a compressed Rust-toolchain erofs image from virtio-pmem with `dax=always`, and four guests can attach the same backing file. It did not prove that compressed erofs file contents actually use file-level DAX mappings or produce the intended host page-sharing behavior under representative reads.

This is no longer a casual Phase G follow-up. It gates the verified memory-sharing claims in `m80-q420k.3.8` and `m80-q420k.6.3`: a Shared pmem mount is not enough if the erofs image layout routes file reads through page-cache behavior that does not provide the claimed sharing property.

## What to touch

- Build a tiny controlled erofs matrix:
  - uncompressed flat file image
  - compressed file image matching the PoC shape
  - representative Rust/toolchain-style image shape, or a documented smaller proxy that exercises the same erofs feature flags
- Boot each layout on real KVM with virtio-pmem and `dax=always`.
- Run a workload that reads enough bytes to fault meaningful data from the mounted layer.
- Measure host-memory/page-fault behavior strongly enough to decide which layouts can be used for `PmemSharing::Shared` density measurements.
- Update the Phase C/F measurement beads with the required image layout/workload constraints.
- If a layout is unsuitable for Shared layers, update the relevant image-build/import/BootSpec validation plan so m80 fails closed before a misleading density run.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Written result names the erofs inode/image layouts that satisfy the Shared memory-sharing requirement and the layouts that do not.
- [ ] Result cites the real-KVM command/substrate used and the observed numeric or kernel-level evidence; mount success alone is not accepted.
- [ ] `m80-q420k.3.8` is updated with the required image layout/workload constraints for `docs/perf/pmem-shared-density.md`.
- [ ] `m80-q420k.6.1` / `m80-q420k.6.3` are updated, if needed, so the composed e2e uses a layout that actually proves host sharing.
- [ ] If compressed erofs is unsuitable, follow-up implementation beads are filed or updated to reject that layout for Shared layers at the typed API/import boundary.

## Smoke note

Real-KVM evidence is required because the property under test is kernel/filesystem/DAX behavior. Mock substrate, static manifest checks, and `mount -o dax=always` success are not enough.

title: m80-firecracker: reject compressed erofs files for Shared pmem admission
description:
## Why

`m80-q420k.8.12` proved on real KVM that `dax=always` on an erofs pmem mount is not enough for Shared-pmem density claims. Only uncompressed non-inlined erofs files receive guest-visible `STATX_ATTR_DAX`; compressed erofs files mount successfully but do not provide file-level DAX for the payload.

Today m80 can import or reference arbitrary erofs artifacts and then admit them as `PmemSharing::Shared`. That means a caller can accidentally choose a compressed image, get a successful launch, and silently lose the memory-sharing property that justified the trust-domain acknowledgement.

## What to design/implement

- Add a typed erofs layout validation path for Shared pmem inputs. Prefer a store/import-time metadata model over shelling out in the launch hot path.
- Reject compressed regular-file layouts for `PmemSharing::Shared` before Firecracker admission/launch. The error must be finite and typed, not `Other(String)`.
- Preserve `PmemSharing::PerVm` behavior unless a separate bead proves PerVm also needs the restriction.
- Document the accepted layout: uncompressed non-inlined files for payloads that participate in density claims.
- Keep hard cutover semantics. No tolerant fallback to PerVm, no silent warning-only mode.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A Shared layer whose erofs artifact contains compressed payload files is rejected before any VM launch or jail materialization.
- [ ] A Shared layer built by the current uncompressed `m80-image-store::build_minimal_test_image(..., ImageKind::Erofs)` path still admits.
- [ ] Regression tests cover compressed-reject and uncompressed-accept cases without requiring KVM where possible.
- [ ] Behavior docs and crate README surfaces that mention Shared pmem link to `docs/perf/erofs-dax-sharing-layout.md`.

## Evidence

- Real-KVM proof: `docs/perf/erofs-dax-sharing-layout.md`.
- Test scaffold/proof: `crates/m80-firecracker/tests/erofs_dax_layout_real_kvm.rs::erofs_dax_layout_matrix_real_kvm`.

## Dependency

Depends on `m80-q420k.8.12`.
close_reason: implemented fail-closed Shared pmem erofs layout admission: storage prep runs dump.erofs -S for Shared artifacts, rejects compressed regular-file layouts with ConfigError::SharedPmemCompressedErofs before shared refs, jail materialization, or Firecracker admission, and preserves PerVm behavior; updated m80-firecracker README plus pmem/dax behavior docs linking docs/perf/erofs-dax-sharing-layout.md; verified cargo test -p m80-firecracker --lib storage_prep, cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test error_variant_displays shared_pmem_compressed_erofs_is_user_input, cargo test -p m80-firecracker --test erofs_dax_layout_real_kvm --no-run, cargo check -p m80-firecracker, cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check

title: Tooling: split oversized source sets into multiple pmem layers
description:
## Why

Bead m80-q420k.8.4 confirmed the pinned Firecracker v1.15.1 virtio-pmem address window is 512 GiB per backing after 2 MiB rounding. m80 now rejects oversize erofs artifacts before Firecracker admission. Very large toolchain/source payloads can still be represented as multiple pmem layers, but operators have no first-class helper to split one source set and recompose it in the guest.

## Shape

Design tooling that can split a large source tree or artifact set into multiple erofs pmem layer images, emit a BootSpec layer set within MAX_PMEM_LAYERS, and optionally provide a mount-time composition convention that does not collapse rootfs/scratch/pmem mechanics.

## Acceptance

- Proposal names the split unit, digest/manifest shape, and guest mount/recompose contract.
- It stays outside kernel-facing Firecracker plumbing unless a later single-purpose kernel-touching bead carries real-KVM smoke evidence.
- Existing users can continue declaring independent PmemLayer entries without the helper.
close_reason: Added proposal doc docs/future-directions/pmem-layer-splitting.md. It names path-prefix groups as the split unit, a future PmemLayerSetManifest shape with source_set_digest/layers/guest_contract, guest consumption as explicit many-mounted directories rather than new kernel composition, Shared/PerVm interaction, and non-goals that keep rootfs/scratch/pmem mechanics distinct. Verification: git diff --check --no-index for the new doc.

title: Implement image-store GC with retention pins and race-free template coordination
description:
## Why

ADR 0009 defines image-store GC as operator-driven mark-and-sweep. The existing explicit `m80 image rm` path checks committed template manifests and Shared active-use markers, but a safe executable GC needs cross-store coordination so template builds cannot commit a manifest referencing an image deleted between scan and remove.

## Shape

Implement `m80 image gc` in report-only mode first, then enable `--execute` only after adding a durable template-build image-use marker or a documented image-store lock shared by template commit and GC. The mark set must include committed template references, Shared active-use markers, operator pin files / `--keep`, and optional minimum artifact age.

## Acceptance

- Default `m80 image gc` is dry-run and reports candidates, protected digests, reasons, and total reclaimable bytes.
- `--execute` reuses typed `ImageStore::remove` semantics and cannot bypass template-reference or Shared-marker checks.
- Template build/commit has a race-free coordination story with image GC before executable deletion is enabled.
- Tests cover active Shared markers, committed template references, pin files, min-age retention, and the template-build race guard.
close_reason: implemented m80 image gc dry-run/execute with keep and pin-file retention, min-age retention, committed-template and Shared-marker protection, and shared/exclusive template-build GC coordination; verified with cargo test -p m80-cli --test image_smoke; cargo test -p m80-image-store; cargo test -p m80-cli --test parse_args --test help_smoke; cargo test -p m80-firecracker template_build --lib; cargo fmt --all -- --check; git diff --check

title: Measure ext4 overlay-template byte-copy fallback before reconsidering dm-snapshot
description:
## Why

The Phase G dm-snapshot recheck found that the current ext4 fallback is not the old full base-rootfs copy: `Rootfs::prepare` byte-copies only a run-root-local empty sparse overlay template. Existing committed data shows `phase_3b_rootfs_prepare` around 13-14 ms P50, but no committed artifact was found that isolates a representative ext4-host byte-copy run-root and compares it to dmsetup setup/teardown cost.

## Observable

`docs/perf/ext4-overlay-template-clone.md` contains N>=30 measurements on a representative ext4 run-root host with these named values:

- `phase_3b_rootfs_prepare` P50/P95/P99 for byte-copy overlay-template clone.
- dmsetup snapshot create+teardown P50/P95/P99 if a prototype is built; otherwise a source-backed explanation of why dm-snapshot was not prototyped.
- teardown residue count after the run: leaked dm devices = 0, leaked mounts = 0.

The artifact must state host filesystem, kernel version, run-root path, command line, commit, and whether the run occurred on a real Firecracker/KVM launch path or a storage-only substrate.

## Acceptance

- The measurement artifact is committed and cited in the close reason as `verified: docs/perf/ext4-overlay-template-clone.md @ <commit>`.
- Reconsider dm-snapshot only if ext4 byte-copy `phase_3b_rootfs_prepare` exceeds 80 ms P50 or 100 ms P95 on the representative host, or if operator evidence shows byte-copy residue/pressure that the current path cannot handle.
- Any dm-snapshot implementation follow-up is a single-purpose kernel/device-mapper diff and must include real-KVM smoke evidence before close.

title: Investigate: VMGenID userspace reseed for non-systemd guests (busybox, minimal images)
description:
## Why

Phase D Task 10 audits the guest kernel config for VMGenID kernel-side support. But for guests without systemd (busybox, minimal images), there's no `/var/lib/systemd/random-seed` to update. What's the userspace reseed path for non-systemd guests?

## What to investigate

- Identify per-guest-type userspace state that benefits from VMGenID-driven reseed: `/etc/machine-id`, application-level PRNG caches, SSH host keys if applicable, long-lived daemons holding cached entropy.
- For each, name the reseed mechanism (file rewrite, ioctl, daemon reload, kill+restart).
- Decide which become `HookSpec` variants in the closed enum vs which are caller-handled via a typed seam.

## Output

- New `HookSpec` variants if appropriate, with PR linked from this task.
- OR: doc note that non-systemd guests rely on caller-provided hooks and `m80-guestd` exposes a typed seam for them.

## Dependencies

Phase D shipped.
close_reason: Resolved non-systemd VMGenID/userspace reseed question: documented that v0.1 guarantees host restore nonce + RNDRESEEDCRNG even for empty hook lists, treats missing systemd random-seed as normal, keeps machine-id/hostname as generic HookSpec variants, and leaves SSH host keys, daemon restarts, and app PRNG cache flushing to future closed typed HookSpec variants. Added regression test crates/m80-guestd/src/post_restore/tests.rs::empty_hook_list_still_mixes_nonce_and_reseeds and updated docs/behaviors/warm-pool/vmgenid-reseed-path.md, docs/behaviors/warm-pool/post-restore-hooks.md, crates/m80-guestd/README.md, and crates/m80-proto/README.md. title: Investigate: post-restore hook timeout semantics (per-hook? aggregate? fail-closed vs partial?)
description:
## Why

Phase D's hook executor runs sequentially and fail-closed on first error. But what if a hook hangs? Per-hook timeout? Lease-wide deadline? Hook ordering on partial timeout? The current design doesn't say.

## What to investigate

- Cap on total hook execution time per lease (suggest: 5s? 30s?).
- Per-hook vs aggregate timeout — which gives better operator-visible failure modes?
- What happens to the lease on timeout: fail-closed (current model) or partial-success (return lease without subsequent hooks)? Fail-closed is safer but more expensive in latency.
- Telemetry for hook latency outliers; alerting threshold.

## Output

- Decision record extension to `0006-snapshot-template-lifecycle.md` (or sibling ADR).
- Phase D Task 9 update if implementation changes.
- Possibly: new `HookTimeoutPolicy` typed knob in `WarmStrategy::SnapshotRestore { hooks, hook_timeout_policy, ... }`.

## Dependencies

Phase D shipped.

title: Investigate: pmem device size limits in Firecracker (admission validation + multi-layer fallback)
description:
## Why

Firecracker has a maximum pmem device size. What is it for the FC version we depend on? If an operator builds an erofs that exceeds the limit (a giant toolchain or multi-toolchain image), what's m80's behavior — admission rejection, silent truncation, fail-at-boot?

## What to investigate

- Identify FC's documented or de-facto max pmem device size at the version we pin.
- Behavior at admission: should we validate `ErofsImage::size_bytes` against the limit at `PmemLayer::new` construction?
- Mitigation if a workload genuinely needs more: split into multiple pmem layers (works today — Phase B's `Vec<PmemLayer>` supports it), or refuse at admission with a typed `FcError::PmemImageTooLarge { max, got }`.

## Output

- Validation in `PmemLayer::new` if there's a fixed FC limit worth pinning.
- Operator runbook note in Phase E or as a follow-up.
- If splitting is the recommended answer for large workloads: a small sub-epic for multi-layer-from-one-source tooling (chunking helper, mount-time recomposition).

## Dependencies

Phase B shipped.

Added ConfigError::PmemImageTooLarge, unit/display coverage, README/behavior/runbook/ADR notes, and follow-up epic m80-q420k.8.14 for optional split/recompose tooling. title: Investigate: image store GC + retention policy (refcount-aware, concurrency-safe)
description:
## Why

Phase B Task 5 ships a flat-directory store with no GC. Eventually the store grows unbounded and operators need to prune unreferenced images. Phase E mentioned this as a runbook concern; this task makes it real.

## What to investigate

- Refcount: cross-reference image digests against active templates + active VMs + pinned images.
- Triggering: on-demand via CLI (`m80 image gc`) vs background daemon vs disk-usage threshold-based.
- Concurrency: how to GC safely while attaches/restores are in flight (existing flock model + refcount markers from Phase C should compose, but the composition needs design).
- Retention policy knobs: TTL since last reference, min-keep-count, never-evict pin list.
- Path scheme migration: if flat-dir eventually becomes a problem (filesystem inode pressure at >>10k images), what's the migration to a sharded layout?

## Output

- Decision record `docs/decisions/00NN-image-store-gc.md`.
- Implementation as a follow-up sub-epic.

## Dependencies

Phase B + Phase C shipped (refcount markers from C inform the GC model).

title: Investigate: template hot-reload during host upgrade (drain vs serve-old-while-rebuilding)
description:
## Why

Phase D's invalidation contract: a fingerprint mismatch makes a template unusable; the fill worker rebuilds. But during the rebuild window, can the warm pool still serve from the invalidated templates? Or must the pool fully drain on every host upgrade?

## What to investigate

- Safety of serving from a fingerprint-mismatched template — depends on which fingerprint input changed:
  - Host kernel ABI break: restore-fatal; cannot serve.
  - FC patch bump: usually safe; restore typically still works.
  - Guest kernel version drift: maybe safe; depends on the change.
- Per-template invalidation severity classification.
- Cutover model options: drain-and-rebuild (safe, high lease-latency spike during upgrade) vs serve-old-while-rebuilding (faster, requires versioning the template pool and explicit "expiring" state).

## Output

- Decision record extension to `0006-snapshot-template-lifecycle.md`.
- Phase D Task 5 or 14 update if implementation changes.
- Possibly: `TemplateInvalidationSeverity` typed enum on the template store API.

## Dependencies

Phase D shipped + a host upgrade event observed in production.

No TemplateInvalidationSeverity or serve-old-while-rebuilding behavior lands now; that needs a separate future design with versioned slots if a real deployment requires it. title: Investigate: dm-snapshot vs reflinks revisit after Phase A real fill data (ext4 host path)

Phase A picked reflinks (XFS/Btrfs) with full-copy fallback on ext4. The alternative is dm-snapshot for per-VM CoW on any host FS, including ext4. After Phase A ships and we have real fill-latency numbers from ext4 hosts, re-evaluate.

title: Investigate: erofs version compatibility floor (guest kernel features vs mkfs.erofs defaults)
description:
## Why

Guest-side erofs support varies by kernel version. The guest kernel m80 ships today may or may not support the erofs feature set the host's `mkfs.erofs` produces. Mismatches surface as mount failures at guest boot, not at host build time — which is the worst failure window.

## What to investigate

- What erofs feature set does the guest kernel support (lz4, lz4hc, lzma, zstd, chunked, big-pcluster, ...)?
- Default `mkfs.erofs` behavior on the build host: what features does it enable by default?
- Pinning strategy: do we require `mkfs.erofs` to emit a specific feature set (host-side constraint), or do we relax requirements on the guest kernel (longer guest LTS support window)?

## Output

- Decision record or a runtime validation that rejects unsupported erofs feature combinations at `import_existing` time, before the image is ever attached to a guest.
- Phase B Task 5 update if `import_existing` should reject incompatible artifacts at ingest.

## Dependencies

Phase B shipped.

ImageKind::Erofs now runs dump.erofs -s before hashing/copying and admits only the guest-pinned floor: sb_csum, mtime, 0padding, and lz4/lz4hc compression if compr_algs is declared; non-erofs bytes, chunked_file, zstd/lzma/deflate-class outputs fail before content-addressing. Updated crate README plus docs/behaviors/rootfs/pmem-layers.md and docs/behaviors/image-build/pmem-erofs-dax-kernel.md. title: Investigate: memory pressure interaction with DAX pages (Phase C side-channel implication)
description:
## Why

Pmem-backed erofs pages are host page-cache backed. Under host memory pressure they can be evicted and safely re-faulted from the read-only backing file, but that behavior interacts with the Phase C same-trust-domain story: eviction/refault timing may reveal access-pattern information between guests sharing one DAX-backed image.

## Observable

`docs/perf/pmem-dax-memory-pressure.md` contains a real-substrate memory-pressure run using the `.8.12`-valid Shared payload layout: uncompressed, non-inlined erofs files mounted through virtio-pmem with guest-visible DAX.

The artifact records these named values:

- baseline Shared-payload read latency P50/P95/P99 before pressure, from at least two live Shared guests;
- post-pressure Shared-payload read/refault latency P50/P95/P99 after a documented host or sibling-VM memory-pressure workload;
- cross-guest signal delta: attacker-visible timing difference between cached-hit and post-pressure refault windows;
- host memory and page-cache deltas from before pressure, during pressure, and after the refault probe;
- teardown residue: leaked Shared markers = 0, leaked Firecracker/jailer processes = 0, leaked mounts = 0.

The artifact must state host kernel, filesystem, memory size, pressure command/workload, VM count, image digest/layout, run command, m80 commit, Firecracker version, and whether unrelated VMs were running.

## Decision Output

If the measured signal is acceptable under the existing same-trust-domain assumption, extend `docs/positioning.md` and `docs/runbook/layered-rootfs-operations.md` with the residual risk and no new runtime mitigation. If the signal is not acceptable, file single-purpose follow-up beads for candidate mitigations such as host-side `mlock`, `MAP_POPULATE`, or `madvise(MADV_WILLNEED)`; do not implement them inside this measurement bead.

## Acceptance

- Close reason cites `verified: docs/perf/pmem-dax-memory-pressure.md @ <commit>`.
- The artifact contains all named observable fields above and was produced on real KVM with actual Shared pmem guests.
- Any mitigation recommendation is backed by the measured numbers and has either a docs-only residual-risk update or a new implementation bead.

title: Concurrency / lock-ordering audit (W23)
description: Wave 23 of 25. Audited WarmPool locks, RunningSandbox concurrency, process spawn+reap, JSON state atomicity, bridge+iptables ordering, snapshot pause races, vsock send+recv, semaphore+lease ordering, OnceLock statics, Drop ordering. ~60% null/correct. Confirmed: single-Mutex design is sound, RAII guards correct order, &mut self exclusion enforces serialization, atomics use defensible Relaxed ordering with mutex fences. New findings: write_json_atomically not shared/factored, target_ready vs max_concurrent_vms unvalidated, watcher_thread not joined on fallback Drop, capture() should set watcher_stop pre-pause.

title: Extract write_json_atomically to a shared helper crate; multiple crates write JSON non-atomically
description:
**Finding:** The correct atomic-write pattern (tmp + write_all + sync_all + rename + dir-sync_all) is implemented ONCE — privately in crates/m80-net-outbound/src/state.rs:303 (write_json_atomically). Every other JSON state write reimplements (or skips) the pattern independently:

- m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:312 — O_TRUNC + O_NOFOLLOW, no rename (m80-o870o.2 covers)
- m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:106 — fs::write (cgroup-path.txt; W20L3)
- m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/status.rs:233 — fs::write (owner.json)
- m80-image-manifest/src/lib.rs:214 — fs::write (Manifest::write)
- m80-firecracker/src/boot_identity.rs:41 — fs::write
- m80-preflight/src/cache.rs:102 — fs::write (sentinel; best-effort by design)

No shared helper exists. CLAUDE.md anti-junk-drawer rule means no m80-utils — but a domain-named crate (m80-atomic-file or m80-fs) is OK.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (consistency + correctness; partial reads possible on concurrent reader/crash).

**Acceptance:**
- Extract write_json_atomically into a small m80-atomic-file crate (or pub(crate)-promote into a shared module).
- Migrate 5 sites: jailer plan/state, cgroup-path.txt, owner.json, Manifest::write, boot_identity.
- Keep PreflightCache::save and ownership.lock as-is (intentionally non-atomic).
- Cross-link m80-o870o.2 (jailer-state.json specifically).

Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-o870o.2: jailer-state.json truncation race is a concrete bug instance driving the refactor; preserve: the "live VM misclassified as orphan" scenario

title: WarmPool::new should validate target_ready <= max_concurrent_vms
description:
**Finding:** WarmPool::new doesn't check target_ready against the backend's max_concurrent_vms. A misconfigured pool with target_ready > max_concurrent_vms gets backoff churn forever: background fill workers permanently loop on AdmissionRefused after slots are leased. Operator sees consecutive_fill_errors growing + log spam, not a clean ConfigError at construction.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:139-175 (WarmPool::new).

**Severity:** LOW (operator-visible via backoff but should be construction-time rejected).

**Acceptance:**
- In WarmPool::new, after the existing target_ready > 0 + workspace.is_none() validation, add: if target_ready > backend.max_concurrent_vms() → ConfigError::InvalidValue with reason.
- Backend exposes max_concurrent_vms() getter (likely already does).
- Test pin.
notes:
Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-i8rua.4: preallocated_drive_slots == 0 check is a second validation in the same WarmPool::new block; preserve: the golden-VM-capture / restore-path s
close_reason: WarmPool::new and set_target_ready reject target_ready above max_concurrent_vms; pinned by warm_pool tests and documented in docs/behaviors/warm-pool/runtime-control-and-counters.md.

title: watcher_thread not joined in fallback ForceKillGuard::drop; 30s zombie thread per leaked sandbox
description:
**Finding:** RunningSandbox::stop() and force_kill() explicitly destructure + join the watcher_thread after setting watcher_stop. But when RunningSandbox is dropped implicitly (without calling stop/force_kill — e.g., via panic, ?-unwind, or test cleanup), the watcher_thread JoinHandle is dropped without being joined. The thread holds Arc<AtomicBool> for stop_flag, so it doesn't dangle; it exits on its next poll cycle (up to 30s sleep). 30-second zombie thread per implicitly-dropped sandbox.

ForceKillGuard::drop DOES set watcher_stop (correctly), but the JoinHandle is in a different field — when RunningSandbox is destructured by Drop, watcher_thread's JoinHandle drops without join.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs (RunningSandbox.watcher_thread field declaration); lifecycle.rs ForceKillGuard::drop.

**Severity:** LOW (bounded thread lifetime; resource-leak class).

**Acceptance:**
- Move the join logic into ForceKillGuard::drop OR Add a wrapper around watcher_thread that joins on Drop.
- Option B is cleaner: WatcherThreadHandle (Option<JoinHandle> + Arc<AtomicBool>); Drop sets stop_flag and joins with a short timeout (e.g., 100ms).
- Cross-link m80-ag33f.6 (ForceKillGuard docs).

title: capture() should set watcher_stop before PATCH Paused to suppress spurious vsock warn
description:
**Finding:** capture() takes &mut self but doesn't set watcher_stop before issuing PATCH /vm Paused. If the idle watcher happens to fire during the (~100ms) capture window, it calls send_shutdown_request which opens a vsock UDS to a paused FC. Connect either hangs until OS connect timeout or gets refused. Watcher logs a warn and returns — benign but noisy.

The capture() docstring at lifecycle.rs:69-82 documents this gap as known.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs (capture method; the existing PATCH Paused call site).

**Severity:** LOW (cosmetic — spurious warn log; no functional impact).

**Acceptance:**
- At top of capture(), before PATCH Paused: self.watcher_stop.store(true, Relaxed);
- Document that capture()'s &mut self combined with the watcher_stop flag means watcher will exit cleanly.
- Optional: remove the gap note from capture() docstring once fixed.

title: Wave 39 of 45: concurrency primitives + lock ordering + atomics
description:
Wave 39/45. 10 sonnets, lenses:
1. Mutex/RwLock inventory; what each protects
2. Lock ordering — same-resource locks held in different orders
3. Atomic usage — ordering (Relaxed/Acquire/Release/SeqCst) discipline
4. OnceLock/OnceCell init races, retry-on-failure semantics
5. Channel patterns: bounded vs unbounded mpsc; SendError/RecvError handling
6. Thread spawning: who owns the JoinHandle, panic propagation
7. Condvar usage; spurious wakeup correctness; wait_timeout
8. Send + Sync bounds on public types; accidental Sync via UnsafeCell
9. Long-running locks: locks held across IO (mount, network)
10. parking_lot vs std sync drift

title: idle_timed_out + watcher_stop atomics use Relaxed where Release/Acquire is required
description:
**Finding (W39.3):** Several cross-thread signal flags use Ordering::Relaxed where the load-after-store synchronization needs Release/Acquire to establish happens-before with non-atomic state.

HIGH (latent on non-x86):
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:555 — idle_timed_out.store(true, Relaxed). Watcher writes the flag AFTER computing timeout decision (reading last_activity_ns, comparing wall time).
- Loads at:
  - lifecycle/exec.rs:36 (gate before begin_exec_activity)
  - lifecycle/health.rs:16
  - lifecycle/fileops.rs:270
  - lifecycle/hotplug.rs:142
  - lifecycle/metrics.rs:16
  All Relaxed.

On x86 TSO this is invisible (TSO ≈ all-Release on stores). On ARM/RISC-V the compiler+CPU can reorder; LLVM may hoist Relaxed loads. Bug becomes visible on aarch64 hosts.

MED (delayed shutdown only — no data published):
- watcher_stop / stop_flag / shutdown atomics in lifecycle.rs:136,219, types.rs:370 (ForceKillGuard::drop), exec.rs:573,591 (forwarder threads), warm_pool.rs:180,295,340.
All Relaxed. Worst outcome: a few extra loop iterations before exit. Fix-along-with-idle_timed_out.

Severity: HIGH (correctness latent on non-x86; m80 targets Linux x86_64 today per W35.4, but aarch64 inevitable).

Acceptance:
- idle_timed_out: stores → Release, loads → Acquire.
- watcher_stop / stop / shutdown: stores → Release, loads → Acquire (or SeqCst for uniformity).
- Counter-only atomics (active_execs, last_activity_ns, next_slot, REQUESTS_TOTAL) stay Relaxed — correct as audited.
- Add doc comment block at each atomic field explaining the chosen ordering.
- Cross-link m80-jcwcy.* (idle-timeout state machine) and m80-9jfaz.* (vm_id spans).

title: Thread spawn discipline: no thread names, panic silently lost in let _ = join() patterns
description:
**Finding (W39.6):** Workspace-wide gap: no thread::Builder::new().name(...) anywhere in prod paths; panics in spawned threads silently lost on Drop.

Sites:
- crates/m80-guestd/src/connection.rs:311 — detached spawn (let _); exec worker. Panic surfaces only as channel RecvError.
- crates/m80-guestd/src/uevent.rs:218 — spawn_netlink_listener; loop runs forever; no shutdown signal.
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:502 spawn_idle_watcher — handle held in RunningSandbox.watcher_thread; verify join path.
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/exec.rs:365 + :744 — cancel_forwarder, pty_event_forwarder. CancelForwarder::Drop and PtyEventForwarder::Drop do `let _ = thread.join()`. Panic lost.
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool/fill_worker.rs:35 — detached; no handle stored. Panic leaves filling counter stuck → pool stalls.
- crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/run_stream.rs:94 + pty.rs — signal-watcher; `let _ = join()` in SignalWatcher::Drop.

Severity: MEDIUM (observability + reliability — silent thread death breaks correctness invisibly).

Acceptance:
- Thread naming: thread::Builder::new().name(format!("m80-{}", role)).spawn(...). Names visible in /proc/<pid>/task/*/comm and tracing.
- fill_worker: capture JoinHandle into WarmPool.fill_workers: Vec<JoinHandle>; on Drop, join + log panics.
- Forwarder::Drop: replace `let _ = join()` with match join() { Err(panic) => tracing::error!(?panic, "forwarder panicked") }.
- guestd connection.rs:311 — propagate panic via dedicated error channel or wrap in catch_unwind so RecvError → typed error variant.
- Cross-link m80-9jfaz.2 (spans + vm_id on errors).
close_reason: Merged into m80-wok08.3: Both address panic-in-spawned-thread silently swallowed

title: Misc concurrency cleanups: incoherent Mutex<UnixStream> contract + redundant OnceLock+Mutex patterns
description:
**Finding (W39.1 + W39.4):**

LOW (contract incoherence):
- crates/m80-firecracker-client/src/lib.rs:25 — `Mutex<UnixStream>` field with comment "concurrency is caller's responsibility". The mutex either exists for a reason or doesn't. Resolution: keep mutex AND remove the comment (real reason: Firecracker doesn't handle concurrent writes — per W39.9 finding), OR drop the mutex and switch send() to take &mut self.

LOW (redundant double-locking):
- crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:40 — SUBTREE_CONTROL_PRIMED: OnceLock<()> AND SUBTREE_CONTROL_PRIME_LOCK: OnceLock<Mutex<()>>. The second OnceLock is redundant; OnceLock::get_or_init alone provides at-most-one-init. Collapse.
- crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/hotplug.rs:24 — static Mutex<()> alongside OnceLock<Arc<UeventRegistry>>. Same redundancy.
- crates/m80-guestd/src/guest_log.rs:12 — OnceLock<Mutex<Option<File>>>. After init the Option is always Some; the Mutex serializes /dev/kmsg writes, which the kernel already atomicizes for <4096-byte lines. Switch to OnceLock<File> + remove Mutex.

LOW (overkill primitive):
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs:29 — Arc<Mutex<u32>> as Semaphore. Switch to Arc<AtomicU32> with CAS loop; eliminates a mutex and matches the atomic-only style elsewhere.

NULL audits:
- W39.2 (lock ordering): only one site with two simultaneous locks (NETWORK_ALLOCATION_MUTEX → flock); single call site enforces order; no inversion possible.
- W39.5 (channels): no unbounded amplification risk in practice; pty event_tx noted as low risk only.
- W39.7 (Condvar): both sites correct — spurious-wakeup loops in place, notify_all matches multi-waiter shape.
- W39.8 (Send/Sync/UnsafeCell): zero hits — CLAUDE.md `unsafe forbidden` rule fully honored.
- W39.9 (locks across IO): no problematic patterns; documented intent in firecracker-client + net-outbound.
- W39.10 (parking_lot drift): zero parking_lot in workspace; uniformly std::sync.

Severity: LOW (clarity/simplification).
Acceptance: 4 targeted refactors per the list above; no semantic change.

title: Define JoinNetns guest NIC attachment contract
description:
m80-mx2t.3 asks for a functional JoinNetns E2E where guest traffic routes through a caller-created netns. The current JoinNetns implementation only passes --netns to the official Firecracker jailer so the VMM process enters the namespace; preboot emits no NetworkInterfaceConfig, no TAP is created inside or moved into that namespace, and the guest sees no NIC.

Before a functional guest-traffic E2E can be honest, m80 needs an explicit hard-cutover contract for how JoinNetns supplies a guest NIC. Decide and implement one shape, likely either: (a) m80 creates/configures a TAP inside the caller netns from a supplied guest IPv4/MAC/gateway contract, or (b) caller provides an already-created TAP/device descriptor and m80 only wires Firecracker. Update m80-net-mode, m80-firecracker, m80-jailer docs/READMEs, and real-KVM tests in the same diff.

Acceptance: JoinNetns launch creates or consumes a concrete guest NIC according to the chosen contract; Firecracker gets a network-interface PUT for that NIC; a real-KVM test proves a guest can reach a veth peer available only inside the joined netns; NoEgress and AllowOutbound behavior remain unchanged.

title: Warm-pool subsystem deep-dive (W11 epic)
description:
Captures findings from goal-driven Wave 11 (slot state machine, fill backoff, lease lifecycle, owner socket protocol, drain semantics, dynamic config, observability, startup ordering, shutdown signal handling, per-slot isolation). ~30-35% null. Cross-links: m80-243wj (reliability), m80-mrjqs (observability), m80-kv4ri (snapshot).

Key findings worth highlighting:
- Owner has NO signal handler — SIGTERM orphans socket + owner.json
- last_fill_error never forwarded to status RPC response (always null)
- WarmPool::Drop can hang forever if fill thread panics after FillGuard disarm

title: Warm owner has no signal handler; SIGTERM orphans owner.sock + owner.json
description:
**Finding:** owner.rs:run_foreground_inner runs a synchronous accept loop with NO signal handler installed. signal_hook infrastructure exists in the same module tree (used by pty.rs:172) but is unused here. On SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, the default Rust handler terminates immediately. The post-loop cleanup at owner.rs:183-185 (status::remove_owner_state + fs::remove_dir_all(snapshot_dir)) is NEVER reached. UnixListener::drop does NOT unlink the socket on Linux. Result: owner.sock + owner.json + warm/snapshot/ all orphan. Next 'm80 warm owner' start fails at socket_path.exists() check with WarmOwnerSocketExists.

**File:** crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/owner.rs:74 (bind), :183-185 (unreachable cleanup).

**Severity:** HIGH (real bug; clean SIGTERM is broken). Compounds m80-kv4ri.11 (no crash-orphan GC).

**Acceptance:**
- Install signal_hook (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) before listener.incoming(); pattern in pty.rs:172.
- On signal: set shutdown flag; break the accept loop; let normal post-loop cleanup run.
- Test: spawn warm owner, send SIGTERM, assert socket+identity files are gone.
- Cross-link: m80-243wj (reliability).

title: WarmPoolConfig: no target_ready upper bound + immutable post-construction
description:

No max_pool_size field. Config is also fully immutable post-construction: no set_target_ready, no live snapshot swap (cross m80-kv4ri.10). Scaling 4→8 requires drain+restart, undocumented anywhere.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:84-91 (config), :127-139 (validation), no resize API.

**Severity:** LOW (operational ergonomics + safety).

**Acceptance:**
- Add max_pool_size: usize to WarmPoolConfig (default 32 or operator-configured). Reject target_ready > max_pool_size at construction.
- Document drain→restart procedure as the only reconfigure path in m80-cli/README.md.
- Defer live resize to a follow-up if/when needed.

title: Owner startup: socket bind after full fill = O(N) silent window before owner accepts
description:
**Finding:** owner.rs:74 (UnixListener bind) executes only after the entire synchronous fill_to_target_blocking completes. With target_ready=N and each slot taking ~restore-time + RESTORED_SLOT_SETTLE=1s, startup latency is O(N) seconds before the socket appears. Clients see ENOENT during this window — correct gating, but the silence is invisible. No progress reporting, no 'initializing' identity file.

**File:** crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/owner.rs:72-74.

**Severity:** LOW (operational UX; correctness is fine).

**Acceptance:**

Option B (higher-effort): bind socket first; accept Status requests during fill; only reject Run requests until first slot is ready.

title: WarmPool::set_target_ready — live runtime resize API for consumers with dynamic load
description:
**Follow-up to closed m80-r4308.10** which deliberately deferred live resize: 'Defer live resize to a follow-up if/when needed.' A consumer now needs it.

## Motivation

A downstream consumer (Torpor2 — see /tank/projects/torpor2 br-7717u 'Pressure-based sandbox pool autoscaling') wants to dynamically adjust target_ready based on observed pressure. Today m80 forces drain+restart of the entire Backend to change the configured target_ready, which is heavyweight for a single-tenant consumer doing routine autoscaling.

The distinction we'd like to honor: **mechanism vs policy.**
- Mechanism (changing pool size, evicting surplus slots, replenishing): touches VM state -> m80's scope (VM mechanics).
- Policy (when/why to scale, pressure detection, hysteresis): consumer-shape decisions -> consumer's scope.

The Bestiary doc (docs/future-directions/bestiary-conveyor-belt.md) correctly out-of-scopes 'elastic buffer, scale-to-zero, profile management, tenant routing' for m80 — but the consumer-side reading is that 'profile management + tenant routing' is genuinely multi-tenant orchestration (Bestiary territory), while 'elastic buffer + scale-to-zero' is policy that can be driven from a single consumer if m80 exposes the resize *mechanism*.

## Proposed API (sketch)

    impl WarmPool {
        /// Adjust target_ready at runtime. The pool will replenish (if growing)
        /// or mark surplus slots for eviction (if shrinking). Returns the new
        /// target_ready after admission-limit clamping.
        pub fn set_target_ready(&self, new: NonZeroUsize) -> Result<NonZeroUsize, FcError>;
    }

**Semantics:**
- Growing: deficit_calc(target - (ready+filling)) increases -> existing fill_worker (warm_pool.rs:345-372) replenishes naturally. No new code path needed for grow.
- Shrinking: surplus slots get marked for eviction at next acquire-or-idle-timeout; never force-drops a leased slot. Or: just stop replenishing and let natural attrition + idle_timeout shrink the pool — simpler.
- Clamping: new <= configured max_pool_size (or max_concurrent_vms admission limit per m80-qei44.2). Returns clamped value so the caller knows.
- Validation: same as new() — non-zero, workspace-config compatibility (warm_pool.rs:139-152).

## Why a setter instead of a 'control trait'

CLAUDE.md ('we are the someone', :177) — no abstraction without a second consumer. A simple setter on WarmPool keeps the surface minimal. Policy lives outside; only the primitive moves.

## Acceptance

- WarmPool exposes set_target_ready (or equivalent name)
- Growing: deficit recalculates correctly; fill_worker replenishes; integration test asserts pool grows
- Shrinking: surplus slots are evicted at next opportunity; never drops a leased slot; integration test asserts pool shrinks
- WarmPoolSnapshot reflects new target_ready immediately even before deficit settles
- No regression in m80-target-e2e-warm-pool / m80-target-e2e-warmpool real-KVM tests

## Out of scope

- Tenant-aware sizing, profile-aware buffers, scale-to-zero policy — those remain Bestiary's job per the future-directions doc.
- Live config swap for non-pool fields — m80-r4308.10's broader 'immutable post-construction' decision stands for everything except target_ready.

## Consumer use case (informational)

Torpor2's br-7717u plans an adapter-side scaler that:
1. Observes pressure (PoolEmpty hit rate, busy-ratio from WarmPoolSnapshot)
2. Computes a new target_ready with hysteresis + decay
3. Calls set_target_ready(N)

Without this API, Torpor's scaler is forced to drain-and-rebuild from outside (~200+ LOC of state coordination). With this API, the scaler is ~100 LOC of pure policy.
close_reason: WarmPool::set_target_ready implemented with grow/shrink semantics, immediate snapshot update, admission/cpuset validation, README/doc updates, warm_pool regression coverage, and selected real-KVM warm-pool coverage.

title: Forward typed fileops through WarmLease: read_file/write_file/list_dir/stat_file/mkdir/remove
description:
**Finding:** WarmLease (warm_pool/lease.rs) exposes only exec variants + attach_drive_verified. The typed fileops surface on RunningSandbox (crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle/fileops.rs:22,104,123,131,144,159,178: read_file, write_file, list_dir, stat_file, mkdir, remove_file, plus chunked variants) is unreachable through the lease.

For the v0.1 anchor consumer (torpor — see m80-f20y0.1), this forces three bad options:
- Wrap each fileop as exec /bin/cat /bin/tee — loses typed FileError variants (NotFound vs PermissionDenied vs ELOOP etc.), loses path identity verification, payloads round-trip through argv quoting.
- Cold-boot per file op — defeats the warm pool's reason to exist.
- Maintain a separate non-warm path for file-op tools — branches the consumer code unnecessarily.

The right fix is option (c): mirror WarmLease::exec*'s shape with thin pass-throughs that take &mut self, drop into the inner RunningSandbox, return the same FileError result.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (blocks consumer adoption of warm-pool for file-op tools).

**Acceptance:**
- Add to crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool/lease.rs:
  - pub fn read_file(&mut self, req: &FileReadRequest) -> Result<FileReadResponse, FcError>
  - pub fn write_file(&mut self, req: &FileWriteRequest) -> Result<FileWriteResponse, FcError>
  - pub fn list_dir, stat_file, mkdir, remove_file, plus the chunked write/read variants if surface review keeps them.
  - Each is a one-liner delegating to the inner RunningSandbox method.
- Add a test mirroring tests/bestiary_stand_in_real_kvm.rs that exercises read+write through WarmLease.
- Update crates/m80-firecracker/README.md WarmLease section to list the new surface.
- Cross-link m80-f20y0.1 (consumer-gap framing) and m80-r4308 epic.

**Why this wasn't caught by the 4 dedupe passes:** the surface analysis only saw what's filed; this is a new gap revealed by an actual consumer-side design walkthrough.
close_reason: WarmLease now forwards typed fileops including read/write/list/stat/mkdir/remove/upload plus README/doc updates; exercised through bestiary real-KVM WarmLease fileops coverage and cargo test gates.

title: Per-lease drive-hotplug workspace contract has single test exerciser; first consumer regression undetected
description:
**Finding:** The per-lease workspace-via-hotplug contract — WarmLease::attach_drive_verified(HotplugDriveAttach { slot, path_on_host, mount_path, identity_path, expected_identity }) at warm_pool/lease.rs:93-114 — has exactly one integration test exerciser: tests/bestiary_stand_in_real_kvm.rs:66-82.

Surrounding facts:
- WarmPool::new (warm_pool.rs:146-152) REJECTS any SandboxConfig.workspace value, so pool slots boot with no workspace and no scratch — the only path to give a slot a workspace is post-lease via attach_drive_verified.
- The warm-owner CLI sets preallocated_drive_slots: 0 and never attaches drives (cross-link m80-f20y0.1).
- Zero production consumers exercise the contract today; if torpor or any future consumer adopts it, the first regression that breaks the contract goes undetected by `cargo test --workspace`.

What can silently break:
- HotplugDriveAttach field semantics (path_on_host = host vs in-jail — cross m80-h3k02.1 path-wrapper bead)
- identity verification flow (expected_identity matching)
- mount_path validation
- slot-index bounds
- drive-not-yet-attached vs drive-already-attached state
- error variant typing on hotplug failure

**Severity:** MEDIUM (latent; bites the first real consumer).

**Acceptance:**
- Add at minimum 3 more tests under crates/m80-firecracker/tests/ exercising HotplugDriveAttach corners:
  1. Identity mismatch rejected with the typed FcError variant.
  2. Out-of-range slot index rejected.
  3. Attach-then-detach-then-attach to the same slot (covers placeholder PATCH lifecycle).
- Add a behavior doc at docs/behaviors/warm-pool/per-lease-workspace.md describing the contract: pool slots boot empty, workspace attaches post-lease, identity verification model.
- Update crates/m80-firecracker/README.md WarmLease section to name the workspace-attach pattern as a first-class adapter surface.
- Cross-link m80-f20y0.1 (consumer gap), m80-h3k02.1 (path wrappers — HotplugDriveAttach.path_on_host is one of the 5 mix-up sites), m80-r4308.15 (fileops-on-WarmLease).
close_reason: Implemented per-lease drive-hotplug coverage: identity mismatch, out-of-range slot, attach-detach-attach lifecycle; added docs/behaviors/warm-pool/per-lease-workspace.md and README WarmLease contract; verified with selected real-KVM bestiary tests and cargo test gates.

title: Lease-counter + cpuset unrecoverable on mem::forget/leak; no leak detector
description:
**Finding:** WarmLease, WarmSlot, AdmissionPermit decrement state.leased / release cpuset / decrement permits via Drop only. A `std::mem::forget(lease)`, `Box::leak(Box::new(lease))`, or an Arc cycle preventing the final drop means state.leased never decrements, cpuset CPUs never return to free_cpuset_cpus, and the admission permit stays held. Pool gradually starves; PoolEmpty surfaces only after the leak count grows past target_ready.

CLAUDE.md forbids `unsafe`, so the workspace itself won't produce mem::forget directly — but a consumer crate or future test scaffold could (precedent: m80-xeaey.4 covers RunningSandbox::force_kill which already uses mem::forget).

**Severity:** MEDIUM (consumer-facing footgun; blocks adoption confidence).

**Acceptance:**
- Add `#[must_use = "..."]` on WarmLease, WarmSlot, AdmissionPermit with crisp warning text. Cross-link m80-xeaey.5 which already proposes #[must_use] discipline on guard-returning fns; this extends it to the guard *types* themselves.
- Add a `pub fn release(self)` on WarmLease that performs the decrement explicitly + documents that drop is best-effort. Consumers who want defensive code call .release() at known release points; mem::forget on a non-released lease is then a static-analyzable bug instead of a silent leak.
- Document the constraint in m80-firecracker README's WarmLease section.
- Cross-link m80-xeaey.3 (silent discard_sandbox), m80-r4308.4 (snapshot fields), m80-r4308.15/.16 (consumer surface).

title: target_ready growth silently stalls if cpu_allocator window not extended
description:
**Finding:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:361-364: target_ready is silently bounded by the CPU allocator's window. WarmPool::new initializes free_cpuset_cpus from a fixed range; if a future `set_target_ready(n)` setter (or external scaler-driven grow) requests target_ready > cpu_allocator capacity, fill_worker will spin trying to allocate cpuset slots that don't exist, returning Err(...) on each attempt.

Today this is latent because target_ready is fixed at WarmPool::new time and validated against cpuset capacity at construction. The bug fires the moment a `set_target_ready` setter is added (which is the natural shape for an external scaler).

**Severity:** LOW (latent; no setter exists today).

**Acceptance:**
- Document the coupling at the cpu_allocator field with a // INVARIANT: comment.
- When set_target_ready is added (likely as part of m80-r4308.* scaler work), either (a) reject grow requests above cpu_allocator window with a typed error, or (b) extend the cpu_allocator window atomically before bumping target_ready.
- Add a test that constructs a pool with target_ready=N+1 against cpu_allocator window=N and asserts WarmPool::new rejects rather than silently stalling.
- Cross-link m80-r4308.15+.16 (consumer-facing surface), m80-mrjqs.3 (scaler/metrics work).

title: Emit warm-pool lifecycle tracing events (slot_filled, slot_leased, fill_failed) for scaler consumption
description:
**Finding:** warm_pool.rs has zero tracing emissions for slot lifecycle. An external scaler/autoscaler watching pool health must poll WarmPoolSnapshot and derive everything from deltas:
- "slot just filled" = ready++ vs prior snapshot
- "fill failed" = ready stayed flat AND consecutive_fill_errors++ (and that's not in snapshot today — m80-r4308.4)
- "lease acquired" = leased++ vs prior
- "lease returned + discarded" = leased-- AND discarded++

Polling-delta is fragile (loses transitions between samples), expensive (forces fast poll intervals), and forces every consumer to re-implement state-machine inference.

The fix is structured tracing events at lifecycle transitions. m80-9jfaz.2 adds vm_id correlation broadly but does NOT specifically address warm-pool lifecycle events; that's the gap.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (blocks practical external autoscaling).

**Acceptance:**
- Emit tracing::info!(target = "m80_firecracker::warm_pool::lifecycle", vm_id, slot_id, ...) at each transition:
  - filling → ready ("warm_pool.slot_filled")
  - ready → leased ("warm_pool.slot_leased")
  - leased → returned ("warm_pool.lease_returned", outcome=success/error/discarded)
  - filling/ready → discarded ("warm_pool.fill_failed", reason=...)
  - shutdown drain ("warm_pool.shutdown_discarded")
- Cross-link m80-mrjqs.3 (Prometheus scrape — these tracing events can ALSO drive counter updates), m80-9jfaz.2 (vm_id span discipline), m80-9jfaz.1 (sub-target naming convention — m80_firecracker::warm_pool::lifecycle fits the convention).
- Document the event taxonomy in docs/behaviors/warm-pool/lifecycle-events.md.
- Add a test that runs a fill→lease→return cycle and asserts the 4 expected events fire (use tracing_subscriber::fmt::TestWriter — depends on m80-9jfaz.6 tracing-subscriber adoption).

title: WarmControlRequest::Status always passes last_error=None; live fill error never surfaced
description:
**Finding:** WarmPoolState::last_fill_error is set on every fill failure (warm_pool.rs:117), cleared on success. But WarmPool::snapshot() at :395-404 does NOT copy it into WarmPoolSnapshot. owner.rs:104-112 handling WarmControlRequest::Status hardcodes `last_error: None` in the response. Operators running 'm80 warm status' while fills are repeatedly failing ALWAYS see last_error: null. The error is only set by the static 'unavailable' / 'profile_mismatch' code paths in status.rs.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:395-404 (snapshot omits field), crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/owner.rs:104-112 (hardcoded None).

**Severity:** HIGH (real bug; operator observability silently broken).

**Acceptance:**
- Add `last_fill_error: Option<String>` and `consecutive_fill_errors: u32` to WarmPoolSnapshot.
- Plumb through control.rs StatusResponse → status.rs available()/render().
- Test pin: trigger 3 consecutive fill failures, assert status RPC returns the error string.
- Cross-link m80-mrjqs.3 (warm-pool depth gauges).
notes:
Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-wok08.9: /4 (combined observability bead) — `WarmPoolFillFailed
- m80-r4308.9: /4/wok08.9 — Per-lease age tracking / stuck leases invisible.
close_reason: Merged into m80-r4308.4: `last_fill_error` never surfaced in Status response;

title: WarmPool::Drop hangs forever if fill thread panics after FillGuard disarm
description:
**Finding:** FillGuard is disarmed immediately on thread entry (warm_pool.rs:340-341) before launch_slot(). If launch_slot or subsequent code panics, state.filling is never decremented. WarmPool::Drop (:261-286) loops on wait_timeout(50ms) until state.filling == 0 — with no decrement, this spins forever. The FillGuard was intended only to cover thread::spawn failure, not panics inside the spawned closure.

This is the same hang vector that would also bite SIGTERM (once m80-r4308.1 lands the signal handler) and Drain (which calls wait_for_idle).

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:340-341 (premature disarm), :261-286 (unbounded spin).

**Severity:** MEDIUM. Cross-link m80-243wj.17 (similar finding; verify dedup vs extend).

**Acceptance:**
- Re-arm FillGuard inside the closure with a catch_unwind boundary: panic→decrement filling→resume_unwind.
- Add bounded spin budget in WarmPool::Drop (e.g., 30s) with last-resort SIGKILL on tracked fill-worker pids.
- Test: inject panic in launch_slot; assert Drop completes within budget.
close_reason: Merged into m80-xeaey.3: `WarmPool::Drop` hangs forever if fill thread panics

title: Failed slots invisible in WarmPoolSnapshot (no failed_fill_count)
description:
**Finding:** WarmPoolSnapshot exposes ready/filling/leased/discarded but omits consecutive_fill_errors and any monotonic fill_attempts_total / fill_failures_total counters. A pool in a permanent fill-failure loop renders as {ready:0, filling:0, leased:0} — indistinguishable from idle, not-yet-warmed pool. last_fill_error is the only signal and it's not surfaced (cf m80-r4308.2).

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:61-72 (snapshot type), :395-404 (snapshot() impl), :117-120 (state fields not copied).

**Severity:** LOW-MEDIUM. Folded into m80-mrjqs.3 conceptually — this is the warm-pool side of the metrics gap.

**Acceptance:**
- Add consecutive_fill_errors, fill_attempts_total, fill_failures_total, lease_acquired_total, lease_returned_total to WarmPoolSnapshot.
- Plumb to status.rs render so 'm80 warm status' shows them.
- Cross-link m80-mrjqs.3, m80-r4308.2.
notes:
Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-r4308.2: `last_fill_error` never surfaced in Status response;
close_reason: WarmPoolSnapshot now exposes consecutive fill errors, fill attempts/failures, and lease acquire/return totals; warm status renders them; covered by warm_pool and CLI status tests plus docs/behaviors/warm-pool/runtime-control-and-counters.md.

title: Owner accept loop has no read timeout; slow/stalled client freezes pool
description:
**Finding:** Owner accepts on a single-threaded UnixListener loop. read_request calls read_to_end which blocks until client half-closes (Shutdown::Write). A client that connects, writes 1 byte, and stalls freezes the entire accept loop indefinitely — no other client can be served, including Status/Drain. set_read_timeout is never called on the accepted stream.

**File:** crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/owner.rs:101-102 (no set_read_timeout), crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/control.rs:287-289 (read_to_end).

**Severity:** MEDIUM (single client can freeze pool operability; local-user only, so not remote-DoS).

**Acceptance:**
- Call accepted.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(30))) before read_request.
- Also set_write_timeout to prevent symmetric block.
- On WouldBlock/TimedOut, drop the connection with a typed Protocol error logged.
- Cross-link m80-r4308.6 (unbounded request size — same socket hardening).
notes:
Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-r4308.7: Client crash during owner response write exits owner
- m80-r4308.6: Unbounded request

title: Owner request parser has unbounded request size; large stdin can pin owner memory
description:
**Finding:** control.rs:read_request uses read_to_end with no size cap. A client sending a pathologically large ExecRequest.stdin forces the owner to buffer the entire payload before parsing. Local-only Unix socket so exploit surface is self-inflicted, but as stdin passthrough grows (e.g., large data piped into warm exec) the implicit unbounded buffering becomes an operational footgun.

**File:** crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/control.rs:287-289 (read_to_end).

**Severity:** LOW (local Unix socket; closed call graph). Pair with m80-r4308.5 for socket hardening.

**Acceptance:**
- Read into a Vec<u8> with a configurable MAX_REQUEST_BYTES cap (default e.g. 16 MiB).
- On overflow: return typed Protocol error to client.
- Or: switch to length-prefix framing (4-byte BE u32, matching vsock framing in m80-vsock).

title: Client crash during owner response write → owner exits (entire pool dies)
description:
**Finding:** If client disconnects after the owner started writing the response, write_all returns BrokenPipe → FcError::Io → owner.rs:177 returns the error from run_foreground_inner — the entire owner process exits, killing all ready slots and any in-flight leases. A misbehaving local client can tear down the entire warm pool.

**File:** crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/warm/owner.rs:175-180 (error propagation from handler exits the accept loop).

**Severity:** MEDIUM (pool resilience).

**Acceptance:**
- Per-request errors (Io/BrokenPipe on the per-connection stream) should log + continue the accept loop, NOT propagate out of the accept-loop iteration.
- Only fatal owner-state errors (cgroup gone, pool poisoned) should exit the loop.
- Test: connect; receive partial response; close abruptly; assert owner still serves a follow-up Status request.
close_reason: Merged into m80-r4308.5: Client crash during owner response write exits owner

title: fill_to_target_blocking does not increment filling — transient ready > target_ready
description:
**Finding:** fill_to_target_blocking (warm_pool.rs:160-177) holds the state lock only long enough to check ready.len() >= target_ready, then releases before launch_slot. If start_background_fill runs concurrently (e.g., a second caller thread or a lease-finished callback), it sees the deficit and spawns a fill worker for a slot fill_to_target_blocking is already producing. Both succeed; both push to ready; ready.len() transiently > target_ready.

No process leak — slots are killed on Drop — but the invariant ready.len() ≤ target_ready can be violated.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:160-177 (no filling++), :300-316 (background path correctly increments).

**Severity:** LOW (transient; benign).

**Acceptance:**
- Increment state.filling in fill_to_target_blocking before releasing the lock, matching the background path's accounting.
- Decrement on launch_slot return (success or failure).
- Test: race fill_to_target_blocking against start_background_fill; assert ready.len() ≤ target_ready throughout.

title: No per-lease age tracking; stuck leases invisible
description:
**Finding:** WarmLease carries no timestamp. No tracing span opened in WarmLease::new and closed in release_and_refill. No 'oldest lease age' metric in WarmPoolSnapshot. Operator sees leased=1 indefinitely with no signal whether it's a normal slow exec or a stuck one. Cross-link m80-r4308.5 (no read timeout) — combined, a stuck client + stuck lease are invisible.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool/lease.rs (WarmLease struct).

**Severity:** LOW (observability + debugging).

**Acceptance:**
- Add lease_started_at: Instant to WarmLease.
- Add lease_age_p50/p95/max gauge to WarmPoolSnapshot.
- Open tracing span (target = 'warm_lease', vm_id field) at WarmLease::new; close on release_and_refill.
- Cross-link m80-mrjqs.6.
close_reason: Merged into m80-r4308.2: /4/wok08.9 — Per-lease age tracking / stuck leases invisible.

title: Wave 44 of 45: CLI command surface + arg validation + help text + UX
description:
Wave 44/45. 10 sonnets on CLI UX.

Lenses:
1. Command tree inventory (m80-cli subcommands; depth)
2. Arg validation completeness (clap validators)
3. Help text quality (each subcommand has --help with examples?)
4. Default value documentation
5. Output formats: human vs JSON; consistency
6. Error-to-stderr discipline; --quiet semantics
7. Environment variable inventory: M80_* knobs
8. Shell completion availability
9. Manpage / SYNOPSIS quality (or none)
10. Confirmation prompts on destructive ops (warm-owner takeover, etc.)

title: CLI UX gaps: missing examples + clap env() wiring + no --quiet/--verbose + stdout leaks
description:
**Finding (W44.3 + W44.4 + W44.6):**

MED (help text quality):
- WarmEnableArgs (args.rs:214 area) has NO struct-level doc comment. Missing operational explanation of "resident warm owner".
- No usage examples in any subcommand --help. Critical for `warm enable`, `run --warm`, `quickstart`, `logs --request-id`.
- No cross-references (warm enable ↔ run --warm ↔ warm status).

MED (defaults visibility):
- args.rs:234,238 quickstart --artifact-dir/--run-root document M80_ARTIFACT_DIR/M80_RUN_ROOT fallback in /// doc-comment ONLY; clap `env()` attribute NOT used. Help output lacks the [env: M80_ARTIFACT_DIR=] and [default: /opt/m80/artifacts] machine-readable annotations.
- --egress / --writeback show value-enum defaults but no note that M80_EGRESS/M80_WRITEBACK do NOT exist; user setting them gets silently ignored.

LOW (stdout/stderr leaks):
- crates/m80-cli/src/cmds.rs:627 — `println!("cleanup complete")` status prose on stdout. Should be stderr.
- crates/m80-cli/src/cmds_walk.rs:147 — `println!("(no run-root at {})")` informational prose on stdout. Should be stderr.
- No --quiet / --verbose flag exists at all; only --json. No tracing-subscriber init in CLI (cross-link m80-9jfaz.6).

NULL audits:
- W44.1: command tree is well-shaped (11 top-level, 2 nested groups, no aliases/hidden cmds, --json is global).
- W44.5: --json discipline is excellent — all error paths consistently use errors::render_error(&e, json); ErrorEnvelope wraps with {version, request_id, data}.

NULL with action items below:
- W44.8 shell completions: no clap_complete usage. Add `m80 completions <shell>` subcommand when CLI stabilizes (low priority for v0.x).
- W44.9 manpages: no clap_mangen, no man/. Future bead.

Severity: LOW-MEDIUM.

Acceptance:
- Add struct-level docs + usage examples to each major subcommand (`run`, `warm enable`, `quickstart`, `logs`).
- Wire clap `env("M80_ARTIFACT_DIR")` etc. on quickstart args; remove the manual unwrap_or_else.
- Fix the 2 stdout-leak `println!`s to `eprintln!`.
- Document --json envelope schema in docs/behaviors/cli/json-schema.md (cross W44.5).
- M80_DEBUG_WIRE env var: add to docs/behaviors/configuration/env-schema.md (currently only in source-file module docs).

title: Add arg validation + clap value_parser ranges: paths-exist, url-scheme, vcpu/mem ranges
description:
**Finding (W44.2):** Arg validation is deferred from clap-parse-time to runtime, producing late errors that bypass clap's own error formatting.

MEDIUM:
- args.rs:230 quickstart --artifact-url: no URL scheme validation. Passed verbatim to curl. At minimum reject inputs without http:// or https://.

LOW (range-on-parse):
- args.rs:75 Run::vcpu_count: u32 — zero-check at cmds.rs:125. Use `value_parser = clap::value_parser!(u32).range(1..)`.
- args.rs:78 Run::mem_size_mib: u32 — same pattern. Range 64..=65536 (cross-link m80-nns65.2).
- args.rs:214 WarmEnableArgs::size: usize — same.
- args.rs:71 Run::scratch_size: u64 — zero-check at cmds.rs:118; consider 1..=MAX_SCRATCH (cross m80-nns65.2).

LOW (type smell):
- args.rs:51 Run::cwd: Option<String> — should be PathBuf; downstream path-building is already PathBuf.

LOW (existence checks deferred):
- args.rs:47 Run::workspace: Option<PathBuf>
- args.rs:237 QuickstartArgs::artifact_dir
- args.rs:241 QuickstartArgs::run_root
None check existence at parse time; errors surface deep in jailer setup. Add `value_parser = path_exists_validator` (custom) or accept the deferred-validation tradeoff and document it.

LOW (env --key=value parsed late):
- args.rs:54 Run::env: Vec<String> — KEY=VAL format documented in value_name only. Parse fn at cmds.rs:428. Custom `value_parser` would give clap-style errors.

Severity: LOW.

Acceptance:
- URL scheme validator on --artifact-url (HIGH-value, low-effort).
- Apply value_parser.range() on vcpu_count/mem_size_mib/warm-size.
- Switch Run::cwd to PathBuf.
- Document deferred-validation policy in args.rs module doc.

title: Destructive CLI ops missing --yes/--confirm/--dry-run; warm disable silent over dead socket
description:
**Finding (W44.10):** Destructive CLI ops act immediately with zero friction; no confirmation, no dry-run, no pre-action summary.

HIGH (silent destroy):
- `m80 warm disable` — if owner unreachable, disable_owner() silently calls remove_owner_state() and prints "disabled" — indistinguishable from clean shutdown. Operator who ran disable expecting a graceful drain has no way to know live state was just deleted.
- `m80 warm enable` — if snapshot dir already exists, silently `remove_dir_all`s before recreate. No warning that existing warm state is being destroyed.

MEDIUM:
- `m80 warm drain` — fires WarmControlRequest::Drain immediately; no "this will stop accepting leases and tear down N slots" pre-message; no `--yes`.
- `m80 cleanup [--force]` — no pre-action summary of what will be reaped/deleted; --force bypasses ambiguous-state guard silently.

NULL: m80 stop --force, m80 reap, m80 walk delete, m80 env reset — none of these subcommands exist in the CLI surface today.

Severity: HIGH (operator surprise + accidental data loss).

Acceptance:
- Add `--yes` flag to: warm drain, warm disable, warm enable (when state pre-exists), cleanup --force.
- For `warm disable`: detect dead-socket vs running-owner cases distinctly and message clearly ("owner socket unresponsive; removing stale state" vs "graceful disable").
- Add `--dry-run` to: warm drain, cleanup.
- Pre-action summary: "warm drain will release N slots (ready=X, filling=Y); proceed?" gated on isatty AND no --yes.
- Cross-link m80-emon8.* (api/visibility) and m80-9jfaz.2 (tracing observability) — destruction events should also emit at warn! level.

title: Warm-pool / Blank VM Allocator (active v0.2 clean-VM latency path)
description:
Warm-pool / blank-VM allocator for sub-200 ms clean-VM allocation on the request path. The snapshot-restore primitive is now captured under m80-rrp.3 with measured restore latency of 274.204 ms P50 idle and 444.972 ms P50 loaded; that is too high to put directly on every clean stateless request. The remaining warm-pool goal is to pre-restore guestd-ready slots ahead of demand and hand them out cheaply.

Current active sequence:

1. m80-rrp.1: reset evidence vocabulary. Reuse requires explicit proof; any missing or ambiguous input discards the VM.
2. m80-rrp.2: non-inference rule. Liveness, sockets, metrics, or clean-looking dirs never imply reusable state.
3. m80-rrp.4: design allocator contract, state machine, targets, and sizing model.
4. m80-rrp.5: implement fill / lease / discard / refill.
5. m80-rrp.6: benchmark request-path allocation latency idle and loaded.

Relationship: persistent VMs (m80-qokt.2) are now implemented and measured around 20.6 ms for stateful turn-to-turn sessions. Warm pool is for clean stateless calls where persistence is wrong. Adapter-level routing remains outside m80 core.
notes: active warm-pool performance lane captured: design, reset evidence, non-inference, fill/lease/discard/refill, idle+loaded real-KVM benchmark artifacts

description:

title: Snapshot-restore launch path: 0-boot via firecracker snapshot
description:
Wire m80-snapshot's capture()/restore() execution lane to Firecracker's snapshot REST endpoints. Today the schemas + persistence-path helpers are active in v0.1 but capture() and restore() return SnapshotError::Deferred; this bead replaces those stubs with real plumbing.

## Scope

Snapshot CAPTURE/RESTORE PLUMBING ONLY. Specifically:

- m80-firecracker-client: add put_snapshot_create + put_snapshot_load REST methods + their config types (CreateSnapshot, LoadSnapshot)
- m80-snapshot: real capture() that pauses the VM, calls CreateSnapshot, writes the manifest + restore-metadata, and verifies the artifact set; real restore() that reads the manifest, validates compat (firecracker version + image identity), and orchestrates the LoadSnapshot REST call
- m80-firecracker: a Sandbox::launch_from_snapshot(...) alternative path that skips the cold-boot phases (3,4 partial,11) and instead PUTs LoadSnapshot then InstanceStart-from-snapshot, joining the regular Phase 12b ready-probe path
- m80-cli: m80 launch --from-snapshot <path> wired to the new code path
- Bench: P50/P95 of restore-launched ready latency on idle + loaded host
- Docs: suitability bounds (stale clocks, pre-baked process trees) + compat-check decisions

## NOT in scope (other m80-rrp children)

- Warm-pool management (allocator that holds N pre-restored VMs ready)
- Eviction policy / pool sizing / refill triggers
- Allocation contract surface (lease / handoff to caller)
- Reset-evidence vocabulary integration with restored VMs

This bead delivers the primitive; m80-rrp.4+ (TBD) consumes it for warm pools.

## Acceptance

- m80-firecracker-client exposes put_snapshot_create + put_snapshot_load with fixture-server tests
- m80-snapshot capture() and restore() return Ok in happy-path; SnapshotError::Deferred is removed
- A Sandbox can be launched from a captured snapshot end-to-end on real-KVM (gated behind the existing end_to_end_real_kvm flag)
- m80 launch --from-snapshot <path> works in the CLI
- Bench numbers landed in docs/behaviors/snapshot/restore-latency.md
- README updates for m80-snapshot (capture/restore active), m80-firecracker-client (snapshot endpoints), m80-firecracker (launch_from_snapshot), m80-cli

## Open design questions, captured in leaves

- Capture preconditions: does the VM need to be Paused? Is snapshot a stop-the-world primitive vs concurrent? (DESIGN leaf)
- Compat checks at restore: firecracker version (already in RestoreMetadata), kernel sha, rootfs sha, machine-config (vcpu/mem) — what's the minimum viable check, what produces silent corruption on mismatch? (DESIGN leaf)
- Vsock state across snapshot: does the in-VM guestd's vsock channel survive a snapshot/restore? (research leaf, may overlap with DESIGN)
- Are CreateSnapshot/LoadSnapshot covered by Firecracker's stable API guarantees, or version-pinned? (DESIGN leaf)

## Relationship

This + minimal-init (m80-6a0q) together get end-to-end agent-ready VMs in roughly 300ms steady-state. SmolVM has snapshots too at ~500ms; with both pieces m80 should beat them at roughly half the latency. Warm-pool management on top (other m80-rrp children) makes that latency the steady-state for every exec, not just the second one.
notes: Update 2026-05-04 (post-kata recon): differentiation is stronger than the smolvm framing alone implied. Kata-containers ALSO did not wire firecracker's snapshot REST API — their FC backend's PauseVM/SaveVM/ResumeVM are silent no-ops; their 'VM factory' is QEMU-only and uses QEMU migration machinery (migrate exec:cat>file), not snapshot. No production runtime we surveyed (smolvm libkrun, kata-containers) has a working firecracker snapshot lifecycle. m80-rrp.3 is unclaimed territory in the firecracker microVM space. See kata-exploration/09-snapshot-templates-lifecycle.md and kata-exploration/00-synthesis.md.
