title: Idle watcher panic silently swallowed by `let _ = handle.join()`; leaks VM
description:
**Finding:** lifecycle.rs:177 joins the idle-watcher handle with `let _ = handle.join()`. The _ discards Err(payload) returned when a thread panicked. If the idle watcher panics mid-loop: join silently succeeds from the caller's view; VM leaks (idle timeout never fires, sandbox never force-killed, run-dir never cleaned).

Similar pattern: warm_pool.rs:340 fill worker spawned with bare std::thread::spawn — if launch_slot panics (vs Err), thread dies, FillGuard rolls back filling, last_fill_error is NEVER updated. Pool stalls silently. Partial overlap with m80-r4308.3 (Drop hang on FillGuard); this is the visibility side of the same gap.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:176-177 (idle watcher join), crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:340 (fill worker spawn).

**Severity:** HIGH (silent reliability degradation; invisible failure mode).

**Acceptance:**
- Replace `let _ = handle.join()` with explicit match on join result; on Err(payload), log via tracing::error! including the panic payload string.
- Wrap warm-pool fill worker body in catch_unwind; on panic, set last_fill_error = 'panic: <msg>' + decrement filling.
- Test: inject panic in idle watcher; assert tracing::error! is emitted with payload.

title: m80 quickstart probe failure buries the real preflight error
description:
**Finding:** quickstart.rs:159-183 run_echo_probe spawns 'm80 run -- echo hello' as a child. When the child fails because FC/jailer/jailer-harden binaries are absent, child exits non-zero. Parent receives FcError::CommandFailed { command: 'm80 run -- echo hello', status: 2, output: String::new() } — output is empty because the child's stderr is INHERITED, not captured. User sees:
  error: command `m80 run -- echo hello` failed with exit status: 2
The actual PreflightError variant (FirecrackerBinaryNotFound etc) with its actionable hint() is swallowed entirely.

**File:** crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/quickstart.rs:159-183 (run_echo_probe).

**Severity:** HIGH for first-time UX (poisons the first interaction; user must read source or set up logging to discover the cause).

**Acceptance:**
- Either: run m80_preflight::run() inline before spawning the probe; surface PreflightError directly.
- Or: capture the child's stderr (Command::output() not status()) and re-render it in the CommandFailed error message.
- Test: run quickstart with M80_FIRECRACKER_BIN pointing nowhere; assert the rendered error includes 'firecracker binary not found' + actionable hint.
- Cross-link m80-uh6ex.11 (subprocess stderr capture pattern), m80-ij49d (docs).

title: M80_PHASE_TRACE stderr-only — phase timings lost on failure
description:
**Finding:** diagnostics.rs:237-247 writes 'M80_PHASE name=... vm_id=... elapsed_us=...' to STDERR only when M80_PHASE_TRACE=1. These lines are NOT written to the run-dir's diagnostics.jsonl. Process exits → lines lost unless caller captured stderr. Durable diagnostics.jsonl carries only lifecycle milestones, not per-phase timing. Operator given a preserved run-dir gets lifecycle events but no phase timing on failure.

**File:** crates/m80-observability/src/diagnostics.rs:237-247.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (forensics; combined with launch-failure cleanup deleting partial diagnostics.jsonl = m80-mrjqs.1 — both gaps together = no post-mortem).

**Acceptance:**
- Wire phase_event output into diagnostics.jsonl unconditionally (or behind a separate M80_PHASE_DURABLE env var; not the trace-to-stderr one).
- Keep stderr emit for live operator visibility when M80_PHASE_TRACE=1.
- Cross-link m80-mrjqs.1 (preserve on failure).

title: Firecracker internal log (PUT /logger) never captured — VMM internals invisible on failure
description:

Guest serial (console.log) captures kernel printk + guestd output; FC's own VMM log is discarded. When vsock/boot failure happens inside FC, the only artifact is binary guessing from error timing.

**File:** crates/m80-firecracker/src/launch.rs (entire — no logger PUT).

**Severity:** MEDIUM (forensic blind spot for FC-internal failures).

**Acceptance:**

- m80 list / m80 inspect / m80 logs surfaces fc.log alongside console.log.
- StoppedSandbox::preserve_for_triage retains fc.log along with everything else.

title: Process-wrapper product surface: constrained host view
description:
Grand epic for the user-facing m80 product surface: run a host-like process with an explicitly constrained view of filesystem, environment, runtime image, network, and lifetime. The VM remains an implementation detail.

End state:
- `m80 run [visibility/effect/world/profile options] -- <cmd>` is the front door. Pipe mode streams stdout/stderr in real time and preserves exit code. PTY mode supports TUIs.
- Egress, workspace, cwd, env, stdin, scratch, writeback, credentials, selected image/profile, and warm/cold lifetime are named as process visibility/effect/world policies, not VM machinery.
- Warm execution is exposed as an optional lifecycle acceleration with an explicit resident owner; no hidden daemon and no silent cold fallback.
- First-run UX can get from install/artifacts to `m80 run -- echo hello` without archaeology.
- Debuggability is built in: request_id, typed errors, JSON error envelopes, run-root inspection, console/diagnostics correlation, and KVM e2e smoke.

Non-goals:
- Agent tool semantics in m80 core.
- Docker-compatible lifecycle UX as the primary model.
- Hidden daemon/process manager.
- Silent fallback from requested policy to a weaker/different policy.
- Implicit runtime package installation or OCI image pulling in `m80 run`.

Acceptance:
- Child epics cover command contract, visibility/effects, image/profile selection, pipe streaming, egress, PTY/TUI, warm lifetime, config/errors/diagnostics, quickstart, docs/examples, and e2e smoke.
- Top-level README/help teach the constrained-process model.
- The graph has a single ready first gate for command contract and no dependency cycles.

title: m80-dev: dev-ergonomics wrapper consumer (separate crate/CLI sitting on m80 primitives)
description:
**Status:** Deferred indefinitely. Captures a design conversation (2026-05-08) about whether/how m80 can preserve smolvm-style dev ergonomics while keeping its multi-tenant security model. The conclusion: yes, a meaningful subset, via a **separate consumer that sits on m80 primitives** — not via flags in m80 core.

## Concept

m80's positioning is multi-tenant-first: jailer mandatory, virtio-blk + overlay, FC-only, no host-side daemon coordinator. This is the right call for the production agent-execution use case. But it produces ergonomics that are notably worse than smolvm/libkrun for **single-user developer workflows** (testing m80, sandboxing local builds, dogfooding agents).

A "dev-flavored consumer" — call it `m80-dev` — would package m80's existing primitives with developer-friendly defaults to close most of the gap. Lives **outside m80 core** per CLAUDE.md scope discipline (m80 = mechanics; consumer = product flavor).

## What's already shipped in m80 that helps (no new work)

- **Persistent VM mode** (m80-qokt closed) — VM survives across exec calls, state preserved between commands. The single biggest dev-feel improvement; closes most of the gap from \"throwaway sandbox\" to \"feels like my local box.\"
- **Snapshot/restore** (m80-rrp.3 closed) — fast warm-VM bring-up.
- **Stripped kernel** (m80-ci9i closed) — sub-second boot for minimal images.
- **Inverted readiness** (m80-7tpy closed) — no polling, deterministic startup timing.
- **DNS allowlist via vsock proxy** (m80-3xwa.5 G3 closed) — name-based egress allowlist already exists.

## Achievable with small focused additions to m80 core

These are real m80 primitives that would unblock specific ergonomics. File concretely **only when this consumer is committed to**, not pre-emptively:

- **SSH agent forwarding via vsock** — was proposed as m80-3xwa.7 during the 2026-05-07 deep audit; the umbrella was closed with narrowed scope and 3xwa.7 was not filed. Resurrect as a small standalone bead when dev mode is concrete; ~400 LOC + protocol additions per the audit findings (smolvm pattern at /tank/projects/smolvm/crates/smolvm-agent/src/ssh_agent.rs).
- **Workspace-from-CWD bootstrap** — pre-attach pattern; loop-mount the per-VM workspace disk on host, copy CWD contents in, unmount, then PATCH /drive. Uses existing m80-storage primitives; no new m80 surface needed. Just a recipe for the consumer.
- **Mkdir+chown via FileMkdir** (m80-oye1 closed) — already shipped; useful for dev wrapper directory bootstrap.

## Structurally blocked by FC architecture (cannot deliver without VMM swap)

These are real ceilings on what dev ergonomics m80 can offer while staying on Firecracker:

| smolvm ergonomic | Why blocked on FC |
|---|---|
| Live host file access (\`tail -f\` workspace from host while VM runs) | virtio-fs not in upstream FC; closed device set is intentional |
| In-process VMM (function call instead of fork+exec) | FC is a separate binary by design; ~50-200 ms launch overhead is structural |
| Embedded kernel (no separate vmlinux) | FC takes kernel as a separate file |
| TSI rootless networking | libkrun-specific; FC needs taps/bridges/iptables |
| GPU passthrough | virtio-gpu not in FC upstream |

If any of these become must-haves for the dev case, the answer is **VMM swap** — most likely to **dragonball** (kata's FC-derivative that adds virtio-fs while keeping FC-compatible REST API and most of m80's existing primitives). Treat as a separate (very large) decision; not part of this bead.

## Proposed shape (when un-deferred)

A separate crate / CLI sitting on m80, e.g., \`m80-dev\` (or any other adapter consumer the team chooses to build):

**Defaults:**
- Persistent VM by default (use m80-qokt mode)
- Workspace bootstrapped from CWD pre-attach (host-side loop-mount + content copy)
- SSH agent forwarding active (requires m80-side primitive — deferred)
- DNS allowlist preconfigured for common dev domains (github.com, registry.npmjs.org, crates.io, pypi.org, etc.)
- Short stop timeouts (devs iterate fast)
- Color output, friendly errors, progress reporting on long ops

**Optional flags:**
- \`--persist\` (default on for dev mode; off when the user wants a clean VM per command)
- \`--no-jailer\` (single-user mode; relaxes some isolation in exchange for ~50-100 ms faster boot)
- \`--share <path>\` (host directory bind-pattern; pre-attach copy or virtio-fs if VMM ever supports it)

**What it does NOT do:**
- Replace m80 core. m80 stays generic and multi-tenant-first.
- Add dev-mode flags inside m80 core. Those would be scope creep; they belong in the consumer.
- Compete with smolvm for general developer-laptop use cases. smolvm/libkrun is the right tool for that audience already.

## Triggers to un-defer

1. **Concrete dev user demand** — someone committing to use m80 as their daily-driver sandbox tool, beyond just testing m80 itself.
2. **\"Live file access during VM run\" emerging as required** — at which point the answer is probably VMM swap to dragonball, and this consumer becomes the natural surface for the new ergonomics.
3. **An adopter team committing to build the wrapper.**

Until any of these surface, the existing m80 primitives + ad-hoc dev recipes (CLI invocation patterns) are sufficient.

## What's NOT in scope

- Changing m80 core defaults (m80 stays multi-tenant-first; jailer mandatory; FC-only).
- Switching VMM (separate decision; would unlock more ergonomics but is much larger).
- Dev-mode flags inside m80 core.
- Single-binary \"smolvm-equivalent\" — that's a different product, not a m80 consumer.

## Sources

- 2026-05-08 conversation: smolvm ergonomics → virtio-fs gating → \"no jailer\" architectural reasoning → dev consumer pattern.
- /tank/projects/m80/smolvm-exploration/ (prior research on libkrun/smolvm).
- docs/future-directions/bestiary-conveyor-belt.md (sibling future direction; production-multi-tenant pattern).
- docs/adapter-boundary.md (the \"consumer above m80\" pattern + Promotion Bar For New Core Verbs).
- 20-agent guest-daemon audit, 2026-05-07 (Lens N: SSH agent forwarding details from smolvm).

title: Wave 38 of 45: RAII / Drop discipline / resource cleanup correctness
description:
Wave 38/45. 10 sonnets on RAII + Drop semantics + cleanup correctness.

Lenses:
1. Drop impl inventory — what fires what side effects (umount, kill, rmdir, unlink)
2. Drop ordering hazards: nested guards, struct field order, partial drops on panic
3. LeaseGuard footgun (CLAUDE.md): tail-expression temporaries dropping too early
4. mem::forget / ManuallyDrop usage
5. RAII guard return signatures: does pub fn return a guard that's easy to misuse?
6. Async-vs-sync Drop: any block-on inside Drop?
7. Cleanup-on-error paths: launch failure_cleanup completeness vs. happy-path
8. tempfile / NamedTempFile leak risk on panic
9. fd leak: File / Socket / UDS that don't close on drop (raw fd handling)
10. Drop guard self-coordination: when multiple guards share state, deadlock risk

title: RunningSandbox field-drop order: kill_guard fires after jail/cgroup torn down
description:
**Finding (W38.2 + W38.10):** Two real ordering hazards in RunningSandbox (crates/m80-firecracker/src/types.rs:407).

Field declaration order (relevant subset):
1. jail: MaterializedJail            (drops 1st: umount bind-mounts, rmdir chroot)
2. cgroup: Option<Subtree>           (drops 2nd: kill procs, rmdir subtree)
...
16. watcher_thread: JoinHandle       (drops late)
18. kill_guard: ForceKillGuard       (drops LAST: SIGKILL + unmount_snapshot_bind)

Hazards on implicit Drop (no explicit stop() called):
1. ForceKillGuard.drop runs umount_snapshot_bind AFTER MaterializedJail already swept its bind mounts. If snapshot bind path lives inside the chroot tree, the directory is already gone → silent failure → mount may stay live on host.
2. watcher_thread.join() runs BEFORE kill_guard kills the process. Watcher may block waiting for a process that's still alive.
3. Subtree.drop (cgroup) may rmdir before kill happens; remove_dir fails silently if procs still inside; cgroup leaf leaks.

Severity: HIGH (silent host-side resource leaks).

Acceptance:
- Reorder RunningSandbox so kill_guard is the FIRST substantive field (drops first: kill process + unmount snapshot bind), watcher_thread second (join the now-stopping watcher), then cgroup (kill+rmdir on emptied cgroup), then jail (unmount chroot + remove dir).
- Add a comment block above the struct documenting the required field order as a load-bearing invariant.
- Add a regression test that constructs a RunningSandbox in test mode and drops it without stop(), then asserts no leftover mounts via /proc/self/mountinfo. (Needs real-KVM substrate — measurement-shaped bead.)
- Kernel-touching diff: PR must include real-KVM smoke evidence per CLAUDE.md.
notes:
Absorbed from merge plan 2026-05-14:
- m80-xeaey.2: `failure_cleanup` cgroup-subtree gap + snapshot-bind

title: failure_cleanup gaps: cgroup subtree + snapshot bind on restore-path latent window
description:
**Finding (W38.7):**

GAP 1 (material): cgroup subtree
- Subtree is created in phase_5b_cgroup_create and held as a local Option<Subtree> in launch().
- No LaunchCgroupCleanupGuard exists in failure_cleanup.rs.
- If a phase after 5b fails, cgroup drops implicitly. Subtree::drop kills procs + rmdir. Drop runs after Rust unwinds the let-binding, but ordering vs LaunchProcessCleanupGuard isn't enforced — ProcessCleanupGuard SIGKILLs the FC pid in its Drop, while Subtree::drop runs concurrently. Race: Subtree::drop may run remove_dir before LaunchProcessCleanupGuard finishes SIGKILL → remove_dir fails → cgroup leaks.
- Fix: add a LaunchCgroupCleanupGuard that runs AFTER process cleanup; disarmed on launch success.

GAP 2 (latent — zero-width today): restore path
- launch_from_snapshot: snapshot_bind.into_mount_path() sets active=false at line 675. run_dir_cleanup.disarm() at line 684. No phases between these lines today, so the window is zero. But any inserted phase between them creates a window where run_dir_cleanup will fs::remove_dir_all over a live snapshot bind mount → leak.
- Fix: defer into_mount_path() until immediately before disarm(), OR convert SnapshotBind into a disarm()/forget() pattern so the window is impossible to introduce.

Severity: MEDIUM (gap 1: real); LOW (gap 2: latent).

Acceptance: add cgroup cleanup guard; restructure restore-path final block.
close_reason: Merged into m80-xeaey.1: `failure_cleanup` cgroup-subtree gap + snapshot-bind

title: Silent discard_sandbox failures in WarmLease/WarmPool drops; lock-file remove errors swallowed
description:
**Finding (W38.1):** Several Drop impls silently swallow cleanup failures via `let _ = ...`.

HIGH (zombie VM risk):
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool/lease.rs:210 WarmLease::drop — `let _ = discard_sandbox(sandbox);` Failure means VM may still be running while slot is returned to pool.
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:293 WarmPool::drop — same `let _ =` on discard_sandbox during shutdown drain. Pool exit appears clean while zombie VMs persist.

MEDIUM (lock-file leaks):
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/runroot.rs:102 LeaseGuard::drop — `let _ = remove_file(lock)`. EROFS or perm failure → lock leak → blocks future launch with no diagnostic.
- crates/m80-storage/src/rootfs.rs:317 TemplateLock::drop — same pattern.

LOW:
- crates/m80-guestd/src/connection/fileops.rs:45 Uploads::drop — temp-file removal silently swallowed. Guest disk fill on guestd crash.
- crates/m80-cli/src/cmds/signal_watcher.rs:40 SignalWatcher::drop — let _ on thread join; panic in watcher invisible.

Severity: MEDIUM. Acceptance: replace each `let _ = ...` with explicit tracing::error!/warn! on Err arm. Cross-link m80-9jfaz.2 (vm_id + spans on lifecycle errors)."
notes:
Absorbed pass 2:
- m80-243wj.13: ` — 243wj.13 ("WarmLease + WarmPool Drop silently swallow discard_sandbox errors") is nearly word-for-word the HIGH finding already in xeaey
- m80-243wj.14: ` — 243wj.14 ("TemplateLock + LeaseGuard Drop silently discard remove_file errors") covers two sites: (a) rootfs.rs TemplateLock Drop (alrea
close_reason: Drop cleanup failures now log explicitly across WarmLease/WarmPool discard, runroot/template lock removal, guestd upload temp cleanup, and signal watcher join; documented in docs/behaviors/lifecycle/drop-cleanup-diagnostics.md and covered by cargo test gates.

title: Replace mem::forget(self) in RunningSandbox::force_kill with explicit poison() pattern
description:
**Finding (W38.4):** 3 mem::forget hits found.

ACCEPTABLE:
- crates/m80-jailer/src/materialized.rs:200 — mem::forget(child) after exec into Firecracker. PID captured in jailer_pid + persisted; teardown owned by JailedFirecracker::drop. Clear comment in code. Could be a tiny `into_pid()` helper but low priority.

NEEDS REFACTOR:
- crates/m80-firecracker/src/lifecycle.rs:225 + :231 — mem::forget(self) in force_kill error path. Ambiguous kill outcome: process may or may not be dead; record_forced_kill_ambiguous logs it. mem::forget skips Drop to avoid re-entrant teardown but ALSO skips MaterializedJail::drop and Subtree::drop, leaving bind mounts + cgroup subtree leaked. Intentional but invisible to reader.

Severity: LOW (cleanup clarity).

Acceptance:
- Add a `poisoned: bool` field to RunningSandbox (or ForceKillGuard).
- Replace mem::forget(self) with `self.poisoned = true; self.kill_guard.disarm(); return Err(...)`. Drop impls of MaterializedJail and Subtree can check the poisoned flag and switch to "log-and-skip" mode if cleanup is ambiguous.
- Cross-link m80-xeaey.1 (field ordering) — both touch RunningSandbox lifecycle.

title: Add #[must_use] to RAII-guard-returning fns: WarmPool::try_lease, Subtree::create, JailerPlan::materialize
description:
**Finding (W38.5):** Three public fns return guard types whose early-drop tears down a live resource. None marked #[must_use]. All call sites SAFE today, but unguarded against future misuse.

- crates/m80-firecracker/src/warm_pool.rs:219 WarmPool::try_lease → Result<WarmLease, FcError>. Lease::drop returns slot to pool. `let _ = pool.try_lease()?` would silently drop lease before exec.
- crates/m80-cgroup/src/lib.rs:59 Subtree::create → Result<Subtree, CgroupError>. Drop kills cgroup procs + rmdir. Early drop tears cgroup down mid-VM.
- crates/m80-jailer/src/plan.rs:86 JailerPlan::materialize → Result<MaterializedJail, JailerError>. Drop unmounts + rmdirs chroot.

Severity: LOW (preventive).

Acceptance:
- Add `#[must_use = "..."]` with crisp warning text on each fn.
- Add doc-comment block above each warning of premature drop.
- For try_lease specifically: consider making WarmLease itself `#[must_use]` so the warning sticks at the type level.

NULL: W38.3 (LeaseGuard tail-expression footgun) audit found zero violations — runroot.rs:91-96 has a clear doc warning and no call site violates the pattern. Discipline is holding.

title: m80-proto: envelope-level call deadline (max-duration field)
description:
m80-proto envelopes today carry payload + request_id + version. There's no per-call deadline / max-duration field. Channel-level timeouts (BRIDGE_IO_TIMEOUT) catch stuck I/O but don't bound a long-running exec. A 60-minute exec keeps streaming as long as I/O moves; there's no wire-level "this whole call must complete within N ms" mechanism.

## Why this matters

The Bestiary or any embedder will want to cap tenant-scoped time budgets:
- Compute-time billing ("kill if over 90 seconds")
- SLA enforcement ("max 5 minutes for this exec")
- Cancellation deadlines that propagate to the guest without a separate Cancel round-trip

Today the workaround is opening a separate vsock connection and sending CancelRequest after the deadline expires. Works but extra round-trip + timing imprecision.

## Scope

- m80-proto: add `max_duration_ms: Option<u64>` to ExecRequest / ExecStreamingRequest (or to Envelope generically — pick one, document).
- m80-guestd: when present, install a deadline timer; when it fires, cancel the in-flight call as if a CancelRequest arrived. Reuse existing cancel-forwarder infrastructure.
- m80-firecracker host-side: optional helper to set the field; existing call sites pass None for unchanged behavior.

## Acceptance
- Envelope with max_duration_ms=N kills the running exec if it exceeds N ms.
- Test verifies process gets SIGTERM/SIGKILL via the existing cancel path.
- max_duration_ms=None is the default and preserves today's unbounded behavior.

## Out of scope
- Wall-clock vs CPU-time semantics (start with wall-clock).
- Cross-call / session-level budget across multiple calls. Per-call only.

## Audit reference
20-agent deep audit Lens K2 (kata-agent vsock transport), 2026-05-07: kata's ttrpc supports per-call deadline via TtrpcContext (rpc.rs:12,777-822). m80 has no equivalent.

title: Cold fresh launch performance exploration
description:
Explore true cold fresh launch performance after the warm-pool/persistent/snapshot paths have landed. This epic is not an alternative to warm pool; it is the residual cold-start improvement lane for cases that must boot a brand-new VM.

Current measured baseline on 2026-05-05:
- minimal cold launch post-storage pivot: about 1517 ms P50 idle
- storage prep after RO-base/overlay pivot: about 216 ms P50
- stripped kernel only bought about 100 ms, so more blind kernel trimming is low confidence
- direct snapshot restore is about 274 ms P50 idle and warm-pool allocation is about 21 ms typical, so cold-launch work must prove value with phase evidence

Angles:
1. guest-ready path reduction: reduce what PID 1 / guestd must do before readiness
2. pre-created overlay/rootfs artifacts: remove residual per-VM mkfs/template setup where safe
3. Firecracker setup/API path audit: quantify and trim jailer/materialization/REST/device setup
4. direct/no-jailer launch experiment: measure the ceiling, not necessarily productize it

Non-goals:
- Replacing warm pool, direct snapshot restore, or persistent VM routing
- Adapter-level policy or agent semantics
- Hidden compatibility fallbacks or tolerant launch behavior
- More kernel trimming without phase evidence

Acceptance:
- Each angle has a concrete measurement artifact, a yes/no recommendation, and either a narrow implementation bead or an explicit dead-end note
- Cold-launch docs summarize the residual bottleneck stack after the four explorations
- No implementation bead is accepted without idle and loaded evidence, or a clear reason the loaded cell is not meaningful
notes: duplicate draft superseded by completed epic m80-w4vc; no children or dependencies
